declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor
declarations.doc:
Stacks 010Q: a cohomological δ-functor from `A` to `B`: additive functors `Fⁿ : A ⥤ B`
(`n ≥ 0`) and, for every short exact sequence `0 → X₁ → X₂ → X₃ → 0` of `A`, connecting
morphisms `δ : Fⁿ(X₃) ⟶ Fⁿ⁺¹(X₁)`, natural in the short exact sequence, such that
`0 → F⁰(X₁) → F⁰(X₂) → F⁰(X₃) → F¹(X₁) → F¹(X₂) → …` is exact.
declarations.statement: structure DeltaFunctor [Preadditive A] [Preadditive B]
declarations.comment: cohomological δ-functor: additive `Fⁿ`, long exact sequence, natural `δ`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor.Hom
declarations.doc:
Stacks 010R: a morphism of δ-functors `F ⟶ G` is a family of natural transformations
`tⁿ : Fⁿ ⟶ Gⁿ` commuting with the connecting morphisms of every short exact sequence.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (F G : DeltaFunctor A B)
declarations.comment: morphism of δ-functors: `tⁿ : Fⁿ ⟶ Gⁿ` commuting with the `δ`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor.IsUniversal
declarations.doc:
Stacks 010S: a δ-functor `F` is universal if every natural transformation `t : F⁰ ⟶ G⁰`
extends uniquely to a morphism of δ-functors `F ⟶ G`.
declarations.statement: class IsUniversal (F : DeltaFunctor A B) : Prop
declarations.comment: universal δ-functor: every `t : F⁰ ⟶ G⁰` extends uniquely to `F ⟶ G`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor.isUniversal_of_effaceable
declarations.doc: Stacks 010T: an effaceable δ-functor is universal.
declarations.statement: theorem isUniversal_of_effaceable [F.Effaceable] : F.IsUniversal
declarations.comment: an effaceable δ-functor is universal (Grothendieck's Tohoku argument)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor.isUniversal_of_forall_exists_mono
declarations.doc:
Stacks 010T in its literal form: if for every `n > 0` and every `X` there is a monomorphism
`u : X ⟶ I` with `Fⁿ(u) = 0`, then `F` is universal.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversal_of_forall_exists_mono
    (h : ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : A), ∃ (I : A) (u : X ⟶ I), Mono u ∧ (F.functor (n + 1)).map u = 0) :
    F.IsUniversal
declarations.comment: literal form: monos `u : A → B` with `Fⁿ(u) = 0` for all `n > 0`, `A`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor.isUniversal_of_isZero_injective
declarations.doc:
Stacks 010T for the standard source of effaceability: if `A` has enough injectives and `Fⁿ`
vanishes on injectives for `n > 0`, then `F` is universal. This is the form used for derived
functors and Čech cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversal_of_isZero_injective [Balanced B] [EnoughInjectives A]
    (h : ∀ (n : ℕ) (I : A) [Injective I], IsZero ((F.functor (n + 1)).obj I)) : F.IsUniversal
declarations.comment: enough injectives and `Fⁿ(I) = 0` for `I` injective, `n > 0`: universal

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor.IsUniversal.iso_ext
declarations.doc:
Stacks 010U, uniqueness: an isomorphism of universal δ-functors is determined by its
degree-zero component.
declarations.statement: lemma iso_ext {α β : F ≅ G} (h : α.hom.app 0 = β.hom.app 0) : α = β
declarations.comment: the isomorphism is unique: it is determined by its degree-zero component

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor.IsUniversal.isoOfIso
declarations.doc:
Stacks 010U: two universal δ-functors with isomorphic degree-zero parts are isomorphic as
δ-functors, by the isomorphism extending the given one.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def isoOfIso (e : F.functor 0 ≅ G.functor 0) : F ≅ G
declarations.comment: universal δ-functors with the same `F⁰` are isomorphic, extending `F⁰ ≅ G⁰`

declarations.name: CochainComplex.shiftIso_hom_app_comp_δ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0117**, third clause: the long exact cohomology sequence is compatible with shifts,
in the sense of the identification `H^{i+k}(A^•) = H^i(A[k]^•)` of Definition 12.14.8 (tag 011H).

The two functorial maps of the sequence are unsigned, but the connecting map picks up `(-1)^k`.
The Stacks project's proof says "compatibility with shifts is immediate from the definitions" and
records no sign; with its own conventions there is one, because 011G shifts differentials by
`(-1)^k` while the 011H identification is the plain unsigned re-indexing. `δ_eq_of_shift` is where
that sign appears.

`shiftIso_hom_app_comp_δ'` is the same statement with the short exactness of the shifted sequence
derived rather than assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem shiftIso_hom_app_comp_δ (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex C ℤ)) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (k i j i' j' : ℤ) (hij : (up ℤ).Rel i j) (hij' : (up ℤ).Rel i' j')
    (hi' : k + i = i') (hj' : k + j = j')
    (hS' : (S.map (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (CochainComplex C ℤ) k)).ShortExact) :
    ((homologyFunctor C (up ℤ) 0).shiftIso k i i' hi').hom.app S.X₃ ≫ hS.δ i' j' hij' =
      k.negOnePow • (hS'.δ i j hij ≫
        ((homologyFunctor C (up ℤ) 0).shiftIso k j j' hj').hom.app S.X₁)
declarations.comment:
third clause, compatibility with shifts; note the `(-1)^k`, which the Stacks
wording does not lead one to expect

declarations.name: CochainComplex.shiftIso_hom_app_comp_δ'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0117**, third clause, with the short exactness of the shifted sequence produced
internally rather than assumed.
declarations.statement:
lemma shiftIso_hom_app_comp_δ' (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex C ℤ)) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (k i j i' j' : ℤ) (hij : (up ℤ).Rel i j) (hij' : (up ℤ).Rel i' j')
    (hi' : k + i = i') (hj' : k + j = j') :
    ((homologyFunctor C (up ℤ) 0).shiftIso k i i' hi').hom.app S.X₃ ≫ hS.δ i' j' hij' =
      k.negOnePow •
        ((hS.map_of_exact (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (CochainComplex C ℤ) k)).δ i j hij ≫
          ((homologyFunctor C (up ℤ) 0).shiftIso k j j' hj').hom.app S.X₁)

declarations.name: ChainComplex.shiftFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 011A.** The shift functor by `n : ℤ` on `ChainComplex C ℤ`, sending a chain complex
`K` to the complex which is `K.X (i + n)` in degree `i` and whose differentials are those of `K`
multiplied by `(-1)^n`.

This mirrors `CochainComplex.shiftFunctor`, which Mathlib has and which is tag 011G; the two
definitions differ only in the complex shape and in the arithmetic discharging `shape`.
declarations.statement: abbrev shiftFunctor (n : ℤ) : ChainComplex C ℤ ⥤ ChainComplex C ℤ
declarations.comment: the definition, together with its three `@[simps]` clauses below

declarations.name: ChainComplex.shiftIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 011B.** For `k : ℤ` the identification `H_{i+k}(A_•) = H_i(A[k]_•)` coming from
`A_{i+k} = A[k]_i`, as an isomorphism of functors.

As for its cochain twin 011H, Mathlib's direction is the opposite of the Stacks project's: the
`hom` component runs `H_a(K[n]) ⟶ H_{a'}(K)` for `a + n = a'`, so the arrow the Stacks project
writes is `inv`. Being an isomorphism it carries the tag either way.

No sign enters, even though the shift multiplies differentials by `(-1)^k`: in
`shiftShortComplexFunctor'` the sign sits on the outer two terms and homology is the subquotient
cut out by the middle one.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def shiftIso (n a a' : ℤ) (ha' : a + n = a') :
    CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (ChainComplex C ℤ) n ⋙
        homologyFunctor C (ComplexShape.down ℤ) a ≅
      homologyFunctor C (ComplexShape.down ℤ) a'
declarations.comment: the identification; the Stacks arrow `H_{i+k}(A_•) → H_i(A[k]_•)` is its `inv`

declarations.name: Homotopy.equivHomShiftChain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 011C**, second sentence. Given one homotopy `h₀` from `a` to `b`, the homotopies from
`a` to `b` correspond to the morphisms of complexes `A_• ⟶ B[1]_•`, by `h ↦ h - h₀`. Together with
the fact that the target is a group, this is the assertion that the homotopies from `a` to `b`
form a principal homogeneous space under it whenever they are nonempty.
declarations.statement: def equivHomShiftChain (h₀ : Homotopy a b) : Homotopy a b ≃ (A ⟶ B⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)

declarations.name: Homotopy.equivHomShiftChainSelf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 011C**, first sentence. The self-homotopies of `a` correspond to the morphisms of
complexes `A_• ⟶ B[1]_•`.
declarations.statement: def equivHomShiftChainSelf (a : A ⟶ B) : Homotopy a a ≃ (A ⟶ B⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
declarations.comment: first sentence, the `b = a` case based at the zero homotopy

declarations.name: ChainComplex.homOfDegreewiseSplit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 011D.** The morphism of complexes `δ(s) : C_• ⟶ A[-1]_•` attached to a degreewise
split complex of chain complexes, with components `π_{n-1} ∘ d_{B,n} ∘ s_n` read in diagrammatic
order.

As for its cochain twin 011J, no exactness is needed: the splittings supply degreewise whatever
the Stacks statement asks of the short exact sequence, so the hypotheses are `Preadditive` and a
`ShortComplex`. The Stacks proof's trailing minus is supplied by `d_{A[-1]} = -d_A`, which is the
`k = -1` case of the `(-1)^k` of 011A.
declarations.statement: def homOfDegreewiseSplit : S.X₃ ⟶ S.X₁⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧

declarations.name: ChainComplex.homOfDegreewiseSplit_f
declarations.doc:
The components of `δ(s)`, `δ(s)_n = π_{n-1} ∘ d_{B,n} ∘ s_n`. Writing the definition at the
index `n - 1`, which is what `(ComplexShape.down ℤ).next` normalises to, makes this hold by `rfl`
with no `XIsoOfEq` in sight.
declarations.statement:
lemma homOfDegreewiseSplit_f (n : ℤ) :
    (homOfDegreewiseSplit S σ).f n
      = sectionHom S σ n ≫ S.X₂.d n (n - 1) ≫ retractionHom S σ (n - 1)

declarations.name: ChainComplex.homologyMap_homOfDegreewiseSplit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 011E.** The map `H_i(δ(s)) : H_i(C_•) ⟶ H_i(A[-1]_•) = H_{i-1}(A_•)` induced by the
morphism `δ(s)` of 011D is the connecting morphism of the long exact homology sequence of 0111.

There is no sign: the identification of 011B is the unsigned re-indexing, because the `(-1)^k` of
the shift sits on the outer two terms of the short complex and homology is cut out by the middle
one. The opposite convention is not merely unproved but false — it forces every such connecting
map to be `2`-torsion.

The identification is taken through `ChainComplex.homologyShiftIso` rather than through
`Functor.shiftIso`, which would need a `(homologyFunctor C (ComplexShape.down ℤ) 0).ShiftSequence ℤ`
instance that the chain side does not have. Registering one is possible but buys only spelling
parity with the cochain twin 011K: `ChainComplex.shiftIso` already *is* the natural isomorphism
the statement wants.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologyMap_homOfDegreewiseSplit (S : ShortComplex (ChainComplex C ℤ))
    (σ : ∀ n, (S.map (eval C (down ℤ) n)).Splitting) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (i j : ℤ) (hij : (down ℤ).Rel i j) (h : i + -1 = j) :
    HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (homOfDegreewiseSplit S σ) i ≫
        (homologyShiftIso S.X₁ (-1) i j h).hom =
      hS.δ i j hij

declarations.name: ChainComplex.homotopyHomOfDegreewiseSplit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 011F.** The family `h_n : C_n ⟶ A_n = A[-1]_{n+1}` is a homotopy between the
morphisms `δ(s)` and `δ(s')` of 011D attached to two choices of splittings.

Unlike its cochain twin 011L, this is stated with `h` and not with `g = -h`: a homotopy of chain
complexes has components `C_n ⟶ D_{n+1}`, and going from `D = A` to `D = A[-1]` shifts by `-1`
rather than by `+1`, which is the other sign. Concretely, `prevD` pairs `h_n` with
`d_{A[-1],n+1} = -d_{A,n}`, and that minus is what turns 011L's `g` into 011F's `h`.
declarations.statement:
def homotopyHomOfDegreewiseSplit :
    Homotopy (homOfDegreewiseSplit S σ) (homOfDegreewiseSplit S σ')
