`F_{II}^p Tot^n = ⨁_{i + j = n, j ≥ p} K^{i,j}` is the companion statement
`isLeast_totalFiltration₂`, which shares the parameters `F` and `hF` with this one; the two
together are the content of [Stacks, Tag 0130] for the second filtration.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_pages_totalFiltration₂
    (F : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n))
    (hF : ∀ p n : ℤ, F p n = Subobject.mk ((K.totalFiltration₂.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n))
    (Z : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n))
    (hZ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Z r p n = F p n ⊓
      (Subobject.pullback ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).d n (n + 1))).obj (F (p + r) (n + 1)))
    (D : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n))
    (hD : ∀ r p n : ℤ, D r p n = Z (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
      (Subobject.«exists» ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).d (n - 1) n)).obj
        (Z (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1)))
    (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C 0)
    (e : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q), (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
      cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)))
    (hδ : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hn : n = p + q),
      ∃ δ : (Z r p n : C) ⟶ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1) : C),
        δ ≫ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1)).arrow =
          (Z r p n).arrow ≫ (K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).d n (n + 1) ∧
        cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)) ≫
            (e r p q n hr hn).inv ≫ (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) =
          δ ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right :
              D r (p + r) (n + 1) ⊓ Z r (p + r) (n + 1) ≤ Z r (p + r) (n + 1))) ≫
            (e r (p + r) (q - r + 1) (n + 1) hr (by omega)).inv) :
    (∃ α : ∀ p q : ℤ, (E.page 0 le_rfl).X (p, q) ≅ (K.X q).X p,
      ∀ p q : ℤ, (E.page 0 le_rfl).d (p, q) (p, q + 1) ≫ (α p (q + 1)).hom =
        (α p q).hom ≫ (K.d q (q + 1)).f p) ∧
    (∃ β : ∀ p q : ℤ, (E.page 1 zero_le_one).X (p, q) ≅ (K.homology q).X p,
      ∀ p q : ℤ, (E.page 1 zero_le_one).d (p, q) (p + 1, q) ≫ (β (p + 1) q).hom =
        (β p q).hom ≫ (q.negOnePow • (K.homology q).d p (p + 1))) ∧
    ∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty ((E.page 2 zero_le_two).X (p, q) ≅ (K.homology q).homology p)

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₂.isLeast_totalFiltration₁
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0130, the first filtration is the one intended.** The degreewise steps `F p n` of the
filtration of `Tot(K^{•,•})` by the first coordinate are `F_I^p Tot^n = ⨁_{i + j = n, i ≥ p}
K^{i,j}`, characterized without arbitrary suprema of subobjects: `F p n` contains the image of
every summand inclusion `K^{i,j} ⟶ Tot^n` with `i ≥ p`, and it is the least subobject of `Tot^n`
that does. Consequently the filtration is decreasing in `p`. Together with
`exists_iso_pages_totalFiltration₁`, which is stated for the same `F` under the same hypothesis
`hF`, this is the content of [Stacks, Tag 0130] for the first filtration: the identifications of
the pages there are identifications for *this* filtration.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLeast_totalFiltration₁
    (F : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n))
    (hF : ∀ p n : ℤ, F p n = Subobject.mk ((K.totalFiltration₁.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n)) :
    (∀ (p i j n : ℤ) (hij : i + j = n), p ≤ i →
      imageSubobject (K.ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ) i j n hij) ≤ F p n) ∧
    (∀ (p n : ℤ) (W : Subobject ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n)),
      (∀ (i j : ℤ) (hij : i + j = n), p ≤ i →
        imageSubobject (K.ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ) i j n hij) ≤ W) → F p n ≤ W) ∧
    (∀ p p' n : ℤ, p ≤ p' → F p' n ≤ F p n)
declarations.comment: the first filtration is ⨁_{i ≥ p} K^{i,j}

declarations.statement:
public theorem isLeast_totalFiltration₂
    (F : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject ((K.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n))
    (hF : ∀ p n : ℤ, F p n = Subobject.mk ((K.totalFiltration₂.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n)) :
    (∀ (p i j n : ℤ) (hij : i + j = n), p ≤ j →

5. `'E_2^{p,q} = H^p_I(H^q_{II}(K^{•,•}))`, the cohomology in degree `p` of the complex

    (hδ : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hn : n = p + q),
      ∃ δ : (Z r p n : C) ⟶ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1) : C),
        δ ≫ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1)).arrow =

        cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)) ≫
            (e r p q n hr hn).inv ≫ (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) =
          δ ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right :

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.AbutsTo.prop_of_prop_page_firstQuadrant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0132 part (4) for a first quadrant spectral sequence.**  Let `E` be a cohomological
spectral sequence of an abelian category which abuts to a graded object `H`, let `P` be a weak
Serre subcategory, and let `r` be a page of `E`.  If the terms of `E_r` vanish outside the first
quadrant and those at the nonnegative bidegrees lie in `P`, then every `H n` lies in `P`.

This is `CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.AbutsTo.prop_of_prop_page` with its hypothesis on the
page split into the two clauses a first quadrant spectral sequence provides: `P` contains the
zero object and is closed under isomorphisms, so the vanishing clause gives `P` at the bidegrees
the other clause does not reach.
declarations.statement:
theorem AbutsTo.prop_of_prop_page_firstQuadrant {r₀ : ℤ}
    {E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C r₀} {H : ℤ → C} (hE : AbutsTo E H)
    (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsWeakSerreClass] {r : ℤ} (hr : r₀ ≤ r)
    (hzero : ∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 ∨ q < 0 → IsZero ((E.page r hr).X (p, q)))
    (hP : ∀ p q : ℕ, P ((E.page r hr).X ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ)))) (n : ℤ) : P (H n)
declarations.comment:
part (4), for a first-quadrant `CohomologicalSpectralSequence` presented by
  `SpectralSequence.AbutsTo`, with the page hypothesis split into vanishing outside the first
  quadrant and membership at the nonnegative bidegrees

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₂.isBounded_and_converges_totalFiltration₁
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0132, the first filtration.** If every diagonal of the double complex `K^{•,•}` has
only finitely many nonzero terms, then the spectral sequence `E` of `Tot(K^{•,•})` filtered by the
first coordinate, presented as in `CochainComplex.isBounded_and_converges_of_isDegreewiseFinite`, is
bounded, the filtration it induces on each `H^n(Tot(K^{•,•}))` is finite, `E` converges to
`H^*(Tot(K^{•,•}))`, and a weak Serre subcategory containing one whole page of `E` contains every
`H^n(Tot(K^{•,•}))`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBounded_and_converges_totalFiltration₁
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, {pq : ℤ × ℤ | pq.1 + pq.2 = n ∧ ¬ IsZero ((K.X pq.1).X pq.2)}.Finite)
    (F : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.totalFiltration₁.X.X n))
    (hF : ∀ p n : ℤ, F p n = Subobject.mk ((K.totalFiltration₁.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n))
    (Z : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.totalFiltration₁.X.X n))
    (hZ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Z r p n =
      F p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (K.totalFiltration₁.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (F (p + r) (n + 1)))
    (D : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.totalFiltration₁.X.X n))
    (hD : ∀ r p n : ℤ, D r p n = Z (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
      (Subobject.«exists» (K.totalFiltration₁.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Z (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1)))
    (FH : ∀ (n _p : ℤ), Subobject (K.totalFiltration₁.X.homology n))
    (hFH : ∀ n p : ℤ, FH n p =
      imageSubobject
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.totalFiltration₁.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n))
    (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C 0)
    (hE : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q), (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
      cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n))) :
    (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((E.page 0 le_rfl).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
    (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ FH n a = ⊤ ∧ FH n b = ⊥) ∧
    (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r), b ≤ r →
      (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) = 0) ∧
    (∀ p n : ℤ,
      IsGLB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
          F p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (K.totalFiltration₁.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (F (p + r) (n + 1))
            ⊔ F (p + 1) n)
        (kernelSubobject (K.totalFiltration₁.X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ F p n ⊔ F (p + 1) n) ∧
      IsLUB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
          F p n ⊓ (Subobject.«exists» (K.totalFiltration₁.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (F (p - r) (n - 1))
            ⊔ F (p + 1) n)
        (imageSubobject (K.totalFiltration₁.X.d (n - 1) n) ⊓ F p n ⊔ F (p + 1) n)) ∧
    (∀ (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.IsWeakSerreClass] (r : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r),
      (∀ p q : ℤ, P ((E.page r hr).X (p, q))) → ∀ n : ℤ, P (K.totalFiltration₁.X.homology n))

    (FH : ∀ (n _p : ℤ), Subobject (K.totalFiltration₂.X.homology n))

            ⊔ F (p + 1) n)
        (kernelSubobject (K.totalFiltration₂.X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ F p n ⊔ F (p + 1) n) ∧
      IsLUB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>

            ⊔ F (p + 1) n)

declarations.name: quasiIso_total_of_resolution
declarations.doc:
Under the hypotheses, the total complex of `DA` exists and the induced
map `K^• → Tot(A^{•,•})` is a quasi-isomorphism (variant in the first
variable `p`).
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_total_of_resolution
    (K : HomologicalComplex A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (DA : HomologicalComplex₂ A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (α : K ⟶ rowZero DA)
    (h : Hypotheses K DA α) :
    ∃ _ : DA.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ),
      ∃ (f : K ⟶ DA.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)),
        (∀ n : ℤ, f.f n =
          α.f n ≫ DA.ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n 0 n (by simp)) ∧
          QuasiIso f

declarations.name: quasiIso_total_of_resolution_flip
declarations.doc:
Under the hypotheses for `DA.flip`, the total complex of `DA` exists and the induced
map `K^• → Tot(A^{•,•})` is a quasi-isomorphism (variant in the second variable `q`).
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_total_of_resolution_flip
    (K : HomologicalComplex A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (DA : HomologicalComplex₂ A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (α : K ⟶ rowZero DA.flip)
    (h : Hypotheses K DA.flip α) :
    ∃ _ : DA.HasTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ),
      ∃ (f : K ⟶ DA.total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)),
        (∀ n : ℤ, f.f n =
          α.f n ≫ DA.ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 n n (by simp)) ∧
          QuasiIso f

declarations.name: injective_iff_everySES_splits
declarations.doc: `I` is injective iff every short exact sequence `0 ⟶ I ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ 0` is split.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_iff_everySES_splits (I : 𝒜) :
    Injective I ↔ EverySESStartingAtSplits I

declarations.name: subsingleton_ext_one_of_injective
declarations.doc:
If `I` is injective then `Ext¹(B, I) = 0` (encoded as `Subsingleton (Ext B I 1)`) for every
object `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_ext_one_of_injective [HasExt 𝒜]
    (I : 𝒜) (hI : Injective I) (B : 𝒜) :
    Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext B I 1)

declarations.name: HasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings
declarations.doc:
The notion of *functorial injective embeddings* for an abelian category `𝒜`: there exists a
functor `J : 𝒜 ⥤ Arrow 𝒜` satisfying the three conditions `IsFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings₁`,
`IsFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings₂`, and `IsFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings₃`.
declarations.statement: def HasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings : Prop

declarations.name: homFunctor_shortExact_of_projective
declarations.doc: `(1) → (2)`: if `P` is projective then `Hom(P, -)` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem homFunctor_shortExact_of_projective {P : 𝒜} [hP : Projective P]
    (S : ShortComplex 𝒜) (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    ((homFunctor P).mapShortComplex.obj S).ShortExact

declarations.name: projective_iff_every_ses_splits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 013C** (narrowed). `(1) ↔ (3)`: `P` is projective iff every short exact
sequence ending in `P` splits.

The Stacks lemma states the equivalence of four conditions; this records the
equivalence between projectivity and the splitting property. The forward
implications to the other two conditions are given by
`homFunctor_shortExact_of_projective` and `ext_one_eq_zero_of_projective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_iff_every_ses_splits (P : 𝒜) :
    Projective P ↔ EverySESEndingInPSplits P

declarations.name: ext_one_eq_zero_of_projective
declarations.doc:
`(1) → (4)`: if `P` is projective then `Ext^1(P, A) = 0` for every `A`.
We use the standard `HasExt` instance from `HasExt.standard 𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ext_one_eq_zero_of_projective {P : 𝒜} [Projective P] (A : 𝒜) :
    haveI : HasExt.{max u v} 𝒜 := HasExt.standard 𝒜
    ∀ (e : Abelian.Ext.{max u v} P A 1), e = 0

declarations.name: HasFunctorialProjectiveSurjections
declarations.doc:
An abelian category `𝒜` *has functorial projective surjections* if there
exists a functor `P : 𝒜 ⥤ Arrow 𝒜` satisfying conditions (1), (2) and (3)
above.
declarations.statement: def HasFunctorialProjectiveSurjections : Prop

declarations.name: CochainComplex.minus
declarations.doc: The property of cochain complexes that are bounded above.
declarations.statement: public def minus : ObjectProperty (CochainComplex C ℤ)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
An injective resolution of a cochain complex `K` in a category `C`: a bounded below cochain
complex `cocomplex` of injective objects of `C`, together with a quasi-isomorphism
`ι : K ⟶ cocomplex`.
declarations.statement: public structure InjectiveResolution (K : CochainComplex C ℤ)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.toCochainComplexResolution
declarations.doc:
An injective resolution of an object `X`, indexed by `ℕ`, read as an injective resolution of
the cochain complex `X[0]`, indexed by `ℤ`: the resolving complex is extended by zero in the
negative degrees, which is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.cochainComplex`.
declarations.statement:
def toCochainComplexResolution (R : InjectiveResolution X) :
    CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor C 0).obj X)
declarations.comment: the identification of the `ℕ`-graded half of the tag with the `ℤ`-graded one

declarations.name: CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution.toNatResolution
declarations.doc:
An injective resolution of the cochain complex `X[0]`, indexed by `ℤ` and vanishing in the
negative degrees, read as an injective resolution of the object `X`, indexed by `ℕ`: the resolving
complex is restricted along `ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat`.

The hypothesis that the resolving complex vanish in the negative degrees cannot be dropped; see
the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
def toNatResolution
    (R : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor C 0).obj X))
    [R.cocomplex.IsStrictlyGE 0] : CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution X
declarations.comment: the identification of the `ℤ`-graded half of the tag with the `ℕ`-graded one, for a resolving complex vanishing in the negative degrees

declarations.name: CochainComplex.isGE_iff_exists_quasiIso_isStrictlyGE
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a category with zero morphisms, a zero object and homology for every short complex,
and let `K` be a cochain complex of `C`. The cohomology of `K` vanishes in all degrees `< n` if and
only if there is a quasi-isomorphism `f : K ⟶ L` with `L` zero in all degrees `< n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGE_iff_exists_quasiIso_isStrictlyGE {C : Type*} [Category C]
    [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroObject C] [CategoryWithHomology C]
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    K.IsGE n ↔ ∃ (L : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : K ⟶ L) (_ : QuasiIso f), L.IsStrictlyGE n

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_injectiveResolution_isStrictlyGE
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian category with enough injectives, let `a : ℤ` and let `K` be a cochain
complex of `A` with `H ^ n (K) = 0` for `n < a`. Then `K` has an injective resolution `R` whose
resolving complex satisfies `R.cocomplex.X n = 0` for `n < a`; and if moreover `K.X n = 0` for
`n < a`, then `R` can be chosen with all the components `R.ι.f n : K.X n ⟶ R.cocomplex.X n`
monomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_injectiveResolution_isStrictlyGE [EnoughInjectives A] (a : ℤ)
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) [K.IsGE a] :
    ∃ (R : K.InjectiveResolution) (_ : K.IsStrictlyGE a → ∀ n, Mono (R.ι.f n)),
      R.cocomplex.IsStrictlyGE a

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_factorization_isDegreewiseSplitMono
declarations.doc:
Let `α : K ⟶ L` be a morphism of cochain complexes of an additive category. Then there are a
complex `L'`, a factorization `α = α' ≫ π` of `α` through `L'` with `α'` a termwise split
injection, and a section `s : L ⟶ L'` of `π` with `π ≫ s` homotopic to `𝟙 L'`. Moreover `L'`
inherits the vanishing bounds of `K` and `L`, so that `L'` is bounded below, bounded above or
bounded as soon as both `K` and `L` are.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_factorization_isDegreewiseSplitMono {A : Type*} [Category A]
    [Preadditive A] [HasBinaryBiproducts A] {K L : CochainComplex A ℤ} (α : K ⟶ L) :
    ∃ (L' : CochainComplex A ℤ) (α' : K ⟶ L') (π : L' ⟶ L) (s : L ⟶ L'),
      α' ≫ π = α ∧ α'.IsDegreewiseSplitMono ∧ s ≫ π = 𝟙 L ∧
        Nonempty (Homotopy (π ≫ s) (𝟙 L')) ∧
        (∀ a : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyGE (a + 1) → L.IsStrictlyGE a → L'.IsStrictlyGE a) ∧
        (∀ a : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyLE a → L.IsStrictlyLE a → L'.IsStrictlyLE a)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.IsKInjective.exists_factorization_of_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian category, let `α : K ⟶ L` be a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of
`A`, let `I` be a K-injective cochain complex of `A` and let `γ : K ⟶ I`. Then (1) there is a
morphism of complexes `β : L ⟶ I` such that `α ≫ β` is homotopic to `γ`, and (2) if every term of
`I` is an injective object and `α` is a monomorphism in every degree, then there is a `β` with
`α ≫ β = γ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsKInjective.exists_factorization_of_quasiIso [I.IsKInjective] (α : K ⟶ L)
    [QuasiIso α] (γ : K ⟶ I) :
    (∃ β : L ⟶ I, Nonempty (Homotopy (α ≫ β) γ)) ∧
      (∀ [∀ n, Injective (I.X n)] [∀ n, Mono (α.f n)], ∃ β : L ⟶ I, α ≫ β = γ)
declarations.comment: for a K-injective target, which by 013R covers the source's hypothesis that the target be bounded below with injective terms; the extra hypotheses of part (2) are attached to its own conjunct

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_desc_of_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 013P, part (2), for `ℕ`-indexed complexes: descent with minimal hypotheses.** Let `C`
be an abelian category, let `ε : Z[0] ⟶ K` be a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of `C`
indexed by `ℕ`, let `L` be a cochain complex of injective objects and let `γ : Z[0] ⟶ L`. Then
`γ = ε ≫ β` for a (unique up to homotopy, see
`CochainComplex.nonempty_homotopy_of_precomp_quasiIso`) morphism `β : K ⟶ L`.

Neither `K` nor `L` is required to be an injective resolution: the terms of `K` are arbitrary and
`L` resolves nothing. Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.desc` is the special case
where both are the resolving complexes of injective resolutions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_desc_of_quasiIso [∀ n, Injective (L.X n)] (ε : (single₀ C).obj Z ⟶ K) [QuasiIso ε]
    (γ : (single₀ C).obj Z ⟶ L) : ∃ β : K ⟶ L, ε ≫ β = γ
declarations.comment: part (2), for `ℕ`-indexed complexes, with the source required only to be quasi-isomorphic to a complex concentrated in degree zero and the target only to have injective terms

registrations.name: CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective
registrations.comment: the lemma's induction, with a supplied bound `d` for the boundedness below: a complex which is strictly bounded below by `d` and whose terms are injective objects is K-injective

registrations.name: CochainComplex.IsKInjective.nonempty_homotopy_zero
registrations.comment: the conclusion at one morphism, the source's sentence: a morphism from an acyclic complex to a K-injective complex is homotopic to zero

registrations.name: CochainComplex.IsKInjective.rightOrthogonal
registrations.comment: the conclusion in `K(A)`: a K-injective complex is right orthogonal to the acyclic complexes, i.e. every morphism `K ⟶ I` of `K(A)` with `K` acyclic is zero

declarations.name: CochainComplex.IsKInjective.nonempty_homotopy_of_precomp_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian category, let `α : K ⟶ L` be a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of
`A` and let `I` be a K-injective cochain complex of `A`. Then two morphisms `β₁, β₂ : L ⟶ I` with
`α ≫ β₁` homotopic to `α ≫ β₂` are homotopic.
declarations.comment: for a K-injective target, which by Tag 013R covers the source's bounded below complex of injective objects; the source's intermediary `γ : K ⟶ I` is eliminated by transitivity of homotopy

declarations.name: CochainComplex.nonempty_homotopy_of_precomp_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 013S, for `ℕ`-indexed complexes: uniqueness of the descent with minimal
hypotheses.** Two morphisms `β₁, β₂ : K ⟶ L` from a cochain complex quasi-isomorphic to `Z[0]`
into a cochain complex of injective objects which agree, up to homotopy, after precomposition with
a quasi-isomorphism `ε : Z[0] ⟶ K`, are homotopic.

As in `CochainComplex.exists_desc_of_quasiIso`, neither complex need be an injective resolution.
Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.descHomotopy` is the special case where both are;
`CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.descHomotopy'` weakens the target alone.
declarations.comment: for `ℕ`-indexed complexes, with the source required only to be quasi-isomorphic to a complex concentrated in degree zero and the target only to have injective terms

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.exists_shortExact_injectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian category with enough injectives, let `S : 0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0` be a
short exact sequence of cochain complexes of `A` with `X₂` (hence `X₁` and `X₃`) vanishing in the
degrees `< a`, and let `R₁` be any injective resolution of `X₁`. Then there are injective
resolutions `R₂` of `X₂` and `R₃` of `X₃` and a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ I₁ ⟶ I₂ ⟶ I₃ ⟶ 0` of the
resolving complexes making both squares commute; and if `I₁` also vanishes in the degrees `< a`,
then `I₂` and `I₃` may be chosen to do so as well.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_shortExact_injectiveResolution [EnoughInjectives A] (a : ℤ)
    {S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex A ℤ)} (hS : S.ShortExact) [S.X₂.IsStrictlyGE a]
    (R₁ : S.X₁.InjectiveResolution) :
    ∃ (R₂ : S.X₂.InjectiveResolution) (R₃ : S.X₃.InjectiveResolution)
      (f : R₁.cocomplex ⟶ R₂.cocomplex) (g : R₂.cocomplex ⟶ R₃.cocomplex)
      (w : f ≫ g = 0) (_ : (ShortComplex.mk f g w).ShortExact)
      (_ : R₁.cocomplex.IsStrictlyGE a →
        R₂.cocomplex.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ R₃.cocomplex.IsStrictlyGE a),
      R₁.ι ≫ f = S.f ≫ R₂.ι ∧ R₂.ι ≫ g = S.g ≫ R₃.ι
declarations.comment: parts (1)–(3); the given resolution of the first term is a hypothesis and the degree bound of parts (2) and (3) is an implication in the conclusion, so the source's plain assertion follows by resolving the first term with 013K

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.exists_injectiveResolution_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**The injective horseshoe for `ℕ`-indexed resolutions of objects.** Let `A` be an abelian
category with enough injectives and let `0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0` be a short exact sequence of
objects of `A`. Then there are injective resolutions `J₁`, `J₂`, `J₃` of the three terms and a
short exact sequence `0 ⟶ J₁ ⟶ J₂ ⟶ J₃ ⟶ 0` of the resolving complexes over it: the two squares
built from the augmentations commute in degree zero, and the sequence is split in every degree.

This is the `ℕ`-indexed form of Stacks 013T for a sequence of objects. It is deduced from the
`ℤ`-indexed `StacksDraft.CartanEilenbergResolutions.horseshoeProperty`, with the two outer
resolutions prescribed to be the extensions by zero of arbitrary `ℕ`-indexed ones, by restricting
the resulting sequence of complexes back along `ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat`.

The degreewise splitting is what makes the sequence stay short exact under an arbitrary additive
functor applied degreewise; it is not read off the twisted-biproduct construction of the
horseshoe but recovered afterwards from
`CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.splittingOfInjective`, the first term of the sequence in
degree `n` being the injective object `J₁.cocomplex.X n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injectiveResolution_shortExact [EnoughInjectives A]
    {S : ShortComplex A} (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    ∃ (J₁ : InjectiveResolution S.X₁) (J₂ : InjectiveResolution S.X₂)
      (J₃ : InjectiveResolution S.X₃) (f : J₁.cocomplex ⟶ J₂.cocomplex)
      (g : J₂.cocomplex ⟶ J₃.cocomplex) (w : f ≫ g = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk f g w).ShortExact ∧
      J₁.ι.f 0 ≫ f.f 0 = S.f ≫ J₂.ι.f 0 ∧ J₂.ι.f 0 ≫ g.f 0 = S.g ≫ J₃.ι.f 0 ∧
      ∀ n, ∃ _ : (ShortComplex.mk (f.f n) (g.f n)
        (congrFun (congrArg HomologicalComplex.Hom.f w) n)).Splitting, True
declarations.comment: the `ℕ`-graded form for a short exact sequence of objects, with the degreewise splitting of the resulting sequence of resolving complexes

declarations.name: qhPlus_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**(Claim 1: Exactness.)** The functor of Definition 6 is exact, i.e. it is a triangulated
functor: it commutes with the shift (the `CommShift ℤ` structure on `QhPlus A`) and sends
distinguished triangles of `K^+(I)` to distinguished triangles of `D^+(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem qhPlus_isTriangulated [HasDerivedCategory A] :
    (QhPlus A).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: qhPlus_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**(Main theorem, Stacks 013V.)** The canonical functor `K^+(I) → D^+(A)` of Definition 6
is an equivalence of categories.  Combined with exactness (`qhPlus_isTriangulated`) this
exhibits it as an equivalence of triangulated categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem qhPlus_isEquivalence [EnoughInjectives A] [HasDerivedCategory A] :
    (QhPlus A).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.ResolutionFunctor
declarations.doc:
A *resolution functor* for an abelian category `C` is the data of a bounded below
complex of injectives `(j K).X₁`, i.e. an object of `K⁺(ℐ)`, for every object `K` of
`K⁺(C)`, together with a quasi-isomorphism `(j K).w : K ⟶ (j K).X₁` in `K⁺(C)`: that is,
of a right resolution of every `K` for the inclusion `K⁺(ℐ) ⥤ K⁺(C)`. (Functoriality of
`K ↦ (j K).X₁` is automatic, see [Stacks, Tag 05TJ].)
declarations.statement: public abbrev ResolutionFunctor

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.nonempty_resolutionFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be an abelian category with enough injectives. Then a resolution functor for `C`
exists ([Stacks, Tag 013W]): every object `K` of `K⁺(C)` admits a bounded below complex of
injectives `(j K).X₁` together with a quasi-isomorphism `(j K).w : K ⟶ (j K).X₁` in `K⁺(C)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_resolutionFunctor (C : Type*) [Category C] [Abelian C]
    [EnoughInjectives C] :
    Nonempty (HomotopyCategory.Plus.ResolutionFunctor C)
declarations.comment: T_013X, existence: a resolution functor exists when `C` has enough injectives

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.nonempty_isTerminal_rightResolution
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be an abelian category. A right resolution of an object `K` of `K⁺(C)` is unique up
to unique isomorphism: every right resolution `R` of `K` is a terminal object of the category
`(localizerMorphism C).RightResolution K` of right resolutions of `K`, in which a morphism
`R' ⟶ R` is a morphism `f : R'.X₁ ⟶ R.X₁` of `K⁺(ℐ)` with `R'.w ≫ f = R.w` in `K⁺(C)`. So any
two right resolutions of `K` are related by exactly one morphism compatible with their
comparison maps, and every such morphism is an isomorphism; applied to two resolution functors
this is the uniqueness up to unique isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 013X], and it needs no hypothesis
on `C` beyond `Abelian C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_isTerminal_rightResolution (C : Type*) [Category C] [Abelian C]
    {K : HomotopyCategory.Plus C} (R : (localizerMorphism C).RightResolution K) :
    Nonempty (IsTerminal R)
declarations.comment: T_013X, uniqueness up to unique isomorphism; no hypothesis on `C`

declarations.name: CochainComplex.Plus.exists_functorial_injective_resolution_and_exists_resolutionFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be an abelian category.

(1) If `C` has functorial injective embeddings, i.e. is equipped with a functor
`J : C ⥤ ℐ` to the full subcategory of injective objects and a natural transformation
`η : 𝟭 C ⟶ J` with monomorphic components ([Stacks, Tag 0139]), then there is a functor
`F : Comp⁺(C) ⥤ Comp⁺(ℐ)` on bounded below cochain complexes and a natural transformation
`α : 𝟭 ⟶ F ⋙ ι` whose components are quasi-isomorphisms, i.e. a functorial injective
resolution of bounded below complexes.

(2) Any such pair `(F, α)` — over an arbitrary abelian `C` — induces a resolution functor
for `C` ([Stacks, Tag 013W]), namely the one whose value at `K` is the image of `F K` in
`K⁺(ℐ)` and whose comparison map is the homotopy class of `α_K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_functorial_injective_resolution_and_exists_resolutionFunctor :
    (∀ (J : C ⥤ InjectiveObject C) (η : 𝟭 C ⟶ J ⋙ InjectiveObject.ι C),
        (∀ A, Mono (η.app A)) →
        ∃ (F : CochainComplex.Plus C ⥤ CochainComplex.Plus (InjectiveObject C))
          (α : 𝟭 (CochainComplex.Plus C) ⟶ F ⋙ (InjectiveObject.ι C).mapCochainComplexPlus),
          ∀ K, CochainComplex.Plus.quasiIso C (α.app K)) ∧
      ∀ (F : CochainComplex.Plus C ⥤ CochainComplex.Plus (InjectiveObject C))
        (α : 𝟭 (CochainComplex.Plus C) ⟶ F ⋙ (InjectiveObject.ι C).mapCochainComplexPlus),
        (∀ K, CochainComplex.Plus.quasiIso C (α.app K)) →
        ∃ R : HomotopyCategory.Plus.ResolutionFunctor C,
          ∀ K : CochainComplex.Plus C,
            ∃ h : (R ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient C).obj K)).X₁ =
                (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient (InjectiveObject C)).obj (F.obj K),
              (R ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient C).obj K)).w =
                (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient C).map (α.app K) ≫
                  eqToHom (congrArg (InjectiveObject.ι C).mapHomotopyCategoryPlus.obj h.symm)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsHomological
registrations.comment:
homological functor: sends every distinguished triangle to a sequence
  H(X) → H(Y) → H(Z) exact in the abelian category; it extends `PreservesZeroMorphisms` and
  implies `Additive` (instance), so it is the Stacks notion for an additive functor

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.map_distinguished_op_exact
registrations.comment:
cohomological functor: Mathlib's form is a homological functor `H : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ A`
  for the opposite pretriangulated structure, whose defining exactness is
  H(Z) → H(Y) → H(X) for each distinguished triangle of `D`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.homologySequenceδ
registrations.comment: the connecting map H(h) : H^n(Z) → H^(n+1)(X), with H^n = `F.shift n`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.homologySequenceComposableArrows₅_exact
registrations.comment:
the exact sequence itself, as a `ComposableArrows A 5` from H^n(X) to
  H^(n+1)(Z); the long exact sequence is the family of these over all n

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.ComponentwiseInvertibility.isIso_of_five
declarations.doc:
**The five lemma in a pretriangulated category.**  Two distinguished triangles connected by
five morphisms whose four consecutive squares commute, with the first, second, fourth and fifth
invertible, have invertible third morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_five {C : Type*} [Category* C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [HasZeroObject C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C]
    (T T' : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) (hT' : T' ∈ distTriang C)
    (a₁ : T.obj₁ ⟶ T'.obj₁) (a₂ : T.obj₂ ⟶ T'.obj₂) (a₃ : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₃)
    (a₄ : T.obj₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ T'.obj₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (a₅ : T.obj₂⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ T'.obj₂⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (ha₁ : IsIso a₁) (ha₂ : IsIso a₂) (ha₄ : IsIso a₄) (ha₅ : IsIso a₅)
    (h₁ : T.mor₁ ≫ a₂ = a₁ ≫ T'.mor₁)
    (h₂ : T.mor₂ ≫ a₃ = a₂ ≫ T'.mor₂)
    (h₃ : T.mor₃ ≫ a₄ = a₃ ≫ T'.mor₃)
    (h₄ : T.mor₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' ≫ a₅ = a₄ ≫ T'.mor₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧') :
    IsIso a₃
declarations.comment: the rotation `two of (a, b, c) isomorphisms give the third` in the case `a, b` give `c`, in an arbitrary pretriangulated category. The five independent morphisms with four commuting squares are a weaker hypothesis than a morphism of triangles, which forces the fourth and fifth to be `a⟦1⟧'` and `b⟦1⟧'`; Mathlib's `isIso₃_of_isIso₁₂` consumes a morphism of triangles and so does not apply in this form, and the proof here is from the exactness of the Yoneda sequences of the two triangles rather than from it. The other two rotations, for data that is a morphism of triangles, are Mathlib's `isIso₁_of_isIso₂₃` and `isIso₂_of_isIso₁₃`

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex.Hom.IsDegreewiseSplitMono
declarations.doc:
A morphism of complexes `α : K ⟶ L` is a *termwise split injection*, in the terminology
of [Stacks, Tag 014G], if each component `α.f n` is a split monomorphism, i.e. admits a
retraction. The retractions are not required to be compatible with the differentials, so
that such an `α` need not be a split monomorphism of complexes.
declarations.statement: public def IsDegreewiseSplitMono (α : K ⟶ L) : Prop

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex.Hom.IsDegreewiseSplitEpi
declarations.doc:
A morphism of complexes `β : K ⟶ L` is a *termwise split surjection*, in the terminology
of [Stacks, Tag 014G], if each component `β.f n` is a split epimorphism, i.e. admits a
section. The sections are not required to be compatible with the differentials, so that such
a `β` need not be a split epimorphism of complexes.
declarations.statement: public def IsDegreewiseSplitEpi (β : K ⟶ L) : Prop

declarations.name: exists_homotopic_comm_of_isTermwiseSplitInjection
declarations.doc:
Consider a square

      A ---f---> B
      |          |
      a          b
      |          |
      v          v
      C ---g---> D

of morphisms of cochain complexes that commutes up to homotopy
(`b ∘ f ∼ g ∘ a`, i.e. `Nonempty (Homotopy (f ≫ b) (a ≫ g))`). If `f` is a
termwise split injection, then there is a morphism `b'` homotopic to `b` such
that the square commutes on the nose: `b' ∘ f = g ∘ a` (`f ≫ b' = a ≫ g`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopic_comm_of_isTermwiseSplitInjection {Ac Bc Cc Dc : CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ}
    (f : Ac ⟶ Bc) (a : Ac ⟶ Cc) (b : Bc ⟶ Dc) (g : Cc ⟶ Dc)
    (hsq : Nonempty (Homotopy (f ≫ b) (a ≫ g)))
    (hf : IsTermwiseSplitInjection f) :
    ∃ b' : Bc ⟶ Dc, Nonempty (Homotopy b' b) ∧ f ≫ b' = a ≫ g

declarations.name: exists_homotopic_comm_of_isTermwiseSplitSurjection
declarations.doc:
Consider a square of morphisms of cochain complexes `f : A ⟶ B`, `a : A ⟶ C`, `b : B ⟶ D`,
`g : C ⟶ D` that commutes up to homotopy (`Nonempty (Homotopy (f ≫ b) (a ≫ g))`). If `g` is a
termwise split surjection, then there is a morphism `a'` homotopic to `a` such that the square
commutes on the nose: `g ∘ a' = b ∘ f` (`a' ≫ g = f ≫ b`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopic_comm_of_isTermwiseSplitSurjection {Ac Bc Cc Dc : CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ}
    (f : Ac ⟶ Bc) (a : Ac ⟶ Cc) (b : Bc ⟶ Dc) (g : Cc ⟶ Dc)
    (hsq : Nonempty (Homotopy (f ≫ b) (a ≫ g)))
    (hg : IsTermwiseSplitSurjection g) :
    ∃ a' : Ac ⟶ Cc, Nonempty (Homotopy a' a) ∧ a' ≫ g = f ≫ b

declarations.name: CochainComplex.mappingCone.isIso₃_of_isIso₁₂
declarations.doc:
Let `f₁ : K₁ ⟶ L₁` and `f₂ : K₂ ⟶ L₂` be morphisms of cochain complexes of an additive
category `𝒜`, and let `φ = (a, b, c)` be a morphism of triangles of the homotopy category `K(𝒜)`
from the cone triangle `K₁ ⟶ L₁ ⟶ C(f₁) ⟶ K₁⟦1⟧` of `f₁` to the cone triangle of `f₂`. If `a`
and `b` are homotopy equivalences, i.e. isomorphisms in `K(𝒜)`, then so is `c`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso₃_of_isIso₁₂ [HasZeroObject 𝒜] [HasBinaryBiproducts 𝒜]
    {K₁ L₁ K₂ L₂ : CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ} {f₁ : K₁ ⟶ L₁} {f₂ : K₂ ⟶ L₂}
    (φ : triangleh f₁ ⟶ triangleh f₂) (h₁ : IsIso φ.hom₁) (h₂ : IsIso φ.hom₂) :
    IsIso φ.hom₃

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_triangleh_iso_trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit_and_exists_iso_triangleh
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒜` be an additive category.

(1) Given a termwise split exact sequence of cochain complexes — a short complex `S` together
with a splitting `σ n` of each of its degreewise evaluations — the cone triangle
`S.X₁ → S.X₂ → C(S.f) --(-p)--> S.X₁[1]` of its first map is isomorphic in `K(𝒜)` to the triangle
`S.X₁ → S.X₂ → S.X₃ --δ--> S.X₁[1]` associated to the sequence, by an isomorphism of triangles
which is the identity on `S.X₁` and on `S.X₂` and whose third component is the class of the
canonical morphism `C(S.f) ⟶ S.X₃` given by the projection onto `S.X₂` followed by `S.g`; in
particular that canonical morphism is a homotopy equivalence.

(2) Given a morphism of cochain complexes `f : K ⟶ L`, there are a termwise split exact sequence
`K → L̃ → M` starting at `K` and an isomorphism in `K(𝒜)` from its associated triangle
`K → L̃ → M --δ--> K[1]` to the cone triangle `K → L → C(f) --(-p)--> K[1]` of `f` which is the
identity on `K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_triangleh_iso_trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit_and_exists_iso_triangleh
    {𝒜 : Type*} [Category 𝒜] [Preadditive 𝒜] [HasZeroObject 𝒜] [HasBinaryBiproducts 𝒜] :
    (∀ (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ))
        (σ : ∀ n, (S.map (eval 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).Splitting),
        ∃ e : mappingCone.triangleh S.f ≅ trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit S σ,
          e.hom.hom₁ = 𝟙 ((HomotopyCategory.quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj S.X₁) ∧
            e.hom.hom₂ = 𝟙 ((HomotopyCategory.quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj S.X₂) ∧
            e.hom.hom₃ = (HomotopyCategory.quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map
              (mappingCone.desc S.f 0 S.g (by simp))) ∧
      ∀ {K L : CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ} (f : K ⟶ L),
        ∃ (L' M : CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) (f' : K ⟶ L') (g : L' ⟶ M) (w : f' ≫ g = 0)
          (σ : ∀ n, ((ShortComplex.mk f' g w).map (eval 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).Splitting)
          (e : trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit (ShortComplex.mk f' g w) σ ≅ mappingCone.triangleh f),
          e.hom.hom₁ = 𝟙 ((HomotopyCategory.quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_composableArrows_isDegreewiseSplitMono
declarations.doc:
Let `F : A₀ ⟶ A₁ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ Aₙ` be a sequence of composable morphisms of cochain complexes of an
additive category. Then there are a sequence `G : B₀ ⟶ B₁ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ Bₙ` and a morphism of diagrams
`φ : G ⟶ F` such that each `Bᵢ ⟶ Bᵢ₊₁` is a termwise split injection and each `Bᵢ ⟶ Aᵢ` is a
homotopy equivalence. Moreover, if all the `Aᵢ` are bounded below (resp. bounded above), then so
are all the `Bᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_composableArrows_isDegreewiseSplitMono {n : ℕ}
    (F : ComposableArrows (CochainComplex A ℤ) n) :
    ∃ (G : ComposableArrows (CochainComplex A ℤ) n) (φ : G ⟶ F),
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (_ : i + 1 ≤ n), (G.map' i (i + 1)).IsDegreewiseSplitMono) ∧
      (∀ i, HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (φ.app i)) ∧
      ((∀ i, CochainComplex.plus A (F.obj i)) → ∀ i, CochainComplex.plus A (G.obj i)) ∧
      ((∀ i, CochainComplex.minus A (F.obj i)) → ∀ i, CochainComplex.minus A (G.obj i))

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_triangleOfDegreewiseSplit_invRotate_iso_mappingCone_triangle
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒜` be an additive category and let `S` be a termwise split short exact sequence of
cochain complexes of `𝒜`, split by `σ`, with associated triangle
`S.X₁ → S.X₂ → S.X₃ --δ--> S.X₁[1]` (`CochainComplex.triangleOfDegreewiseSplit`). Then the
inverse rotation `S.X₃[-1] --δ[-1]--> S.X₁ --S.f--> S.X₂` of that triangle is isomorphic, by an
isomorphism of triangles of complexes which is the identity on `S.X₃[-1]` and on `S.X₁`, to the
cone triangle `S.X₃[-1] --δ[-1]--> S.X₁ --i--> C(δ[-1]) --(-p)--> S.X₃[-1][1]` of its own first
map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_triangleOfDegreewiseSplit_invRotate_iso_mappingCone_triangle
    (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ))
    (σ : ∀ n, (S.map (eval 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).Splitting) :
    ∃ e : (triangleOfDegreewiseSplit S σ).invRotate ≅
        mappingCone.triangle (triangleOfDegreewiseSplit S σ).invRotate.mor₁,
      e.hom.hom₁ = 𝟙 ((triangleOfDegreewiseSplit S σ).invRotate.obj₁) ∧
        e.hom.hom₂ = 𝟙 S.X₁

declarations.name: exists_octahedron_of_termwiseSplitInj
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Tag 014R, Lemma 13.10.2).**
Let `A` be an additive category and let `α : Acx → Bcx` and `β : Bcx → Ccx` be termwise split
injections of complexes. Then there exist complexes `Q₁ Q₂ Q₃` of `A`, morphisms
`p₁ : Q(Bcx) → Q(Q₁)`, `p₂ : Q(Ccx) → Q(Q₂)`, `p₃ : Q(Ccx) → Q(Q₃)` and connecting morphisms
`d₁ : Q(Q₁) → Q(Acx)⟦1⟧`, `d₂ : Q(Q₂) → Q(Acx)⟦1⟧`, `d₃ : Q(Q₃) → Q(Bcx)⟦1⟧` in `K(A)` such that:

* the three triangles
  `(Q(Acx), Q(Bcx), Q(Q₁), Q(α), p₁, d₁)`,
  `(Q(Acx), Q(Ccx), Q(Q₂), Q(β ∘ α), p₂, d₂)`,
  `(Q(Bcx), Q(Ccx), Q(Q₃), Q(β), p₃, d₃)`
  are distinguished triangles of `K(A)`; and

* axiom TR4 (Definition 6) holds for these three distinguished triangles with respect to the
  composable morphisms `Q(α)` and `Q(β)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_octahedron_of_termwiseSplitInj
    {Acx Bcx Ccx : Cpx A}
    (α : TermwiseSplitInj Acx Bcx) (β : TermwiseSplitInj Bcx Ccx) :
    ∃ (Q₁ Q₂ Q₃ : Cpx A)
      (p₁ : (Qfun A).obj Bcx ⟶ (Qfun A).obj Q₁)
      (p₂ : (Qfun A).obj Ccx ⟶ (Qfun A).obj Q₂)
      (p₃ : (Qfun A).obj Ccx ⟶ (Qfun A).obj Q₃)
      (d₁ : (Qfun A).obj Q₁ ⟶ ((Qfun A).obj Acx)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (d₂ : (Qfun A).obj Q₂ ⟶ ((Qfun A).obj Acx)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (d₃ : (Qfun A).obj Q₃ ⟶ ((Qfun A).obj Bcx)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      -- The three distinguished triangles `(X, Y, Q(Q_i), f, p_i, d_i)`.
      letI T₁ : Triangle (HoCat A) := Triangle.mk ((Qfun A).map α.hom) p₁ d₁
      letI T₂ : Triangle (HoCat A) := Triangle.mk ((Qfun A).map (α.hom ≫ β.hom)) p₂ d₂
      letI T₃ : Triangle (HoCat A) := Triangle.mk ((Qfun A).map β.hom) p₃ d₃
      IsDistinguished T₁ ∧ IsDistinguished T₂ ∧ IsDistinguished T₃ ∧
      -- Axiom TR4 (Definition 6) for these three distinguished triangles, with respect to the
      -- composable morphisms `f = Q(α) : Q(Acx) → Q(Bcx)` and `g = Q(β) : Q(Bcx) → Q(Ccx)`.
      TR4Holds ((Qfun A).map α.hom) ((Qfun A).map β.hom) T₁ T₂ T₃
        rfl rfl rfl rfl rfl rfl

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.commShiftOfQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
**The commutation of a resolution functor with the shift**, the source's `ξ`: its component
at `a` and `K` is the unique `ξ_K : F(K⟦a⟧) ⟶ (F K)⟦a⟧` with `α_{K⟦a⟧} ≫ ι ξ_K = (α_K)⟦a⟧`. It
is the only commutation compatible with `α` (`commShiftOfQuasiIso_compatibility`,
`eq_commShiftOfQuasiIso`), and `F` is exact for it (`isTriangulated_of_quasiIso`).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def commShiftOfQuasiIso : F.CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the commutation with the shift itself; `commShiftOfQuasiIso_compatibility` is its compatibility with the comparison maps and `eq_commShiftOfQuasiIso` its uniqueness

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.commShiftOfQuasiIso_compatibility
declarations.doc:
`commShiftOfQuasiIso` is compatible with the comparison maps `α`: each of its components
satisfies `α_{K⟦a⟧} ≫ ι ξ_K = (α_K)⟦a⟧`.
declarations.statement:
lemma commShiftOfQuasiIso_compatibility :
    letI := commShiftOfQuasiIso F α hα
    NatTrans.CommShift α ℤ
declarations.comment: the commutation is compatible with the comparison maps

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.eq_commShiftOfQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
Uniqueness of the source's `ξ`: a commutation of `F` with the shift which is compatible with
the comparison maps `α` has `ξ` for each of its components, hence is `commShiftOfQuasiIso`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_commShiftOfQuasiIso :
    ∀ h : F.CommShift ℤ, (letI := h; NatTrans.CommShift α ℤ) →
      h = commShiftOfQuasiIso F α hα
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the commutation compatible with the comparison maps

declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.Plus.isTriangulated_of_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
A resolution functor is exact: it carries distinguished triangles of `K⁺(C)` to
distinguished triangles of `K⁺(ℐ)`, for its commutation with the shift.
declarations.statement:
lemma isTriangulated_of_quasiIso :
    letI := commShiftOfQuasiIso F α hα
    F.IsTriangulated
