declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.DeltaFunctorStructure
declarations.doc:
The structure of a **`δ`-functor** from an abelian category `𝒜` to a (pre)triangulated
category `𝒟` on a functor `G : 𝒜 ⥤ 𝒟`: a rule assigning to every short exact sequence
`0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` of `𝒜` a connecting morphism `δ : G(C) ⟶ G(A)⟦1⟧` such that the triangle
`(G(A), G(B), G(C), G(a), G(b), δ)` — the image of the short exact sequence under the
`δ`-functor — is distinguished, and such that `δ` is natural in the short exact sequence.
declarations.statement: public structure DeltaFunctorStructure (G : 𝒜 ⥤ 𝒟)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.DeltaFunctorStructure.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0151 (1).** If `G : 𝒜 ⥤ 𝒟` is a `δ`-functor and `F : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟'` is an exact functor
of pre-triangulated categories, then `F ∘ G` is a `δ`-functor, with connecting morphisms
`δ'_{A → B → C} = ξ_{G(A)} ∘ F(δ_{A → B → C})`, where `ξ : F(X⟦1⟧) ≅ F(X)⟦1⟧` is the
commutation of `F` with the shift (`DeltaFunctorStructure.comp_δ`).
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def DeltaFunctorStructure.comp (d : G.DeltaFunctorStructure 𝒜 𝒟)
    {𝒟' : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} 𝒟'] [HasZeroObject 𝒟'] [HasShift 𝒟' ℤ] [Preadditive 𝒟']
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor 𝒟' n).Additive] [Pretriangulated 𝒟']
    (F : 𝒟 ⥤ 𝒟') [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] :
    (G ⋙ F).DeltaFunctorStructure 𝒜 𝒟'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.DeltaFunctorStructure.precomp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0151 (2).** If `G : 𝒜 ⥤ 𝒟` is a `δ`-functor and `H : 𝒜' ⥤ 𝒜` is an exact functor
of abelian categories, then `G ∘ H` is a `δ`-functor, with connecting morphisms
`δ''_{A → B → C} = δ_{H(A) → H(B) → H(C)}` (`DeltaFunctorStructure.precomp_δ`).
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def DeltaFunctorStructure.precomp (d : G.DeltaFunctorStructure 𝒜 𝒟)
    {𝒜' : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} 𝒜'] [Abelian 𝒜'] (H : 𝒜' ⥤ 𝒜)
    [H.PreservesZeroMorphisms] [PreservesFiniteLimits H] [PreservesFiniteColimits H] :
    (H ⋙ G).DeltaFunctorStructure 𝒜' 𝒟

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.exists_deltaFunctorStructure_δ_eq
declarations.doc:
**The canonical `δ`-functor.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category. The localization functor
`Q : CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ ⥤ DerivedCategory 𝒜` has the structure of a `δ`-functor whose connecting
morphism is `DerivedCategory.triangleOfSESδ = -p ∘ q⁻¹`: for every short exact sequence
`0 ⟶ A^• ⟶ B^• ⟶ C^• ⟶ 0` of complexes the triangle
`(Q A^•, Q B^•, Q C^•, Q a, Q b, triangleOfSESδ)` is distinguished, and `triangleOfSESδ` is
natural in the short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_deltaFunctorStructure_δ_eq
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] :
    ∃ h : Functor.DeltaFunctorStructure (CochainComplex C ℤ) (DerivedCategory C) Q,
      ∀ {S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex C ℤ)} (hS : S.ShortExact),
        h.δ hS = triangleOfSESδ hS

declarations.name: triangleOfSESIsoOfQuasiIsoHom
declarations.doc:
The two distinguished triangles associated to `S₁` and `S₂` are isomorphic in
`D(𝒜)`, via the canonical isomorphism with components `Q φ₁, Q φ₂, Q φ₃`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def triangleOfSESIsoOfQuasiIsoHom
    {S₁ S₂ : ShortComplex (CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ)}
    (hS₁ : S₁.ShortExact) (hS₂ : S₂.ShortExact) (f : S₁ ⟶ S₂)
    (h₁ : QuasiIso f.τ₁) (h₂ : QuasiIso f.τ₂) (h₃ : QuasiIso f.τ₃) :
    DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES hS₁ ≅ DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES hS₂

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.mapTriangle_triangleOfDegreewiseSplit_eq_triangleOfSES
declarations.doc:
**The `δ`-functor on a termwise split short exact sequence.** Let `𝒜` be an abelian category
and let `S` be a short exact sequence of cochain complexes in `𝒜` which is split in each degree,
with splitting `σ`. Then the image under `Q : Comp(𝒜) ⥤ D(𝒜)` of the distinguished triangle
`(S.X₁, S.X₂, S.X₃, S.f, S.g, CochainComplex.homOfDegreewiseSplit S σ)` attached to the splitting
is the distinguished triangle that the canonical `δ`-functor attaches to `S`; in particular the
connecting morphism `triangleOfSESδ hS` is the image of
`CochainComplex.homOfDegreewiseSplit S σ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mapTriangle_triangleOfDegreewiseSplit_eq_triangleOfSES
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C]
    {S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex C ℤ)} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (σ : ∀ n, (S.map (HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).Splitting) :
    Q.mapTriangle.obj (CochainComplex.triangleOfDegreewiseSplit S σ) = triangleOfSES hS

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.rightAcyclic
declarations.doc:
An object `A` of an abelian category `C` is **right acyclic** for an additive functor
`F : C ⥤ D` to an abelian category, or **acyclic for `RF`**, if the complex `A[0]` with `A` in
degree zero computes the right derived functor `RF` of `F : K⁺(C) ⥤ D⁺(D)`, that is, if the
canonical map `α_{A[0]} : F(A[0]) ⟶ RF(Qh(A[0]))`, the unit of `RF` at `A[0]`, is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public def rightAcyclic (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
    [(F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).HasRightDerivedFunctor
      (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C)] : ObjectProperty C

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isTriangulated_of_isRightDerivedFunctor_mapHomotopyCategoryPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0159**, part (1). Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an additive functor between abelian
categories, where `𝒜` has enough injectives. Then any right derived functor
`RF : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` of `K⁺(F) ⋙ Q⁺_ℬ` along the localization `Q⁺_𝒜 : K⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(𝒜)` at the
quasi-isomorphisms, with unit `α`, is an exact functor of triangulated categories.

The source's `RF` is the case `RF := F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus` and
`α := F.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith`, with the commutation with the shift induced by the
universal property. The induced exact functor `K⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` of part (2) is then
`DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⋙ RF`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTriangulated_of_isRightDerivedFunctor_mapHomotopyCategoryPlus
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C)]
    [RF.CommShift ℤ] [NatTrans.CommShift α ℤ] :
    RF.IsTriangulated

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedPlus
declarations.doc:
The `i`-th right derived functor `R^i F = H^i ∘ RF : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` of an additive functor
`F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` between abelian categories, where `RF : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` is the right derived
functor of `F` on bounded below derived categories and `𝒜 → D⁺(𝒜)` sends an object to the
complex concentrated in degree `0`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def rightDerivedPlus (i : ℤ) : C ⥤ D

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isZero_rightDerivedPlus_obj_injective
declarations.doc:
**Injective objects are right acyclic**, [Stacks, Tag 015B] part (3): if `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` is an
additive functor between abelian categories, `𝒜` has enough injectives and `I` is an injective
object of `𝒜`, then the higher right derived functors of `F` vanish on `I` outside degree `0`:
`R ⁱ F (I) = 0` for `i ≠ 0`.

The source states this for `i > 0` and a left exact `F`; neither restriction is needed, as
`RF(I[0])` is `F(I)[0]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_rightDerivedPlus_obj_injective {A B : Type*} [Category* A] [Category* B]
    [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [EnoughInjectives A] (i : ℤ) (hi : i ≠ 0) (I : A) [Injective I] :
    IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus i).obj I)
declarations.comment: part (3), for i ≠ 0 and an arbitrary additive functor

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.rightAcyclic_iff_isIso_and_isZero_rightDerivedPlus
declarations.doc:
**Characterization of right acyclic objects**, [StacksProject 015C].
Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an additive functor between abelian categories, where `𝒜` has enough
injectives, so that the right derived functor `RF : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)`, with unit `α`, is
everywhere defined and `R ⁱ F = H ⁱ ∘ RF ∘ (·[0])`. Let `A` be an object of `𝒜`. Then
1. `A` is right acyclic for `F` if and only if the canonical map `F(A) ⟶ R ⁰ F(A)`, that is
   `H ⁰(α)` at `A[0]`, is an isomorphism and `R ⁱ F(A) = 0` for all `i > 0`, and
2. if `F` is left exact, then `A` is right acyclic for `F` if and only if `R ⁱ F(A) = 0` for
   all `i > 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightAcyclic_iff_isIso_and_isZero_rightDerivedPlus
    {C D : Type*} [Category* C] [Category* D] [Abelian C] [Abelian D]
    [HasDerivedCategory C] [HasDerivedCategory D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
    [EnoughInjectives C] (A : C) :
    (F.rightAcyclic A ↔
        (IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor D 0).map
            (F.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith.app
              ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor C 0).obj A))) ∧
          ∀ i > 0, IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus i).obj A))) ∧
      (PreservesFiniteLimits F →
        (F.rightAcyclic A ↔ ∀ i > 0, IsZero ((F.rightDerivedPlus i).obj A)))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.rightAcyclic_and_shortExact_map_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Right acyclicity in a short exact sequence**, [StacksProject 015D].
Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be a left exact functor between abelian categories, where `𝒜` has enough
injectives, so that `RF : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` is everywhere defined, and let
`S : 0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ 0` be a short exact sequence of `𝒜`. Then
1. if `A` and `C` are right acyclic for `F`, so is `B`,
2. if `A` and `B` are right acyclic for `F`, so is `C`, and
3. if `B` and `C` are right acyclic for `F` and `F(B) ⟶ F(C)` is epi, then so is `A`,
and in each of the three cases `0 ⟶ F(A) ⟶ F(B) ⟶ F(C) ⟶ 0` is a short exact sequence of `ℬ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightAcyclic_and_shortExact_map_of_shortExact
    {C D : Type*} [Category* C] [Category* D] [Abelian C] [Abelian D]
    [HasDerivedCategory C] [HasDerivedCategory D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [EnoughInjectives C]
    (S : ShortComplex C) (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    (F.rightAcyclic S.X₁ → F.rightAcyclic S.X₃ →
        F.rightAcyclic S.X₂ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact) ∧
      (F.rightAcyclic S.X₁ → F.rightAcyclic S.X₂ →
        F.rightAcyclic S.X₃ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact) ∧
      (F.rightAcyclic S.X₂ → F.rightAcyclic S.X₃ → Epi (F.map S.g) →
        F.rightAcyclic S.X₁ ∧ (S.map F).ShortExact)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_totalRightDerivedUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic
declarations.doc:
**Leray's acyclicity lemma**, [StacksProject 015E].
Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an additive functor between abelian categories, with `𝒜` having enough
injectives, so that the right derived functor `RF : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)`, with unit `α`, is everywhere
defined. Let `K` be a bounded below cochain complex of `𝒜` all of whose terms are right acyclic
for `F`. Then `K` computes `RF`: the canonical map `F(K) ⟶ RF(K)`, the component of `α` at the
image of `K` in `K⁺(𝒜)`, is an isomorphism in `D⁺(ℬ)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_totalRightDerivedUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic
    {C D : Type*} [Category* C] [Category* D] [Abelian C] [Abelian D]
    [HasDerivedCategory C] [HasDerivedCategory D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [EnoughInjectives C]
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (hK : CochainComplex.plus C K)
    (hacyclic : ∀ n, F.rightAcyclic (K.X n)) :
    IsIso (((F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh).totalRightDerivedUnit
      DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso C)).app
      ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient C).obj ⟨K, hK⟩))

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedFunctor.HigherDerivedOfExact.everywhere_defined_plus
declarations.doc:
**Statement (2): `RF : D⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(B)` is everywhere defined.**
`RF` relative to `Qis⁺(A)` is defined at every object of `K⁺(A)` (Stacks Definition 2,
tag 05SV), and the constructed functor `RFPlus F : D⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(B)`, together with its
canonical comparison `canonicalPlus F`, *is* the right derived functor of
`functorPlus F : K⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(B)` along `Qis⁺(A)` (it satisfies the universal property
`Functor.IsRightDerivedFunctor`).
declarations.statement:
theorem everywhere_defined_plus :
    (functorPlus F).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor (qisPlus (A := A)) ∧
      (RFPlus F).IsRightDerivedFunctor (canonicalPlus F) (qisPlus (A := A))

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedFunctor.HigherDerivedOfExact.everywhere_defined
declarations.doc:
**Statement (3): `RF : D(A) ⥤ D(B)` is everywhere defined.**
`RF` relative to `Qis(A)` is defined at every object of `K(A)` (Stacks Definition 2,
tag 05SV), and the chosen functor `RF F = F.mapDerivedCategory`, together with its
canonical comparison `canonical F`, *is* the right derived functor of
`functorKtoD F : K(A) ⥤ D(B)` along `Qis(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem everywhere_defined :
    (functorKtoD F).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor (qis (A := A)) ∧
      (RF F).IsRightDerivedFunctor (canonical F) (qis (A := A))

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedFunctor.HigherDerivedOfExact.complexes_compute
declarations.doc:
**Statement (4), unbounded: every complex computes `RF`.**
For every complex `K` of `A` (an object of `K(A)`), `RF` is defined at `K` and the
canonical map `F(K) ⟶ RF(K)`, i.e. the component `(canonical F).app K` of the comparison
transformation that exhibits `RF F` as the right derived functor, is an isomorphism in
`D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem complexes_compute (K : HomotopyCategory A shape) :
    (functorKtoD F).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctorAt (qis (A := A)) K ∧
      IsIso ((canonical F).app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedFunctor.HigherDerivedOfExact.objects_right_acyclic
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1): Every object of `A` is right acyclic for `F` (bounded-below).**
For every object `X` of `A`, the complex `X[0]`, viewed in `K⁺(A)`, computes
`RF : D⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺(B)` (Stacks Definition 4, tag 0157): `RF` is defined at `X[0]` relative
to `Qis⁺(A)` and the canonical map `F(X[0]) ⟶ RF(X[0])`, i.e. the component of the
comparison `canonicalPlus F` exhibiting `RFPlus F` as the right derived functor, is an
isomorphism in `D⁺(B)`.  Here `X[0]` is `(HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor A 0).obj X`,
the single complex concentrated in degree `0` regarded in `K⁺(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem objects_right_acyclic (X : A) :
    (functorPlus F).HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctorAt (qisPlus (A := A))
        ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor A 0).obj X) ∧
      IsIso ((canonicalPlus F).app
        ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor A 0).obj X))

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedFunctor.HigherDerivedOfExact.higherDerived_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
theorem higherDerived_eq_zero (i : ℤ) (hi : i ≠ 0) :
    IsZero (higherDerived F i)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.CartanEilenbergResolution
declarations.doc:
A Cartan-Eilenberg resolution of a cochain complex `K` in an abelian category: a double
complex `I` of injective objects, vanishing in first degrees `≪ 0` and in negative second
degrees, together with an augmentation `ε` from `K` placed in second degree `0`, such that
the complexes `I^{p,•}`, `Ker(d₁^{p,•})`, `Im(d₁^{p,•})` and `H^p_I(I^{•,•})` are
injective resolutions of `K^p`, `Ker(d_K^p)`, `Im(d_K^p)` and `H^p(K^•)`.
declarations.statement: public structure CartanEilenbergResolution (K : CochainComplex C ℤ)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_cartanEilenbergResolution
declarations.doc:
**Existence of Cartan-Eilenberg resolutions.** A cochain complex `K` over an abelian
category with enough injectives which is strictly `≥ n` admits a Cartan-Eilenberg
resolution whose double complex is strictly `≥ n` in the first direction.
declarations.statement:
public theorem _root_.CochainComplex.exists_cartanEilenbergResolution {C : Type u}
    [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [EnoughInjectives C] (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (n : ℤ)
    [CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE K n] :
    ∃ I : CochainComplex.CartanEilenbergResolution K,
      CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE I.bicomplex n

declarations.name: CochainComplex.CartanEilenbergResolution.exists_homologyIso_rightDerivedPlus
declarations.doc:
**The spectral sequences of a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution.** Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an
additive functor of abelian categories, with `𝒜` having enough injectives, let `K` be a
bounded below cochain complex of `𝒜` and let `I` be a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution of `K`.
For the double complex `L = F(I)`: the `'E₁`-page `H^q(L^{p,•})` is the complex `R^qF(K^p)`
in `p`, with differential induced by that of `K`; the `''E₂`-page
`H^p_{II}(H^q_I(L^{•,•}))` is `R^pF(H^q(K^•))`; and `H^n(Tot(L))` is `H^n(RF(K^•))`, the
abutment of both spectral sequences.
declarations.statement:
public theorem _root_.CochainComplex.CartanEilenbergResolution.exists_homologyIso_rightDerivedPlus
    {A : Type u} {B : Type u'} [Category.{v} A] [Category.{v'} B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive]
    [EnoughInjectives A] {K : CochainComplex A ℤ} (hK : CochainComplex.plus A K)
    (I : K.CartanEilenbergResolution)
    [HomologicalComplex₂.HasTotal
      (((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I.bicomplex) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)] :
    (∀ q, ∃ e : ∀ p, ((((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I.bicomplex).X p).homology q ≅
          (F.rightDerivedPlus q).obj (K.X p),
      ∀ p p', homologyMap ((((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I.bicomplex).d p p') q ≫ (e p').hom =
          (e p).hom ≫ (F.rightDerivedPlus q).map (K.d p p')) ∧
    (∀ p q, Nonempty (((((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I.bicomplex).homology q).homology p ≅
          (F.rightDerivedPlus p).obj (K.homology q))) ∧
    (∀ n, Nonempty ((HomologicalComplex₂.total
        (((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I.bicomplex) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).homology n ≅
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B n).obj
            (F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj (DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.obj ⟨K, hK⟩))))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_iff_rightAcyclic_obj_injective
declarations.doc:
Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` and `G : ℬ ⥤ 𝒞` be additive functors between abelian categories, with `𝒜`
and `ℬ` having enough injectives. The canonical transformation `t : R(G ∘ F) ⟶ RG ∘ RF` of
functors `D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(𝒞)`, namely the unique one whose composite with the unit of `R(G ∘ F)` is
the transformation `G(F(K)) ⟶ RG(F(K)) ⟶ RG(RF(K))` built from the units of `RG` and of `RF`
(the hypothesis `ht`), is an isomorphism if and only if `F(I)` is right acyclic for `G` for every
injective object `I` of `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_iff_rightAcyclic_obj_injective (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E)
    [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [EnoughInjectives C] [EnoughInjectives D]
    (t : (F ⋙ G).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⟶
      F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙ G.rightDerivedFunctorPlus)
    (ht : (F ⋙ G).rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith ≫ whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh t =
      whiskerRight (mapHomotopyCategoryPlusCompIso (Iso.refl (F ⋙ G))).inv
          DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ≫
        whiskerLeft F.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus G.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith ≫
        whiskerRight F.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith G.rightDerivedFunctorPlus) :
    IsIso t ↔ ∀ I : C, Injective I → G.rightAcyclic (F.obj I)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_spectralSequence_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_comp
declarations.doc:
The Grothendieck spectral sequence. Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` and `G : ℬ ⥤ 𝒞` be additive functors
between abelian categories, with `𝒜` and `ℬ` having enough injectives, such that `F(I)` is right
acyclic for `G` for every injective object `I` of `𝒜`, and let `X` be an object of `D⁺(𝒜)`.
There is a filtered complex `K` of `𝒞` with `H^n(K) ≅ H^n(R(G ∘ F)(X))` for all `n`, whose
filtration is finite in each degree and whose spectral sequence `E`, presented by its pages
`Z_r^{p,q}/D_r^{p,q}`, has `E_2^{p,q} ≅ R^pG(H^q(RF(X)))`, is bounded, induces a finite
filtration on each `H^n(K)`, and converges to `H^*(K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_spectralSequence_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_comp (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C)
    [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [EnoughInjectives A] [EnoughInjectives B]
    (hFG : ∀ I : A, Injective I → G.rightAcyclic (F.obj I)) (X : DerivedCategory.Plus A) :
    ∃ K : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ,
      (∀ n : ℤ, Nonempty (K.X.homology n ≅
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor C n).obj
          ((F ⋙ G).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj X))) ∧
      K.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite ∧
      ∀ (Fil : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ p n : ℤ, Fil p n = Subobject.mk ((K.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n))
        (Z : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Z r p n =
          Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (K.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (Fil (p + r) (n + 1)))
        (D : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, D r p n = Z (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
          (Subobject.«exists» (K.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Z (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1)))
        (FH : ∀ (n _p : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.homology n))
        (_ : ∀ n p : ℤ, FH n p =
          imageSubobject (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)),
      ∃ (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence C 0)
        (_ : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q), (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
          cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n))),
        (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty ((E.page 2 zero_le_two).X (p, q) ≅
          (G.rightDerivedPlus p).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B q).obj (F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj X)))) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((E.page 0).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ FH n a = ⊤ ∧ FH n b = ⊥) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r), b ≤ r →
          (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) = 0) ∧
        (∀ p n : ℤ,
          IsGLB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
              Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (K.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (Fil (p + r) (n + 1)) ⊔
                Fil (p + 1) n)
            (kernelSubobject (K.X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ Fil p n ⊔ Fil (p + 1) n) ∧
          IsLUB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
              Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.«exists» (K.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Fil (p - r) (n - 1)) ⊔
                Fil (p + 1) n)
            (imageSubobject (K.X.d (n - 1) n) ⊓ Fil p n ⊔ Fil (p + 1) n))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FilteredObject.IsFilteredInjective
declarations.doc:
An object `I` of `Fil^f(C)` is *filtered injective* if each graded piece
`gr^p(I) = F^p I / F^{p + 1} I` is an injective object of `C`. As a property of a filtered object
of `C`, it records that `I` lies in `Fil^f(C)`, i.e. that its filtration is finite.
declarations.statement:
public structure FilteredObject.IsFilteredInjective {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasCokernels C] (I : FilteredObject C ℤᵒᵖ) : Prop

declarations.name: CochainComplex.FilteredDerivedCategory.isEquivalence_isTriangulated_toPlus_and_squares
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒜` be an abelian category with enough injectives, let `I^f ⊂ Fil^f(𝒜)`
be the filtered injective objects and `I ⊂ 𝒜` the injective objects. The canonical functor
`K⁺(I^f) ⥤ DF⁺(𝒜)` is exact, fully faithful and essentially surjective, i.e. an equivalence of
triangulated categories. Furthermore the squares
```
K⁺(I^f) ──→ DF⁺(𝒜)          K⁺(I^f) ──→ DF⁺(𝒜)
  │gr^p        │gr^p           │forget F    │forget F
  ↓            ↓               ↓            ↓
K⁺(I) ────→ D⁺(𝒜)           K⁺(I) ────→ D⁺(𝒜)
```
commute. Here `gr^p, forget F : DF(𝒜) ⥤ D(𝒜)` are the functors induced by
`gr^p, forget F : K(Fil^f(𝒜)) ⥤ K(𝒜)`, as recorded by the isomorphisms
`Qh ⋙ gr^p ≅ gr^p ⋙ Q` and `Qh ⋙ forget F ≅ forget F ⋙ Q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_isTriangulated_toPlus_and_squares [EnoughInjectives 𝒜] :
    (toPlus 𝒜).IsEquivalence ∧ (toPlus 𝒜).IsTriangulated ∧
      (∀ p : ℤ, Nonempty (Qh (𝒜 := 𝒜) ⋙ grDF p ≅
          (FiniteFilteredObject.grP p).mapHomotopyCategory _ ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) ∧
        Nonempty (toPlus 𝒜 ⋙ liftDFPlus (FiniteFilteredObject.grP p) (grP_inverts p) ≅
          (injectivePlus 𝒜).lift ((filteredInjectivePlus 𝒜).ι ⋙
              (FiniteFilteredObject.grP p).mapHomotopyCategory _)
            (fun X => injectivePlus_grP_obj p X.property) ⋙ injectivePlusQ 𝒜)) ∧
      Nonempty (Qh (𝒜 := 𝒜) ⋙ forgetDF ≅
        FiniteFilteredObject.forget.mapHomotopyCategory _ ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) ∧
      Nonempty (toPlus 𝒜 ⋙ liftDFPlus FiniteFilteredObject.forget forget_inverts ≅
        (injectivePlus 𝒜).lift ((filteredInjectivePlus 𝒜).ι ⋙
            FiniteFilteredObject.forget.mapHomotopyCategory _)
          (fun X => injectivePlus_forget_obj X.property) ⋙ injectivePlusQ 𝒜)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_iso_gradedPiece_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_of_filteredQuasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 015U.** Let `T : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an additive functor of abelian categories with `𝒜` having
enough injectives, and let `RT : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` be its right derived functor. Let `α : K^• ⟶ I^•`
be a filtered quasi-isomorphism of filtered cochain complexes of `𝒜` with `I^•` filtered
injective, i.e. every `gr^p I^n` injective — a filtered injective resolution of `K^•` — and let
`M^•` be a filtered cochain complex of `ℬ` together with isomorphisms
`e p : gr^p M^• ≅ T(gr^p I^•)` in the homotopy category, the datum of `M^• = T_ext(I^•)` out of
which the filtered right derived functor is built, so that `M^•` presents `RT(K^•)` in `DF⁺(ℬ)`;
assume the graded pieces of `K^•`, `I^•` and `M^•` are bounded below. Then, for every `p`, there
is an isomorphism `gr^p(RT(K^•)) = gr^p M^• ≅ RT(gr^p K^•)` in `D⁺(ℬ)` compatible with
`RT(gr^p α)` and with the canonical map `Q(T(gr^p I^•)) ⟶ RT(Q(gr^p I^•))` of the right derived
functor; since the former is an isomorphism, the compatibility determines it uniquely. This is the
isomorphism of functors `gr^p ∘ RT ≅ RT ∘ gr^p` on `DF⁺(𝒜)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_gradedPiece_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_of_filteredQuasiIso
    {A : Type u} {B : Type u'} [Category.{v} A] [Category.{v'} B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} B] [EnoughInjectives A]
    (T : A ⥤ B) [T.Additive]
    {K I : FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ} (α : K ⟶ I)
    (hα : filteredQuasiIso A α)
    (hinj : ∀ p n : ℤ, Injective (((gr p).obj I).X n))
    (M : FilteredObject (CochainComplex B ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ)
    (hK : ∀ p : ℤ, CochainComplex.plus A ((gr p).obj K))
    (hI : ∀ p : ℤ, CochainComplex.plus A ((gr p).obj I))
    (hM : ∀ p : ℤ, CochainComplex.plus B ((gr p).obj M))
    (e : ∀ p : ℤ, (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient B).obj ⟨_, hM p⟩ ≅
      T.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus.obj ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient A).obj ⟨_, hI p⟩)) (p : ℤ) :
    ∃ Φ : DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.obj ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient B).obj ⟨_, hM p⟩) ≅
        T.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj (DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.obj
          ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient A).obj ⟨_, hK p⟩)),
      Φ.hom ≫ T.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map (DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.map
          ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient A).map (ObjectProperty.homMk
            (X := ⟨_, hK p⟩) (Y := ⟨_, hI p⟩)
            ((gr p).map α)))) =
        DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.map (e p).hom ≫
          T.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith.app
            ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient A).obj ⟨_, hI p⟩)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_forget_of_injective_gradedPiece
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 015V.** Let `T : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an additive functor of abelian categories with `𝒜` having
enough injectives, and let `I` be a bounded below complex of filtered injective objects: a bounded
below filtered cochain complex of `𝒜` every term `(I^n, F^• I^n)` of which is a filtered injective
object of `Fil^f(𝒜)`. Then the canonical map
```
Q(T((forget F) I)) ⟶ RT(Q((forget F) I))
```
in `D⁺(ℬ)` — the component at `(forget F) I` of the unit of the right derived functor
`RT : D⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)` — is an isomorphism. Since the left-hand side is `(forget F)(RT(I))`, `RT`
here being the filtered right derived functor of [Stacks, Tag 05U2], and every object of `DF⁺(𝒜)`
is isomorphic to such an `I` ([Stacks, Tag 015Q]), this is the source's isomorphism
`(forget F) ∘ RT ≅ RT ∘ (forget F)` of functors `DF⁺(𝒜) ⥤ D⁺(ℬ)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_forget_of_injective_gradedPiece
    {A : Type u} {B : Type u'} [Category.{v} A] [Category.{v'} B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} B] [EnoughInjectives A]
    (T : A ⥤ B) [T.Additive]
    (I : FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ) (a : ℤ) [I.X.IsStrictlyGE a]
    (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective) :
    IsIso (T.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith.app ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient A).obj
      ⟨FilteredObject.forget.obj I,
        (CochainComplex.plus_iff A _).2 ⟨a, ‹I.X.IsStrictlyGE a›⟩⟩))

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_spectralSequence_rightDerivedFunctorPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 015W.** Let `T : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be an additive functor of abelian categories, `𝒜` having
enough injectives, and let `(K^•, F)` be an object of `Comp⁺(Fil^f(𝒜))`: a filtered complex with
`K^n = 0` for `n < a` whose filtration is finite in each degree. Let `α : K^• ⟶ I^•` be a filtered
quasi-isomorphism to a bounded below complex of filtered injective objects — such a filtered
injective resolution exists ([Stacks, Tag 05TW],
`exists_mono_isStrictHom_filteredQuasiIso_isStrictlyGE_injective_gradedPiece`) and the statement
holds for every choice of it. Let `E` be the spectral sequence of the filtered complex
`T(I^•) = RT(K^•)` of `ℬ`, presented as in [Stacks, Tag 012M] by its pages
`E_r^{p,q} = Z_r^{p,q}/D_r^{p,q}` and its differentials `d_r` of bidegree `(r, -r + 1)` induced by
the differential of `T(I^•)`. Then

1. `E_1^{p,q} ≅ R^{p+q}T(gr^p K^•)`;
2. `E` is bounded: for each `n` only finitely many `E_0^{p, n - p}` are nonzero;
3. `E` converges to `H^*(T(I^•)) = R^*T(K^•)`: `d_r^{p,q} = 0` for `r ≫ 0`, and the stable
   cycles and boundaries exist and are those of (012S) and (012T) with equality;
4. the induced filtration on each `R^nT(K^•) = H^n(T(I^•))` is finite;
5. `H^n(T(I^•)) ≅ R^nT(K^•)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_spectralSequence_rightDerivedFunctorPlus
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [EnoughInjectives A] (T : A ⥤ B) [T.Additive]
    {K I : FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ} (a b : ℤ) [K.X.IsStrictlyGE a]
    [I.X.IsStrictlyGE b] (hK : K.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite) (α : K ⟶ I)
    (hα : filteredQuasiIso A α) (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective)
    (F : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.X n))
    (hF : ∀ p n : ℤ, F p n =
      Subobject.mk (((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n))
    (Z : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.X n))
    (hZ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Z r p n = F p n ⊓
      (Subobject.pullback ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.d n (n + 1))).obj (F (p + r) (n + 1)))
    (D : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.X n))
    (hD : ∀ r p n : ℤ, D r p n = Z (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
      (Subobject.«exists» ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.d (n - 1) n)).obj
        (Z (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1)))
    (FH : ∀ (n _p : ℤ), Subobject ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.homology n))
    (hFH : ∀ n p : ℤ, FH n p = imageSubobject
      (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)) :
    ∃ (e : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q),
        ((spectralSequenceOf (mapFilteredInjective T I hI) F hF).page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
        cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n))),
      (∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hn : n = p + q),
        ∃ δ : (Z r p n : B) ⟶ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1) : B),
          δ ≫ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1)).arrow =
            (Z r p n).arrow ≫ (mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.d n (n + 1) ∧
          cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)) ≫
              (e r p q n hr hn).inv ≫
                ((spectralSequenceOf (mapFilteredInjective T I hI) F hF).page r hr).d
                  (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) =
            δ ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right :
                D r (p + r) (n + 1) ⊓ Z r (p + r) (n + 1) ≤ Z r (p + r) (n + 1))) ≫
              (e r (p + r) (q - r + 1) (n + 1) hr (by omega)).inv) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
        (((spectralSequenceOf (mapFilteredInjective T I hI) F hF).page 1).X (p, q) ≅
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B (p + q)).obj
          (T.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj (DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.obj
            ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient A).obj
              ⟨(FilteredObject.gr p).obj K, ⟨a, isStrictlyGE_gr K a p⟩⟩))))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero
        (((spectralSequenceOf (mapFilteredInjective T I hI) F hF).page 0).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r), b ≤ r →
        ((spectralSequenceOf (mapFilteredInjective T I hI) F hF).page r hr).d
          (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) = 0) ∧
      (∀ p n : ℤ,
        IsGLB (Set.range fun r : ℕ => F p n ⊓
            (Subobject.pullback ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.d n (n + 1))).obj
              (F (p + r) (n + 1)) ⊔ F (p + 1) n)
          (kernelSubobject ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ F p n ⊔
            F (p + 1) n) ∧
        IsLUB (Set.range fun r : ℕ => F p n ⊓
            (Subobject.«exists» ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.d (n - 1) n)).obj
              (F (p - r) (n - 1)) ⊔ F (p + 1) n)
          (imageSubobject ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.d (n - 1) n) ⊓ F p n ⊔
            F (p + 1) n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ p₀ p₁ : ℤ, p₀ ≤ p₁ ∧ FH n p₀ = ⊤ ∧ FH n p₁ = ⊥) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, Nonempty ((mapFilteredInjective T I hI).X.homology n ≅
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B n).obj
          (T.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj (DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.obj
            ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient A).obj ⟨K.X, ⟨a, inferInstance⟩⟩)))))
declarations.comment:
the spectral sequence, its `E_1` page, boundedness, convergence and finiteness of
the induced filtration

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_spectralSequenceMap_rightDerivedFunctorPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 015W, functoriality.** Let `f : K^• ⟶ L^•` be a morphism of
`Comp⁺(Fil^f(𝒜))` and let `α : K^• ⟶ I^•`, `β : L^• ⟶ J^•` be filtered injective resolutions.
There is a morphism `γ : I^• ⟶ J^•` with `α ≫ γ` filtered homotopic to `f ≫ β`
([Stacks, Tag 05TY]); it induces a morphism of spectral sequences
`E_r(T(I^•)) ⟶ E_r(T(J^•))` ([Stacks, Tag 012O]), and on the pages `E_r`, `r ≥ 1`, this
morphism does not depend on the choice of `γ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_spectralSequenceMap_rightDerivedFunctorPlus
    {K L I J : FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ}
    (hK : K.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite)
    (a b : ℤ) [I.X.IsStrictlyGE a] [J.X.IsStrictlyGE b]
    (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective)
    (hJ : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil J n).IsFilteredInjective)
    (α : K ⟶ I) (hα : filteredQuasiIso A α) (β : L ⟶ J) (f : K ⟶ L) :
    (∃ γ : I ⟶ J, FilteredHomotopic (α ≫ γ) (f ≫ β)) ∧
      ∀ γ γ' : I ⟶ J, FilteredHomotopic (α ≫ γ) (f ≫ β) →
        FilteredHomotopic (α ≫ γ') (f ≫ β) → ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 1 ≤ r),
          (filteredSpectralSequenceMap (mapFilteredInjectiveMap T γ hI hJ)).hom r (by omega) =
            (filteredSpectralSequenceMap (mapFilteredInjectiveMap T γ' hI hJ)).hom r
              (by omega)
declarations.comment:
functoriality in `K^•`: the induced morphism of spectral sequences, independent of
choices on `E_r` for `r ≥ 1`

declarations.name: CochainComplex.filteredHomotopic_comp_and_spectralSequenceMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 015W, compatibility with composition.** If `γ` lifts `f : K^• ⟶ L^•` and `δ` lifts
`g : L^• ⟶ M^•` along filtered injective resolutions, then `γ ≫ δ` lifts `f ≫ g`, and the
morphism of spectral sequences induced by `γ ≫ δ` is the composite of those induced by `γ` and
`δ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem filteredHomotopic_comp_and_spectralSequenceMap_comp
    {K L M I J P : FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ}
    (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective)
    (hJ : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil J n).IsFilteredInjective)
    (hP : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil P n).IsFilteredInjective)
    (α : K ⟶ I) (β : L ⟶ J) (ε : M ⟶ P) (f : K ⟶ L) (g : L ⟶ M) (γ : I ⟶ J) (δ : J ⟶ P)
    (hγ : FilteredHomotopic (α ≫ γ) (f ≫ β)) (hδ : FilteredHomotopic (β ≫ δ) (g ≫ ε)) :
    FilteredHomotopic (α ≫ γ ≫ δ) ((f ≫ g) ≫ ε) ∧
      filteredSpectralSequenceMap (mapFilteredInjectiveMap T (γ ≫ δ) hI hP) =
        filteredSpectralSequenceMap (mapFilteredInjectiveMap T γ hI hJ) ≫
          filteredSpectralSequenceMap (mapFilteredInjectiveMap T δ hJ hP)
declarations.comment: the construction is compatible with composition

declarations.name: CochainComplex.isIso_spectralSequenceMap_rightDerivedFunctorPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 015W, independence of choices.** For two filtered injective resolutions
`α : K^• ⟶ I^•` and `α' : K^• ⟶ I'^•` of the same object, any `γ : I^• ⟶ I'^•` with
`α ≫ γ` filtered homotopic to `α'` induces isomorphisms `E_r(T(I^•)) ≅ E_r(T(I'^•))` on all pages
`r ≥ 1`; when `I'^• = I^•` and `α' = α` the induced morphism is the identity on these pages. So
the terms `(E_r, d_r)`, `r ≥ 1`, do not depend on the choice of resolution.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_spectralSequenceMap_rightDerivedFunctorPlus
    {K I I' : FilteredObject (CochainComplex A ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ} (hK : K.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite)
    (a a' : ℤ) [I.X.IsStrictlyGE a] [I'.X.IsStrictlyGE a']
    (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I n).IsFilteredInjective)
    (hI' : ∀ n : ℤ, (evalFil I' n).IsFilteredInjective)
    (α : K ⟶ I) (hα : filteredQuasiIso A α) (α' : K ⟶ I') (hα' : filteredQuasiIso A α')
    (γ : I ⟶ I') (hγ : FilteredHomotopic (α ≫ γ) α') :
    (∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 1 ≤ r),
      IsIso ((filteredSpectralSequenceMap (mapFilteredInjectiveMap T γ hI hI')).hom r
        (by omega))) ∧
    ∀ γ₀ : I ⟶ I, FilteredHomotopic (α ≫ γ₀) α → ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 1 ≤ r),
      (filteredSpectralSequenceMap (mapFilteredInjectiveMap T γ₀ hI hI)).hom r (by omega) =
        𝟙 _
declarations.comment: the terms `(E_r, d_r)` for `r ≥ 1` do not depend on any choices

declarations.name: preservesInjectiveObjects_of_exact_of_adjunction

declarations.name: exact_iff_preservesInjectiveObjects_of_adjunction

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: hasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings_of_adjunction
declarations.doc:
Let `A` and `B` be abelian categories, `u : A ⥤ B` and `v : B ⥤ A` additive functors.
Assume `u` is right adjoint to `v`, `v` transforms injective maps into injective maps, `A` has
enough injectives, `v B = 0` implies `B = 0`, and `A` has functorial injective embeddings. Then
`B` has functorial injective embeddings.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings_of_adjunction
    (A : Type*) [Category A] [Abelian A]
    (B : Type*) [Category B] [Abelian B]
    (u : A ⥤ B) (v : B ⥤ A)
    [u.Additive] [v.Additive]
    (adj : v ⊣ u)
    (hv_mono : ∀ {X Y : B} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f], Mono (v.map f))
    [EnoughInjectives A]
    (h_reflectZero : ∀ (X : B), IsZero (v.obj X) → IsZero X)
    (hA : HasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings A) :
    HasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings B

declarations.name: SimplexCategoryGenRel.toSimplexCategory_full_faithful_bijective_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0168**.
The category `Δ` is presented by the face and degeneracy generators and the simplicial
relations: the canonical functor from the category defined by those generators and relations is
full and faithful and is bijective on objects. Thus every morphism is generated by faces and
degeneracies, and every equality between such composites follows from the defining relations.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject
registrations.comment: (1), (3), (4), (5): simplicial objects of C, the functor category Δᵒᵖ ⥤ C (morphisms are natural transformations); (3) is C = abelian groups

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.bijective_comp_toSimplexCategory_op_and_whiskerLeft
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 016B** (parts (2) and (3), via the presented category `SimplexCategoryGenRel`).
Restriction along the canonical functor `SimplexCategoryGenRel.toSimplexCategory` from the
category presented by the generators `δ^n_j`, `σ^n_j` and the relations of [Stacks, Tag 0167]
is bijective on simplicial objects of `C` and on morphisms of simplicial objects: every system
`(U_n, d^n_j, s^n_j)` satisfying those relations — that is, every functor
`SimplexCategoryGenRelᵒᵖ ⥤ C` — comes from a unique simplicial object `U` with `U_n = U([n])`,
`d^n_j = U(δ^n_j)` and `s^n_j = U(σ^n_j)`, and every family of morphisms `U_n ⟶ U'_n`
commuting with the faces and the degeneracies comes from a unique morphism of simplicial
objects.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_comp_toSimplexCategory_op_and_whiskerLeft (C : Type u)
    [Category.{v} C] :
    Function.Bijective (fun X : SimplicialObject C => toSimplexCategory.op ⋙ X) ∧
      ∀ X Y : SimplicialObject C,
        Function.Bijective (fun f : X ⟶ Y => Functor.whiskerLeft toSimplexCategory.op f)
declarations.comment: part (1) is `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.δ_comp_δ` and its companions in Mathlib; parts (2) and (3) are stated in terms of the presented category `SimplexCategoryGenRel`, so that no equality of objects of `C` is transported

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.isSplitMono_σ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 016F**.
Each degeneracy map `X.σ i : Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₊₁` of a simplicial object `X` of a category `C` has a left
inverse, namely the face map `X.δ i.castSucc`; in particular `X.σ i` is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public instance isSplitMono_σ (X : SimplicialObject C) {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
    IsSplitMono (X.σ i)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.existsUnique_hom_app_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 016H**.
Let `U`, `U'` be simplicial objects of a category `C`, and let `d n : U_n ⟶ U'_n` be a family of
morphisms commuting with the face maps `δ i` and with the degeneracy maps `σ i`. Then there is a
unique morphism of simplicial objects `f : U ⟶ U'` — equivalently, by definition, a unique morphism
`U ⟶ U'` of `C`-valued presheaves on `Δ` — whose component in degree `n` is `d n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_hom_app_eq {U U' : SimplicialObject C}
    (d : ∀ n : ℕ, U.obj (op ⦋n⦌) ⟶ U'.obj (op ⦋n⦌))
    (hδ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), U.δ i ≫ d n = d (n + 1) ≫ U'.δ i)
    (hσ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), U.σ i ≫ d (n + 1) = d n ≫ U'.σ i) :
    ∃! f : U ⟶ U', ∀ n : ℕ, f.app (op ⦋n⦌) = d n
declarations.comment: the common hom-set is the set of degreewise families commuting with the faces and the degeneracies

registrations.comment: cosimplicial objects of C, the functor category Δ ⥤ C (morphisms are natural transformations); cosimplicial sets and abelian groups are C = sets, abelian groups

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject.existsUnique_comp_toSimplexCategory_and_hom_app_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 016K** (parts (2) and (3), via the presented category `SimplexCategoryGenRel`).
Let `C` be a category. (2) Given objects `Uₙ` of `C` and morphisms `δⁿⱼ : Uₙ ⟶ Uₙ₊₁`,
`σⁿⱼ : Uₙ₊₁ ⟶ Uₙ` satisfying the cosimplicial identities — that is, a functor `F` out of the
presentation `SimplexCategoryGenRel` of `Δ` by these generators and relations — there is a unique
cosimplicial object `U` of `C` with `Uₙ = U ⦋n⦌`, `δⁿⱼ = U (δ j)` and `σⁿⱼ = U (σ j)`. (3) Given
cosimplicial objects `U`, `U'` and a family of morphisms `a n : Uₙ ⟶ U'ₙ` commuting with the coface
and the codegeneracy maps, there is a unique morphism `f : U ⟶ U'` of cosimplicial objects with
`f.app ⦋n⦌ = a n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_comp_toSimplexCategory_and_hom_app_eq
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] :
    (∀ F : SimplexCategoryGenRel ⥤ C,
        ∃! U : CosimplicialObject C, SimplexCategoryGenRel.toSimplexCategory ⋙ U = F) ∧
      ∀ (U U' : CosimplicialObject C) (a : ∀ n : ℕ, U ^⦋n⦌ ⟶ U' ^⦋n⦌),
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), U.δ i ≫ a (n + 1) = a n ≫ U'.δ i) →
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), U.σ i ≫ a n = a (n + 1) ≫ U'.σ i) →
        ∃! f : U ⟶ U', ∀ n : ℕ, f.app ⦋n⦌ = a n
declarations.comment: part (1) is `CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject.δ_comp_δ` and its companions in Mathlib; parts (2) and (3) are stated with the coface–codegeneracy datum encoded as a functor out of the presented category `SimplexCategoryGenRel`, so that no equality of objects of `C` is transported

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject.cosimplicial_identities_of_val
declarations.statement:
public theorem cosimplicial_identities_of_val (X : CosimplicialObject C) :
    (∀ {n : ℕ} {i : Fin (n + 2)} {j : Fin (n + 3)} {i' : Fin (n + 3)} {j' : Fin (n + 2)},
        (i : ℕ) < (j : ℕ) → (i' : ℕ) = (i : ℕ) → (j' : ℕ) + 1 = (j : ℕ) →
          X.δ i ≫ X.δ j = X.δ j' ≫ X.δ i') ∧
      (∀ {n : ℕ} {i : Fin (n + 3)} {j : Fin (n + 2)} {i' : Fin (n + 2)} {j' : Fin (n + 1)},
        (i : ℕ) < (j : ℕ) → (i' : ℕ) = (i : ℕ) → (j' : ℕ) + 1 = (j : ℕ) →
          X.δ i ≫ X.σ j = X.σ j' ≫ X.δ i') ∧
      (∀ {n : ℕ} {j : Fin (n + 1)} {i : Fin (n + 2)},
        (i : ℕ) = (j : ℕ) → X.δ i ≫ X.σ j = 𝟙 (X ^⦋n⦌)) ∧
      (∀ {n : ℕ} {j : Fin (n + 1)} {i : Fin (n + 2)},
        (i : ℕ) = (j : ℕ) + 1 → X.δ i ≫ X.σ j = 𝟙 (X ^⦋n⦌)) ∧
      (∀ {n : ℕ} {i : Fin (n + 3)} {j : Fin (n + 2)} {i' : Fin (n + 2)} {j' : Fin (n + 1)},
        (j : ℕ) + 1 < (i : ℕ) → (i' : ℕ) + 1 = (i : ℕ) → (j' : ℕ) = (j : ℕ) →
          X.δ i ≫ X.σ j = X.σ j' ≫ X.δ i') ∧
      ∀ {n : ℕ} {i : Fin (n + 2)} {j : Fin (n + 1)} {i' : Fin (n + 1)} {j' : Fin (n + 2)},
        (i : ℕ) ≤ (j : ℕ) → (i' : ℕ) = (i : ℕ) → (j' : ℕ) = (j : ℕ) + 1 →
          X.σ i ≫ X.σ j = X.σ j' ≫ X.σ i'

Each coface map `X.δ i : Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₊₁` of a cosimplicial object `X` of a category `C` has a left

declarations.statement:
public instance isSplitMono_δ (X : CosimplicialObject C) {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 2)) :

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.fibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 016T.** The fibre product `V ×_U W` of two simplicial objects `V`, `W` of a category
`C` over a third one `U`, along morphisms `a : V ⟶ U` and `b : W ⟶ U`, when the fibre product
`V_n ×_{U_n} W_n` exists in `C` in every degree: the simplicial object with
`(V ×_U W)_n = V_n ×_{U_n} W_n` on which a morphism `φ : ⦋m⦌ ⟶ ⦋n⦌` of `Δ` acts by the morphism
that `V φ`, `W φ` and `U φ` induce on the pullbacks, so that `d^n_i = (d^n_i, d^n_i)` and
`s^n_i = (s^n_i, s^n_i)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev fibreProduct (a : V ⟶ U) (b : W ⟶ U)
    [∀ n, Limits.HasPullback (a.app n) (b.app n)] : SimplicialObject C
declarations.comment: the case `D = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ` of `CategoryTheory.Limits.pointwisePullback`, Tag 0172, which is stated for an arbitrary index category `D`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.isBijective_canonicalMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 016U**.
Let `C` be a category, let `U V W` be simplicial objects of `C` and let `a : V ⟶ U`, `b : W ⟶ U`
be morphisms of simplicial objects whose fibre product `V ×_U W` exists in `SimplicialObject C`,
witnessed by a limit pullback cone `c` with projections `p`, `q`. For every simplicial object `T`
the map `h ↦ (h ≫ p, h ≫ q)` is a bijection from `Mor(T, V ×_U W)` onto
`Mor(T, V) ×_{Mor(T, U)} Mor(T, W)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBijective_canonicalMap
    {U V W T : SimplicialObject C} (a : V ⟶ U) (b : W ⟶ U)
    (c : PullbackCone a b) (hc : IsLimit c) :
    Function.Bijective (PullbackCone.canonicalMap a b c (T := T))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.pointwisePushout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 016W.** The pushout of simplicial objects, as a pointwise pushout in a functor
category. Given a span `f : F ⟶ G`, `g : F ⟶ H` of morphisms of functors `D ⥤ C` all of whose
pointwise pushouts `G d ⨿_{F d} H d` exist, `pointwisePushout f g` is the functor
`d ↦ G d ⨿_{F d} H d`, a morphism `φ : d ⟶ d'` acting by the morphism `G φ ⨿_{F φ} H φ` that
`G φ`, `H φ` and `F φ` induce on the pushouts. For simplicial objects `U`, `V`, `W` of `C` and
`a : U ⟶ V`, `b : U ⟶ W`, so for `D = Δᵒᵖ`, this is the pushout `V ⨿_U W`, with
`(V ⨿_U W)_n = V_n ⨿_{U_n} W_n`, `d^n_i = (d^n_i, d^n_i)` and `s^n_i = (s^n_i, s^n_i)`; for
cosimplicial objects, so for `D = Δ`, it is their pushout. It is the dual of
`pointwisePullback`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointwisePushout (f : F ⟶ G) (g : F ⟶ H)
    [∀ d, HasPushout (f.app d) (g.app d)] : D ⥤ C
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary index category `D`: the pushout of simplicial objects is the case `D = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`, and that of cosimplicial objects the case `D = SimplexCategory`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.IsPushout.existsUnique_desc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 016X** (for a pushout square in an arbitrary category, elementwise).
For a pushout square

```
U --a--> V
|        |
b        f
v        v
W --g--> P
```

in a category `C` and an object `T` of `C`, composition with `f` and with `g` identifies
`Mor(P, T)` with the fibre product `Mor(V, T) ×_{Mor(U, T)} Mor(W, T)`: a pair `p : V ⟶ T`,
`q : W ⟶ T` with `a ≫ p = b ≫ q` extends to `P` in exactly one way.
declarations.comment: for a pushout square in an arbitrary category rather than for the pushout `V ∐_U W` of simplicial objects, and elementwise: an element of the fibre product `Mor(V, T) ×_{Mor(U, T)} Mor(W, T)` is a pair `(p, q)` with `a ≫ p = b ≫ q`, and bijectivity of `φ ↦ (f ≫ φ, g ≫ φ)` is existence and uniqueness of `φ`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Square.isPushout_iff_op_map_yoneda_isPullback
registrations.comment: the same identification of hom-sets, bundled and in both directions: a square is a pushout square if and only if for every `T` the image of the opposite square under `Mor(-, T)` is a pullback square of types, whose four maps are composition with `f`, `g`, `a`, `b` by `rfl`, so at each `T` it is the source's `Mor(P, T) = Mor(V, T) ×_{Mor(U, T)} Mor(W, T)`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.IsPushout.of_forall_isPushout_app
registrations.comment: with the source's hypothesis that `V ∐_U W` exists: the degreewise pushout of Tag 016W, whose squares `V_n ∐_{U_n} W_n` are pushout squares, is a pushout in the category `Δᵒᵖ ⥤ C` of simplicial objects, to which the statements above then apply

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.pointwiseProd
declarations.doc:
The **pointwise product** of two functors `F G : D ⥤ C`, defined when the products
`F.obj d ⨯ G.obj d` exist in `C`: it sends `d` to `F.obj d ⨯ G.obj d` and a morphism
`f : d ⟶ d'` to `prod.map (F.map f) (G.map f)`.

For `D = SimplexCategory` this is the product `U × V` of two cosimplicial objects `U`, `V`
of `C` of [Stacks, Tag 016Z]. It is the product formed pointwise in `C`, not by definition a
product in the category `D ⥤ C`; that it is one is `pointwiseProdIsProd`, [Stacks, Tag 0170].
declarations.statement: def pointwiseProd (F G : D ⥤ C) [∀ d, HasBinaryProduct (F.obj d) (G.obj d)] : D ⥤ C

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.map_eq_prod_lift_comp_prod_map_comp_inv
declarations.doc:
**The product of two cosimplicial objects acts on morphisms by the product of the maps**,
[Stacks, Tag 016Z]: let `F G P : D ⥤ C` be functors such that the products `F.obj d ⨯ G.obj d`
exist in `C`, let `π₁ : P ⟶ F` and `π₂ : P ⟶ G` be natural transformations, and let `φ : d ⟶ d'`
be a morphism such that the comparison map `prod.lift (π₁.app d') (π₂.app d')` is an isomorphism.
Then `P.map φ` is `prod.map (F.map φ) (G.map φ)`, read through the comparison maps at `d` and
`d'`.

So the second clause of the definition of the product of `F` and `G` holds of every functor which
is degreewise the product over its two projections. The functor of the definition itself is
`pointwiseProd F G`, and that it is a product in `D ⥤ C` is `pointwiseProdIsProd`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_eq_prod_lift_comp_prod_map_comp_inv {F G P : D ⥤ C}
    [∀ d, HasBinaryProduct (F.obj d) (G.obj d)] (π₁ : P ⟶ F) (π₂ : P ⟶ G) {d d' : D} (φ : d ⟶ d')
    [IsIso (prod.lift (π₁.app d') (π₂.app d'))] :
    P.map φ = prod.lift (π₁.app d) (π₂.app d) ≫ prod.map (F.map φ) (G.map φ) ≫
      inv (prod.lift (π₁.app d') (π₂.app d'))
declarations.comment: the definition's second clause, stated for an arbitrary functor satisfying the first: it is forced by the degrees and the two projections. Stated over an arbitrary index category `D`: the product of two cosimplicial objects is the case `D = SimplexCategory` and that of simplicial objects the case `D = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.pointwiseProdIsProd
declarations.doc:
**The pointwise product of two functors is their product**, [Stacks, Tag 0170]: for functors
`F G : D ⥤ C` whose pointwise products exist, the binary fan on `F` and `G` with point the
pointwise product `pointwiseProd F G` of [Stacks, Tag 016Z] and with projections `π₁`, `π₂`
given degreewise by `prod.fst` and `prod.snd` is a limit. Thus `F` and `G` have a product in
`D ⥤ C`, computed pointwise, and `Mor(W, F × G) = Mor(W, F) × Mor(W, G)` for every functor `W`.

For `D = Δ` this is the statement that the product `U × V` of two cosimplicial objects of `C`
is the product in the category of cosimplicial objects of `C`.
declarations.statement:
def pointwiseProdIsProd (F G : D ⥤ C)
    [∀ d, HasBinaryProduct (F.obj d) (G.obj d)]
    (π₁ : pointwiseProd F G ⟶ F) (π₂ : pointwiseProd F G ⟶ G)
    (h₁ : ∀ d, π₁.app d = prod.fst) (h₂ : ∀ d, π₂.app d = prod.snd) :
    IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk π₁ π₂)
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary index category `D`: the product of cosimplicial objects is the case `D = SimplexCategory`, that of simplicial objects the case `D = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.pointwisePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0172.** The fibre product of cosimplicial objects, as a pointwise pullback in a
functor category. Given a cospan `f : F ⟶ H`, `g : G ⟶ H` of morphisms of functors `D ⥤ C` all
of whose pointwise pullbacks `F d ×_{H d} G d` exist, `pointwisePullback f g` is the functor
`d ↦ F d ×_{H d} G d`, a morphism `φ : d ⟶ d'` acting by the morphism `F φ ×_{H φ} G φ` that
`F φ`, `G φ` and `H φ` induce on the pullbacks. For cosimplicial objects `U`, `V`, `W` of `C`
and `a : V ⟶ U`, `b : W ⟶ U`, so for `D = Δ`, this is the fibre product `V ×_U W`, with
`(V ×_U W)_n = V_n ×_{U_n} W_n` and `(V ×_U W)(φ) = V(φ) ×_{U(φ)} W(φ)`; for simplicial objects,
so for `D = Δᵒᵖ`, it is the fibre product of [Stacks, Tag 016T].
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointwisePullback (f : F ⟶ H) (g : G ⟶ H)
    [∀ d, HasPullback (f.app d) (g.app d)] : D ⥤ C
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary index category `D`: the fibre product of cosimplicial objects is the case `D = SimplexCategory`, and that of simplicial objects, Tag 016T, the case `D = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject.isBijective_canonicalMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0173**.
Let `C` be a category, `U V W` cosimplicial objects of `C`, and `a : V ⟶ U`, `b : W ⟶ U`
morphisms of cosimplicial objects. If `V ×_U W`, with projections `p` and `q`, is a fibre
product of `a` and `b`, then for every cosimplicial object `T` the comparison map
`Mor(T, V ×_U W) → Mor(T, V) ×_{Mor(T, U)} Mor(T, W)`, `f ↦ (f ≫ p, f ≫ q)`, is a bijection.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CategoryOfElements.exists_opOverEquivalenceElements
declarations.doc:
**`C/X` is fibred in sets over `C`, and as a presheaf of sets it is represented by `X`.**
There is an equivalence of categories from the opposite of the category `C/X` of objects of
`C` over `X` to the category of elements of the presheaf `uliftYoneda.obj X` represented by
`X`, which sends an object `ψ : Y ⟶ X` of `C/X` to the element `ψ` of `Mor_C(Y, X)`, and which
commutes with the projections to `Cᵒᵖ`. For `C` the simplex category and `X = ⦋n⦌` this says
that `Δ/⦋n⦌`, fibred in sets over `Δ`, is the simplicial set `Δ[n]`.

This is `CategoryTheory.overEquivElementsOp` ([Stacks, Tag 0044]) transported along
`CategoryTheory.elementsUliftEquiv`; the two pinning clauses hold by `rfl` because every step
of the transport is definitional.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opOverEquivalenceElements (X : C) :
    ∃ e : (Over X)ᵒᵖ ≌ (uliftYoneda.{w}.obj X).Elements,
      (∀ ψ : Over X, e.functor.obj (op ψ) =
        (uliftYoneda.{w}.obj X).elementsMk (op ψ.left) (ULift.up ψ.hom)) ∧
      e.functor ⋙ Functor.Elements.π _ = (Over.forget X).op
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary category C and X : C, of which Δ/⦋n⦌ fibred in sets over Δ being the presheaf Δ[n] is the case C = Δ, X = ⦋n⦌, since SSet.stdSimplex is uliftYoneda; the formula Mor(Δ/⦋n⦌, U) = U_n is then SSet.yonedaEquiv

declarations.name: SSet.existsUnique_hom_app_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017B**.
Let `U` be a simplicial set, let `V`, `W` be simplicial objects of a category `C`, and let
`d n u : V_n ⟶ W_n` be a family of morphisms, indexed by `n : ℕ` and by the `n`-simplices `u` of
`U`, which commutes with the face maps and with the degeneracy maps. Then `d` is the family of
components of a unique element of the displayed set of families
`(f_{n, u} : V_n ⟶ W_n)_{n ≥ 0, u ∈ U_n}` satisfying `f_{m, U(φ)(u)} ∘ V(φ) = W(φ) ∘ f_{n, u}` for
every `φ : [m] → [n]`, that set being the hom-set `π U ⋙ V ⟶ π U ⋙ W` of functors on the category
of elements of `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_hom_app_eq (U : SSet.{w}) {V W : SimplicialObject C}
    (d : ∀ n : ℕ, U.obj (op ⦋n⦌) → (V.obj (op ⦋n⦌) ⟶ W.obj (op ⦋n⦌)))
    (hδ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) (u : U.obj (op ⦋n + 1⦌)),
      V.δ i ≫ d n (U.δ i u) = d (n + 1) u ≫ W.δ i)
    (hσ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)) (u : U.obj (op ⦋n⦌)),
      V.σ i ≫ d (n + 1) (U.σ i u) = d n u ≫ W.σ i) :
    ∃! f : CategoryOfElements.π U ⋙ V ⟶ CategoryOfElements.π U ⋙ W,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : U.obj (op ⦋n⦌)), f.app ⟨u⟩ = d n u
declarations.comment: the displayed set is the hom-set `π U ⋙ V ⟶ π U ⋙ W` over the category of elements of `U`; here its elements are described by the faces and the degeneracies

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.copower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017C**.
The copower of `V : J ⥤ C` by `U : J ⥤ Type w`, defined whenever the coproduct of `U j`-many copies
of `V j` exists for every `j`: the functor `j ↦ ∐_{u ∈ U j} V j` whose value on `f : i ⟶ j` sends
the component indexed by `u ∈ U i` into the component indexed by `U f u ∈ U j` by `V f`.

For `J = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`, a simplicial set `U` and a simplicial object `V` of `C` this is the
product `U × V` of [Stacks, Tag 017C]: `(U × V)_n = ∐_{u ∈ U_n} V_n`, and for `φ : [m] → [n]` the
component `V_n` indexed by `u ∈ U_n` maps to the component `V_m` indexed by `U(φ)(u) ∈ U_m` via
`V(φ)`. It exists in particular when `C` has the coproduct of any two objects and every `U_n` is
finite nonempty.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def copower (V : J ⥤ C) (U : J ⥤ Type w)
    [∀ j, HasCoproduct fun _ : U.obj j => V.obj j] : J ⥤ C
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary index category `J` in place of `SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`, and under the source's looser hypothesis that the coproducts exist

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_corepresentableBy_copower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017D**.
Let `V : J ⥤ C` and `U : J ⥤ Type w` be such that the coproducts defining the copower
`V.copower U` exist. Then the covariant functor sending `W : J ⥤ C` to the hom-set
`π U ⋙ V ⟶ π U ⋙ W` of functors on the category of elements of `U` is corepresented by
`V.copower U`, by the bijection which sends `g : V.copower U ⟶ W` to the family of its
restrictions `Sigma.ι _ u ≫ g.app j : V.obj j ⟶ W.obj j` to the components of the coproducts.

For `J = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`, a simplicial set `U` and simplicial objects `V`, `W` of `C` this
says that the functor `W ↦ Mor_{Simp(C)}(U × V, W)` is canonically isomorphic to the functor
sending `W` to the set of Equation [Stacks, Tag 017B] of families
`(f_{n, u} : V_n ⟶ W_n)_{n ≥ 0, u ∈ U_n}` with `f_{m, U(φ)(u)} ∘ V(φ) = W(φ) ∘ f_{n, u}`, the
isomorphism sending `g : U × V ⟶ W` to `f_{n, u} = Sigma.ι _ u ≫ g_n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_corepresentableBy_copower (V : J ⥤ C) (U : J ⥤ Type w)
    [∀ j, HasCoproduct fun _ : U.obj j => V.obj j] :
    ∃ h : ((whiskeringLeft U.Elements J C).obj (CategoryOfElements.π U) ⋙
        coyoneda.obj (op (CategoryOfElements.π U ⋙ V))).CorepresentableBy (V.copower U),
      ∀ (W : J ⥤ C) (g : V.copower U ⟶ W) (j : J) (u : U.obj j),
        (h.homEquiv g).app ⟨u⟩ =
          Sigma.ι (fun _ : U.obj j => V.obj j) u ≫ g.app j
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary index category `J` in place of `SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`, under the source's looser hypothesis that the coproducts exist, and with the canonical isomorphism pinned by its components; the set of Equation 017B is the hom-set `π U ⋙ V ⟶ π U ⋙ W` over the category of elements of `U`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.copowerProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017E** (2).
The canonical projection `V.copower U ⟶ V`, whose component at `j` is the identity of `V j` on
each summand of `(V.copower U) j = ∐_{u ∈ U j} V j`. For `J = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`, a simplicial
set `U` and a simplicial object `V` this is the projection `U × V ⟶ V`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def copowerProj (V : J ⥤ C) (U : J ⥤ Type w)
    [∀ j, HasCoproduct fun _ : U.obj j => V.obj j] : V.copower U ⟶ V
declarations.comment: (2); stated for an arbitrary index category `J` in place of `SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ`, and under the looser hypothesis that the coproducts exist

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.prodFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017E** (1).
The functor `FSSets × SimplicialObject C ⥤ SimplicialObject C` sending a pair `(U, V)` to the
product `U × V = V.copower U` and a pair of morphisms `(a, b)` to `Functor.copowerMap b a`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def prodFunctor : SSet.FSSets.{w} × SimplicialObject C ⥤ SimplicialObject C

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.constProdStd.phi_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017F** (part 1).
For any simplicial object `V` of `C`, the map
`Φ : Mor_{Simp(C)}(X × Δ[k], V) → Mor_C(X, V_k)`, `Φ(γ) = γ_k ∘ ι_{id_[k]}`, is a bijection.
declarations.statement:
theorem phi_bijective (V : SimplicialObject C) :
    Function.Bijective (phi X k V)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.constProdStd.phi_trunc_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017F** (part 2).
Let `n ≥ k` and let `W` be an `n`-truncated simplicial object of `C`. Then the map
`Φ_n : Mor_{Simp_n(C)}(sk_n (X × Δ[k]), W) → Mor_C(X, W_k)`, `Φ_n(γ) = γ_k ∘ ι_{id_[k]}`, is a
bijection.
declarations.statement:
theorem phi_trunc_bijective (n : ℕ) (hkn : k ≤ n) (W : SimplicialObject.Truncated C n) :
    Function.Bijective (phiTrunc X k n hkn W)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.IsHomFromSSet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017I**.
`IsHomFromSSet U V H` is the datum exhibiting a simplicial object `H` of a category `C` as a
`Hom(U, V)` for a simplicial set `U` and a simplicial object `V` of `C`: a bijection
`Mor(W, H) ≃ Mor(W × U, V)`, functorial in the simplicial object `W` of `C`. The right-hand side is
written as `U ⟶ sHom W V`, the morphisms of simplicial sets from `U` into the enriched hom of `W`
and `V`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsHomFromSSet (U : SSet.{v}) (V H : SimplicialObject C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.simpHomFromSSet_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017J**. Let `C` be a category with coproducts of any two objects and with countable
limits, let `U` be a simplicial set with `U_n` finite and nonempty for all `n ≥ 0`, and let `V`
be a simplicial object of `C`. Then the functor `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets`, `X ↦ Mor_{Simp(C)}(X × U, V)`, is
representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem simpHomFromSSet_isRepresentable
    [HasBinaryCoproducts C] [HasCountableLimits C]
    (U : SSet.{0}) [∀ n, Finite (U.obj n)] [∀ n, Nonempty (U.obj n)]
    (V : SimplicialObject C) :
    (simpHomFromSSet U V).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: SSet.hasLimitsOfShape_elements
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017K**.
Let `U` be a simplicial set with finitely many nondegenerate simplices, i.e. with `U_n`
finite for all `n` and with all `n`-simplices degenerate for `n ≫ 0`, and let `C` be a
category with finite limits. Then every diagram indexed by the category `U.Elements` of
simplices of `U` has a limit in `C`.
declarations.statement:
public instance hasLimitsOfShape_elements (U : SSet.{w}) [U.Finite] (C : Type u)
    [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] : HasLimitsOfShape U.Elements C

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.exists_representableBy_sHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017L**.
Let `C` be a category with finite limits, let `U` be a finite simplicial set and let `V` be a
simplicial object of `C`. Then the simplicial object `Hom(U, V)` exists: the functor
`W ↦ (U ⟶ sHom W V)` on `(SimplicialObject C)ᵒᵖ`, which is `W ↦ Mor(W × U, V)`, is representable
by a simplicial object `H` of `C`; moreover `H _⦋n⦌` represents `X ↦ Mor(X × U × Δ[n], V)`, the
functor represented by `Hom(U × Δ[n], V)_0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_representableBy_sHom {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C]
    (U : SSet.{v}) [U.Finite] (V : SimplicialObject C) :
    ∃ H : SimplicialObject C,
      Nonempty ((sHomFunctor (SimplicialObject C) ⋙
        (evaluation (SimplicialObject C) SSet.{v}).obj V ⋙
        coyoneda.obj (op U)).RepresentableBy H) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (((SimplicialObject.const C).op ⋙ sHomFunctor (SimplicialObject C) ⋙
        (evaluation (SimplicialObject C) SSet.{v}).obj V ⋙
        coyoneda.obj (op (U ⊗ Δ[n]))).RepresentableBy (H _⦋n⦌))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.bijective_comp_proj_id_of_prod_coyoneda
declarations.doc:
**`Hom(C[k], X)` represents evaluation in degree `k`.** Let `X` be an object of a category
`C`, let `k : ℕ`, and let `U` be a simplicial object of `C` with coordinates
`pr n : C[k]_n → (U_n ⟶ X)` indexed by the terms `C[k]_n = Mor_Δ(⦋k⦌, ⦋n⦌)` of the standard
cosimplicial set `C[k]` of [Stacks, Tag 0B13], such that the coordinates exhibit `U_n` as the
self product `∏_{α ∈ C[k]_n} X` — the `T`-valued points of `U_n` are the maps of sets
`C[k]_n → Mor_C(T, X)`, `f ↦ (f ≫ pr n α)_α` — and such that the structure maps reindex along
`C[k]`, that is `U(φ) ≫ pr_α = pr_{C[k](φ)(α)} = pr_{φ ∘ α}`; so `U` is an incarnation of
`Hom(C[k], X)` for `X` read as the constant simplicial object. Then `U` represents evaluation in
degree `k`: (1) for every simplicial object `V` of `C` the map `γ ↦ γ_k ≫ pr_{id_⦋k⦌}` is a
bijection `Mor_{Simp(C)}(V, U) → Mor_C(V_k, X)`, and (2) for every `j ≥ k` and every
`j`-truncated simplicial object `W` of `C` the same formula is a bijection
`Mor_{Simp_j(C)}(W, sk_j U) → Mor_C(W_k, X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_comp_proj_id_of_prod_coyoneda (X : C) (k : ℕ) (U : SimplicialObject C)
    (pr : ∀ n : ℕ, uliftCoyoneda.{w}.obj (op ⦋k⦌) ^⦋n⦌ → (U _⦋n⦌ ⟶ X))
    (hpr : ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : C), Function.Bijective fun (f : T ⟶ U _⦋n⦌)
      (α : uliftCoyoneda.{w}.obj (op ⦋k⦌) ^⦋n⦌) => f ≫ pr n α)
    (hmap : ∀ (n m : ℕ) (φ : ⦋m⦌ ⟶ ⦋n⦌) (α : uliftCoyoneda.{w}.obj (op ⦋k⦌) ^⦋m⦌),
      U.map φ.op ≫ pr m α = pr n ((uliftCoyoneda.{w}.obj (op ⦋k⦌)).map φ α)) :
    (∀ V : SimplicialObject C, Function.Bijective fun γ : V ⟶ U =>
        (γ.app (op ⦋k⦌) ≫ pr k (ULift.up (𝟙 ⦋k⦌)) : V _⦋k⦌ ⟶ X)) ∧
    (∀ (j : ℕ) (hkj : k ≤ j) (W : Truncated C j),
      Function.Bijective fun γ : W ⟶ (truncation j).obj U =>
        (γ.app (op ⟨⦋k⦌, hkj⟩) ≫ pr k (ULift.up (𝟙 ⦋k⦌)) :
          W.obj (op (⟨⦋k⦌, hkj⟩ : SimplexCategory.Truncated j)) ⟶ X))
declarations.comment: the source's U is characterised rather than constructed: its terms being the self products indexed by C[k]_n of Tag 0B13, and its structure maps the reindexing, are the hypotheses, which is part (3); the two conjuncts are parts (1) and (2), the latter for an arbitrary truncation level j ≥ k

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.isPullback_hom_of_isPushout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017N**.
Let `T` be a simplicial object of a category `C`, let `a : U ⟶ V` and `b : U ⟶ W` be morphisms
of simplicial sets, and let `P = V ⨿_U W` be their pushout, with structure morphisms
`f : V ⟶ P`, `g : W ⟶ P`. Assume that for each of the four simplicial sets `K = U, V, W, P` the
presheaf `X ↦ Mor_{Simp(C)}(X × K, T) = Mor_{SSet}(K, T ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op X))` on `C` is
represented by an object `Hom(K, T)₀` of `C` — as it is, by [Stacks, Tag 017L], when `C` has
coproducts of any two objects and finite limits, the `U_n`, `V_n`, `W_n` are finite nonempty and
all simplices of `U`, `V`, `W` in high enough degree are degenerate. Then
`Hom(P, T)₀ = Hom(V, T)₀ ×_{Hom(U, T)₀} Hom(W, T)₀`
via the morphisms induced by `f`, `g`, `a` and `b`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPullback_hom_of_isPushout {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (T : SimplicialObject C) {U V W P : SSet.{v}}
    {a : U ⟶ V} {b : U ⟶ W} {f : V ⟶ P} {g : W ⟶ P} (h : IsPushout a b f g)
    {HU HV HW HP : C}
    (hU : (coyoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ C (Type v)).obj T ⋙
        coyoneda.obj (op U)).RepresentableBy HU)
    (hV : (coyoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ C (Type v)).obj T ⋙
        coyoneda.obj (op V)).RepresentableBy HV)
    (hW : (coyoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ C (Type v)).obj T ⋙
        coyoneda.obj (op W)).RepresentableBy HW)
    (hP : (coyoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ C (Type v)).obj T ⋙
        coyoneda.obj (op P)).RepresentableBy HP) :
    IsPullback (hV.homEquiv.symm (f ≫ hP.homEquiv (𝟙 HP)))
      (hW.homEquiv.symm (g ≫ hP.homEquiv (𝟙 HP)))
      (hU.homEquiv.symm (a ≫ hV.homEquiv (𝟙 HV)))
      (hU.homEquiv.symm (b ≫ hW.homEquiv (𝟙 HW)))
declarations.comment: stated in degree 0, for the representing objects of `X ↦ Mor(X × K, T)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.SubobjectSplitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017P**, for full simplicial objects.
A splitting by subobjects is a Mathlib splitting whose structure maps `N(U_n) ⟶ U_n` are
monomorphisms, so that they represent the subobjects required by the source definition.
declarations.statement: structure SubobjectSplitting (X : SimplicialObject C) extends X.Splitting
declarations.comment: the definition for full simplicial objects; a monomorphism represents each source subobject, and `Splitting.isColimit'` is exactly the displayed coproduct isomorphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.SubobjectSplitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017P**, for truncated simplicial objects.
A splitting of an `r`-truncated simplicial object consists of subobjects in every degree at most
`r` whose images under all surjections form a coproduct decomposition in each truncated degree.
declarations.statement: structure SubobjectSplitting {r : ℕ} (X : SimplicialObject.Truncated C r)
declarations.comment: the definition for truncated simplicial objects; the index category is the surjections `[n] → [m]`, automatically with `m ≤ n ≤ r`

declarations.name: SSet.Splitting.existsUnique_equiv_nonDegenerate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017R**.
If `s` is a splitting of a simplicial set `X`, then for every `n` there is a unique bijection
between `s.N n` and the set of nondegenerate `n`-simplices of `X` compatible with the maps `s.ι n`
and `Subtype.val` to `X _⦋n⦌`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Splitting.existsUnique_equiv_nonDegenerate (s : X.Splitting) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! e : s.N n ≃ X.nonDegenerate n, ∀ x, (e x : X _⦋n⦌) = s.ι n x

declarations.name: SSet.injective_of_injective_on_nonDegenerate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017S** (part 1).
Let `f : U ⟶ V` be a morphism of simplicial sets sending nondegenerate simplices to
nondegenerate simplices, whose induced map on nondegenerate simplices is injective. Then
`f.app ⦋n⦌` is injective for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_of_injective_on_nonDegenerate
    {U V : SSet} (f : U ⟶ V)
    (ha : PreservesNonDegenerate f) (hb : InjectiveOnNonDegenerate f) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ), Function.Injective (f.app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))

declarations.name: SSet.surjective_of_surjective_on_nonDegenerate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017S** (part 2).
Let `f : U ⟶ V` be a morphism of simplicial sets whose induced map on nondegenerate simplices is
surjective. Then `f.app ⦋n⦌` is surjective for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_of_surjective_on_nonDegenerate
    {U V : SSet} (f : U ⟶ V)
    (hb : SurjectiveOnNonDegenerate f) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ), Function.Surjective (f.app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))

declarations.name: SSet.bijective_of_bijective_on_nonDegenerate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017S** (part 3).
Let `f : U ⟶ V` be a morphism of simplicial sets sending nondegenerate simplices to
nondegenerate simplices, whose induced map on nondegenerate simplices is both injective and
surjective. Then `f.app ⦋n⦌` is bijective for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_of_bijective_on_nonDegenerate
    {U V : SSet} (f : U ⟶ V)
    (ha : PreservesNonDegenerate f)
    (hbinj : InjectiveOnNonDegenerate f) (hbsurj : SurjectiveOnNonDegenerate f) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ), Function.Bijective (f.app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))

declarations.name: SSet.skeleton_obj_eq_top_and_hasDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017T**.
The sub-simplicial set generated by the simplices of `X` in degrees at most `n` is
`X.skeleton (n + 1)`. It agrees with `X` through degree `n`, and every simplex in a higher degree
is degenerate.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.exists_splitting_range_ι_eq_iInf_ker_δ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017U**.
Every simplicial abelian group `U` has a splitting whose nondegenerate part is `N(U_0) = U_0` and
`N(U_m) = ⋂_{i = 0}^{m - 1} Ker(d^m_i)` for `m ≥ 1`, and this splitting is functorial: any morphism
of simplicial abelian groups carries `N(U_m)` into `N(V_m)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_splitting_range_ι_eq_iInf_ker_δ :
    ∃ s : ∀ U : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}, U.Splitting,
      (∀ (U : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (n : ℕ), Mono ((s U).ι n)) ∧
      (∀ U : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}, ((s U).ι 0).hom.range = ⊤) ∧
      (∀ (U : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (n : ℕ), ((s U).ι (n + 1)).hom.range =
        ⨅ i : Fin (n + 1), (U.δ i.castSucc).hom.ker) ∧
      (∀ (U V : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (f : U ⟶ V) (n : ℕ),
        ∃ g : (s U).N n ⟶ (s V).N n, (s U).ι n ≫ f.app (op ⦋n⦌) = g ≫ (s V).ι n)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.exists_splittingFunctor_mk_ι_eq_inf_kernelSubobject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017V**.
Every simplicial object `U` of an abelian category `A` has a splitting whose nondegenerate parts
are `N(U₀) = U₀` and `N(U_{n + 1}) = ⋂_{i = 0}^{n} Ker(d^{n + 1}_i)`, and this splitting is
functorial: the splittings are the values of a functor `SimplicialObject A ⥤ Split A` which is a
section of the functor forgetting the splitting.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_splittingFunctor_mk_ι_eq_inf_kernelSubobject :
    ∃ F : SimplicialObject A ⥤ Split A,
      F ⋙ Split.forget A = 𝟭 (SimplicialObject A) ∧
      (∀ U : SimplicialObject A, IsIso ((F.obj U).s.ι 0)) ∧
      ∀ (U : SimplicialObject A) (n : ℕ), ∃ _ : Mono ((F.obj U).s.ι (n + 1)),
        Subobject.mk ((F.obj U).s.ι (n + 1)) =
          Finset.univ.inf
            fun i : Fin (n + 1) => kernelSubobject ((F.obj U).X.δ i.castSucc)

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.NormalizedMooreComplex.mono_epi_isIso_app_iff_map_f
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017W**.
The normalized Moore complex functor `N` of an abelian category reflects (and preserves) degreewise
monomorphisms, epimorphisms and isomorphisms: for a morphism `f : U ⟶ V` of simplicial objects, `f`
is a monomorphism in each degree if and only if `N(f)_m` is a monomorphism for every `m`, and
likewise for epimorphisms and for isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem NormalizedMooreComplex.mono_epi_isIso_app_iff_map_f (f : U ⟶ V) :
    ((∀ Δ : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Mono (f.app Δ)) ↔
        ∀ m : ℕ, Mono (((normalizedMooreComplex A).map f).f m)) ∧
      ((∀ Δ : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Epi (f.app Δ)) ↔
        ∀ m : ℕ, Epi (((normalizedMooreComplex A).map f).f m)) ∧
      ((∀ Δ : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, IsIso (f.app Δ)) ↔
        ∀ m : ℕ, IsIso (((normalizedMooreComplex A).map f).f m))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.normalizedMoore_factors_arrow_comp_δ_last
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017X**.
The last face carries the Stacks-convention normalized Moore subobject in degree `n + 1` into the
normalized Moore subobject in degree `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalizedMoore_factors_arrow_comp_δ_last (U : SimplicialObject C) (n : ℕ) :
    (normalizedMoore U n).Factors
      ((normalizedMoore U (n + 1)).arrow ≫ U.δ (Fin.last (n + 1)))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Usub_isSubSimplicial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017Y** (1).
`U'` is a sub simplicial object of `U`: for every order-preserving map `ψ : [m'] → [m]` the
morphism `U(ψ) : U_m → U_{m'}` maps `U'_m` into `U'_{m'}`, that is, the composite
`(U'_m).arrow ≫ U(ψ)` factors through `U'_{m'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Usub_isSubSimplicial (U : SimplicialObject C) (n m m' : ℕ)
    (ψ : SimplexCategory.mk m' ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk m) :
    (Usub U n m').Factors ((Usub U n m).arrow ≫ U.map ψ.op)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Usub_eq_top_of_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017Y** (2).
For every `i ≤ n` one has `U'_i = U_i`, that is, `U'_i` is the top subobject of `U_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Usub_eq_top_of_le (U : SimplicialObject C) (n i : ℕ) (h : i ≤ n) :
    Usub U n i = ⊤

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Usub_inf_moore_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 017Y** (3).
For every `m > n` one has `N(U'_m) = 0`. By the splitting of [Stacks, Tag 017V] one has
`N(U'_m) = U'_m ∩ N(U_m)` as subobjects of `U_m`, so the assertion is that the intersection
`U'_m ⊓ N(U_m)` is the zero subobject.
declarations.statement:
theorem Usub_inf_moore_eq_bot (U : SimplicialObject C) (n m : ℕ) (h : n < m) :
    Usub U n m ⊓ normalizedMoore U m = ⊥

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated
registrations.comment: Simp_n(C), functors Δ_{≤n}ᵒᵖ ⥤ C (morphisms are natural transformations)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.coskAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The bijection `Mor(U, cosk_m V) = Mor(sk_m U, V)`** of [Stacks, Equation 0181], over a
category with finite limits: the coskeleton functor is right adjoint to the skeleton functor, an
adjunction being exactly that bijection, natural in both variables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coskAdjunction [HasFiniteLimits C] (m : ℕ) :
    SimplicialObject.truncation (C := C) m ⊣ Truncated.cosk m

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.bijective_app_zero_comp_π
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0182**.
The `0`-coskeleton of an object `X` is the simplicial object `n ↦ X^{n + 1}`. Let `U` be a
simplicial object of `C` whose term `U_n` is the product of `n + 1` copies of `X`, with projections
`π n i : U_n ⟶ X` indexed by the vertices `i` of `⦋n⦌` (`hU`), the simplicial structure maps acting
on coordinates by `(x_0, …, x_m) ↦ (x_{φ(0)}, …, x_{φ(n)})` (`hπ`). Then for every simplicial
object `V` of `C`, a morphism `V ⟶ U` is determined by and determines a single morphism `V_0 ⟶ X`,
