namely the composite of its degree-`0` component with the projection `π 0 0`. In other words
`Mor(V, U) = Mor(V_0, X)`, so that `U` is the coskeleton `cosk₀(X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_app_zero_comp_π {X : C} {U : SimplicialObject C}
    (π : ∀ n : ℕ, Fin (n + 1) → (U.obj (op ⦋n⦌) ⟶ X))
    (hU : ∀ n : ℕ, IsLimit (Fan.mk (U.obj (op ⦋n⦌)) (π n)))
    (hπ : ∀ {n m : ℕ} (φ : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌) (i : Fin (n + 1)),
      U.map φ.op ≫ π n i = π m (φ.toOrderHom i))
    (V : SimplicialObject C) :
    Function.Bijective (fun f : V ⟶ U => f.app (op ⦋0⦌) ≫ π 0 0)
declarations.comment: the self-product simplicial object is stated abstractly, by product cones on the terms of an arbitrary `U`, rather than by choosing a model of `X ^ (n + 1)`; the hom-set formula is reduced, as in the source, to `Mor(V, U) = Mor(V₀, X)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_of_hasFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
If `C` has finite limits, every truncated simplicial object has the pointwise right Kan
extension along `( Δ_{≤ k} ⊆ Δ )ᵒᵖ` which defines its `k`-coskeleton. Pointwiseness says that its
value at `[n]` is the limit over the finite structured-arrow category `((Δ/[n])_{≤ k})ᵒᵖ`, and
functoriality supplies the maps induced by `[n] → [n']`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_of_hasFiniteLimits [HasFiniteLimits C]
    (k : ℕ) (F : SimplicialObject.Truncated C k) :
    (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion k).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F
declarations.comment: existence and the displayed limit formula; the formula is the defining universal property of `HasPointwiseRightKanExtension` at each simplex

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.sliceCone_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0184**.
Let `C` be a category and let `U` be an `m`-truncated simplicial object of `C`. For `n ≤ m` the
limit of the diagram `U(n)` exists in `C` and is canonically isomorphic to `U_n`: the canonical
cone, with apex `U_n` and component `U(α) : U_n → U_k` at an object `α : [k] → [n]`, is a limit
cone.
declarations.statement:
theorem sliceCone_isLimit {m : ℕ} (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) {n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit (sliceCone U h))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.isIso_ranAdjunction_counit_app_of_hasFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a category with finite limits and let `U` be an `n`-truncated simplicial object
of `C`. Then the morphism `sk_n cosk_n U → U` is an isomorphism. Here `sk_n` is the truncation
functor `truncation n : SimplicialObject C ⥤ SimplicialObject.Truncated C n`, its right adjoint
`cosk_n` is the right Kan extension along `(Δ_{≤n} ⊆ Δ)ᵒᵖ`, which exists by [Stacks, Lemma 0183]
(`hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_of_hasFiniteLimits`), and the morphism is the counit at `U` of the
adjunction `ranAdjunction` between them.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_ranAdjunction_counit_app_of_hasFiniteLimits [HasFiniteLimits C] (n : ℕ)
    (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C n) :
    haveI := hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_of_hasFiniteLimits (C := C) n
    IsIso (((SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion n).op.ranAdjunction C).counit.app U)
declarations.comment: `sk_n` is the truncation `truncation n` and the morphism is the counit at `U` of `ranAdjunction`, truncation ⊣ `cosk_n`, whose right Kan extensions exist by Lemma 0183

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.existsUnique_cone_app_δ_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0186**.
A matching family of morphisms into the top term of a truncated simplicial object is the same thing
as a cone over the truncated slice category. Let `U` be an `(n + 1)`-truncated simplicial object of
`C` and let `f i : T ⟶ U_{n + 1}`, `i = 0, …, n + 2`, be a family of morphisms. Then `f` extends,
in exactly one way, to a cone over the diagram `(Δ/⦋n + 2⦌)^{opp}_{≤ n + 1} → C` defined by `U`
whose leg at the face `δ_i : ⦋n + 1⦌ ⟶ ⦋n + 2⦌` is `f i`, if and only if `f` is a matching family:
`f i ≫ d_j = f (j + 1) ≫ d_i` for all `i ≤ j`.
Consequently, if the functor of matching families is represented by an object `U_{n + 2}`, then
`U_{n + 2} = lim_{(Δ/⦋n + 2⦌)^{opp}_{≤ n + 1}} U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_cone_app_δ_eq_iff (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C (n + 1)) (T : C)
    (f : Fin (n + 3) →
      (T ⟶ U.obj (op (⟨⦋n + 1⦌, le_rfl⟩ : SimplexCategory.Truncated (n + 1))))) :
    (∃! π : (Functor.const (StructuredArrow (op ⦋n + 2⦌)
          (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion (n + 1)).op)).obj T ⟶
        StructuredArrow.proj (op ⦋n + 2⦌)
          (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion (n + 1)).op ⋙ U,
      ∀ i : Fin (n + 3), π.app (StructuredArrow.mk
        (Y := op (⟨⦋n + 1⦌, le_rfl⟩ : SimplexCategory.Truncated (n + 1)))
        (SimplexCategory.δ i).op) = f i) ↔
      ∀ i j : Fin (n + 2), i ≤ j →
        f i.castSucc ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) j n.le_succ le_rfl).op =
          f j.succ ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) i n.le_succ le_rfl).op
declarations.comment: the representing object of the functor of matching families is the limit over the truncated slice category, via restriction of a cone to its legs at the faces

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.exists_isRightKanExtension_of_matchingFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0187**.
One-step extension of a truncated simplicial object, and its adjointness. Let `U` be an
`(n + 1)`-truncated simplicial object of `C`, and suppose that the contravariant functor sending
`T` to the set of families `(g_0, …, g_{n + 2})` of morphisms `T ⟶ U_{n + 1}` with
`d_{j - 1} ∘ g_i = d_i ∘ g_j` for `i < j` is representable: it is represented by an object `Y`
together with a universal such family `f`. Then `U` extends to an `(n + 2)`-truncated simplicial
object `Ũ` whose `(n + 1)`-skeleton is identified with `U` by an isomorphism `α` and whose degree
`n + 2` part is identified with `Y` compatibly with the faces, such that `(Ũ, α)` is a right Kan
extension of `U` along the inclusion of truncated simplex categories; the latter is the adjointness
`Mor(V, Ũ) = Mor(sk_{n + 1} V, U)`, natural in `V` and given by restricting along the skeleton.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isRightKanExtension_of_matchingFamily {n : ℕ}
    (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C (n + 1)) (Y : C)
    (f : Fin (n + 3) → (Y ⟶ U _⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁))
    (hf : ∀ i j : Fin (n + 2), i ≤ j →
      f i.castSucc ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) j (by trunc) (by trunc)).op =
        f j.succ ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) i (by trunc) (by trunc)).op)
    (huniv : ∀ (T : C) (g : Fin (n + 3) → (T ⟶ U _⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁)),
      (∀ i j : Fin (n + 2), i ≤ j →
        g i.castSucc ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) j (by trunc) (by trunc)).op =
          g j.succ ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) i (by trunc) (by trunc)).op) →
      ∃! h : T ⟶ Y, ∀ i, h ≫ f i = g i) :
    ∃ (Ũ : SimplicialObject.Truncated C (n + 2))
      (α : (SimplicialObject.Truncated.trunc C (n + 2) (n + 1)).obj Ũ ⟶ U),
      IsIso α ∧ Ũ.IsRightKanExtension α ∧
        ∃ e : Ũ _⦋n + 2⦌ₙ₊₂ ≅ Y, ∀ i : Fin (n + 3),
          e.hom ≫ f i =
            Ũ.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 2) i (by trunc) (by trunc)).op ≫
              α.app (op ⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁)
declarations.comment: the adjointness is stated as the universal property of a right Kan extension along the inclusion of the truncated simplex categories

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.eq_σ_comp_iff_of_matchingFamily
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be an `(n + 1)`-truncated simplicial object of `C` whose functor of matching families in
degree `n + 2` is represented by `Y` with universal matching family `f` ([Stacks, Tag 0187]), let
`Ũ` be an `(n + 2)`-truncated object with a comparison morphism `α : sk_{n + 1} Ũ ⟶ U` and an
identification `e : Ũ_{n + 2} ≅ Y` under which the faces `d_i : Ũ_{n + 2} ⟶ Ũ_{n + 1}` become the
projections `f_i`. Then a family `s` of morphisms `Ũ_{n + 1} ⟶ Y` records the degeneracies
`s_j : Ũ_{n + 1} ⟶ Ũ_{n + 2}` of `Ũ` if and only if, componentwise, `s_j` sends `g` to
`(s_{j - 1} d_0 g, …, s_{j - 1} d_{j - 1} g, g, g, s_j d_{j + 1} g, …, s_j d_{n + 1} g)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eq_σ_comp_iff_of_matchingFamily {n : ℕ}
    {U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C (n + 1)} {Ũ : SimplicialObject.Truncated C (n + 2)}
    (α : (SimplicialObject.Truncated.trunc C (n + 2) (n + 1)).obj Ũ ⟶ U) {Y : C}
    (f : Fin (n + 3) → (Y ⟶ U _⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁))
    (hf : ∀ i j : Fin (n + 2), i ≤ j →
      f i.castSucc ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) j (by trunc) (by trunc)).op =
        f j.succ ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) i (by trunc) (by trunc)).op)
    (huniv : ∀ (T : C) (g : Fin (n + 3) → (T ⟶ U _⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁)),
      (∀ i j : Fin (n + 2), i ≤ j →
        g i.castSucc ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) j (by trunc) (by trunc)).op =
          g j.succ ≫ U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) i (by trunc) (by trunc)).op) →
      ∃! h : T ⟶ Y, ∀ i, h ≫ f i = g i)
    (e : Ũ _⦋n + 2⦌ₙ₊₂ ≅ Y)
    (he : ∀ i : Fin (n + 3), e.hom ≫ f i =
      Ũ.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 2) i (by trunc) (by trunc)).op ≫
        α.app (op ⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁))
    (s : Fin (n + 2) → (Ũ _⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₂ ⟶ Y)) :
    (∀ j : Fin (n + 2),
        Ũ.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.σ (n + 2) j (by trunc) (by trunc)).op = s j ≫ e.inv) ↔
      (∀ j : Fin (n + 2), s j ≫ f j.castSucc = α.app (op ⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁)) ∧
      (∀ j : Fin (n + 2), s j ≫ f j.succ = α.app (op ⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁)) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin (n + 2)) (j : Fin (n + 1)), i ≤ j.castSucc →
        s j.succ ≫ f i.castSucc = α.app (op ⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁) ≫
          U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) i (by trunc) (by trunc)).op ≫
            U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.σ (n + 1) j (by trunc) (by trunc)).op) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin (n + 2)) (j : Fin (n + 1)), j.castSucc < i →
        s j.castSucc ≫ f i.succ = α.app (op ⦋n + 1⦌ₙ₊₁) ≫
          U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.δ (n + 1) i (by trunc) (by trunc)).op ≫
            U.map (SimplexCategory.Truncated.σ (n + 1) j (by trunc) (by trunc)).op)
declarations.comment: the description of the faces is the identification `he` of Lemma 0187; the description of the degeneracies is stated as a characterisation of them by their components, which the representability of the functor of matching families makes possible

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_of_incl_succ
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a category, let `m : ℕ` and let `F` be an `m`-truncated simplicial object of `C`.
Assume that every `k`-truncated simplicial object of `C`, for `k ≥ m`, can be extended by one
degree, i.e. admits a pointwise right Kan extension along the inclusion `(Δ_{≤k} ⊆ Δ_{≤k+1})ᵒᵖ` —
the one-degree step of [Stacks, Tag 0187]. Then:

* for every `n ≥ m` the `n`-truncated object `U^n` extending `F` exists, as a pointwise right Kan
  extension of `F` along `(Δ_{≤m} ⊆ Δ_{≤n})ᵒᵖ`; its universal property is the source's
  `Mor_{Simp_n(C)}(V, U^n) = Mor_{Simp_m(C)}(sk_m V, F)`;
* the coskeleton `cosk_m F` exists, as a pointwise right Kan extension of `F` along
  `(Δ_{≤m} ⊆ Δ)ᵒᵖ`; its universal property is the source's
  `Mor_{Simp(C)}(V, cosk_m F) = Mor_{Simp_m(C)}(sk_m V, F)`;
* the tower is compatible: the `n`-truncation of any right Kan extension `X` of `F` along
  `(Δ_{≤m} ⊆ Δ)ᵒᵖ` is again a right Kan extension of `F` along `(Δ_{≤m} ⊆ Δ_{≤n})ᵒᵖ`, which is the
  source's `(cosk_m F)_n = U^n_n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_of_incl_succ {m : ℕ}
    (H : ∀ (k : ℕ), m ≤ k → ∀ G : SimplicialObject.Truncated C k,
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.incl k (k + 1)).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G)
    (F : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) :
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n),
        (SimplexCategory.Truncated.incl m n h).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F) ∧
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion m).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n) (X : SimplicialObject C) (β : (truncation m).obj X ⟶ F),
        X.IsRightKanExtension β →
          ((truncation n).obj X).IsRightKanExtension
            (((truncationCompTrunc (C := C) h).app X).hom ≫ β)
declarations.comment: the source's three displayed assertions, with each `Mor` formula stated as the universal property of the right Kan extension it is; the hypothesis is the one-degree step of Lemma 0187 rather than finite limits in the ambient category

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.nonempty_truncCoskAdj_and_isIso_coskAdj_unit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018B** (parts 2, 3 and 4).
Coskeleta of different levels. Let `C` be a category, let `n ≤ m` and assume the `n`-th and `m`-th
coskeleton functors of `C` exist. Then:

* (2) the further truncation `sk_n : Simp_m(C) ⥤ Simp_n(C)` has a right adjoint, namely
  `sk_m cosk_n`;
* (3) for every `n`-truncated simplicial object `U` of `C` the canonical map
  `cosk_n U ⟶ cosk_m sk_m cosk_n U` is an isomorphism, i.e. `cosk_m sk_m cosk_n U = cosk_n U`;
* (4) if the canonical map `X ⟶ cosk_n sk_n X` is an isomorphism for a simplicial object `X` of
  `C`, then so is the canonical map `X ⟶ cosk_m sk_m X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_truncCoskAdj_and_isIso_coskAdj_unit_app {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m)
    [∀ F : (SimplexCategory.Truncated n)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C,
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion n).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    [∀ F : (SimplexCategory.Truncated m)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C,
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion m).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] :
    Nonempty (Truncated.trunc C m n h ⊣ Truncated.cosk n ⋙ truncation m) ∧
      (∀ U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C n,
        IsIso ((coskAdj m).unit.app ((Truncated.cosk n).obj U))) ∧
      (∀ X : SimplicialObject C,
        IsIso ((coskAdj n).unit.app X) → IsIso ((coskAdj m).unit.app X))
declarations.comment: parts (2), (3) and (4); part (1) is the hypothesis that the coskeleta exist, i.e. Tag 0183 for a category with finite limits

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.coskProdIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018C**.
The canonical isomorphism `cosk_n (U ⨯ V) ≅ cosk_n U ⨯ cosk_n V` in `Simp(C)`, for `U`, `V`
`n`-truncated simplicial objects of `C`, coming from the preservation of the binary product of
`U` and `V` by the coskeleton functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coskProdIso (n : ℕ)
    [∀ (F : (SimplexCategory.Truncated n)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C),
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion n).op.HasRightKanExtension F]
    (U V : SimplicialObject.Truncated C n)
    [HasBinaryProduct U V]
    [HasBinaryProduct ((Truncated.cosk n).obj U) ((Truncated.cosk n).obj V)] :
    (Truncated.cosk n).obj (U ⨯ V) ≅
      (Truncated.cosk n).obj U ⨯ (Truncated.cosk n).obj V

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.cosk.preservesLimitsOfSize
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018D**.
The `n`-th coskeleton functor `cosk n : Simp_n(C) ⥤ Simp(C)` preserves all limits, being right
adjoint to `truncation n`. In particular, for morphisms `f : U ⟶ V` and `g : W ⟶ V` of
`n`-truncated simplicial objects of `C`, `cosk n (U ×_V W) = cosk n U ×_{cosk n V} cosk n W`
whenever both sides exist, the canonical comparison `Limits.pullbackComparison (cosk n) f g` being
an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public instance cosk.preservesLimitsOfSize (n : ℕ)
    [∀ F : (SimplexCategory.Truncated n)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C,
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion n).op.HasRightKanExtension F] :
    PreservesLimitsOfSize.{w, w'} (Truncated.cosk (C := C) n)

declarations.name: SSet.canonicalMap_stdSimplex_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018E**.
For every `n`, the canonical map `c_{Δ[n]} : Δ[n] ⟶ cosk_1 sk_1 Δ[n]`, the unit of the adjunction
`sk_1 ⊣ cosk_1` at the standard `n`-simplex, is an isomorphism of simplicial sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMap_stdSimplex_isIso (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso (cosk1Unit (Δ[n]))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.existsUnique_hom_const_app_zero_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be a simplicial object of a category `C`, let `X : C` and let `ε₀ : U_0 ⟶ X`. Then `ε₀`
extends to a unique augmentation of `U` towards `X`, i.e. to a unique morphism
`U ⟶ (const C).obj X` with `ε₀` as its degree `0` component, precisely when
`U.δ 0 ≫ ε₀ = U.δ 1 ≫ ε₀`.
declarations.comment: restriction to degree 0 is a bijection from augmentations of U towards X onto the morphisms ε₀ : U_0 ⟶ X with ε₀ ∘ d^1_0 = ε₀ ∘ d^1_1

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Arrow.truncation_bijective_into_cechNerve
declarations.doc:
For a simplicial object `V` and the Čech nerve `U` of `f : Y ⟶ X`,
the map `Mor(V, U) → Mor(sk₁ V, sk₁ U)`, `g ↦ sk₁ g`, induced by the `1`-truncation functor, is a
bijection.
declarations.statement:
theorem truncation_bijective_into_cechNerve
    (f : Arrow C) [HasCechPullbacks f] (V : SimplicialObject C) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun g : V ⟶ cechNerve f => (truncation 1).map g)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Arrow.truncated_mor_equiv_setOf
declarations.doc:
Morphisms `sk₁ V ⟶ sk₁ U` of `1`-truncated simplicial objects
correspond bijectively to the morphisms `g₀ : V₀ ⟶ Y` satisfying
`f ∘ g₀ ∘ d¹₀ = f ∘ g₀ ∘ d¹₁`, the bijection sending `g` to its degree-`0` component
`deg0Component g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem truncated_mor_equiv_setOf
    (f : Arrow C) [HasCechPullbacks f] (V : SimplicialObject C) :
    ∃ e : ((truncation 1).obj V ⟶ (truncation 1).obj (cechNerve f)) ≃
        { g₀ : V.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0)) ⟶ f.left //
            V.δ (0 : Fin 2) ≫ g₀ ≫ f.hom = V.δ (1 : Fin 2) ≫ g₀ ≫ f.hom },
      ∀ g, (e g : V.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0)) ⟶ f.left) = deg0Component g

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Arrow.cechNerve_isCoskeletal
declarations.doc:
The Čech nerve `U` is `1`-coskeletal: the unit
`U ⟶ cosk₁ (sk₁ U)` of the `sk₁`/`cosk₁` adjunction is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechNerve_isCoskeletal
    (f : Arrow C) [HasCechPullbacks f] [HasCosk₁ C] :
    IsIso ((coskAdj (C := C) 1).unit.app (cechNerve f))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.existsUnique_hom_cechNerve_app_zero_comp_π_eq_id
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a category with fibre products, let `V` be a simplicial object of `C` and let
`ε : V ⟶ (const C).obj X` be an augmentation of `V` towards `X : C`, with degree `0` component
`ε₀ : V_0 ⟶ X`. Let `U` be the Čech nerve of `ε₀`, whose `n`th term is the `(n + 1)`-fold fibre
product `V_0 ×_X ⋯ ×_X V_0`. Then there is exactly one morphism `V ⟶ U` whose degree `0` component
is the canonical isomorphism `V_0 ≅ V_0 ×_X X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_hom_cechNerve_app_zero_comp_π_eq_id [HasFiniteWidePullbacks C]
    (V : SimplicialObject C) (X : C) (ε : V ⟶ (const C).obj X) :
    ∃! g : V ⟶ (Arrow.mk (ε.app (op ⦋0⦌) : V _⦋0⦌ ⟶ X)).cechNerve,
      g.app (op ⦋0⦌) ≫ WidePullback.π _ 0 = 𝟙 (V _⦋0⦌)
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism V ⟶ U, pinned as the unique morphism to the Čech nerve of ε₀ which is the identity of V_0 in degree 0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.hasPointwiseLeftKanExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018L**.
An `m`-truncated simplicial object `U` of a category `C` with finite colimits has a pointwise
left Kan extension along `(SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion m).op`: for every `⦋n⦌`, the
colimit of `U` over `(⦋n⦌/Δ)^{opp}_{≤ m}` exists. Hence the left adjoint `i_{m!}` of the
skeleton functor `sk_m` exists (`CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.sk m`, with
adjunction `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.skAdj m`) and `(i_{m!}U)_n` is that colimit.
declarations.statement:
public instance hasPointwiseLeftKanExtension (m : ℕ) (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) :
    (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion m).op.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension U

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.underCocone_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018M**.
Let `C` be a category and let `U` be an `m`-truncated simplicial object of `C`. For an object
`[n]` of `Δ_{≤ m}` the cocone `underCocone`, with apex `U_n` and leg `U(α) : U_k → U_n` at an
object `α : [n] → [k]`, exhibits `U_n` as the colimit of the diagram `U(n)`.
declarations.statement: theorem underCocone_isColimit : Nonempty (IsColimit (underCocone U n))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.isIso_lanAdjunction_unit_app
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a category with finite colimits and let `U` be an `m`-truncated simplicial object
of `C`. The unit `U ⟶ sk_m i_{m!} U` of the adjunction `i_{m!} ⊣ sk_m`, where
`i_{m!} = CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.sk m` is the left Kan extension along the
inclusion `Δ_{≤ m} ⊆ Δ` and `sk_m = CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.truncation m` is restriction
along it, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lanAdjunction_unit_app (m : ℕ) (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) :
    IsIso (X := U) (Y := (truncation m).obj ((Truncated.sk m).obj U))
      (((SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion m).op.lanAdjunction C).unit.app U)

declarations.name: SSet.Truncated.mem_degenerate_sk_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018O**.
For an `m`-truncated simplicial set `U` and `n > m`, every `n`-simplex of
`i_{m!} U = (SSet.Truncated.sk m).obj U` is degenerate.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_degenerate_sk_obj (m : ℕ) (U : SSet.Truncated m) (n : ℕ) (hn : m < n)
    (x : ((Truncated.sk m).obj U).obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk n))) :
    x ∈ ((Truncated.sk m).obj U).degenerate n

declarations.name: SSet.exists_iso_skeleton_hom_ι_eq_skAdj_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018P**.
For a simplicial set `X` and `n : ℕ`, the canonical morphism `i_{n!} sk_n X ⟶ X`, i.e. the counit
of the adjunction `SSet.skAdj n`, factors as an isomorphism from `(sk n).obj X` onto the
subcomplex `X.skeleton (n + 1)` generated by the simplices of dimension `≤ n`, followed by the
inclusion of that subcomplex.

declarations.name: SSet.Subcomplex.isPushout_boundary_ι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018R**.
Let `U` be a simplicial subset of a simplicial set
`V` and let `x` be an `n`-simplex of `V` not in `U` such that `U` contains all simplices of `V`
of dimension `< n` (`hlt`), `x` is the only `n`-simplex of `V` outside `U` (`hn`), and every
simplex of `V` outside `U` in a degree `> n` is degenerate (`hgt`). Then the square formed by
the boundary inclusion `∂Δ[n] ⟶ Δ[n]`, the inclusion `U ⟶ V`, and the morphism
`Δ[n] ⟶ V` classifying `x` is a pushout square: `V = U ∐_{∂Δ[n]} Δ[n]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPushout_boundary_ι {V : SSet.{u}} {U : V.Subcomplex} {n : ℕ} (x : V _⦋n⦌)
    (hx : x ∉ U.obj (op ⦋n⦌)) (hlt : V.skeleton n ≤ U)
    (hn : ∀ y : V _⦋n⦌, y ∈ U.obj (op ⦋n⦌) ∨ y = x)
    (hgt : ∀ j : ℕ, n < j → ∀ z : V _⦋j⦌, z ∉ U.obj (op ⦋j⦌) → z ∈ V.degenerate j)
    (hbd : range (∂Δ[n].ι ≫ yonedaEquiv.symm x) ≤ U) :
    IsPushout (lift (∂Δ[n].ι ≫ yonedaEquiv.symm x) hbd) ∂Δ[n].ι U.ι (yonedaEquiv.symm x)

declarations.name: SSet.Subcomplex.exists_monotone_sup_ofSimplex_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018S**.
Let `U` be a simplicial subset of a simplicial set `V` such that only finitely
many nondegenerate simplices of `V` lie outside `U`. Then there are `r : ℕ` and an increasing
sequence `W` of simplicial subsets of `V` with `W 0 = U` and `W r = V` such that, for each
`i < r`, the subcomplex `W (i + 1)` is obtained from `W i` by adjoining a single simplex `x`
of `V` which does not lie in `W i` and whose boundary does; equivalently, by
`SSet.Subcomplex.isPushout_boundary_ι`, each `W i ⊆ W (i + 1)` is the attachment of a cell along
`∂Δ[n] ⟶ Δ[n]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_monotone_sup_ofSimplex_eq_top {V : SSet.{u}} (U : V.Subcomplex)
    [Finite U.N] :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (W : ℕ → V.Subcomplex), Monotone W ∧ W 0 = U ∧ W r = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i < r, ∃ (n : ℕ) (x : V _⦋n⦌), x ∉ (W i).obj (op ⦋n⦌) ∧
        range (∂Δ[n].ι ≫ yonedaEquiv.symm x) ≤ W i ∧
        W (i + 1) = W i ⊔ ofSimplex x

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.NormalizedMooreComplex.objX_sk_obj_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018T**.
Let `A` be an abelian category and let `U` be an `m`-truncated simplicial object of `A`. For
`n > m` the degree `n` normalized Moore subobject of the simplicial object `i_{m!}U` obtained
from `U` by the left adjoint `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.sk m` of truncation is
the zero subobject: `N(i_{m!}U)ₙ = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem objX_sk_obj_eq_bot {m : ℕ}
    [∀ F : (SimplexCategory.Truncated m)ᵒᵖ ⥤ A,
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion m).op.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension F]
    (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated A m) {n : ℕ} (hmn : m < n) :
    objX ((SimplicialObject.Truncated.sk m).obj U) n = ⊥

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.isLeast_subobject_mk_skAdj_counit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018U**.
Let `U` be a simplicial object of an abelian category `A` and let `n : ℕ`.
The canonical morphism `i_{n!} sk_n U ⟶ U` — the counit of `i_{n!} ⊣ sk_n` — is in each degree
`m` a monomorphism, and the subobject of `U_m` it defines is the least subobject through which
every operator `U(φ) : U_i ⟶ U_m` with `φ : ⦋m⦌ → ⦋i⦌` and `i ≤ n` factors, that is, the sum
`U'_m = Σ_{φ : ⦋m⦌ → ⦋i⦌, i ≤ n} Im(U(φ))`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.nonempty_representableBy_hom_sk_stdSimplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018V**.
Let `V` be a simplicial object of a category `C` and let `n m : ℕ`, and assume the `n`-th
coskeleton of `C` exists pointwise, as it does when `C` has finite limits. Then the object of
`m`-simplices of `cosk_n sk_n V` represents the presheaf
`X ↦ Mor_{Simp(C)}(X × i_{n!} sk_n Δ[m], V)` on `C`, equally
`X ↦ Mor_{SSet}(i_{n!} sk_n Δ[m], V ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op X))`; that is,
`(cosk_n sk_n V)_m = Hom(i_{n!} sk_n Δ[m], V)₀`. For `m = n + 1` the simplicial
set `i_{n!} sk_n Δ[n + 1]` is the boundary `∂Δ[n + 1]`, and a morphism
`X ⟶ (cosk_n sk_n V)_{n + 1}` is a matching family of `(n + 1)`-simplices of `V` with values in
`X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_representableBy_hom_sk_stdSimplex {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (n : ℕ)
    [∀ F : (SimplexCategory.Truncated n)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C,
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion n).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    (V : SimplicialObject C) (m : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((coyoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ C (Type v)).obj V ⋙
      coyoneda.obj (op ((sk n).obj Δ[m]))).RepresentableBy (((cosk n).obj V) _⦋m⦌))
declarations.comment: stated in an arbitrary degree `m`, the source's display being the case `m = n + 1`, and as representability of the presheaf that the source's `Hom(-, V)₀` represents, so that neither finite coproducts nor Tag 017L is needed

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.exact_iff_exact_map_evaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 018Z**.
A short complex `S` of functors `J ⥤ A`, with `A` an abelian category, is exact if and only if
evaluating it at each object `j` of `J` gives an exact short complex of `A`. For
`J = SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ` (resp. `J = SimplexCategory`) this says that a sequence of (co)simplicial
objects of `A` is exact if and only if it is exact in each degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_iff_exact_map_evaluation (S : ShortComplex (J ⥤ A)) :
    S.Exact ↔ ∀ j : J, (S.map ((evaluation J A).obj j)).Exact

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.app_top_injective_and_exists_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0190** (part 1).
Let `U` be a `k`-truncated simplicial object of `C` with `U_i = 0` for `i < k`, and write
`A = U_k`. Then for every `k`-truncated simplicial object `V`:

* a morphism `U ⟶ V` is determined by its top component `A ⟶ V_k`, and a morphism `f : A ⟶ V_k`
  is the top component of one if and only if `f ≫ V(φ) = 0` for every non-surjective
  `φ : ⦋m⦌ ⟶ ⦋k⦌`, i.e. if and only if `d^k_i ∘ f = 0` for `i = 0, …, k`;
* a morphism `V ⟶ U` is determined by its top component `V_k ⟶ A`, and a morphism `f : V_k ⟶ A`
  is the top component of one if and only if `V(ψ) ≫ f = 0` for every non-injective
  `ψ : ⦋k⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌`, i.e. if and only if `f ∘ s^{k-1}_i = 0` for `i = 0, …, k - 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem app_top_injective_and_exists_iff {k : ℕ} {U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C k}
    (hU : ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : m < k), IsZero (U _⦋m,hm.le⦌ₖ)) (V : SimplicialObject.Truncated C k) :
    (Function.Injective (fun g : U ⟶ V => g.app (op ⦋k⦌ₖ)) ∧
      ∀ f : U _⦋k⦌ₖ ⟶ V _⦋k⦌ₖ, (∃ g : U ⟶ V, g.app (op ⦋k⦌ₖ) = f) ↔
        ∀ (m : SimplexCategory.Truncated k) (φ : m ⟶ ⦋k⦌ₖ),
          ¬ Function.Surjective φ.hom.toOrderHom → f ≫ V.map φ.op = 0) ∧
    (Function.Injective (fun g : V ⟶ U => g.app (op ⦋k⦌ₖ)) ∧
      ∀ f : V _⦋k⦌ₖ ⟶ U _⦋k⦌ₖ, (∃ g : V ⟶ U, g.app (op ⦋k⦌ₖ) = f) ↔
        ∀ (m : SimplexCategory.Truncated k) (ψ : ⦋k⦌ₖ ⟶ m),
          ¬ Function.Injective ψ.hom.toOrderHom → V.map ψ.op ≫ f = 0)
declarations.comment: part (1): both hom-sets, with the vanishing conditions stated over all non-surjective (resp. non-injective) operators instead of the faces (resp. degeneracies)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.eilenbergMacLane
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0191**.
For an object `A` of `C` and an integer `k ≥ 0`, the *Eilenberg-MacLane object* `K(A, k)` is
`K(A, k) = i_{k!}U`, the left Kan extension along the inclusion of the `k`-truncated simplex
category (equivalently, the image under the left adjoint of `k`-truncation) of the `k`-truncated
simplicial object `U` of [Stacks, Tag 0190] with `U_i = 0` for `i < k`, `U_k = A` and all
operators `U(φ)` zero except `U(id_⦋k⦌) = id_A`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def eilenbergMacLane (A : C) (k : ℕ)
    [∀ F : (SimplexCategory.Truncated k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ C,
      (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion k).op.HasLeftKanExtension F] :
    SimplicialObject C

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.EilenbergMacLane.emSplit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0192**.
The sequence `0 → K(A,k) → E → K(A,k+1) → 0` is term by term split exact: for each degree `n`
the short complex obtained by evaluating it at `[n]` admits a splitting in `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem emSplit (A : 𝒜) (k : ℕ) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) :
    Nonempty
      (((emShortComplex A k).map ((CategoryTheory.evaluation _ _).obj n)).Splitting)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.EilenbergMacLane.emShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0192**.
The sequence `0 → K(A,k) → E → K(A,k+1) → 0` is a short exact sequence of simplicial objects
of `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
theorem emShortComplex_shortExact (A : 𝒜) (k : ℕ) :
    (emShortComplex A k).ShortExact

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.exists_mono_isColimit_sk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0193**.
Let `V` be a simplicial object of an abelian category `A`. Then there are monomorphisms
`f n : i_{n!} sk_n V ⟶ i_{(n + 1)!} sk_{n + 1} V` between consecutive skeleta of `V` such that `V`,
equipped with the canonical morphisms `i_{n!} sk_n V ⟶ V` (the counits of `i_{n!} ⊣ sk_n`), is the
colimit of the resulting sequence: `V = colim_n i_{n!} sk_n V`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mono_isColimit_sk (V : SimplicialObject A) :
    ∃ (f : (n : ℕ) → (sk n).obj V ⟶ (sk (n + 1)).obj V)
      (ι : Functor.ofSequence (X := fun n ↦ (sk n).obj V) f ⟶ (Functor.const ℕ).obj V),
      (∀ n, Mono (f n)) ∧ (∀ n, ι.app n = (skAdj n).counit.app V) ∧
        Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk V ι))

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComplex_preservesHomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0195**.
The Moore complex functor `s : Simp(C) ⥤ Ch_{≥0}(C)`, sending a simplicial object `U` of a
preadditive category `C` to the chain complex `U₀ ← U₁ ← U₂ ← …` with differentials the alternating
sums of the face maps, is exact: it preserves kernels and cokernels.
declarations.statement:
public instance alternatingFaceMapComplex_preservesHomology :
    (alternatingFaceMapComplex C).PreservesHomology

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.acyclic_alternatingFaceMapComplex_Γ₀_double
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0196**.
The Moore complex of the simplicial object `E` of [Stacks, Tag 0192], the termwise split extension
of `K(A, k + 1)` by `K(A, k)`, that is `Γ₀` of the two-term complex `A --𝟙--> A` in degrees `k + 1`
and `k`, is acyclic.

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.homology_alternatingFaceMapComplex_Γ₀_single
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0197**.
The Moore complex of the Eilenberg-MacLane object `K(A, k)` of an object `A` of an additive
category with homology has homology `A` in degree `k` and zero homology in every other degree. Here
`K(A, k)` is `Γ₀.obj L` for `L` the chain complex `A` concentrated in degree `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homology_alternatingFaceMapComplex_Γ₀_single (A : C) (k : ℕ) :
    IsIsomorphic
        (K[Γ₀.obj ((HomologicalComplex.single C (ComplexShape.down ℕ) k).obj A)].homology k) A ∧
      ∀ i ≠ k, IsZero
        (K[Γ₀.obj ((HomologicalComplex.single C (ComplexShape.down ℕ) k).obj A)].homology i)

registrations.name: AlgebraicTopology.inclusionOfMooreComplexMap
registrations.comment: the morphism of complexes N(U) -> s(U)

registrations.name: AlgebraicTopology.inclusionOfMooreComplexMap_f
registrations.comment: its components are the inclusions N(U_n) -> U_n

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.isIsomorphic_normalizedMooreComplex_eilenbergMacLane_single
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0199**.
The normalized complex `N(K(A, k))` of the Eilenberg-MacLane object `K(A, k) = i_{k!}U` of an
object `A` of an abelian category is isomorphic to the chain complex `A` concentrated in degree
`k`; in particular `N(K(A, k))ᵢ` is `A` for `i = k` and `0` otherwise.

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.exists_degenerateComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019A**.
Let `A` be an abelian category. The canonical morphism of chain complexes `N(U) ⟶ s(U)` from the
normalized complex of a simplicial object `U` of `A` to its Moore complex is split, functorially in
`U`: there are a functor `D` from simplicial objects of `A` to chain complexes, the degenerate
part, and a natural isomorphism `N ⊞ D ≅ s` which on the first summand is the canonical inclusion.
In other words `s(U) = N(U) ⊕ D(U)`, naturally in `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_degenerateComplex :
    ∃ (D : SimplicialObject A ⥤ ChainComplex A ℕ)
      (e : normalizedMooreComplex A ⊞ D ≅ alternatingFaceMapComplex A),
      biprod.inl ≫ e.hom = inclusionOfMooreComplex A

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.exactFunctor_normalizedMooreComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019B**.
The normalized complex functor `N : Simp(C) ⥤ Ch_{≥0}(C)` of an abelian category `C` is exact, i.e.
it preserves finite limits and finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exactFunctor_normalizedMooreComplex :
    exactFunctor (SimplicialObject C) (ChainComplex C ℕ) (normalizedMooreComplex C)

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.quasiIso_inclusionOfMooreComplexMap_and_acyclic_degenerateComplex
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian category and let `V` be a simplicial object of `A`. The canonical
morphism of chain complexes `N(V) ⟶ s(V)` is a quasi-isomorphism, and for every functorial
splitting `e : N ⊞ D ≅ s` which on the first summand is the canonical inclusion, the complex `D(V)`
is acyclic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiIso_inclusionOfMooreComplexMap_and_acyclic_degenerateComplex
    (V : SimplicialObject A) :
    QuasiIso (inclusionOfMooreComplexMap V) ∧
      ∀ (D : SimplicialObject A ⥤ ChainComplex A ℕ)
        (e : normalizedMooreComplex A ⊞ D ≅ alternatingFaceMapComplex A),
        biprod.inl ≫ e.hom = inclusionOfMooreComplex A → (D.obj V).Acyclic

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.normalizedMooreComplex_faithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019E**.
The normalized complex functor `N : Simp(A) ⥤ Ch_{≥0}(A)` of an abelian category `A`, sending a
simplicial object `U` to the complex of normalized chains `N(U)_m = ⋂_i Ker(d^m_i)`, is faithful.
Consequently it reflects monomorphisms, epimorphisms and isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public instance normalizedMooreComplex_faithful :
    (normalizedMooreComplex A).Faithful

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.exists_of_faithful_of_essSurj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019F**.
For abelian categories `A` and `B` and exact functors `N : A ⥤ B`, `S : B ⥤ A` with a natural
isomorphism `g : S ⋙ N ≅ 𝟭 B`, `N` faithful and `S` essentially surjective, `N` and `S` are
quasi-inverse equivalences of categories: there is an equivalence `A ≌ B` whose functor is `N` and
whose inverse functor is `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Equivalence.exists_of_faithful_of_essSurj
    {A B : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B]
    (N : A ⥤ B) (S : B ⥤ A)
    (g : S ⋙ N ≅ 𝟭 B)
    (hN_faithful : N.Faithful)
    (hS_essSurj : S.EssSurj) :
    ∃ e : A ≌ B, e.functor = N ∧ e.inverse = S

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Abelian.DoldKan.equivalence
registrations.comment: the equivalence Simp(A) ≌ Ch_{≥0}(A)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Abelian.DoldKan.equivalence_functor
registrations.comment: the functor of the equivalence is N

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.exists_normalizedCochainComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019I**.
Let `A` be an abelian category. (1) The Moore cochain complex functor
`s : CoSimp(A) ⥤ CoCh_{≥0}(A)` is exact. (2) There is a functor `Q`, the normalized cochain
complex, together with a natural transformation `π : s ⟶ Q` which is an isomorphism in degree `0`
and, in degree `n + 1`, a cokernel of the cofaces `δ i : Uₙ ⟶ Uₙ₊₁`, `i ≤ n`. (3) `π` is a split
epimorphism in the functor category, which is the functorial direct sum decomposition
`s(U) = D(U) ⊕ Q(U)` with `D = ker π`. (4) `Q` is exact. (5) Each `π.app U` is a quasi-isomorphism.
(6) `Q` is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_normalizedCochainComplex :
    (PreservesFiniteLimits (alternatingCofaceMapComplex A) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (alternatingCofaceMapComplex A)) ∧
    ∃ (Q : CosimplicialObject A ⥤ CochainComplex A ℕ)
      (π : alternatingCofaceMapComplex A ⟶ Q),
      (∀ U : CosimplicialObject A, IsIso ((π.app U).f 0)) ∧
      (∀ (U : CosimplicialObject A) (n : ℕ),
        ∃ e : cokernel (Sigma.desc (f := fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => U.obj ⦋n⦌)
            fun i => U.δ i.castSucc) ≅ (Q.obj U).X (n + 1),
          cokernel.π _ ≫ e.hom = (π.app U).f (n + 1)) ∧
      IsSplitEpi π ∧
      (PreservesFiniteLimits Q ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits Q) ∧
      (∀ U : CosimplicialObject A, QuasiIso (π.app U)) ∧
      Q.IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.IsHomotopy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019K** (part 1).
Given simplicial objects `U`, `V` of a category `C` for which the product
`U × Δ[1] = U.copower Δ[1]` of [Stacks, Tag 017C] exists, a morphism `h : U × Δ[1] ⟶ V` is a
*homotopy from `a` to `b`* for `a, b : U ⟶ V` when `a = e₀ ≫ h` and `b = e₁ ≫ h`, where
`e₀, e₁ : U ⟶ U × Δ[1]` come from the two vertices `Δ[0] ⟶ Δ[1]` and the identification
`U × Δ[0] = U`. In degree `m` these two vertex inclusions are the inclusions of the summands of
`∐_{α ∈ Δ[1]_m} U_m` indexed by the constant `m`-simplices `SSet.stdSimplex.const 1 0 m` and
`SSet.stdSimplex.const 1 1 m` of `Δ[1]`, which is how the two conditions are spelled here;
equivalently, `h_{m, m + 1} = a_m` and `h_{m, 0} = b_m` in the notation of [Stacks, Tag 019L].
declarations.statement: public def IsHomotopy (h : U.copower Δ[1] ⟶ V) (a b : U ⟶ V) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1); part (2), being homotopic, is the equivalence relation `Relation.EqvGen (fun a b ↦ ∃ h, IsHomotopy h a b)` generated by it, see the module docstring

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.htpy_forward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019L**.
The components `h_{n, i}` of a homotopy `h : U × Δ[1] ⟶ V` from `a` to `b` satisfy the relations
`HtpyRel a b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem htpy_forward {U V : SimplicialObject C}
    [∀ m, HasCoproduct fun _ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m => U.obj m] (a b : U ⟶ V)
    (h : U.copower Δ[1] ⟶ V) (hh : IsHomotopy h a b) :
    HtpyRel a b (homotopyComponent h)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.htpy_converse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019L**.
Given a family of morphisms `hc n i : U_n ⟶ V_n` satisfying the relations `HtpyRel a b`, there is a
unique morphism of simplicial objects `h : U × Δ[1] ⟶ V` whose components are the given `hc`, and
it is a homotopy from `a` to `b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem htpy_converse {U V : SimplicialObject C}
    [∀ m, HasCoproduct fun _ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m => U.obj m] (a b : U ⟶ V)
    (hc : ∀ (n : ℕ), Fin (n + 2) →
      (U.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk n)) ⟶ V.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk n))))
    (hrel : HtpyRel a b hc) :
    ∃! h : U.copower Δ[1] ⟶ V,
      IsHomotopy h a b ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n+2)), homotopyComponent h n i = hc n i)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.IsHomotopy.exists_whiskerRight
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019M**.
Functors preserve homotopies of simplicial objects. Let `F : C ⥤ D` be any functor between any two
categories, let `U`, `V` be simplicial objects of `C`, and let `a, b : U ⟶ V`. If
`k : U × Δ[1] ⟶ V` is a homotopy from `a` to `b` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 019K], then there is
a homotopy `l : F(U) × Δ[1] ⟶ F(V)` from `F(a)` to `F(b)` whose component at each simplex
`α ∈ Δ[1]_m` is `F` applied to the component of `k` at `α`; in the notation of [Stacks, Tag 019L],
`l` is the family `{F(h_{m, i})}`. No compatibility of `F` with the coproducts making up the two
products with `Δ[1]` is required.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsHomotopy.exists_whiskerRight {U V : SimplicialObject C}
    [∀ m, HasCoproduct fun _ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m => U.obj m] (F : C ⥤ D)
    [∀ m, HasCoproduct fun _ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m => (U ⋙ F).obj m]
    {a b : U ⟶ V} {k : U.copower Δ[1] ⟶ V} (hk : IsHomotopy k a b) :
    ∃ l : (U ⋙ F).copower Δ[1] ⟶ V ⋙ F,
      (∀ (m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m),
          Sigma.ι (fun _ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m => (U ⋙ F).obj m) α ≫ l.app m =
            F.map (Sigma.ι (fun _ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m => U.obj m) α ≫ k.app m)) ∧
        IsHomotopy l (Functor.whiskerRight a F) (Functor.whiskerRight b F)
declarations.comment: the remark's concluding deduction: a functor preserves the notion of homotopy of 019K whenever the two products with `Δ[1]` exist, with the transported homotopy pinned to the family `{F(h_{n, i})}` rather than merely asserted to exist. The remark's other content is already in Mathlib or is a composite of existing declarations, see the module docstring: the notion of homotopy for an arbitrary category is `SimplicialObject.Homotopy`, its preservation by a functor is `SimplicialObject.Homotopy.whiskerRight`, and being homotopic is `Relation.EqvGen fun a b => ∃ h, IsHomotopy h a b` as in 019K

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019N** (the first sentence).
Let `C` be any category. A morphism `a : U ⟶ V` of simplicial objects of `C` is a *homotopy
equivalence* if there is a morphism `b : V ⟶ U` such that `a ≫ b` is homotopic to `𝟙 U` and
`b ≫ a` is homotopic to `𝟙 V`, where two morphisms are *homotopic* when they are related by the
equivalence relation generated by the existence of a simplicial homotopy ([Stacks, Tag 019M]). The
simplicial objects `U` and `V` are *homotopy equivalent* when some `a : U ⟶ V` is a homotopy
equivalence, that is, when `∃ a : U ⟶ V, homotopyEquivalences C a`.
declarations.statement: public def homotopyEquivalences : MorphismProperty (SimplicialObject C)
declarations.comment: the first sentence; being homotopy equivalent, the second sentence, is the composite `∃ a : U ⟶ V, homotopyEquivalences C a` and gets no name, as in Mathlib for complexes, where it is `Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv K L)`. Stated as a `MorphismProperty`, the shape of the sibling `HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences`; being homotopic is `Relation.EqvGen fun f g => Nonempty (Homotopy f g)` as in 019S

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalence_proj_cylinder
declarations.doc:
The projection from the cylinder `U × Δ[1]` is a homotopy equivalence, with either vertex
inclusion as a homotopy inverse. Let `U` be a simplicial object of a category `C`, and let `X`
be a cylinder on `U`: a simplicial object together with morphisms `ι m α : U_m ⟶ X_m`, one for
each `m`-simplex `α` of `Δ[1]`, which exhibit `X_m` as the coproduct `∐_{α ∈ Δ[1]_m} U_m` and
satisfy `ι m α ≫ X(φ) = U(φ) ≫ ι m' (Δ[1](φ) α)`; this is the product `U × Δ[1]` of
[Stacks, Tag 017C]. Let `π : X ⟶ U` be the projection, the identity on each summand, and let
`e₀, e₁ : U ⟶ X` be the two vertex inclusions, in degree `m` the inclusions of the summands
indexed by the constant `m`-simplices `SSet.stdSimplex.const 1 0 m` and
`SSet.stdSimplex.const 1 1 m` of `Δ[1]`. Then `π ∘ e₀ = π ∘ e₁ = id_U`, the composite `e₀ ∘ π`
admits a homotopy to `id_X`, and `id_X` admits a homotopy to `e₁ ∘ π`. In particular `π` is a
homotopy equivalence ([Stacks, Tag 019N]), so `U × Δ[1]` is homotopy equivalent to `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyEquivalence_proj_cylinder
    (ι : ∀ m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m → (U.obj m ⟶ X.obj m))
    (hX : ∀ m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ,
      IsColimit (Cofan.mk (f := fun _ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m => U.obj m) (X.obj m) (ι m)))
    (hι : ∀ {m m' : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ} (φ : m ⟶ m') (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m),
      ι m α ≫ X.map φ = U.map φ ≫ ι m' ((Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).map φ α))
    (π : X ⟶ U) (e₀ e₁ : U ⟶ X)
    (hπ : ∀ (m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{w}).obj m),
      ι m α ≫ π.app m = 𝟙 (U.obj m))
    (he₀ : ∀ m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, e₀.app m = ι m (stdSimplex.const 1 0 m))
    (he₁ : ∀ m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, e₁.app m = ι m (stdSimplex.const 1 1 m)) :
    (e₀ ≫ π = 𝟙 U ∧ e₁ ≫ π = 𝟙 U) ∧
      Nonempty (Homotopy (π ≫ e₀) (𝟙 X)) ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy (𝟙 X) (π ≫ e₁))
declarations.comment: the cylinder is any object with the universal property of `U × Δ[1]`, in place of a chosen construction, so that the source's finite coproducts on `C` are weakened to the coproducts making it up; the maps of [Stacks, Tag 017E] are pinned by their characterizing equations instead of being reconstructed; and the two homotopies are directed, as the source's proof produces them, which is stronger than the source's symmetric `are homotopic`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Arrow.nonempty_homotopy_mapCechNerve_id
declarations.doc:
A self map of a Čech nerve which is the identity on the base is homotopic to the identity. Let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be an arrow of a category `C` whose iterated fibre products `Y ×_X ⋯ ×_X Y` exist, let
`U = f.cechNerve` be the simplicial object of [Stacks, Tag 016E] built from `f`, and let `F` be an
endomorphism of the arrow `f` with `f ≫ F.right = f`, so that the induced self map
`Arrow.mapCechNerve F` of `U`, given by `F.left` on each factor `Y`, is the identity on the base
`X`. Then there is a simplicial homotopy from that self map to `𝟙 U` in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 019M]; in particular the two are homotopic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_homotopy_mapCechNerve_id {f : Arrow C}
    [∀ n : ℕ, HasWidePullback f.right (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f.left) fun _ => f.hom]
    (F : f ⟶ f) (hF : f.hom ≫ F.right = f.hom) :
    Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy (mapCechNerve F) (𝟙 f.cechNerve))
declarations.comment: the first sentence, stated for an arbitrary endomorphism `F` of the arrow `f` with `f.hom ≫ F.right = f.hom`, of which the source's self map is the case `F = (f.hom ≫ s, 𝟙 X)` for a section `s` of `f`; the self map is pinned as `Arrow.mapCechNerve F`, and the conclusion is the existence of a homotopy, which is stronger than the source's `homotopic` of 019M. The second sentence, that `U` is homotopy equivalent to the constant simplicial object `X`, uses the section and is a formal consequence, to be tagged jointly on a second declaration; see the module docstring

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Homotopy.ToChainHomotopy.hom_eq
registrations.comment: the components of the chain homotopy `s(h) = toChainHomotopy` induced by a simplicial homotopy `h`, with the sign `(-1)^{i+1}` pulled out of the sum and `h.h i` denoting the composite `h_{n+1,i+1} ∘ sⁿᵢ`

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.homotopic_normalizedMooreComplex_map
declarations.doc:
**Homotopic morphisms have chain homotopic normalized Moore complexes.** If
`a, b : U ⟶ V` are homotopic morphisms of simplicial objects of an abelian category `A` —
related by a chain of morphisms consecutive members of which admit a simplicial homotopy in
one direction or the other — then the induced maps `N(a), N(b) : N(U) ⟶ N(V)` of normalized
Moore complexes are chain homotopic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopic_normalizedMooreComplex_map
    (h : Relation.EqvGen (fun a b : U ⟶ V => Nonempty (Homotopy a b)) a b) :
    homotopic A (ComplexShape.down ℕ)
      ((normalizedMooreComplex A).map a) ((normalizedMooreComplex A).map b)
declarations.comment: the half about the Moore complex `s` is Mathlib's, so it gets no public name here: a homotopy gives `SimplicialObject.Homotopy.toChainHomotopy`, and `homotopy_congruence` propagates it along the source's chain; stated here is the half about `N`. `homotopic` is Mathlib's chain homotopy relation, and being homotopic is spelled `Relation.EqvGen fun a b => Nonempty (Homotopy a b)` as in 019W

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.homotopyEquivalences_alternatingFaceMapComplex_map
declarations.doc:
**The Moore complex of a homotopy equivalence of simplicial objects is a homotopy
equivalence of chain complexes.** Let `a : U ⟶ V` be a homotopy equivalence of simplicial
objects of a preadditive category `A`: there is `b : V ⟶ U` with `a ≫ b` homotopic to `𝟙 U`
and `b ≫ a` homotopic to `𝟙 V`, homotopic meaning related by the equivalence relation
generated by the existence of a simplicial homotopy ([Stacks, Tag 019N]). Then
`s(a) : s(U) ⟶ s(V)` is a homotopy equivalence of chain complexes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyEquivalences_alternatingFaceMapComplex_map [Preadditive A]
    (ha : SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences A a) :
    HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences A (ComplexShape.down ℕ)
      ((alternatingFaceMapComplex A).map a)
declarations.comment: the first sentence, for the Moore complex `s`, with the source's `additive` weakened to `Preadditive`, Mathlib's hypothesis for `alternatingFaceMapComplex`; the second sentence is `homotopyEquivalences_normalizedMooreComplex_map` below. Being a homotopy equivalence of chain complexes is `HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences`, which pins the map, and the hypothesis is 019N's `SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences`

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.homotopyEquivalences_normalizedMooreComplex_map
declarations.doc:
**The normalized Moore complex of a homotopy equivalence of simplicial objects is a
homotopy equivalence of chain complexes.** Let `a : U ⟶ V` be a homotopy equivalence of
simplicial objects of an abelian category `A` ([Stacks, Tag 019N]). Then
`N(a) : N(U) ⟶ N(V)` is a homotopy equivalence of chain complexes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyEquivalences_normalizedMooreComplex_map [Abelian A]
    (ha : SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences A a) :
    HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences A (ComplexShape.down ℕ)
      ((normalizedMooreComplex A).map a)
declarations.comment: the second sentence, for the normalized Moore complex `N`; the first is `homotopyEquivalences_alternatingFaceMapComplex_map` above, from which this one is deduced by conjugating with the natural homotopy equivalence `inclusionOfMooreComplexMap`. Only `Abelian A` is assumed, which provides the preadditivity the source's `additive` asks for. Being a homotopy equivalence of chain complexes is `HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences`, which pins the map, and the hypothesis is 019N's `SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject.power
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019V.** `Hom(U, V)`, the cosimplicial object of maps from a simplicial set `U` into a
cosimplicial object `V` of `C`. Its degree `n` part is the power `Hom(U, V)_n = ∏_{u ∈ U_n} V_n`,
the object of `C` whose `X`-valued points are the maps `U_n → Mor_C(X, V_n)`, and for
`φ : [m] ⟶ [n]` in `Δ` the structure map `Hom(U, V)_m ⟶ Hom(U, V)_n` is the morphism whose `u`-th
component, for `u ∈ U_n`, is the projection to the `U(φ)(u)`-th factor followed by `V(φ)`; on
`X`-valued points it is `f ↦ V(φ) ∘ f ∘ U(φ)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def power (V : CosimplicialObject C) (U : SSet.{w})
    [∀ n : SimplexCategory, HasProduct fun _ : U.obj (op n) => V.obj n] :
    CosimplicialObject C
declarations.comment: the finiteness and nonemptiness of the `U_n` are replaced by the existence of the products they index, which is all they are used for

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject.Homotopy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019W**.
A *homotopy from `a` to `b`*, for `a b : U ⟶ V` two morphisms of cosimplicial objects of `C`: a
morphism `h : U ⟶ Hom(Δ[1], V)` into the cosimplicial object `Hom(Δ[1], V) = V.power Δ[1]` of
[Stacks, Tag 019V] such that `a = e₀ ∘ h` and `b = e₁ ∘ h`, where `e₀, e₁ : Hom(Δ[1], V) ⟶ V` are
induced by the two vertices of `Δ[1]`. The two conditions are recorded in each degree `n`, where
`e₀` and `e₁` are the projections of `Hom(Δ[1], V)_n = ∏_{α ∈ Δ[1]_n} V_n` onto the factors indexed
by the constant maps `[n] → [1]` with value `0`, resp. `1`; so the components
`h_{n, α} : U_n ⟶ V_n` of `h` satisfy `a_n = h_{n, 0}` and `b_n = h_{n, 1}`, and the naturality of
`h` is the compatibility of the `h_{n, α}` with the structure maps.
declarations.statement: public structure Homotopy (a b : U ⟶ V) : Type v
declarations.comment: the finite products of the source are replaced by the products that name `Hom(Δ[1], V)`; the two conditions `a = e₀ ∘ h`, `b = e₁ ∘ h` are recorded degreewise, `e₀` and `e₁` being pinned there to the two projections; part (2), homotopic, is `Relation.EqvGen fun a b => Nonempty (Homotopy a b)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject.exists_homotopy_iff_nonempty_homotopy_op
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019X**.
A homotopy of morphisms of cosimplicial objects is a simplicial homotopy in the opposite category.
Let `C` be a category with no assumptions whatsoever, let `U`, `V` be cosimplicial objects of `C`
and let `a, b : U ⟶ V`, so that `U`, `V` correspond to simplicial objects `U.op`, `V.op` of `Cᵒᵖ`
and `a`, `b` to morphisms `aᵒᵖ, bᵒᵖ : V.op ⟶ U.op`. Then there exists a homotopy `{h_{n, α}}` from
`a` to `b` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0FKJ] — a family of morphisms `h_{n, α} : U_n ⟶ V_n`,
indexed by the simplices `α ∈ Δ[1]_n`, satisfying `h_{m, α} ∘ U(f) = V(f) ∘ h_{n, α ∘ f}` for every
morphism `f : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌` of `Δ` and having `a_n`, `b_n` as its components at the two constant maps
`⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋1⦌` — if and only if there exists a homotopy `{h_{n, i}}` from `aᵒᵖ` to `bᵒᵖ` in the sense
of [Stacks, Tag 019M]. Hence `a` and `b` are homotopic if and only if `aᵒᵖ` and `bᵒᵖ` are, the two
relations being the equivalence relations generated by these two existence statements.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopy_iff_nonempty_homotopy_op {U V : CosimplicialObject C}
    (a b : U ⟶ V) :
    (∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → (U.obj n ⟶ V.obj n),
        (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (f : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
            U.map f ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map f.op α) ≫ V.map f) ∧
          (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = a.app n) ∧
          (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = b.app n)) ↔
      Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy (NatTrans.op a) (NatTrans.op b))
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (2); the primed objects are spelled `U.op` and `NatTrans.op a` rather than through `cosimplicialSimplicialEquiv`, a homotopy as in 0FKJ by its family of components as in 07KB, and a homotopy as in 019M by Mathlib's `SimplicialObject.Homotopy`, so that neither side needs (co)products and the statement holds over an arbitrary category. The final assertion, homotopic if and only if homotopic, is the equivalence of the `Relation.EqvGen` of the two sides and is formal from this one, by transport along the bijection `NatTrans.op : (U ⟶ V) ≃ (V.op ⟶ U.op)`; it is what 019Y (2) and (4) apply

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.homotopic_whiskerRight
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019Y**.
Functors preserve homotopic morphisms of (co)simplicial objects. Let `C`, `C'`, `D`, `D'` be
categories, with no assumptions whatsoever. (1) If `a, b : U ⟶ V` are homotopic morphisms of
simplicial objects of `D` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 019M] and `F : D ⥤ D'` is a functor, then
`F(a)`, `F(b)` are homotopic morphisms `F(U) ⟶ F(V)` of simplicial objects of `D'`. (2) If
`a, b : U ⟶ V` are homotopic morphisms of cosimplicial objects of `C` in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 0FKJ] — a family `h_{n, α} : Uₙ ⟶ Vₙ`, indexed by the simplices `α ∈ Δ[1]_n`,
satisfying `h_{m, α} ∘ U(f) = V(f) ∘ h_{n, α ∘ f}` and having `aₙ`, `bₙ` as its components at the
two constant maps `⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋1⦌`, and chains of such — and `F : C ⥤ C'` is a functor, then `F(a)`,
`F(b)` are homotopic morphisms `F(U) ⟶ F(V)` of cosimplicial objects of `C'`. (3) For a
contravariant functor, i.e. a functor `F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ C`, homotopic morphisms `a, b : U ⟶ V` of
simplicial objects of `D` have homotopic images `F(a)`, `F(b) : F(V) ⟶ F(U)`, morphisms of
cosimplicial objects of `C`. (4) Likewise a functor `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D` takes homotopic morphisms
`a, b : U ⟶ V` of cosimplicial objects of `C` to homotopic morphisms `F(a)`, `F(b) : F(V) ⟶ F(U)`
of simplicial objects of `D`. No (co)limit in any of the four categories is assumed to exist, and
the functor is not asked to preserve anything.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopic_whiskerRight :
    (∀ {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} D] {D' : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D']
        {U V : SimplicialObject D} {a b : U ⟶ V} (F : D ⥤ D'),
        Relation.EqvGen (fun x y : U ⟶ V => Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy x y)) a b →
          Relation.EqvGen
            (fun x y : U ⋙ F ⟶ V ⋙ F => Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy x y))
            (Functor.whiskerRight a F) (Functor.whiskerRight b F)) ∧
      (∀ {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {C' : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} C']
          {U V : CosimplicialObject C} {a b : U ⟶ V} (F : C ⥤ C'),
          Relation.EqvGen (fun x y : U ⟶ V => ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory,
              (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → (U.obj n ⟶ V.obj n),
              (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (f : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
                  U.map f ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map f.op α) ≫ V.map f) ∧
                (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = x.app n) ∧
                (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = y.app n)) a b →
            Relation.EqvGen (fun x y : U ⋙ F ⟶ V ⋙ F => ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory,
                (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → ((U ⋙ F).obj n ⟶ (V ⋙ F).obj n),
                (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (f : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
                    (U ⋙ F).map f ≫ h m α =
                      h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map f.op α) ≫ (V ⋙ F).map f) ∧
                  (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = x.app n) ∧
                  (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = y.app n))
              (Functor.whiskerRight a F) (Functor.whiskerRight b F)) ∧
        (∀ {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} D] {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} C]
            {U V : SimplicialObject D} {a b : U ⟶ V} (F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ C),
            Relation.EqvGen (fun x y : U ⟶ V => Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy x y)) a b →
              Relation.EqvGen (fun x y : V.rightOp ⋙ F ⟶ U.rightOp ⋙ F =>
                  ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) →
                    ((V.rightOp ⋙ F).obj n ⟶ (U.rightOp ⋙ F).obj n),
                  (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (f : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
                      (V.rightOp ⋙ F).map f ≫ h m α =
                        h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map f.op α) ≫ (U.rightOp ⋙ F).map f) ∧
                    (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = x.app n) ∧
                    (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = y.app n))
                (Functor.whiskerRight (NatTrans.rightOp a) F)
                (Functor.whiskerRight (NatTrans.rightOp b) F)) ∧
          (∀ {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D]
              {U V : CosimplicialObject C} {a b : U ⟶ V} (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D),
              Relation.EqvGen (fun x y : U ⟶ V => ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory,
                  (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) → (U.obj n ⟶ V.obj n),
                  (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (f : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
                      U.map f ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map f.op α) ≫ V.map f) ∧
                    (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = x.app n) ∧
                    (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = y.app n)) a b →
                Relation.EqvGen (fun x y : V.op ⋙ F ⟶ U.op ⋙ F =>
                    Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy x y))
                  (Functor.whiskerRight (NatTrans.op a) F)
                  (Functor.whiskerRight (NatTrans.op b) F))
declarations.comment: all four parts, at the chain level: `homotopic` is `Relation.EqvGen` of the existence of a homotopy, as in 019K, 019W and 0FKJ. Homotopy of simplicial objects over an arbitrary category is `SimplicialObject.Homotopy` (Mathlib), the notion of 019M through the composites of the source's footnote; homotopy of cosimplicial objects is the family of 0FKJ, repeated verbatim. The source's four categories occur as they do there, each part binding the two it names, so that each part applies on its own; the four are one conjunction because they are one assertion read in four dualities. The passage between variances is `Functor.rightOp`/`Functor.op` and `NatTrans.rightOp`/`NatTrans.op`, the anti-equivalences `simplicialCosimplicialEquiv` and `cosimplicialSimplicialEquiv`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Arrow.exists_homotopy_mapCechConerve_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 019Z**.
A self map of a Čech conerve which is the identity on the base is homotopic to the identity. Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be an arrow of a category `C` whose iterated pushouts `Y ⨿_X ⋯ ⨿_X Y` exist, let
`U = f.cechConerve` be the cosimplicial object of [Stacks, Tag 016N] built from `f`, and let `F` be
an endomorphism of the arrow `f` with `F.left ≫ f = f`, so that the induced self map
`Arrow.mapCechConerve F` of `U`, given by `F.right` on each factor `Y`, is the identity on the base
`X`. Then there is a homotopy from that self map to `𝟙 U` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0FKJ]: a
family of morphisms `h_{n, α} : U_n ⟶ U_n`, indexed by the simplices `α ∈ Δ[1]_n`, satisfying
`h_{m, α} ∘ U(g) = U(g) ∘ h_{n, α ∘ g}` for every morphism `g : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌` of `Δ`, whose component
at the constant map `⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋1⦌` with value `0` is the self map and whose component at the constant
map with value `1` is the identity. In particular the two are homotopic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopy_mapCechConerve_id {f : Arrow C}
    [∀ n : ℕ, HasWidePushout f.left (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f.right) fun _ => f.hom]
    (F : f ⟶ f) (hF : F.left ≫ f.hom = f.hom) :
    ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) →
        (f.cechConerve.obj n ⟶ f.cechConerve.obj n),
      (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (g : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
          f.cechConerve.map g ≫ h m α =
            h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map g.op α) ≫ f.cechConerve.map g) ∧
        (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = (mapCechConerve F).app n) ∧
        (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = 𝟙 (f.cechConerve.obj n))
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary endomorphism `F` of the arrow `f` with `F.left ≫ f.hom = f.hom`, of which the source's self map is the case `F = (𝟙 X, f ∘ s)` for a retraction `s` of `f`; the self map is pinned as `Arrow.mapCechConerve F`, and the homotopy is given by its family of components as in 0FKJ and 07KB, which needs no products in `C`, the source's concluding homotopy equivalence with the constant cosimplicial object `X` being a formal consequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.homotopic_alternatingCofaceMapComplex_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01A0**.
The Moore cochain complex functor carries homotopic morphisms to homotopic maps of cochain
complexes. Let `a, b : U ⟶ V` be homotopic morphisms of cosimplicial objects of a preadditive
category `A`: related by a chain of morphisms consecutive members of which admit a homotopy in one
direction or the other, a homotopy from `a` to `b` being a family of morphisms `h_{n, α} : Uₙ ⟶ Vₙ`
indexed by the simplices `α ∈ Δ[1]ₙ` with `h_{m, α} ∘ U(g) = V(g) ∘ h_{n, α ∘ g}` for every
morphism `g : ⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋m⦌` of `Δ`, whose components at the constant maps `⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋1⦌` with values `0`
and `1` are `a_n` and `b_n` ([Stacks, Tag 0FKJ]). Then the induced maps `s(a), s(b) : s(U) ⟶ s(V)`
of Moore cochain complexes are chain homotopic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopic_alternatingCofaceMapComplex_map
    (h : Relation.EqvGen
      (fun a b : U ⟶ V => ∃ h : ∀ n : SimplexCategory, (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op n) →
          (U.obj n ⟶ V.obj n),
        (∀ ⦃n m : SimplexCategory⦄ (g : n ⟶ m) (α : (Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).obj (op m)),
            U.map g ≫ h m α = h n ((Δ[1] : SSet.{0}).map g.op α) ≫ V.map g) ∧
          (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 0 (op n)) = a.app n) ∧
          (∀ n : SimplexCategory, h n (stdSimplex.const 1 1 (op n)) = b.app n)) a b) :
    homotopic A (ComplexShape.up ℕ) ((alternatingCofaceMapComplex A).map a)
      ((alternatingCofaceMapComplex A).map b)
declarations.comment: the source's additive `A` is weakened to preadditive, which is all `s` uses; a homotopy is given by its family of components as in 0FKJ and 07KB, which needs no products in `A`, and being homotopic is spelled `Relation.EqvGen` of the existence of such a family, as in 019S; the source's second assertion, for the normalized cochain complex `Q` of 019I, is the formal consequence of this one obtained from the split epimorphism `π : s ⟶ Q` of 019I via `Homotopy.compLeft` and `Homotopy.compRight`

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex.cylinder.exists_map_descEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01A2**.
Let `C` be an additive category and `c` a complex shape in which every index is the target of a
relation (as for chain complexes). Then the cylinder `⋄K = K.cylinder` of a complex `K` represents
the functor `M ↦ {(a, b, h) | a, b : K ⟶ M and h a homotopy from a to b}`: the map sending
`f : ⋄K ⟶ M` to the triple obtained by composing the two inclusions `ι₀ K, ι₁ K : K ⟶ ⋄K` and the
canonical homotopy between them with `f` is a bijection. Moreover `K ↦ ⋄K` is functorial, by the
unique action on morphisms compatible with the inclusions and with the canonical homotopy.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_map_descEquiv (hc : ∀ j, ∃ i, c.Rel i j) :
    ∃ map : ∀ (K L : HomologicalComplex C c), (K ⟶ L) → (K.cylinder ⟶ L.cylinder),
      (∀ K : HomologicalComplex C c, map K K (𝟙 K) = 𝟙 K.cylinder) ∧
      (∀ (K L M : HomologicalComplex C c) (φ : K ⟶ L) (ψ : L ⟶ M),
        map K M (φ ≫ ψ) = map K L φ ≫ map L M ψ) ∧
      (∀ (K L : HomologicalComplex C c) (φ : K ⟶ L), ι₀ K ≫ map K L φ = φ ≫ ι₀ L) ∧
      (∀ (K L : HomologicalComplex C c) (φ : K ⟶ L), ι₁ K ≫ map K L φ = φ ≫ ι₁ L) ∧
      (∀ (K L : HomologicalComplex C c) (φ : K ⟶ L) (i j : ι) (hij : c.Rel j i),
        inlX K i j hij ≫ (map K L φ).f j = φ.f i ≫ inlX L i j hij) ∧
      ∀ K M : HomologicalComplex C c,
        ∃ e : (Σ (a : K ⟶ M) (b : K ⟶ M), Homotopy a b) ≃ (K.cylinder ⟶ M),
          ∀ x : Σ (a : K ⟶ M) (b : K ⟶ M), Homotopy a b,
            ι₀ K ≫ e x = x.1 ∧ ι₁ K ≫ e x = x.2.1 ∧
              ∀ (i j : ι) (hij : c.Rel j i),
                inlX K i j hij ≫ (e x).f j = x.2.2.hom i j

declarations.name: CochainComplex.diamond.exists_unique_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01A3**.
Let `0 → A ⊕ A → B → Cpx → 0` be a short exact sequence of complexes, split in each degree by
`s n : Cpx_n ⟶ B_n`. If the associated connecting morphism `δ(s) : Cpx → A[-1] ⊕ A[-1]` factors
through `(1, -1) : A[-1] → A[-1] ⊕ A[-1]` as `δ(s) = (1, -1) ∘ f`, then there is a unique morphism
`φ : B ⟶ ⋄A` fitting into a commutative diagram of the two short exact sequences whose vertical
maps are compatible with the splittings `s n` and `σ A n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_comparison
    (A B Cpx : CochainComplex C ℤ)
    (i : double A ⟶ B) (r : B ⟶ Cpx)
    (p q : ∀ n, B.X n ⟶ A.X n) (s : ∀ n, Cpx.X n ⟶ B.X n)
    (f : Cpx ⟶ shift1 A)
    -- degreewise biproduct splitting `B_n ≅ (A_n ⊕ A_n) ⊕ C_n`
    (hsr : ∀ n, s n ≫ r.f n = 𝟙 _)
    (hip : ∀ n, i.f n ≫ biprod.lift (p n) (q n) = 𝟙 _)
    (hsplit : ∀ n,
      biprod.lift (p n) (q n) ≫ i.f n + r.f n ≫ s n = 𝟙 (B.X n))
    -- the factorization `δ(s) = (1,-1) ∘ f`
    (hfac1 : ∀ n, s n ≫ B.d n (n + 1) ≫ p (n + 1) = f.f n)
    (hfac2 : ∀ n, s n ≫ B.d n (n + 1) ≫ q (n + 1) = -(f.f n)) :
    ∃! φ : B ⟶ diamond A,
      (i ≫ φ = ι A) ∧
      (φ ≫ ρ A = r ≫ f) ∧
      (∀ n, s n ≫ φ.f n = f.f n ≫ σ A n)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.exists_homotopy_of_homotopy_normalizedMooreComplex_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01A4**.
Let `a, b : U ⟶ V` be morphisms of simplicial objects of an abelian category and let `H` be a chain
homotopy between the induced maps `N(a), N(b) : N(U) ⟶ N(V)` of normalized Moore complexes. Then
`a` and `b` are simplicially homotopic, and moreover the homotopy `K` can be chosen so that the
chain homotopy it induces on normalized Moore complexes is `H` itself: `Hₙ = p_V ∘ s(K)ₙ ∘ ι_U`,
where `s(K)` is the chain homotopy of `K` on the alternating face map complexes
([Stacks, Tag 019Q]) and `ι_U`, `p_V` are the canonical inclusion of and projection onto the
normalized Moore complex. By [Stacks, Tag 019L] such a `K` is the same thing as a homotopy
`h : U × Δ[1] ⟶ V` from `a` to `b` in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 019K], with
`K.h i = sⁿᵢ ≫ h_{n + 1, i + 1}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopy_of_homotopy_normalizedMooreComplex_map
    (H : _root_.Homotopy ((normalizedMooreComplex A).map a) ((normalizedMooreComplex A).map b)) :
    ∃ K : Homotopy a b, ∀ n : ℕ, H.hom n (n + 1) =
      (inclusionOfMooreComplexMap U).f n ≫ K.toChainHomotopy.hom n (n + 1) ≫
        (PInftyToNormalizedMooreComplex V).f (n + 1)
declarations.comment: the homotopy of 019K is presented by the family of components `h_{n + 1, i + 1} ∘ sⁿᵢ` it corresponds to under 019L, which is Mathlib's `SimplicialObject.Homotopy`, and out of which the chain homotopy `s(h)` of 019Q is built; `N(h)` is `s(h)` conjugated by the canonical splitting `N ⊆ s` of 019A

declarations.name: SSet.trivialKanFibrations_of_coskeletal
declarations.statement:
theorem trivialKanFibrations_of_coskeletal
    {V U : SSet} (f : V ⟶ U) (n : ℕ)
    (h1 : ∀ i : ℕ, i < n → Function.Bijective (f.app (op ⦋i⦌)))
    (h2 : Function.Surjective (f.app (op ⦋n⦌)))

declarations.name: SSet.nonempty_homotopy_of_app_eq_of_isCoskeletal
declarations.doc:
**Two maps into an `n`-coskeletal simplicial set agreeing below degree `n` are homotopic,
[Stacks, Tag 01A9].** Let `f₀, f₁ : V ⟶ U` be maps of simplicial sets whose components
`V_i ⟶ U_i` agree for every `i < n`, and assume that the canonical morphism
`U ⟶ cosk_n sk_n U` is an isomorphism, i.e. that `U` is `n`-coskeletal. Then there is a
simplicial homotopy `V ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ U` from `f₀` to `f₁`; in particular `f₀` and `f₁` are homotopic.
No hypothesis on `V` is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_homotopy_of_app_eq_of_isCoskeletal {V U : SSet.{u}} (n : ℕ) [U.IsCoskeletal n]
    (f₀ f₁ : V ⟶ U) (h : ∀ i < n, f₀.app (op ⦋i⦌) = f₁.app (op ⦋i⦌)) :
    Nonempty (Homotopy f₀ f₁)
declarations.comment: the conclusion is strengthened from `f⁰` and `f¹` being homotopic to the existence of a homotopy from `f⁰` to `f¹`, which is what both of the source's proofs produce; hypothesis (3) of the source, that `V ⟶ cosk_n sk_n V` is an isomorphism, is dropped, since neither of the source's proofs uses it: maps into an `n`-coskeletal object are exactly maps of their `n`-truncations, by `coskAdj n`, for an arbitrary source; coskeletality of `U` is Mathlib's `IsCoskeletal`, equivalent to the source's `U ⟶ cosk_n sk_n U` being an isomorphism

declarations.name: SSet.hasLiftingProperty_augmentedCechNerve_hom
declarations.doc:
**The augmentation of the Čech nerve of a surjection of sets has the right lifting property
with respect to every morphism of simplicial sets injective on vertices, [Stacks, Tag 01AB].**
Monomorphisms of simplicial sets are injective in every degree, so the class of morphisms covered
contains every monomorphism, and in particular the boundary inclusions `∂Δ[n] ⟶ Δ[n]` against which
`trivialKanFibrations` asks for lifts.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasLiftingProperty_augmentedCechNerve_hom (F : Arrow (Type u))
    (hF : Function.Surjective F.hom) {K L : SSet.{u}} {i : K ⟶ L}
    (hi : Function.Injective (i.app (op ⦋0⦌))) :
    HasLiftingProperty i F.augmentedCechNerve.hom
declarations.comment: the lifting property proved is against every map injective on vertices, hence against every monomorphism of simplicial sets, not only the boundary inclusions

declarations.name: SSet.trivialKanFibrations_augmentedCechNerve_hom_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**The Čech nerve of a surjection of sets is a trivial Kan fibration, [Stacks, Tag 01AB].**
Let `f : A ⟶ B` be a surjective map of sets and let `U` be the simplicial set with
`U_n = A ×_B A ×_B ⋯ ×_B A` (`n + 1` factors), the Čech nerve of `f`. Then the augmentation of
`U` over the constant simplicial set with value `B`, given in degree `n` by the projection
`(a_0, …, a_n) ↦ f a_0` to the base, is a trivial Kan fibration.
declarations.statement:
theorem trivialKanFibrations_augmentedCechNerve_hom_of_surjective {A B : Type u} {f : A ⟶ B}
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) : trivialKanFibrations (Arrow.mk f).augmentedCechNerve.hom
declarations.comment: the simplicial set of the source's Example 016E is the Čech nerve `(Arrow.mk f).cechNerve`, and the source's morphism from it to the constant simplicial set with value `B` is the augmentation `(Arrow.mk f).augmentedCechNerve.hom`

declarations.name: generate_iff_generateStalks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01AN, Lemma 17.4.2.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space, `F` a sheaf of
`O_X`-modules, `I` a set, and `s_i ∈ Γ(X, F)` global sections. Then the sections generate
`F` (Definition 2) if and only if for every point `x` the germs `s_{i,x}` generate the
`O_{X,x}`-module `F_x` (Definition 3 at the stalk).

PROOF: a finite chain of iff's. With `φ := assocMap O_X F s` and `ψ := (toSheaf O_X).map φ`:
  Epi φ  ↔ Epi ψ                                   -- toSheaf_preservesEpi + toSheaf_reflectsEpi
        ↔ Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective ψ              -- Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi'
        ↔ Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (sheafToPresheaf.map ψ)
                                    -- Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_sheafToPresheaf_map_iff
        ↔ ∀ x, Surjective ((stalkFunctor _ x).map (sheafToPresheaf.map ψ))
                                                   -- locally_surjective_iff_surjective_on_stalks
                                                   -- (defeq to TopCat version)
        ≡ GenerateStalks                           -- defeq: matches `stalkMapAb`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generate_iff_generateStalks (s : I → F.sections) :
    Generate O_X F s ↔ GenerateStalks O_X F s

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.generated_subsheaf_stalk_eq_span
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01AR.** Let `G` be the smallest subsheaf of `F` containing local sections
`s i ∈ F(U i)`. At a point `x`, the set of germs of local sections of `G`, viewed in the
stalk of `F`, is the `R_x`-submodule spanned by the germs `(s i)_x` for which `x ∈ U i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generated_subsheaf_stalk_eq_span {ι : Type*}
    (U : ι → (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (s : ∀ i, F.val.obj (U i))
    (G : F.Submodule) (hcontains : ∀ i, s i ∈ G.obj (U i))
    (hminimal : ∀ G' : F.Submodule,
      (∀ i, s i ∈ G'.obj (U i)) → G ≤ G')
    (x : X) :
    {t : (show X.Presheaf Ab from F.val.presheaf).stalk x |
      ∃ (V : Opens X) (hxV : x ∈ V) (a : F.val.obj (op V)),
        a ∈ G.obj (op V) ∧
          (show X.Presheaf Ab from F.val.presheaf).germ V x hxV a = t} =
      (Submodule.span ((show X.Presheaf RingCat from R.obj).stalk x)
        {t | ∃ (i : ι) (hxi : x ∈ unop (U i)),
          (show X.Presheaf Ab from F.val.presheaf).germ
            (unop (U i)) x hxi (s i) = t} :
        Submodule ((show X.Presheaf RingCat from R.obj).stalk x)
          ((show X.Presheaf Ab from F.val.presheaf).stalk x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.mem_supp_iff
declarations.doc:

    x ∈ F.supp ↔ ∃ (U : Opens X.carrier) (s : F.toPresheaf.obj (Opposite.op U)),

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.exactFunctor_closedInclusionPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01AX, exactness.** Pushforward of sheaves of abelian groups along a closed
embedding `i : Z ⟶ X` is an exact functor `Ab(Z) ⥤ Ab(X)`.

Exactness is detected on stalks. Over a point of the image of `i` the stalk of `i_* 𝒜` is the
stalk of `𝒜`, naturally in `𝒜`, because a closed embedding is inducing; over a point off the
image the stalk of `i_* 𝒜` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactFunctor_closedInclusionPushforward (hi : IsClosedEmbedding i.hom) :
    exactFunctor (TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} Z) (TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} X)
      (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i)

    PreservesFiniteLimits (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i)

declarations.doc:
