declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.essImage_closedInclusionPushforward_iff_forall_stalk_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01AX, essential image.** A sheaf `G` of abelian groups on `X` is in the essential
image of pushforward along the closed embedding `i : Z ⟶ X` if and only if the stalk of `G`
vanishes at every point outside the image of `i`.

The forward direction is Stacks 00AG
(`closedInclusion_pushforward_essImage_stalk_isZero`). For the converse the preimage is the
sheafification `ℱ` of `i^{-1} G`; the canonical morphism `η : G ⟶ i_* ℱ` is an isomorphism
because it is one on every stalk: off the image of `i` both stalks vanish, and at `i z` the
composite of the stalk of `η` with the isomorphism `(i_* ℱ)_{i z} ⟶ ℱ_z` is an isomorphism by
`stalkFunctor_map_unit_comp_stalkPushforward` together with
`TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_unit_toSheafify_isIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_closedInclusionPushforward_iff_forall_stalk_isZero
    (hi : IsClosedEmbedding i.hom) (G : TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} X) :
    (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i).essImage G ↔
      ∀ x : X, x ∉ Set.range i.hom → IsZero (G.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.essImage_closedInclusionPushforward_iff_support_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01AX, essential image.** The essential image of pushforward along a closed
embedding `i : Z ⟶ X` consists exactly of the sheaves of abelian groups whose support is
contained in the image of `i`.

This is the source's phrasing of
`essImage_closedInclusionPushforward_iff_forall_stalk_isZero`, since the support of an abelian
sheaf is by definition the set of points with nonzero stalk.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_closedInclusionPushforward_iff_support_subset
    (hi : IsClosedEmbedding i.hom) (G : TopCat.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u} X) :
    (closedInclusionPushforward Z X i).essImage G ↔
      Stacks.AbelianSheaf.support G ⊆ Set.range i.hom
declarations.comment: essential image, in terms of the support

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.LocallySurjective.main_theorem
declarations.doc:
Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and `φ : G ⟶ F` a homomorphism of `O_X`-modules. Suppose `F`
is of finite type and the induced map on stalks at `x` is surjective. Then there is an open
neighbourhood `U` of `x` over which `φ` is surjective, i.e. for every `y ∈ U` the induced map on
the stalk at `y` is surjective.

    {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (φ : G ⟶ F)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F) (x : X)
    (hx : SurjOnStalk φ x) :
    ∃ U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y ∈ U, SurjOnStalk φ y

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.pullbackAssociatedSheafIso_hom_app_apply
declarations.doc:
The comparison `pullbackAssociatedSheafIso` carries the image of `1 ⊗ m` under the unit of
`π^* ⊣ π_*` to `1 ⊗ m`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pullbackAssociatedSheafIso_hom_app_apply (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) (m : M) :
    PresheafOfModules.Hom.app ((pullbackAssociatedSheafIso.{u, v} X α).hom.app M).val (op ⊤)
        (PresheafOfModules.Hom.app ((coefficientPointAdjunction.{u, v} X α).unit.app
          ((coefficientPointModuleFunctor.{u, v} (R := R)).obj M)).val (op ⊤)
          (tensorUnitSection (coefficientPoint (CommRingCat.of R)) (pointRing (R := R))

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.presentationSheafIso_hom_app_apply
declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:
lemma presentationSheafIso_hom_app_apply (i : P.G) (U : Opens X.carrier) :
    PresheafOfModules.Hom.app (presentationSheafIso X α M P).hom.val (op U)
        (PresheafOfModules.Hom.app (presentationGenerator X α P i).val (op U)
          (ULift.up (1 : X.presheaf.obj (op U)))) =
      ULift.up (tensorUnitSection X α M (op U)
        (P.toSolution.π (Finsupp.single i 1)))

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.quasicoherentAssociatedSheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01BH, clause (2): the construction is a functor into quasi-coherent sheaves.**
Construction (3) lifts through the full subcategory of quasi-coherent sheaves of `𝒪_X`-modules,
by `Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.isQuasicoherent_associatedSheafFunctor_obj`. The colimit-preservation
half of the clause is
`Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.preservesColimitsOfSize_associatedSheafFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentAssociatedSheafFunctor : ModuleCat.{u} R ⥤
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
      (structureSheafRing X)).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: a functor from R-modules to quasi-coherent sheaves on X

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.associatedSheafStalkLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`(ℱ_M)_x = 𝒪_{X,x} ⊗_A M` as `𝒪_{X,x}`-modules.**  The stalk at a point `x` of the sheaf of
`𝒪_X`-modules associated to an `A`-module `M` and a ring map `α : A → Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is the base
change of `M` to the stalk of the structure sheaf, linearly over that stalk.
declarations.statement:
def associatedSheafStalkLinearEquiv :
    letI := stalkAlgebra X α x
    ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
        ((associatedSheafValFunctor X α).obj M).presheaf x) ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x]
      (X.presheaf.stalk x ⊗[A] M)
declarations.comment: the stalk of ℱ_M is 𝒪_{X,x} ⊗_R M

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.associatedSheafStalkFunctorIso
declarations.statement:
def associatedSheafStalkFunctorIso :
    stalkBaseChangeFunctor X α x ≅ associatedSheafStalkFunctor X α x
declarations.comment: the stalk of ℱ_M is 𝒪_{X,x} ⊗_R M, functorially in M

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.associatedSheafUnitIso
declarations.doc:
**Construction (3) carries the base ring to the structure sheaf:** `ℱ_R ≅ 𝒪_X`.

Both legs are already in the repository: `Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.freeIsoAssociatedSheaf`
identifies `ℱ` of a free module with the free sheaf of modules on the same index type, and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Site.freePUnitIso` identifies the free sheaf of modules on a one-element
index type with the structure sheaf. What is interposed is only the `R`-module isomorphism
`(PUnit →₀ R) ≃ₗ[R] R`.
declarations.comment: construction (3) at the base ring is the structure sheaf

registrations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.associatedSheaf
registrations.comment: associated_sheaf_construction

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.ringedSpacePullbackAssociatedSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01BJ.** The pullback of the sheaf associated to a module is the sheaf associated to
the module obtained by extension of scalars along the map on global sections.

The name says `ringedSpace` because `Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.pullbackAssociatedSheafIso` of
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.AssociatedSheafIsos` is a different
comparison, between the coefficient-point pullback and the associated-sheaf functor.
declarations.statement:
def ringedSpacePullbackAssociatedSheafIso {X Y : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (g : Y ⟶ X) :
    associatedSheafFunctor.{u, u} X (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))) ⋙
        RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback g ≅
      ModuleCat.extendScalars (SheafedSpace.Γ.map g.op).hom ⋙
        associatedSheafFunctor.{u, u} Y (RingHom.id (Y.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.exists_open_associatedSheaf_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01BK.** A quasi-coherent sheaf of modules is locally associated to a
module over the ring of sections near a point with a basis of quasi-compact
neighborhoods.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_open_associatedSheaf_iso (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (x : X)
    (hx : ∀ V : Set X, V ∈ 𝓝 x →
      ∃ K : Set X, IsCompact K ∧ K ∈ 𝓝 x ∧ K ⊆ V)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∃ U : Opens X, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u} ((X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding).presheaf.obj (op ⊤)),
        Nonempty (((modulePullback (X.ofRestrict U.isOpenEmbedding)).obj F) ≅
          associatedSheaf (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding)
            (RingHom.id ((X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding).presheaf.obj (op ⊤))) M)

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.exists_free_iso_associatedSheaf_freeModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01BL, first half.** The free sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules on `I` is isomorphic to the sheaf
associated to the free `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`-module on `I`, by an isomorphism carrying the `i`-th basis
section to the image of `Finsupp.single i 1` under the unit of the tensor-sheafification
adjunction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_free_iso_associatedSheaf_freeModule (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (I : Type u) :
    ∃ s : SheafOfModules.free (R := structureSheafRing X) I ≅
        associatedSheaf X (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))
          (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
            (I →₀ X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))),
      ∀ i : I, s.hom.val.app (op ⊤) (basisSection X ⊤ i) =
        ((associatedSheafAdjunction.{u, u} X
          (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))).unit.app
          (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
            (I →₀ X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))) (Finsupp.single i 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Bouquet.exists_freeSheafMorphism_not_locally_finite
declarations.doc:
The countable bouquet carries a morphism of sheaves associated to free
modules that does not locally come from a homomorphism of the free modules:
its value on a basis section is never a finite target-basis combination on
any neighborhood of the common origin.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_freeSheafMorphism_not_locally_finite :
    ∃ (X : RingedSpace.{0, 0}) (e : X ≃ₜ Point)
      (σ : X.presheaf ≅
        TopCat.presheafToTopCommRing (X := X.carrier) (TopCommRingCat.of ℝ))
      (s : SheafOfModules.free (R := structureSheafRing X) ℕ ≅
        associatedSheaf X (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))
          (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
            (ℕ →₀ X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))))
      (t : SheafOfModules.free (R := structureSheafRing X) (ℕ × ℕ) ≅
        associatedSheaf X (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))
          (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
            ((ℕ × ℕ) →₀ X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))))
      (φ : associatedSheaf X (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))
          (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
            (ℕ →₀ X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))) ⟶
        associatedSheaf X (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))
          (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
            ((ℕ × ℕ) →₀ X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))),
      (∀ j : ℕ, s.hom.val.app (op ⊤) (basisSection X ⊤ j) =
        ((associatedSheafAdjunction X
          (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))).unit.app
          (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
            (ℕ →₀ X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))) (Finsupp.single j 1)) ∧
      (∀ k : ℕ × ℕ, t.hom.val.app (op ⊤) (basisSection X ⊤ k) =
        ((associatedSheafAdjunction X
          (RingHom.id (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))).unit.app
          (ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))
            ((ℕ × ℕ) →₀ X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)))) (Finsupp.single k 1)) ∧
      (∃ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (_ : Continuous f),
        (∀ x : ℝ, |x| < 1 → f x = 0) ∧
        (∀ x : ℝ, 2 < |x| → f x = 1) ∧
        (∃ π : (ℕ × ℕ) →
            (SheafOfModules.free (R := structureSheafRing X) (ℕ × ℕ) ⟶
              SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X)),
          (∀ k l : ℕ × ℕ,
            SheafOfModules.ιFree (R := structureSheafRing X) l ≫ π k = if k = l then 𝟙 _ else 0) ∧
          (∀ (U : Opens X) (j i : ℕ) (x : {x : ℝ // x ≠ 0})
            (hx : e.symm (branch i x) ∈ U) (k : ℕ × ℕ),
            ((σ.hom.app (op U)
              ((π k).val.app (op U)
                (t.inv.val.app (op U)
                  (φ.val.app (op U)
                    (s.hom.val.app (op U) (basisSection X U j))))))).hom
                ⟨e.symm (branch i x), hx⟩ =
              if k = (j, i) then f ((j + 1) * (x : ℝ)) else 0))) ∧
      (∀ U : Opens X, e.symm origin ∈ U →
        ∃ j : ℕ, ∀ g : (ℕ × ℕ) →₀ (structureSheafRing X).obj.obj (op U),
          φ.val.app (op U) (s.hom.val.app (op U) (basisSection X U j)) ≠
            t.hom.val.app (op U)
              (g.sum (fun k r => r • basisSection X U k)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SliceFinite.isFiniteType_kernel_of_epi_from_finite_free
declarations.doc:
On a site with no products and no pullbacks assumed, the kernel of a surjection from a
finite-rank free sheaf of modules onto a sheaf of modules of finite presentation is of finite
type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_kernel_of_epi_from_finite_free {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    {F : SheafOfModules.{u} R} [F.IsFinitePresentation] (psi : free I ⟶ F) [Epi psi] :
    (kernel psi).IsFiniteType

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.LocalKernel.kernel_isFiniteType_of_epi_from_finiteType
declarations.doc:
The kernel of a surjection from a finite-type sheaf of modules onto a finitely presented sheaf
of modules is of finite type.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.modulePullback_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01BQ.** The pullback of a sheaf of modules of finite presentation along a
morphism of ringed spaces is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
lemma modulePullback_isFinitePresentation {X Y : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) [G.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ((modulePullback f).obj G).IsFinitePresentation

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.exists_directed_system_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01BR.** The sheaf associated to a module over a ring mapping to the global sections
of a ringed space is a directed colimit of sheaves of modules of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_system_of_isFinitePresentation (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] (α : R →+* X.presheaf.obj (op ⊤)) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
      (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (D : I ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
      (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj (associatedSheaf X α M)),
      (∀ i, (D.obj i).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
        Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk (associatedSheaf X α M) φ))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.preservesColimitsOfShape_coyoneda_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01BS.**  Let `X` be a ringed space with a cofinal system of open
coverings `X = ⋃_{j ∈ J} U_j` with `J` finite and all `U_j ∩ U_j'` quasi-compact, let `F` be an
`O_X`-module of finite presentation and let `λ ↦ G_λ` be a filtered system of `O_X`-modules.  Then

`colim_λ Hom_X(F, G_λ) = Hom_X(F, colim_λ G_λ)`;

here in the form that `Hom_X(F, -)` preserves colimits of the given filtered shape, which says
exactly that the canonical comparison map out of any colimit of the `Hom_X(F, G_λ)` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_coyoneda_of_isFinitePresentation
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf Rc)) [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (K : Type u) [Category.{u} K] [IsFiltered K]
    (hX : DirectedColimitOfSheaves.HasFiniteCompactCofinalCovers (X := X) ⊤) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape K (coyoneda.obj (op F))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_colimitPost_coyoneda_of_hasFiniteCompactCofinalCovers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01BS as the source displays it.**  The canonical comparison map

`colim_λ Hom_X(F, G_λ) ⟶ Hom_X(F, colim_λ G_λ)`

is an isomorphism of types, for `F` an `O_X`-module of finite presentation and `G` a filtered
system of `O_X`-modules on a ringed space with a cofinal system of finite open coverings having
quasi-compact pairwise intersections.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimitPost_coyoneda_of_hasFiniteCompactCofinalCovers
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf Rc)) [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    {K : Type u} [Category.{u} K] [IsFiltered K]
    (G : K ⥤ _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf Rc))
    (hX : DirectedColimitOfSheaves.HasFiniteCompactCofinalCovers (X := X) ⊤) :
    IsIso (colimit.post G (coyoneda.obj (op F)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules `M` over a ringed space is *coherent* if

1. `M` is of finite type, and
2. for every open `U` and every finite index type `I`, the kernel of every `O_U`-module map
   `free I ⟶ M|_U` — equivalently, of the associated map of every finite family of sections of
   `M` over `U` — is of finite type.
declarations.statement: class IsCoherent (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules
declarations.doc: The full subcategory `Coh(O_X)` of coherent sheaves of modules over a ringed space.
declarations.statement: abbrev CoherentModules (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.CoherentModules
declarations.doc: The full category of coherent sheaves of modules over a ringed space.
declarations.statement:
abbrev CoherentModules {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})

registrations.name: SheafOfModules.IsCoherent
registrations.comment: the coherence predicate

declarations.name: isFinitePresentation_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01BW, implication (1): coherent ⟹ finite presentation.**
A coherent sheaf of modules over a ringed space is of finite presentation.

The decomposition into `bind_isFinitePresentation` (Lemma A) and
`over_quasicoherentData_isFP_of_finiteGenerators_finiteKernel` (Lemma B) makes
this body fully proved (no open goals): take a finite-type local-generators datum,
apply coherence condition (2) to the finite generators over each cover open to
learn the kernel is finite type, feed that to Lemma B, and glue with Lemma A.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_of_isCoherent (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    [M.IsCoherent] : M.IsFinitePresentation

declarations.name: isQuasicoherent_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01BW, implication (2): finite presentation ⟹ quasi-coherent.**
A sheaf of modules of finite presentation is quasi-coherent. (This is immediate
from the definitions, since finite free modules are free modules; in Mathlib it
is recorded as an instance.)
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_of_isFinitePresentation (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    [M.IsFinitePresentation] : M.IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_of_mono
declarations.doc:
A finite type subsheaf of a coherent sheaf of modules is coherent: the second condition of
coherence passes to subsheaves, because a map out of a free module into the subsheaf has the
same kernel as its composite into the ambient sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_of_mono {M N : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (ι : N ⟶ M) [Mono ι]
    [IsCoherent M] [N.IsFiniteType] : IsCoherent N

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteType_kernel_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
The kernel of a morphism from a sheaf of modules of finite type to a coherent sheaf of modules
is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_kernel_of_isCoherent {M N : SheafOfModules.{u} R} [M.IsFiniteType]
    [IsCoherent N] (φ : M ⟶ N) : (kernel φ).IsFiniteType

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_kernel
declarations.doc: The kernel of a morphism of coherent sheaves of modules is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_kernel {M N : SheafOfModules.{u} R} [IsCoherent M] [IsCoherent N]
    (φ : M ⟶ N) : IsCoherent (kernel φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_X₂_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
The middle term of a short exact sequence of sheaves of modules whose outer terms are coherent
is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_X₂_of_shortExact {S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} R)} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : IsCoherent S.X₁) (h₃ : IsCoherent S.X₃) : IsCoherent S.X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_X₃_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
The third term of a short exact sequence of sheaves of modules whose first two terms are
coherent is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_X₃_of_shortExact {S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} R)} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : IsCoherent S.X₁) (h₂ : IsCoherent S.X₂) : IsCoherent S.X₃

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
On a ringed space, the coherent sheaves of modules form a weak Serre subcategory of the
category of all sheaves of modules: they contain the zero object, are closed under isomorphisms,
and are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions.
declarations.statement:
instance coherentModules_isWeakSerreClass :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass (fun M : SheafOfModules.{u} R => IsCoherent M)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules_inclusion_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc: The inclusion of coherent modules preserves finite limits.
declarations.statement:
instance coherentModules_inclusion_preservesFiniteLimits
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (ObjectProperty.ι (coherentModules R))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules_inclusion_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc: The inclusion of coherent modules preserves finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
instance coherentModules_inclusion_preservesFiniteColimits
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (ObjectProperty.ι (coherentModules R))

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.kernel_isCoherent
declarations.doc: A kernel of a morphism of coherent sheaves of modules is coherent.
declarations.statement:
instance kernel_isCoherent {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} R} [F.IsCoherent] [G.IsCoherent]
    (f : F ⟶ G) : (kernel f).IsCoherent

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.cokernel_isCoherent
declarations.doc: The cokernel of a morphism of coherent sheaves of modules is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem cokernel_isCoherent {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} R} [F.IsCoherent] [G.IsCoherent]
    (f : F ⟶ G) : (cokernel f).IsCoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_iff_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01BZ.** Over a ringed space whose structure sheaf is coherent as a module over
itself, a sheaf of modules is coherent if and only if it is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_iff_isFinitePresentation
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u}) (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    [IsCoherent (unit R)] : IsCoherent M ↔ M.IsFinitePresentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isMono_over_of_stalk_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01Y3.** A morphism from a module of finite type to a coherent module
which is injective on one stalk is a monomorphism after restriction to a neighbourhood of that
point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isMono_over_of_stalk_injective {G F : SheafOfModules.{u} R}
    (φ : G ⟶ F) [G.IsFiniteType] [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] (x : X)
    (hx : Function.Injective
      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
        ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R.obj).map φ.val)))) :
    ∃ U : Opens X, x ∈ U ∧ Mono (φ.over U)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag01Y3LocalIso.exists_isMono_over_of_stalk_injective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01C0]**, which is also part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01Y3]. A morphism from a
finite-type module sheaf to a coherent module sheaf which is injective on one stalk is injective
after restriction to a neighbourhood of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isMono_over_of_stalk_injective {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} R}
    [G.IsFiniteType] [F.IsCoherent] (φ : G ⟶ F) (x : X)
    (hx : Function.Injective
      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
        ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R.obj).map φ.val)))) :
    ∃ U : Opens X, x ∈ U ∧ Mono (φ.over U)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isMono_over_of_stalk_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01C0.** A morphism from a finite-type sheaf of modules to a coherent
sheaf of modules which is injective on one stalk is injective after restriction to a
neighbourhood of that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isMono_over_of_stalk_injective
    (φ : G ⟶ F) [G.IsFiniteType] [F.IsCoherent] (x : X)
    (hx : Function.Injective
      (ConcreteCategory.hom ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
        ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf R.obj).map φ.val)))) :
    ∃ U : Opens X, x ∈ U ∧ Mono (φ.over U)

declarations.name: ClosedImmersionSheaves.exists_local_cokernel_presentation_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01C3.** The pushforward of a quasi-coherent module along a
closed immersion is locally a cokernel of quasi-coherent modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_local_cokernel_presentation_pushforward
    {X Z : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [SheafOfModules.IsClosedImmersion i]
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Z)) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (x : X.carrier) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ (A B : SheafOfModules.{u} ((structureSheafRing X).over U)),
        A.IsQuasicoherent ∧ B.IsQuasicoherent ∧
          ∃ (f : A ⟶ B), Nonempty (cokernel f ≅ ((modulePushforward i).obj F).over U)

declarations.name: RS.Modules.IsLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
Definition 1 (locally free, Tag 01C6): a sheaf of `O_X`-modules `M` is locally free if
every point `x ∈ X` has an open neighbourhood `U` such that the restriction `M|_U` is
isomorphic, as a sheaf of `O_X|_U`-modules, to a free module `⨁_{i ∈ I} (O_X|_U)` for some
index type `I` (allowed to be arbitrary and to depend on `x`).

No finiteness is imposed on `I`, nor any bound on its cardinality: it ranges over all of
`Type u`, the universe in which the structure sheaf of `X` takes its values and hence the only
one in which `SheafOfModules.free` forms a direct sum of copies of `O_X|_U`. The finite and
fixed-rank refinements, parts (2) and (3) of the same definition, are
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree` and `.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank`.
declarations.statement:
def RS.Modules.IsLocallyFree {X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (M : RS.Modules X) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1), locally free with an arbitrary index set

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is finite locally free if it has local free presentations whose
basis-indexing types are finite.
declarations.statement: class IsFiniteLocallyFree (M : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} R) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is finite locally free of rank `r` if it has local free presentations
whose basis-indexing types are equivalent to `Fin r`.
declarations.statement: class IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (M : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} R) (r : ℕ) : Prop

Statement 1 (Stacks Tag 01C8, Lemma 17.14.3): the pullback `f^*G` of a locally free

declarations.statement:
theorem pullback_isLocallyFree {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)

declarations.name: LocallyFreeRank.exists_locallyConstant_rank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01C9.**  Let `X` be a ringed space whose structure sheaf `O_X` is a sheaf
of commutative rings all of whose stalks `O_{X,x}` are nonzero, and let `F` be a locally
free sheaf of `O_X`-modules.  Then there is a locally constant function
`rank_F : X → Cardinal` such that for every point `x` and every trivialisation `t` of `F` on
an open neighbourhood `U` of `x`, the cardinality of the index set of `t` equals `rank_F x`.

This single statement encodes both that the rank at a point is well defined (independent of
the trivialisation chosen) and that the resulting function is locally constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_locallyConstant_rank
    (X : TopCat.{u})
    (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u})
    (hO : StalksNontrivial X O)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (toRingSheaf X O))
    (hF : IsLocallyFree X (toRingSheaf X O) F) :
    ∃ rankF : X → Cardinal.{u},
      IsLocallyConstant rankF ∧
      ∀ (x : X) (U : Opens X), x ∈ U →
        ∀ t : Trivialization X (toRingSheaf X O) F U, t.rank = rankF x

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
declarations.doc:
The tensor product of module sheaves in independent section universes, obtained by
sheafifying the canonical objectwise tensor product of their underlying presheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafTensor :
    SheafOfModules.{leftUniverse} (ringSheaf R) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{rightUniverse} (ringSheaf R) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{max leftUniverse rightUniverse} (ringSheaf R)
declarations.comment:
the section's definition of the tensor product sheaf
`F ⊗_O G = (F ⊗_{p, O} G)^#`, the sheafification of the tensor product presheaf; over an
arbitrary site, the ringed-space case being the site of opens of `X`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorRingedSpace.tensorPresheaf_sections
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product presheaf** `ℱ ⊗_{p, 𝒪_X} 𝒢` assigns to an open `U ⊂ X` the
`𝒪_X(U)`-module `ℱ(U) ⊗_{𝒪_X(U)} 𝒢(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPresheaf_sections (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ) :
    ((PresheafOfModules.tensorObj (O := X.presheaf) F.val G.val).obj U : Type u) =
      (F.val.obj U ⊗[(Tensor.ringSheaf (structureSheaf X)).obj.obj U] G.val.obj U)
declarations.comment:
the section's tensor product presheaf `F ⊗_{p, O_X} G`, the rule which assigns
to `U ⊂ X` open the `O_X(U)`-module `F(U) ⊗_{O_X(U)} G(U)`: its sections

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorRingedSpace.tensorPresheaf_restrict_tmul
declarations.doc:
The restriction maps of the tensor product presheaf are the tensor products of the
restriction maps of `ℱ` and `𝒢`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPresheaf_restrict_tmul {U V : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ} (f : U ⟶ V)
    (x : F.val.obj U) (y : G.val.obj U) :
    (PresheafOfModules.tensorObj (O := X.presheaf) F.val G.val).restrictₛₗ f
        (x ⊗ₜ[(Tensor.ringSheaf (structureSheaf X)).obj.obj U] y) =
      F.val.restrictₛₗ f x ⊗ₜ[(Tensor.ringSheaf (structureSheaf X)).obj.obj V]
        G.val.restrictₛₗ f y
declarations.comment:
the section's tensor product presheaf `F ⊗_{p, O_X} G`: its restriction maps,
`x ⊗ y ↦ x|_V ⊗ y|_V`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorRingedSpace.tensorSheaf_eq_sheafification
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product sheaf** `ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢` is the sheafification
`(ℱ ⊗_{p, 𝒪_X} 𝒢)^#` of the tensor product presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSheaf_eq_sheafification :
    ((Tensor.sheafTensor (structureSheaf X)).obj F).obj G =
      (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := Tensor.ringSheaf (structureSheaf X))
        (𝟙 (Tensor.ringSheaf (structureSheaf X)).obj)).obj
        (PresheafOfModules.tensorObj (O := X.presheaf) F.val G.val)
declarations.comment:
the section's definition of the tensor product sheaf as the sheafification
`F ⊗_{O_X} G = (F ⊗_{p, O_X} G)^#` of the tensor product presheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorRingedSpace.tensorCorepresentableBy
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product sheaf represents bilinear maps.** For every sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules
`ℋ`, morphisms `ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢 ⟶ ℋ` are in natural bijection with bilinear maps
`ℱ × 𝒢 → ℋ` of sheaves of `𝒪_X`-modules: `ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢` corepresents the functor
`ℋ ↦ Bilin_{𝒪_X}(ℱ × 𝒢, ℋ)`, which characterises it up to unique isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorCorepresentableBy :
    (bilinFunctor (Tensor.ringSheaf (structureSheaf X)) F G).CorepresentableBy
      (((Tensor.sheafTensor (structureSheaf X)).obj F).obj G)
declarations.comment:
the characterisation of `F ⊗_{O_X} G` as the sheaf of `O_X`-modules with
`Hom_{O_X}(F ⊗_{O_X} G, H) = Bilin_{O_X}(F × G, H)` for every `O_X`-module `H`, naturally in
`H`: the tensor product sheaf corepresents `H ↦ Bilin_{O_X}(F × G, H)`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorRingedSpace.tensorSymmetry
declarations.doc:
**The symmetry of the tensor product sheaf**: the canonical isomorphism
`ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢 ≅ 𝒢 ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℱ`, functorial in `ℱ` and `𝒢`, i.e. an isomorphism between the
tensor bifunctor and its flip. It is the sheafification of the sectionwise symmetry
`M ⊗_R N ≅ N ⊗_R M` of the tensor product of modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorSymmetry :
    Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (structureSheaf X) ≅
      (Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (structureSheaf X)).flip
declarations.comment:
the symmetry `F ⊗_{O_X} G = G ⊗_{O_X} F`, functorial in `F` and `G`: an
isomorphism of the tensor bifunctor with its flip, induced by the symmetry of tensor products of
modules

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorRingedSpace.tensorAssociativity
declarations.doc:
**The associativity of the tensor product sheaf**: the canonical isomorphism
`(ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒢) ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℋ ≅ ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_X} (𝒢 ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℋ)`, functorial in `ℱ`, `𝒢` and `ℋ`, i.e.
an isomorphism of trifunctors. It is induced through sheafification by the associativity of
tensor products of modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorAssociativity :
    bifunctorComp₁₂ (Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (structureSheaf X))
        (Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (structureSheaf X)) ≅
      bifunctorComp₂₃ (Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (structureSheaf X))
        (Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u} (structureSheaf X))
declarations.comment:
the associativity `(F ⊗_{O_X} G) ⊗_{O_X} H = F ⊗_{O_X} (G ⊗_{O_X} H)`,
functorial in `F`, `G` and `H`: an isomorphism of trifunctors, induced by the associativity of
tensor products of modules

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorStalkRingedSpace.tensorStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**The canonical `O_{X,x}`-linear isomorphism `(F ⊗_{O_X} G)_x ≅ F_x ⊗_{O_{X,x}} G_x`
(Stacks Tag 01CB).**  It is extracted (via `Classical.choice`) from `exists_tensorStalkIso`,
and is characterised on germs of pure tensors by `tensorStalkIso_germ` below.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorStalkIso (x : X.carrier)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    letI := stalkModule X
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
        (⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩ : Sheaf (JX X) CommRingCat.{u})).obj F).obj G).val x
    (grpStalk X ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
      (⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩ : Sheaf (JX X) CommRingCat.{u})).obj F).obj G)).val x) ≃ₗ[ringStalk X x]
      ((grpStalk X F.val x) ⊗[ringStalk X x] (grpStalk X G.val x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tensorSheafMap_epi_right
declarations.doc:
Tensoring an epimorphism of `O_X`-modules on the left by an `O_X`-module gives an
epimorphism. This is Tag 01CC in the second variable.
declarations.comment: exactness at the right term, second variable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorSheafMap_exact
declarations.doc:
Tensoring an exact pair of `O_X`-modules whose second map is an epimorphism
on the right by an `O_X`-module gives an exact pair.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSheafMap_exact
    (S : ShortComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    (hS : S.Exact) [Epi S.g] :
    let tensorFunctor :
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X) ×
          _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
          _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X) :=
      Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
        ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩)
    let firstMap := tensorFunctor.map ((S.f, 𝟙 G) : (S.X₁, G) ⟶ (S.X₂, G))
    let secondMap := tensorFunctor.map ((S.g, 𝟙 G) : (S.X₂, G) ⟶ (S.X₃, G))
    ∃ zeroComposite : firstMap ≫ secondMap = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk firstMap secondMap zeroComposite).Exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorSheafMap_epi
declarations.doc:
Tensoring an epimorphism of `O_X`-modules on the right by an
`O_X`-module gives an epimorphism.

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.comparisonBifunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01CD**, unconditionally: pulling back the tensor product of two sheaves of modules
on a ringed space is the tensor product of their pullbacks, naturally in both arguments.  This
is `Stacks.RingedSpace.comparisonIso` with its hypothesis discharged, so by
`Stacks.RingedSpace.comparison_unique` it is the only candidate.

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.comparisonBifunctorIso_hom_homEquiv_unit_tmul
declarations.doc:
**The canonicality clause of Stacks 01CD.**  The adjoint transpose of the forward map of
`comparisonBifunctorIso` at `(A, B)` carries the sheafification-unit image of a pure tensor to
the image, under the corresponding unit on `X`, of the tensor of the two pullback-unit
images.
declarations.statement:
lemma comparisonBifunctorIso_hom_homEquiv_unit_tmul
    (A B : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf Y)) (U : (Opens Y.carrier)ᵒᵖ)
    (a : A.val.obj U) (b : B.val.obj U) :
    Hom.app ((pullbackAdjunction f).homEquiv
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
            ⟨Y.presheaf, Y.IsSheaf⟩).obj A).obj B)
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
            ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj ((pullbackFunctor f).obj A)).obj
              ((pullbackFunctor f).obj B))
          ((comparisonBifunctorIso f).hom.app (A, B))).val U
        (Hom.app ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
          (R := Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ⟨Y.presheaf, Y.IsSheaf⟩)
          (𝟙 (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ⟨Y.presheaf, Y.IsSheaf⟩).obj)).unit.app
            (_root_.PresheafOfModules.tensorObj A.val B.val)) U (a ⊗ₜ b)) =
      Hom.app ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
        (R := Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩)
        (𝟙 (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj)).unit.app
          (_root_.PresheafOfModules.tensorObj ((pullbackFunctor f).obj A).val
            ((pullbackFunctor f).obj B).val))
        ((opensMap f).op.obj U) (pullbackUnit f A U a ⊗ₜ pullbackUnit f B U b)

declarations.name: Stacks.PullbackTensorIso.pullbackTensorIso
declarations.doc:
Stacks 01CD. For a morphism of ringed spaces `f : X ⟶ Y`, pullback of sheaves of
modules commutes with the tensor product: `f^*(A ⊗_{𝒪_Y} B) ≅ f^*A ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*B`, as an
isomorphism of bifunctors, so naturally in both module arguments. This is
`Stacks.RingedSpace.comparisonIso` with its instance hypothesis discharged, and by
`Stacks.RingedSpace.comparison_unique` the comparison is the only candidate.

`Stacks.RingedSpace.comparisonBifunctorIso` reaches the identical statement by the other
unconditional route — discharging the Tag 0098 stalk formula — and is the same isomorphism, both
forward maps being `Stacks.RingedSpace.comparisonNatTrans f`.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackTensorIso :
    Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨Y.presheaf, Y.IsSheaf⟩) ⋙
        Stacks.RingedSpace.pullbackFunctor f ≅
      Functor.prod (Stacks.RingedSpace.pullbackFunctor f)
          (Stacks.RingedSpace.pullbackFunctor f) ⋙
        Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.pullbackTensorObjRingedSpaceIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01CD, the pullback of a tensor product is the tensor product of the
pullbacks**, at the spelling of the tensor product that `K₀(Vect(X))` multiplies with. The
comparison morphism of Tag 01CD is an isomorphism, and its source and target are the two sides
spelled through the monoidal product of Tag 01CA, which is that spelling.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackTensorObjRingedSpaceIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (A B : Y.Modules) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj (Scheme.Modules.tensorObjRingedSpace Y A B) ≅
      Scheme.Modules.tensorObjRingedSpace X ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj A)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj B)
declarations.comment: the pullback of a tensor product of sheaves of modules on a scheme, read at the spelling of the tensor product that the Grothendieck ring of Tag 0FDK multiplies with

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorSheaf_nonempty_localGeneratorsData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CE (1).** On a ringed space, the tensor product of two sheaves of

This is Stacks 03L6 for local generation by sections,

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorSheaf_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CE (2).** On a ringed space, the tensor product of two sheaves of

This is Stacks 03L6 for the finite type condition,
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorLocalProperties.tensorSheaf_isFiniteType`, read at the site of

`SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType` already asks for a covering of the space.

theorem tensorSheaf_isFiniteType [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F]
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} G] :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u}
      ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨((X)).presheaf, ((X)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj (G)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorSheaf_isLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CE (7).** On a ringed space, the tensor product of two locally free
sheaves of modules is locally free.

Following the source: on a member of a covering trivializing both factors, `F` is free on a
basis `B_F` and `G` on a basis `B_G`, and the tensor product is free on `B_F × B_G`. The local
basis is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.localGeneratorsDataTensor`, which is built on the common
refinement of the two given coverings, and its members are bases by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFreeData_localGeneratorsDataTensor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSheaf_isLocallyFree [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree.{u, u, u} F]
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree.{u, u, u} G] :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
      ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨((X)).presheaf, ((X)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj (G)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorSheaf_isFinitePresentation

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.ringedSpaceAlgebras
declarations.doc:
**The tensor, exterior and symmetric algebras of a sheaf of modules on a ringed space**, as
the package Section 17.21 attaches to `F`: the three graded algebras, their three universal
properties, the identification of the homogeneous pieces of `T(F)` with the tensor powers of `F`,
the degree-zero identifications, the vanishing in negative degrees, the direct-sum presentation
and the two quotient maps `T(F) ⟶ ⋀(F)` and `T(F) ⟶ Sym(F)`. It is `SheafOfModules.algebras`,
i.e. `sheafifiedAlgebras`, at the site of open subsets of `X`, so each of the three algebras is
the degreewise sheafification of its sectionwise counterpart, which is the section's own
construction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ringedSpaceAlgebras (F : SheafOfModules.{w} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) F
declarations.comment: the construction of the three algebras themselves, for a sheaf of modules on a ringed space, which is the object the lemmas 01CG, 01CH, 01CJ, 01CK and 01CL of the section are statements about; the section has no finer tag for it

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.exteriorPower_isSheafification
declarations.doc:
For a sheaf of modules `M` on a site with a sheaf of
commutative rings `O♯`, and an exterior algebra `A` of `M` in the sense of Section 17.21, the
degree-`n` exterior power `A.piece n` of `M` is the sheafification of the presheaf
`X ↦ ⋀ⁿ_{O♯(X)}(M(X))`.

The presheaf is exhibited together with the sectionwise identification of its sections with
`⋀ⁿ_{O♯(X)}(M(X))` and the comparison morphism to `A.piece n`; the two equation families fix the
restriction maps and the comparison morphism on wedges of degree-one generators, and the last
conjunct is the sheafification assertion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorPower_isSheafification (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ P : PresheafOfModules.{w} (toRingCat J Osharp).obj,
      ∃ e : ∀ X : Cᵒᵖ, P.obj X ≃ₗ[(toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X]
          ⋀[(toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X]^n (M.val.obj X),
        ∃ cmp : P ⟶ (SheafOfModules.forget (toRingCat J Osharp)).obj (A.piece (n : ℤ)),
          (∀ (X Y : Cᵒᵖ) (f : X ⟶ Y) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj X)
              (x : ⋀[(toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X]^n (M.val.obj X))
              (y : ⋀[(toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj Y]^n (M.val.obj Y)),
            ((x : ExteriorAlgebra ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) (M.val.obj X)) =
                ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) n s) →
            ((y : ExteriorAlgebra ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj Y) (M.val.obj Y)) =
                ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj Y) n
                  fun i => M.val.map f (s i)) →
            e Y (P.map f ((e X).symm x)) = y) ∧
          (∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj X)
              (x : ⋀[(toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X]^n (M.val.obj X)),
            ((x : ExteriorAlgebra ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) (M.val.obj X)) =
                ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) n s) →
            Hom.app cmp X ((e X).symm x) =
              A.toPresheafGradedAlgebra.homogeneousProdLeft X n
                fun i => gen.val.app X (s i)) ∧
          IsIso ((sheafificationHomEquiv (𝟙 (toRingCat J Osharp).obj)).symm cmp)
declarations.comment: exterior_power_sheafification: the exterior assertion, that `⋀ⁿ M` is the sheafification of `X ↦ ⋀ⁿ(M(X))`, with the comparison pinned on wedges of degree-one local sections. The symmetric assertion is `SheafOfModules.symmetricPower_isSheafification`; the tag states those two and nothing else, so that pair is its covering set.

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.symmetricPower_isSheafification
declarations.doc:
**Tag 01CG.** For a sheaf of modules `M` on a site with a sheaf of commutative rings `O♯`, and
a symmetric algebra `A` of `M` in the sense of Section 17.21, the degree-`n` symmetric power
`A.piece n` of `M` is the sheafification of the presheaf `X ↦ Symⁿ_{O♯(X)}(M(X))`.

The presheaf is exhibited together with the sectionwise identification of its sections with
`Symⁿ_{O♯(X)}(M(X))` and the comparison morphism to `A.piece n`; the two equation families fix
the restriction maps and the comparison morphism on products of degree-one generators, and the
last conjunct is the sheafification assertion.

The symmetric algebra is a hypothesis rather than a chosen term: Section 17.21 pins it only up to
canonical isomorphism, and `SheafOfModules.sectionwiseSymmetricAlgebra` together with
`SheafOfModules.isSymmetricAlgebra_sectionwiseSymmetricAlgebra` and
`SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.IsSymmetricAlgebra.comp_iso` shows the hypothesis is satisfiable for
every `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem symmetricPower_isSheafification (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ P : PresheafOfModules.{w} (toRingCat J Osharp).obj,
      ∃ e : ∀ X : Cᵒᵖ, P.obj X ≃ₗ[(toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X]
          SymPow.symmetricPower n ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) (M.val.obj X),
        ∃ cmp : P ⟶ (SheafOfModules.forget (toRingCat J Osharp)).obj (A.piece (n : ℤ)),
          (∀ (X Y : Cᵒᵖ) (f : X ⟶ Y) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj X)
              (x : SymPow.symmetricPower n ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) (M.val.obj X))
              (y : SymPow.symmetricPower n ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj Y) (M.val.obj Y)),
            ((x : SymmetricAlgebra ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) (M.val.obj X)) =
                ∏ i : Fin n, SymmetricAlgebra.ι ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X)
                  (M.val.obj X) (s i)) →
            ((y : SymmetricAlgebra ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj Y) (M.val.obj Y)) =
                ∏ i : Fin n, SymmetricAlgebra.ι ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj Y)
                  (M.val.obj Y) (M.val.map f (s i))) →
            e Y (P.map f ((e X).symm x)) = y) ∧
          (∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj X)
              (x : SymPow.symmetricPower n ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) (M.val.obj X)),
            ((x : SymmetricAlgebra ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X) (M.val.obj X)) =
                ∏ i : Fin n, SymmetricAlgebra.ι ((toRingCat J Osharp).obj.obj X)
                  (M.val.obj X) (s i)) →
            Hom.app cmp X ((e X).symm x) =
              A.toPresheafGradedAlgebra.homogeneousProdLeft X n
                fun i => gen.val.app X (s i)) ∧
          IsIso ((sheafificationHomEquiv (𝟙 (toRingCat J Osharp).obj)).symm cmp)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.symmetricAlgebra_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Tag 01CH, ungraded symmetric assertion.** For a sheaf of modules `M` on a topological space
with a sheaf of commutative rings `O♯`, a symmetric algebra `A` of `M` in the sense of Section
17.21, and a point `x`, there is a canonical isomorphism of `O_x`-modules

`Sym(M)_x ≅ Sym_{O_x}(M_x)`,

where `Sym(M)` is the coproduct `∐ n, Symⁿ M` of the homogeneous pieces of `A`.

It is canonical in the sense Tag 01CH means: its value is prescribed on the germ of every local
section of the form `s₀ ⋯ sₙ₋₁`, in every degree `n`, namely the product of the germs of the
`sᵢ`; such products span each symmetric power of the stalk
(`SymmetricAlgebra.symmetricPower_eq_span_prod_ι`) and the symmetric powers span `Sym(M_x)`
(`SymmetricAlgebra.directSumSymmetricPowerEquiv`), so no other linear map has that behaviour.

The symmetric algebra is a hypothesis rather than a chosen term because Section 17.21 pins it
only up to canonical isomorphism;
`SheafOfModules.isSymmetricAlgebra_sectionwiseSymmetricAlgebra_val` shows the hypothesis is
satisfiable for every `M`, and
`SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras.symmetricAlgebraStalkEquiv` discharges it from a
package of the three algebras of Section 17.21.

The tag carries a clause comment: this declaration carries the ungraded symmetric assertion
alone. The two tensor assertions are `SheafOfModules.tensorPower_stalk` and
`SheafOfModules.tensorAlgebra_stalk` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.TensorPowerStalk`. The ungraded *exterior*
assertion `⋀(M)ₓ ≅ ⋀(Mₓ)` for a sheaf is `SheafOfModules.exteriorAlgebra_stalk` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorStalkUngraded`, which is built from
`SheafOfModules.natStalkCoprodEquiv` below exactly as this declaration is; the ungraded statement
for a **presheaf** of modules, `(⋀ F)ₓ ≅ ⋀(Fₓ)`, is `PresheafOfModules.extAlgStalkRingEquiv` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorPowerStalk` and the degreewise sheaf
statement is `PresheafOfModules.extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso` there.
declarations.statement:
theorem symmetricAlgebra_stalk (x : ↥X) :
    ∃ cmp : ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (∐ fun n : ℕ => A.piece (n : ℤ)).val.presheaf x)
        ≃ₗ[↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)]
        SymmetricAlgebra ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)
          ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Opens ↥X) (hx : x ∈ U) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)),
        cmp (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (∐ fun m : ℕ => A.piece (m : ℤ)).val.presheaf U x hx
            ((Sigma.ι (fun m : ℕ => A.piece (m : ℤ)) n).val.app (op U)
              (A.toPresheafGradedAlgebra.homogeneousProd (op U) n
                fun i => gen.val.app (op U) (s i)))) =
          ∏ i : Fin n, SymmetricAlgebra.ι ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)
            ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x)
            (TopCat.Presheaf.germ M.val.presheaf U x hx (s i))
declarations.comment: the ungraded symmetric assertion `Sym(M)ₓ ≅ Sym(Mₓ)`, with the isomorphism pinned down by its values on germs of products of local sections in every degree. The tensor assertions are `SheafOfModules.tensorPower_stalk` and `SheafOfModules.tensorAlgebra_stalk`; the ungraded exterior assertion `⋀(M)ₓ ≅ ⋀(Mₓ)` for a sheaf is `SheafOfModules.exteriorAlgebra_stalk` in `StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorStalkUngraded`, and the degreewise exterior assertion is `PresheafOfModules.extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso`. With those the three ungraded isomorphisms the source asserts are all proved

declarations.name: PresheafOfModules.extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**The stalk of a sheafification of the sectionwise exterior powers.** If `φ` exhibits `Q` as
having the same stalks as the presheaf `U ↦ ⋀ⁿ_{R(U)}(F(U))` — which the sheafification unit
does, by `PresheafOfModules.isIso_stalkFunctor_map_toSheafify` — then the stalk of `Q` at `x` is
`⋀ⁿ_{R_x}(F_x)`.

This is the form the exterior assertion of Stacks Tag 01CH is consumed in: the degree-`n`
exterior power of a sheaf of modules on a ringed space *is* the sheafification of the sectionwise
exterior powers, so taking `Q` to be that sheafification and `φ` its unit computes the stalk of
`⋀ⁿ F`. The isomorphism is pinned by `extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso_germ_ιMulti`, which is the
reason this and not an abstract uniqueness isomorphism is what the tag asserts.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso (n : ℕ)
    {Q : PresheafOfModules.{u} (R ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})}
    (φ : extPow n F ⟶ Q)
    (h : IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
      ((toPresheaf _).map φ))) :
    ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Q.presheaf x) ≃ₗ[↑(R.stalk x)]
      ⋀[↑(R.stalk x)]^n ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk F.presheaf x)
declarations.comment: the exterior assertion in each graded degree `n`: `(⋀ⁿ M)ₓ ≅ ⋀ⁿ(Mₓ)`, with the isomorphism pinned by `extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso_germ_ιMulti` as the map carrying the germ of a wedge of local sections to the wedge of their germs. The symmetric assertion is `PresheafOfModules.symPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso`. The graded-to-ungraded passage is not proved here; it is `SheafOfModules.exteriorAlgebra_stalk` in `StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorStalkUngraded`, which is the ungraded `⋀(M)ₓ ≅ ⋀(Mₓ)` that the source actually asserts.

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.exteriorAlgebra_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Tag 01CH, ungraded exterior assertion.** For a sheaf of modules `M` on a topological space
with a sheaf of commutative rings `O♯`, an exterior algebra `A` of `M` in the sense of Section
17.21, and a point `x`, there is a canonical isomorphism of `O_x`-modules

`⋀(M)_x ≅ ⋀_{O_x}(M_x)`,

where `⋀(M)` is the coproduct `∐ n, ⋀ⁿ M` of the homogeneous pieces of `A`.

It is canonical in the sense Tag 01CH means: its value is prescribed on the germ of every local
section of the form `s₀ ∧ ⋯ ∧ s_{n-1}`, in every degree `n`, namely the wedge of the germs of the
`sᵢ`; such wedges span each exterior power of the stalk
(`ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti_span_fixedDegree`) and the exterior powers span `⋀(M_x)`
(`ExteriorAlgebra.gradedAlgebra`), so no other linear map has that behaviour.

The exterior algebra is a hypothesis rather than a chosen term because Section 17.21 pins it only
up to canonical isomorphism; `SheafOfModules.isExteriorAlgebra_sectionwiseExteriorAlgebra_val`
shows the hypothesis is satisfiable for every `M`, and
`SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras.exteriorAlgebraStalkEquiv` discharges it from a
package of the three algebras of Section 17.21.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorAlgebra_stalk (x : ↥X) :
    ∃ cmp : ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (∐ fun n : ℕ => A.piece (n : ℤ)).val.presheaf x)
        ≃ₗ[↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)]
        ExteriorAlgebra ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)
          ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Opens ↥X) (hx : x ∈ U) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)),
        cmp (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (∐ fun m : ℕ => A.piece (m : ℤ)).val.presheaf U x hx
            ((Sigma.ι (fun m : ℕ => A.piece (m : ℤ)) n).val.app (op U)
              (A.toPresheafGradedAlgebra.homogeneousProd (op U) n
                fun i => gen.val.app (op U) (s i)))) =
          ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x) n
            fun i => TopCat.Presheaf.germ M.val.presheaf U x hx (s i)
declarations.comment: the ungraded exterior assertion `⋀(M)ₓ ≅ ⋀(Mₓ)` — one of the three isomorphisms the source asserts — with the isomorphism pinned down by its values on germs of wedges of local sections in every degree. The ungraded symmetric assertion `Sym(M)ₓ ≅ Sym(Mₓ)` is `SheafOfModules.symmetricAlgebra_stalk`. The ungraded tensor assertion `T(M)ₓ ≅ T(Mₓ)` is not covered here. The degreewise clauses, which are this library's convention and not assertions of the source, are `SheafOfModules.symmetricPower_stalk` and `PresheafOfModules.extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso`.

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.symmetricPower_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Tag 01CH, symmetric clause, in graded degree `n`.** For a sheaf of modules `M` on a
topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings `O♯`, a symmetric algebra `A` of `M` in the
sense of Section 17.21, and a point `x`, there is a canonical isomorphism of `O_x`-modules

`(Symⁿ M)_x ≅ Symⁿ_{O_x}(M_x)`.

It is canonical in the sense Tag 01CH means: its value is prescribed on the germ of every local
section of the form `s₀ ⋯ sₙ₋₁`, namely the product of the germs of the `sᵢ`, and such products
span the target (`SymmetricAlgebra.symmetricPower_eq_span_prod_ι`), so no other linear map has
that behaviour.

The symmetric algebra is a hypothesis rather than a chosen term because Section 17.21 pins it only
up to canonical isomorphism; `SheafOfModules.isSymmetricAlgebra_sectionwiseSymmetricAlgebra_val`
shows the hypothesis is satisfiable for every `M`, and
`SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras.symmetricPowerStalkEquiv` discharges it from a
package of the three algebras of Section 17.21.

The tag carries a clause comment: this declaration carries the symmetric degreewise assertion
alone. The ungraded symmetric assertion `Sym(M)_x ≅ Sym(M_x)` is proved from this one in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.AlgebraStalkUngraded`, and the two tensor
assertions are `SheafOfModules.tensorPower_stalk` and `SheafOfModules.tensorAlgebra_stalk` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.TensorPowerStalk`.

The exterior assertion in each graded degree is
`PresheafOfModules.extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorPowerStalk`, pinned on germs of wedges of
local sections by `PresheafOfModules.extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso_germ_ιMulti`. It is stated there
for a presheaf of modules together with a morphism out of the sectionwise exterior powers which
is a stalk isomorphism — the form a sheafification presentation supplies — rather than in the
bundled framing used here; `SheafOfModules.exteriorPowerStalkEquiv` in
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorStalkUngraded` is the bundled form, and
`SheafOfModules.exteriorAlgebra_stalk` there is the ungraded exterior assertion. See the
implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem symmetricPower_stalk (n : ℕ) (x : ↥X) :
    ∃ cmp : ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (A.piece (n : ℤ)).val.presheaf x)
        ≃ₗ[↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)]
        SymPow.symmetricPower n ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)
          ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x),
      ∀ (U : Opens ↥X) (hx : x ∈ U) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)),
        (cmp (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (A.piece (n : ℤ)).val.presheaf U x hx
              (A.toPresheafGradedAlgebra.homogeneousProd (op U) n
                fun i => gen.val.app (op U) (s i))) :
            SymmetricAlgebra ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)
              ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x)) =
          ∏ i : Fin n, SymmetricAlgebra.ι ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)
            ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x)
            (TopCat.Presheaf.germ M.val.presheaf U x hx (s i))
declarations.comment: the symmetric assertion in each graded degree `n`: `(Symⁿ M)ₓ ≅ Symⁿ(Mₓ)`, with the isomorphism pinned down by its values on germs of products of local sections. The ungraded `Sym(M)ₓ ≅ Sym(Mₓ)` is `SheafOfModules.symmetricAlgebra_stalk`; the exterior assertion in each degree is `PresheafOfModules.extPowStalkEquivOfStalkIso` and the ungraded `⋀(M)ₓ ≅ ⋀(Mₓ)` is `SheafOfModules.exteriorAlgebra_stalk`; the tensor assertions are `SheafOfModules.tensorPower_stalk` and `SheafOfModules.tensorAlgebra_stalk`. The three assertions the source makes are the ungraded ones; the degreewise statements, this one included, are this library's clause convention

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.tensorPower_stalk
declarations.doc:
For a sheaf of modules `M` on a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings `O♯`, a
tensor algebra `A` of `M` in the sense of Section 17.21, and a point `x`, there is an isomorphism
of `O_x`-modules

`(Tⁿ M)ₓ ≅ Tⁿ_{O_x}(M_x)`

sending the germ of every local section coming from an ordered tensor `s₀ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ s_{n-1}` to the
ordered tensor of the germs of the `sᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPower_stalk (n : ℕ) (x : ↥X) :
    ∃ cmp : ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (A.piece (n : ℤ)).val.presheaf x)
        ≃ₗ[↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)]
        TensorAlgebra.gradedPiece ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x) n
          ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x),
      ∀ (U : Opens ↥X) (hx : x ∈ U) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)),
        cmp (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (A.piece (n : ℤ)).val.presheaf U x hx
              (PresheafOfModules.Hom.app (tensorAlgPieceIso A gen hA (n : ℤ)).hom.val (op U)
                (PresheafOfModules.Hom.app (PresheafOfModules.sheafifyUnit
                    (toRingCatMap (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) (𝟙 Osharp.obj))
                    (PresheafOfModules.tensorPow n M.val)) (op U)
                  (TensorAlgebra.ιMultiPow
                    ((Osharp.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}).obj (op U)) n s)))) =
          TensorAlgebra.ιMultiPow ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x) n
            fun i => TopCat.Presheaf.germ M.val.presheaf U x hx (s i)
declarations.comment: the tensor assertion in each graded degree `n`: `(Tⁿ M)ₓ ≅ Tⁿ(Mₓ)` for a sheaf of modules, with the isomorphism pinned down by its values on germs of ordered tensors of local sections. The ungraded `T(M)ₓ ≅ T(Mₓ)` is `SheafOfModules.tensorAlgebra_stalk`; the symmetric assertions are `SheafOfModules.symmetricPower_stalk` and `SheafOfModules.symmetricAlgebra_stalk`; the exterior assertion is not carried here

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.tensorAlgebra_stalk
declarations.doc:
For a sheaf of modules `M` on a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings `O♯`, a
tensor algebra `A` of `M` in the sense of Section 17.21, and a point `x`, there is an isomorphism
of `O_x`-modules

`T(M)ₓ ≅ T_{O_x}(M_x)`,

where `T(M)` is the coproduct `∐ n, Tⁿ M` of the homogeneous pieces of `A`, sending the germ of
every local section coming from an ordered tensor `s₀ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ s_{n-1}`, in every degree `n`, to the
ordered tensor of the germs of the `sᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorAlgebra_stalk (x : ↥X) :
    ∃ cmp : ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (∐ fun n : ℕ => A.piece (n : ℤ)).val.presheaf x)
        ≃ₗ[↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)]
        TensorAlgebra ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x)
          ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk M.val.presheaf x),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Opens ↥X) (hx : x ∈ U) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)),
        cmp (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (∐ fun m : ℕ => A.piece (m : ℤ)).val.presheaf U x hx
            ((Sigma.ι (fun m : ℕ => A.piece (m : ℤ)) n).val.app (op U)
              (PresheafOfModules.Hom.app (tensorAlgPieceIso A gen hA (n : ℤ)).hom.val (op U)
                (PresheafOfModules.Hom.app (PresheafOfModules.sheafifyUnit
                    (toRingCatMap (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) (𝟙 Osharp.obj))
                    (PresheafOfModules.tensorPow n M.val)) (op U)
                  (TensorAlgebra.ιMultiPow
                    ((Osharp.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}).obj (op U)) n s))))) =
          TensorAlgebra.ιMulti ↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk Osharp.obj x) n
            fun i => TopCat.Presheaf.germ M.val.presheaf U x hx (s i)
declarations.comment: the ungraded tensor assertion `T(M)ₓ ≅ T(Mₓ)`, with the isomorphism pinned down by its values on germs of ordered tensors of local sections in every degree. The degreewise `(Tⁿ M)ₓ ≅ Tⁿ(Mₓ)` is `SheafOfModules.tensorPower_stalk`; the symmetric assertions are `SheafOfModules.symmetricPower_stalk` and `SheafOfModules.symmetricAlgebra_stalk`; the exterior assertion is not carried here

declarations.name: Stacks.PullbackExteriorAlgebra.exteriorAlgebraPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01CI for the exterior algebra of a sheaf of modules.** For a morphism of ringed
spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` and a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules `M`, the pullback of the exterior algebra of `M`
is canonically isomorphic to the exterior algebra of `f^*M`, degreewise and on the underlying
direct-sum sheaf, compatibly with the products, the units and the degree-one generators.

This covers the **exterior algebra** clause of Tag 01CI only. The tensor-algebra clause is
`Stacks.PullbackAlgebra.pullbackTensorPieceIso` and `pullbackTensorSheafIso`; the
symmetric-algebra clause is **not** proved here. Both exterior algebras are given by their
universal properties (`SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.IsExteriorAlgebra`) rather than by a
construction, so nothing here depends on an unconstructed exterior algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def exteriorAlgebraPullbackIso (hA : IsExteriorAlgebra A ι)
    (hB : IsExteriorAlgebra B κ) : ExteriorAlgebraPullbackIso f A ι B κ
declarations.comment: pullback_exterior_algebra: the EXTERIOR algebra clause only; symmetric NOT proved

declarations.name: Stacks.PullbackExteriorAlgebra.exteriorAlgebraPullbackIso_unique
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of Stacks 01CI is unique.** Compatibility with multiplication, with the
unit and with the degree-one generators on the pullback-unit sections determines the comparison
in every degree, and the restriction to the homogeneous summands then determines the comparison
of the underlying direct-sum sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorAlgebraPullbackIso_unique (hA : IsExteriorAlgebra A ι)
    (hB : IsExteriorAlgebra B κ) (e : ExteriorAlgebraPullbackIso f A ι B κ) :
    e = exteriorAlgebraPullbackIso f A ι B κ hA hB
declarations.comment: pullback_exterior_algebra: canonicality of the EXTERIOR algebra comparison only

declarations.name: Stacks.PullbackAlgebra.pullbackTensorPieceIso
declarations.doc:
The pullback of the degree-`n` piece of the tensor algebra of `F` is the degree-`n` piece of
the tensor algebra of `f^*F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackTensorPieceIso (n : ℕ) :
    (pullbackFunctor f).obj (S.tensor.piece (n : ℤ)) ≅ T.tensor.piece (n : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the tensor algebra only. The exterior and symmetric algebras are NOT proved here; see the implementation notes for the two missing inputs.

declarations.name: Stacks.PullbackAlgebra.pullbackTensorSheafIso
declarations.doc:
The pullback of the underlying direct-sum sheaf of the tensor algebra of `F` is the
underlying direct-sum sheaf of the tensor algebra of `f^*F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackTensorSheafIso :
    (pullbackFunctor f).obj S.tensorAlgebraSheaf ≅ T.tensorAlgebraSheaf
declarations.comment: the tensor algebra only, on the underlying direct-sum sheaf. The exterior and symmetric algebras are NOT proved here.

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.pullbackSymmetricPieceIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01CI for the symmetric algebra.** For a morphism of ringed spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` and
a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules `F`, the pullback of the degree-`n` symmetric power of `F` is the
degree-`n` symmetric power of `f^*F`:

`f^*(Symⁿ F) ≅ Symⁿ(f^*F)`.

The two symmetric algebras are given by their universal property, so this is a statement about
*the* symmetric algebras and not about one construction of them.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackSymmetricPieceIso (hA : IsSymmetricAlgebra A ι)
    (hB : IsSymmetricAlgebra B κ) (n : ℤ) :
    (pullbackFunctor f).obj (A.piece n) ≅ B.piece n

declarations.name: Stacks.RingedSpace.pullbackSymmetricPieceIsoOfRingedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01CI for the symmetric algebra, at the constructed symmetric algebras.** For a
morphism of ringed spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` and a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules `F`, the pullback of the
degree-`n` symmetric power of `F` is the degree-`n` symmetric power of `f^*F`, both taken in
`SheafOfModules.ringedSpaceAlgebras`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackSymmetricPieceIsoOfRingedSpace
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf Y)) (n : ℤ) :
    (pullbackFunctor f).obj ((SheafOfModules.ringedSpaceAlgebras Y G).symmetric.piece n) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.ringedSpaceAlgebras X
        ((pullbackFunctor f).obj G)).symmetric.piece n
declarations.comment: symmetric algebra, at the constructed symmetric algebras

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.ExtPresentation.epi_extDesc_app
declarations.doc:
**The surjectivity clause of Stacks Tag 01CJ for exterior powers.** If `p : M₁ ⟶ M` is an
epimorphism of sheaves of modules on a space, `A'` is an exterior algebra of `M₁` and `B'` an
exterior algebra of `M`, then the induced map `⋀ⁿ(M₁) ⟶ ⋀ⁿ(M)` is an epimorphism in every degree.
This is the clause `⟶ 0` of the sequence Tag 01CJ asserts.

The hypothesis `n ≥ 1` of the source is not needed: the statement holds in degree `0` too, where
both powers are the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement: theorem epi_extDesc_app [Epi p] (n : ℕ) : Epi ((extDesc ι κ hA' hB' p).app (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: exterior case, surjectivity clause: the second map of the sequence is an epimorphism, in every degree and with no exactness hypothesis. Exactness at the middle term is covered, by `SheafOfModules.ExtPresentation.exteriorPresentation_exact` below, which carries that clause and states the sequence of the source. The symmetric counterparts are `SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.epi_symDesc_app` and `SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.symmetricPresentation_exact`.

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.ExtPresentation.exteriorPresentation_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01CJ for exterior powers.** Let `M₂ --q--> M₁ --p--> M ⟶ 0` be a presentation of
a sheaf of modules on a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings — `p` an epimorphism
and the complex exact at `M₁` — let `A'` be an exterior algebra of `M₁` and `B'` one of `M`. Then
for every `k` the three-term sequence

`M₂ ⊗ ⋀^k(M₁) ⟶ ⋀^{k+1}(M₁) ⟶ ⋀^{k+1}(M) ⟶ 0`

is exact at the middle term and its second map is an epimorphism, which is the exactness the
source asserts in every degree `n = k + 1 ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exteriorPresentation_exact (hS : (ShortComplex.mk q p hqp).Exact) [Epi p] (k : ℕ) :
    (extComplex ι κ hA' hB' p q hqp k).Exact ∧
      Epi (extComplex ι κ hA' hB' p q hqp k).g
declarations.comment: exterior case, in full: the sequence `M₂ ⊗ ⋀^k(M₁) ⟶ ⋀^{k+1}(M₁) ⟶ ⋀^{k+1}(M) ⟶ 0` is exact at the middle term and its second map is an epimorphism. The surjectivity clause alone, in every degree and with no exactness hypothesis, is `SheafOfModules.ExtPresentation.epi_extDesc_app`. With the symmetric pair `SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.epi_symDesc_app` and `SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.symmetricPresentation_exact` this completes the tag: the source states the two clauses for the symmetric and the exterior powers and nothing else.

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.epi_symDesc_app
declarations.doc:
**The surjectivity clause of Stacks Tag 01CJ for symmetric powers.** If `p : M₁ ⟶ M` is an
epimorphism of sheaves of modules on a space, `A'` is a symmetric algebra of `M₁` and `B'` a
symmetric algebra of `M`, then the induced map `Symⁿ(M₁) ⟶ Symⁿ(M)` is an epimorphism in every
degree. This is the clause `⟶ 0` of the sequence Tag 01CJ asserts.

The hypothesis `n ≥ 1` of the source is not needed: the statement holds in degree `0` too, where
both powers are the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement: theorem epi_symDesc_app [Epi p] (n : ℕ) : Epi ((symDesc ι κ hA' hB' p).app (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: symmetric case, surjectivity clause: the second map of the sequence is an epimorphism, in every degree and with no exactness hypothesis. Exactness at the middle term is covered, by `SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.symmetricPresentation_exact` in `StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.SymmetricPresentationExact`, which carries that clause and states the sequence of the source. The exterior case is covered too, by `SheafOfModules.ExtPresentation.epi_extDesc_app` and `SheafOfModules.ExtPresentation.exteriorPresentation_exact` in `StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorPresentationExact`; those four declarations are the tag's covering set.

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.symmetricPresentation_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01CJ for symmetric powers.** Let `M₂ --q--> M₁ --p--> M ⟶ 0` be a presentation of
a sheaf of modules on a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings — `p` an epimorphism
and the complex exact at `M₁` — let `A'` be a symmetric algebra of `M₁` and `B'` one of `M`. Then
for every `k` the three-term sequence

`M₂ ⊗ Sym^k(M₁) ⟶ Sym^{k+1}(M₁) ⟶ Sym^{k+1}(M) ⟶ 0`

is exact at the middle term and its second map is an epimorphism, which is the exactness the
source asserts in every degree `n = k + 1 ≥ 1`.

The tag carries a clause comment: the surjectivity clause is also carried, at greater generality,
by `SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.epi_symDesc_app`, and the exterior half of Tag 01CJ is not
proved anywhere. See this file's implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem symmetricPresentation_exact (hS : (ShortComplex.mk q p hqp).Exact) [Epi p] (k : ℕ) :
    (symComplex ι κ hA' hB' q p hqp k).Exact ∧ Epi (symComplex ι κ hA' hB' q p hqp k).g
declarations.comment: symmetric case, in full: the sequence `M₂ ⊗ Sym^k(M₁) ⟶ Sym^{k+1}(M₁) ⟶ Sym^{k+1}(M) ⟶ 0` is exact at the middle term and its second map is an epimorphism. The surjectivity clause alone, in every degree and with no exactness hypothesis, is `SheafOfModules.SymPresentation.epi_symDesc_app`. The exterior case is covered too, by `SheafOfModules.ExtPresentation.epi_extDesc_app` and `SheafOfModules.ExtPresentation.exteriorPresentation_exact` in `StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.ExteriorPresentationExact`; those four declarations are the tag's covering set

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.exact_and_epi_symmetricPresentationShortComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01CJ, symmetric powers.** Let `M₂ --q--> M₁ --p--> M --> 0` be an exact
sequence of sheaves of modules on a ringed site, and let `n = 1 + k` with `k ≥ 0`. Then

`M₂ ⊗ Sym^k(M₁) ⟶ Symⁿ(M₁) ⟶ Symⁿ(M) ⟶ 0`

is exact: the complex is exact at the middle term and its second map is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_and_epi_symmetricPresentationShortComplex (q : M₂ ⟶ M₁) (p : M₁ ⟶ M)
    (hqp : q ≫ p = 0) [Epi p] (hex : (ShortComplex.mk q p hqp).Exact)
    (k n : ℤ) (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hn : 1 + k = n) :
    (GradedAlgebra.symmetricPresentationShortComplex
        (isSymmetricAlgebra_sheafifiedSymmetricAlgebra J M₁)
        (isSymmetricAlgebra_sheafifiedSymmetricAlgebra J M).isUniversal.1
        q p hqp k n hn).Exact ∧
      Epi (GradedAlgebra.symmetricPresentationShortComplex
        (isSymmetricAlgebra_sheafifiedSymmetricAlgebra J M₁)
        (isSymmetricAlgebra_sheafifiedSymmetricAlgebra J M).isUniversal.1
        q p hqp k n hn).g

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_exteriorPower
declarations.doc:
**Each exterior power of positive degree of a coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
coherent.** This is clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the exterior powers. The kernel `K` of
the quotient map `Tⁿ(F) ⟶ ⋀ⁿ(F)` is of finite type over each member of a cover presenting `F`
finitely, by Tag 01BP; hence coherent by Tag 01BY (1), since it is a subsheaf of the coherent
sheaf `Tⁿ(F)`; hence `⋀ⁿ(F)` is coherent by Tag 01BY (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_exteriorPower [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) F) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent (A.exteriorPower n)
declarations.comment: exterior powers of a coherent module, in positive degree

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFinitePresentation_exteriorPower
declarations.doc:
**Each exterior power of a sheaf of modules of finite presentation on a ringed space is of
finite presentation.** The covering family is the one that presents `F` finitely; no degree needs
a smaller open, because
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isFinite_presentation_exteriorPower_over` presents every degree
finitely over that same open. This is clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the exterior
powers.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_exteriorPower [F.IsFinitePresentation] (n : ℕ) :
    (A.exteriorPower n).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: exterior powers of a module of finite presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFree_symmetricPower
declarations.doc:
**Each symmetric power of a locally free sheaf of modules is locally free.** This is clause
(6) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the symmetric powers: a covering trivialising `F` with index types
`γ i` trivialises `Symⁿ F` with index types the degree-`n` multidegrees in `γ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFree_symmetricPower
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras J F) (n : ℕ)
    [hF : F.IsLocallyFree] : (A.symmetricPower n).IsLocallyFree
declarations.comment: symmetric powers of a locally free module

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFree_exteriorPower
declarations.doc:
**Each exterior power of a locally free sheaf of modules is locally free.** This is clause
(6) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the exterior powers: a covering trivialising `F` with index types
`γ i` trivialises `⋀ⁿ F` with index types the `n`-element subsets of `γ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFree_exteriorPower
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras J F) (n : ℕ)
    [hF : F.IsLocallyFree] : (A.exteriorPower n).IsLocallyFree
declarations.comment: exterior powers of a locally free module

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFree_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Each tensor power of a locally free sheaf of modules is locally free.** This is clause (6)
of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the tensor powers: a covering trivialising `F` with index types `γ i`
trivialises `Tⁿ F` with index types the `n`-fold products of the `γ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFree_tensorPower
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras J F) (n : ℕ)
    [hF : F.IsLocallyFree] : (A.tensor.piece (n : ℤ)).IsLocallyFree
declarations.comment: tensor powers of a locally free module

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_localGeneratorsData_symmetricPower
declarations.doc:
**Each symmetric power of a sheaf of modules locally generated by sections on a ringed space
is locally generated by sections.** This is clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the symmetric
powers.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_localGeneratorsData_symmetricPower
    (hF : Nonempty (F.LocalGeneratorsData.{u, u, u, u})) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((A.symmetricPower n).LocalGeneratorsData.{u, u, u, u})
declarations.comment: symmetric powers of a module locally generated by sections

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_localGeneratorsData_exteriorPower
