declarations.doc:
**Each exterior power of a sheaf of modules locally generated by sections on a ringed space is
locally generated by sections.** This is clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the exterior
powers.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_localGeneratorsData_exteriorPower
    (hF : Nonempty (F.LocalGeneratorsData.{u, u, u, u})) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((A.exteriorPower n).LocalGeneratorsData.{u, u, u, u})
declarations.comment: exterior powers of a module locally generated by sections

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteType_symmetricPower
declarations.doc:
**Each symmetric power of a sheaf of modules of finite type on a ringed space is of finite
type.** This is clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the symmetric powers: the covering is the one
on which `F` is generated by finitely many sections, and the index type produced in degree `n` is
the set of degree-`n` multidegrees in the given one, hence finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_symmetricPower
    [hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F] (n : ℕ) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} (A.symmetricPower n)
declarations.comment: symmetric powers of a module of finite type

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteType_exteriorPower'
declarations.doc:
**Each exterior power of a sheaf of modules of finite type on a ringed space is of finite
type.** This is clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the exterior powers. The primed name
distinguishes it from `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteType_exteriorPower`, which assumes `F` of
finite presentation and is therefore not this clause.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_exteriorPower'
    [hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F] (n : ℕ) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} (A.exteriorPower n)
declarations.comment: exterior powers of a module of finite type

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_symmetricPower
declarations.doc:
**Each symmetric power of a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
quasi-coherent.** A presentation of the module over an open presents every symmetric power of it
over that same open, by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_presentation_symmetricPower_over`, so the
covering family which presents the module presents the symmetric power too.
declarations.statement: theorem isQuasicoherent_symmetricPower (n : ℕ) : (A.symmetricPower n).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: symmetric powers of a quasi-coherent module

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_symmetricPower
declarations.doc:
**Each symmetric power of positive degree of a coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
coherent.** This is clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the symmetric powers. The sequence used
is `⊕_{p < n - 1} Tⁿ(F) ⟶ Tⁿ(F) ⟶ Symⁿ(F) ⟶ 0`, whose first term is coherent by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_tensorPower` and `isCoherent_sigma`, so that closure of
coherence under cokernels finishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_symmetricPower [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) F) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent (A.symmetricPower n)
declarations.comment: symmetric powers of a coherent module, in positive degree

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFinitePresentation_symmetricPower
declarations.doc:
**Each symmetric power of a sheaf of modules of finite presentation on a ringed space is of
finite presentation.** This is clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the symmetric powers. The
covering family is the one that presents `F` finitely; no degree needs a smaller open, because
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isFinite_presentation_symmetricPower_over` presents every degree
finitely over that same open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_symmetricPower [F.IsFinitePresentation] (n : ℕ) :
    (A.symmetricPower n).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: symmetric powers of a module of finite presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Each tensor power of positive degree of a coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
coherent.** This is clause (4) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the tensor powers.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_tensorPower [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) F) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent (A.tensor.piece (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: tensor powers of a coherent module, in positive degree

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFinitePresentation_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Each tensor power of a sheaf of modules of finite presentation on a ringed space is of
finite presentation.** This is clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01CK] for the tensor powers. The
covering family is the one that presents `F` finitely; no degree needs a smaller open, because
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isFinite_presentation_tensorPiece_over` presents every degree
finitely over that same open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_tensorPower [F.IsFinitePresentation] (n : ℕ) :
    (A.tensor.piece (n : ℤ)).IsFinitePresentation
declarations.comment: tensor powers of a module of finite presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_localGeneratorsData_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
Each tensor power of a sheaf of modules locally generated by sections on a ringed space is
locally generated by sections, on the same covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_localGeneratorsData_tensorPower
    (hF : Nonempty (F.LocalGeneratorsData.{t, t, t, t})) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((A.tensor.piece (n : ℤ)).LocalGeneratorsData.{t, t, t, t})
declarations.comment: tensor powers of a module locally generated by sections

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteType_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
Each tensor power of a sheaf of modules of finite type on a ringed space is of finite
type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_tensorPower [hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{t, t, t} F] (n : ℕ) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{t, t, t} (A.tensor.piece (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: tensor powers of a module of finite type

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Each tensor power of a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
quasi-coherent.** This is clause (5) of Stacks Tag 01CK for the tensor powers. A presentation of
`F` over an open presents `Tⁿ(F)` over that same open, by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_presentation_tensorPower_over`, so the covering family which
presents `F` presents each tensor power too.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_tensorPower {X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{t, t}}
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{t} (structureSheafRing X)) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) F) (n : ℕ) :
    (A.tensor.piece (n : ℤ)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: tensor powers of a quasi-coherent module

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_exteriorPower
declarations.doc:
**Each exterior power of a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
quasi-coherent.** A presentation of the module over an open presents every exterior power of it
over that same open, by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_presentation_exteriorPower_over`, so the
covering family which presents the module presents the exterior power too.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_exteriorPower {X : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) F) (n : ℕ) :
    (A.exteriorPower n).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: exterior powers of a quasi-coherent module

declarations.name: Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Every homogeneous piece of `Sym(E)` is quasi-coherent, for `E` a quasi-coherent module on
an arbitrary scheme.** This discharges the hypothesis
`Stacks.SymGraded.IsQuasicoherentPieces` of `Stacks.SymGraded.schemeSheafGradedAlgebra` and of
`Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle` for a quasi-coherent module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent {X : Scheme.{u}} (E : X.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] : IsQuasicoherentPieces E
declarations.comment: symmetric powers of a quasi-coherent module, at the encoding Stacks.SymGraded.schemeSymAlgebra

declarations.name: Stacks.SliceAlgebra.isQuasicoherent_sheafifiedSymmetricPiece
declarations.doc:
**Symmetric powers of a quasi-coherent module are quasi-coherent.** For a quasi-coherent sheaf
of modules `F` on a scheme `X` and `n : ℕ`, the degree-`n` piece of the symmetric algebra of `F` is
quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem SliceAlgebra.isQuasicoherent_sheafifiedSymmetricPiece (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (n : ℕ) :
    ((sheafifiedSymmetricAlgebra (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥X) F).piece
      (n : ℤ)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: symmetric powers of a quasi-coherent module

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFree_symmetricAlgebraSheaf_of_isLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**The symmetric algebra of a locally free sheaf of modules is locally free.** The covering
family is the one that trivialises `F`; no degree needs a smaller object of the site, because
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.symmetricPowerOverFreeIsoOfIsoFree` trivialises every degree over that
same object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFree_symmetricAlgebraSheaf_of_isLocallyFree :
    A.symmetricAlgebraSheaf.IsLocallyFree
declarations.comment: the symmetric algebra of a locally free module sheaf is locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFree_exteriorAlgebraSheaf_of_isLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**The exterior algebra of a locally free sheaf of modules is locally free.** The covering
family is the one that trivialises `F`, and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exteriorPowerOverFreeIsoOfIsoFree` trivialises every degree over the same
object of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFree_exteriorAlgebraSheaf_of_isLocallyFree :
    A.exteriorAlgebraSheaf.IsLocallyFree
declarations.comment: the exterior algebra of a locally free module sheaf is locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFree_tensorAlgebraSheaf_of_isLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**The tensor algebra of a locally free sheaf of modules is locally free.** The covering
family is the one that trivialises `F`, and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_nonempty_iso_free_tensorPowerOver` trivialises every degree over
the same object of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFree_tensorAlgebraSheaf_of_isLocallyFree :
    A.tensorAlgebraSheaf.IsLocallyFree
declarations.comment: the tensor algebra of a locally free module sheaf is locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_symmetricAlgebraSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The symmetric algebra of a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
quasi-coherent.** The covering family is the one that presents `F`; no degree needs a smaller
open, because
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_presentation_symmetricPower_over` presents every degree over
that same open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_symmetricAlgebraSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent :
    A.symmetricAlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the symmetric algebra of a quasi-coherent module sheaf is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_exteriorAlgebraSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The exterior algebra of a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
quasi-coherent.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_exteriorAlgebraSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent :
    A.exteriorAlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the exterior algebra of a quasi-coherent module sheaf is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_tensorAlgebraSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The tensor algebra of a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed space is
quasi-coherent.** This is the tensor assertion of Stacks Tag 01CL. The covering family is the one
that presents `F`; no degree needs a smaller open, because
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonempty_presentation_tensorPower_over` presents every degree over that
same open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_tensorAlgebraSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent
    {X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{t, t}}
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{t} (structureSheafRing X)) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (A : _root_.SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) F) :
    A.tensorAlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the tensor algebra of a quasi-coherent module sheaf is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.internalHomTensorIso
declarations.doc:
The sheaf-hom out of a tensor product is canonically the corresponding iterated sheaf-hom:
`ℋom(F ⊗ G, H) ≅ ℋom(F, ℋom(G, H))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def internalHomTensorIso
    (F G H : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    sheafHomSpace X (((Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj F).obj G) H ≅
      sheafHomSpace X F (sheafHomSpace X G H)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.internalHomTensorIso_hom_app_tmul
declarations.doc:
The canonical sheaf-hom isomorphism is currying: on every open, its evaluation on two
local sections agrees with evaluation on their pure tensor.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomTensorIso_hom_app_tmul
    (U : Opens X.carrier)
    (s : (sheafHomSpace X
      (((Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj F).obj G) H).val.obj (op U))
    (f : F.val.obj (op U)) (g : G.val.obj (op U)) :
    evalNestedInternalHomSection X U
        ((internalHomTensorIso X F G H).hom.val.app (op U) s) f g =
      evalTensorHomSection X U s f g

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
Giving a morphism `F ⊗ G ⟶ H` is canonically equivalent to giving a morphism
`F ⟶ ℋom(G, H)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorHomEquiv
    (F G H : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    (((Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj F).obj G ⟶ H) ≃ (F ⟶ sheafHomSpace X G H)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorHomEquiv_isTensorCurry
declarations.doc: The forward direction of `tensorHomEquiv` is the canonical currying map.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomEquiv_isTensorCurry
    (t : ((Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩).obj F).obj G ⟶ H) :
    IsTensorCurry X t (tensorHomEquiv X F G H t)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.internalHomTensorIso_natural_left
declarations.doc: The canonical isomorphism commutes with precomposition in its first argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomTensorIso_natural_left
    {F' : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)} (f : F' ⟶ F) :
    (internalHomTensorIso X F G H).hom ≫ sheafHomMapLeft X f =
      sheafHomMapLeft X ((Functor.uncurry.obj (Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩)).map
        ((f, 𝟙 G) : (_, _) ⟶ (_, _))) ≫
        (internalHomTensorIso X F' G H).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.internalHomTensorIso_natural_middle
declarations.doc: The canonical isomorphism commutes with precomposition in its second argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomTensorIso_natural_middle
    {G' : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)} (g : G' ⟶ G) :
    (internalHomTensorIso X F G H).hom ≫ sheafHomMapRight X (sheafHomMapLeft X g) =
      sheafHomMapLeft X ((Functor.uncurry.obj (Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf, X.IsSheaf⟩)).map
        ((𝟙 F, g) : (_, _) ⟶ (_, _))) ≫
        (internalHomTensorIso X F G' H).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.internalHomTensorIso_natural_right
declarations.doc: The canonical isomorphism commutes with postcomposition in its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomTensorIso_natural_right
    {H' : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)} (h : H ⟶ H') :
    sheafHomMapRight X h ≫ (internalHomTensorIso X F G H').hom =
      (internalHomTensorIso X F G H).hom ≫ sheafHomMapRight X (sheafHomMapRight X h)

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.internalHomTensorIso
registrations.comment: canonical_iso

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorHomEquiv
registrations.comment: in_particular

declarations.name: sheafHom_leftExact_fst
declarations.doc:
Left exactness of `SheafHom` in the first argument. Given an exact sequence
`F₂ --α--> F₁ --β--> F → 0` of `O_X`-modules (encoded as the exact `ComposableArrows`
`F₂ → F₁ → F → 0`, whose final node forces `β` epi), and internal homs `SheafHom(F,G)`,
`SheafHom(F₁,G)`, `SheafHom(F₂,G)` with induced precomposition maps `β* = mβ`, `α* = mα`
(morphisms of `O_X`-modules), the induced sequence of `O_X`-modules
  `0 → SheafHom(F, G) --β*--> SheafHom(F₁, G) --α*--> SheafHom(F₂, G)`
is exact in `SheafOfModules R` (`β*` is mono and `im β* = ker α*`).
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHom_leftExact_fst
    (F₂ F₁ F G : SheafOfModules.{v} (structureSheaf Rc)) (α : F₂ ⟶ F₁) (β : F₁ ⟶ F)
    (hin : (ComposableArrows.mk₃ α β (0 : F ⟶ 0)).Exact)
    (HF : SheafHom Rc F G) (HF₁ : SheafHom Rc F₁ G) (HF₂ : SheafHom Rc F₂ G)
    (mβ : HF.obj ⟶ HF₁.obj) (mα : HF₁.obj ⟶ HF₂.obj)
    (hmβ : SheafHom.IsPrecomp Rc β HF HF₁ mβ) (hmα : SheafHom.IsPrecomp Rc α HF₁ HF₂ mα) :
    (ComposableArrows.mk₃
      (0 : (0 : SheafOfModules.{v} (structureSheaf Rc)) ⟶ HF.obj) mβ mα).Exact

declarations.name: sheafHom_leftExact_snd
declarations.doc:
Left exactness of `SheafHom` in the second argument. Given an exact sequence
`0 → G --u--> G₁ --v--> G₂` of `O_X`-modules (encoded as the exact `ComposableArrows`
`0 → G → G₁ → G₂`, whose first node forces `u` mono), and internal homs `SheafHom(F,G)`,
`SheafHom(F,G₁)`, `SheafHom(F,G₂)` with induced postcomposition maps `u_* = mu`, `v_* = mv`
(morphisms of `O_X`-modules), the induced sequence of `O_X`-modules
  `0 → SheafHom(F, G) --u_*--> SheafHom(F, G₁) --v_*--> SheafHom(F, G₂)`
is exact in `SheafOfModules R` (`u_*` is mono and `im u_* = ker v_*`).
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHom_leftExact_snd
    (F G G₁ G₂ : SheafOfModules.{v} (structureSheaf Rc)) (u : G ⟶ G₁) (v : G₁ ⟶ G₂)
    (hin : (ComposableArrows.mk₃
      (0 : (0 : SheafOfModules.{v} (structureSheaf Rc)) ⟶ G) u v).Exact)
    (HG : SheafHom Rc F G) (HG₁ : SheafHom Rc F G₁) (HG₂ : SheafHom Rc F G₂)
    (mu : HG.obj ⟶ HG₁.obj) (mv : HG₁.obj ⟶ HG₂.obj)
    (hmu : SheafHom.IsPostcomp Rc u HG HG₁ mu) (hmv : SheafHom.IsPostcomp Rc v HG₁ HG₂ mv) :
    (ComposableArrows.mk₃
      (0 : (0 : SheafOfModules.{v} (structureSheaf Rc)) ⟶ HG.obj) mu mv).Exact

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SheafHomStalk.injective_sheafHomStalkLinearMap
declarations.doc:
**Injectivity half of Stacks 01CP.** For `F` of finite type the canonical map from the stalk
of the internal hom to the module of homomorphisms of the stalks is injective. Only local
generation by finitely many sections is used, which is exactly `LocalGenerators`; the relations
of a `LocalPresentation` are needed only for surjectivity.

This is `injective_sheafHomStalkLinearMap_of_localGenerators`, whose hypothesis is only that `F`
has local generators at `x`, applied to the generators that finite type produces there.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_sheafHomStalkLinearMap (H : SheafHom Rc F G) (x : X)
    [F.IsFiniteType] : Function.Injective (sheafHomStalkLinearMap H x)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SheafHomStalk.sheafHomStalkLinearEquivOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CP.** If `F` is of finite presentation, the canonical map from the
stalk of `SheafHom(F, G)` at `x` to the module of `O_{X,x}`-linear maps from `F_x` to `G_x` is an
isomorphism. The equivalence produced here is the canonical map `sheafHomStalkLinearMap H x`: its
`germ_apply` field records that it sends the germ of a local homomorphism and the germ of a local
section to the germ of the evaluation, and by `sheafHomStalkLinearMap_unique` that property
determines it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomStalkLinearEquivOfFinitePresentation
    (H : SheafHom Rc F G) (x : X) [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    SheafHomStalkLinearEquiv Rc F G H x

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHom_locallyKernelFiniteCoproduct
declarations.doc:
**The internal hom out of a finitely presented module is locally the kernel of a map
between finite direct sums of copies of the target.**
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHom_locallyKernelFiniteCoproduct [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∀ x : X, ∃ U : Opens X, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ m n : ℕ,
      ∃ f : (∐ fun _ : Fin m => G.over U) ⟶ (∐ fun _ : Fin n => G.over U),
        Nonempty ((sheafHom 𝒪 h𝒪 F G).over U ≅ kernel f)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHom_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**The internal hom out of a finitely presented module into a coherent module is
coherent.**
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHom_isCoherent [F.IsFinitePresentation] [IsCoherent G] :
    IsCoherent (sheafHom 𝒪 h𝒪 F G)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.exists_locally_isoKernel_sheafInternalHom
declarations.doc:
**The first clause of [Stacks, Tag 01CQ].** Let `(Y, 𝒪_Y)` be a ringed space and let `F`,
`G` be `𝒪_Y`-modules with `F` of finite presentation. Then `SheafHom(F, G)` is *locally a kernel
of a map between finite direct sums of copies of `G`*: every point of `Y` has an open
neighbourhood `U` for which `SheafHom(F, G)|_U` is the kernel of a morphism
`∐_{i < m} G|_U ⟶ ∐_{j < n} G|_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_locally_isoKernel_sheafInternalHom
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (spaceRingedSite O).O))
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] (y : Y) :
    ∃ U : Opens Y, y ∈ U ∧ ∃ (m n : ℕ)
      (f : (∐ fun _ : Fin m => G.over U) ⟶ (∐ fun _ : Fin n => G.over U)),
      Nonempty ((sheafInternalHom (spaceRingedSite O) F G).over U ≅ kernel f)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.isCoherent_sheafInternalHom
declarations.doc:
**The second clause of [Stacks, Tag 01CQ].** On a ringed space, the internal Hom from a
module of finite presentation into a coherent module is coherent. This combines the first clause
with the gluing step `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherent_of_locallyKernelFiniteCoproduct`.

The coherence predicate here is the one of
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/Coherent.lean`; for the one of
Stacks Tag 01BW see `isCoherent_sheafInternalHom'`, which is the same
statement and is deliberately left untagged so that the tag is not counted twice.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_sheafInternalHom
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (spaceRingedSite O).O))
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent
      (sheafInternalHom (spaceRingedSite O) F G)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.InternalHomLocalKernel.sheafHom_locallyKernelFiniteCoproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01CQ, first assertion, for a ringed space.** A sheaf Hom from a finitely presented
module is locally the kernel of a map between finite direct sums of copies of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHom_locallyKernelFiniteCoproduct
    (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (structureSheafRing X))
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ m n : ℕ,
        ∃ f : (∐ (fun _ : Fin m => G.over U)) ⟶ (∐ (fun _ : Fin n => G.over U)),
          Nonempty ((_root_.Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHom X.presheaf
              (structureSheafRing X).property F G).over
                U ≅
            (kernel f :
              _root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
                ((structureSheafRing X).over U)))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.InternalHomLocalKernel.sheafHom_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01CQ, second assertion, for a ringed space.** Internal Hom from a finitely
presented module into a coherent module is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHom_isCoherent
    (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (structureSheafRing X))
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] [G.IsCoherent] :
    (_root_.Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHom X.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X).property F G).IsCoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CS**, equivalently **Tag 0409 (2)**. A sheaf of `O`-modules is
*invertible* when its tensor functor is an equivalence. The universal property specifies that
tensor functor independently of any chosen construction of sheafification, hence on every
site; so the ringed-space form of the definition and the ringed-site form coincide here.
declarations.statement:
class IsInvertible
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsTrivial
declarations.doc:
An `O`-module sheaf is trivial when it is isomorphic, as an `O`-module, to `O`
itself.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev IsTrivial
    (L : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
      : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isIso_evaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040A (2), the evaluation clause.** For an invertible sheaf of
`𝒪`-modules `L` on a ringed site the evaluation pairing `SheafHom(L, 𝒪) ⊗_𝒪 L ⟶ 𝒪` is an
isomorphism.

The dual is a left dual of `L` by `exactPairingDualSheafOfIsInvertible`, and the evaluation of an
exact pairing is an isomorphism whenever tensoring on the right by the first object is an
equivalence, which for an invertible sheaf of modules it is.

A ringed space is a ringed site, so this is also the evaluation clause of Tag 01CT (2); see
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_evaluation_of_isInvertible` for that reading.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_evaluation [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] : IsIso (evaluation 𝒪 h𝒪 L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isIso_tensorSheafBraiding_hom_comp_evaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040A (2) and Tag 01CT (2), the evaluation clause in the order the tags
write it.** The evaluation map `L ⊗_𝒪 SheafHom(L, 𝒪) ⟶ 𝒪` is an isomorphism. It is the canonical
pairing of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.evaluation`, whose factors come in the order Tag 0FNV writes
them, preceded by the braiding of the tensor product sheaf, which is what exchanges the two
factors; in this order it is the trivializing pairing identifying `L^∨` as a tensor inverse of
`L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_tensorSheafBraiding_hom_comp_evaluation [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] :
    IsIso ((tensorSheafBraiding 𝒪 h𝒪 L (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 L)).hom ≫ evaluation 𝒪 h𝒪 L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isInvertible_dualSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 040A (2) and Tag 01CT (2), the invertibility clause.** The dual
`L^∨ = SheafHom(L, 𝒪)` of an invertible sheaf of `𝒪`-modules is again invertible: the evaluation
pairing is an isomorphism `L^∨ ⊗_𝒪 L ≅ 𝒪`, which is Tag 0B8K (2) for `L^∨`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_dualSheaf [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] :
    IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 (dualSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪 L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorProduct_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CT (1), Tag 040A (1).** The tensor product of two invertible sheaves
of modules is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorProduct_isInvertible
    (L N : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [IsInvertible O hO L] [IsInvertible O hO N] :
    IsInvertible O hO ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w}
      ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ O (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) hO⟩).obj L)).obj N)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorProduct_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CT**, part (1). The tensor product of two invertible sheaves of
modules is invertible: tensoring by it is the composite of the two tensor functors.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorProduct_isInvertible
    (L N : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O
      hO))
    [IsInvertible O hO L] [IsInvertible O hO N] :
    IsInvertible O hO (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w}
      ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ O (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) hO⟩).obj L).obj N)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.tensorPower
declarations.doc:
The `n`th tensor power of an invertible sheaf of modules `L`, for `n : ℤ`: the image of the
structure sheaf under the `n`th power of the autoequivalence given by tensoring by `L`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorPower
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [(((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w}
      ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ O (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
        hO⟩).flip.obj L)).IsEquivalence] (n : ℤ) :
    SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.isInvertible_tensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Every integer tensor power of an invertible sheaf of modules is invertible.** For
non-negative exponents this is Tag 01CT (1) and the successor comparison; for negative exponents
it is the same two inputs read backwards, cancelling the invertible factor `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_tensorPower [IsInvertible O hO L] (n : ℤ) :
    IsInvertible O hO (tensorPower O hO L n)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.mulIso_comm
declarations.doc:
**The commutativity normalisation of Tag 01CU**: the canonical multiplication on the integer
tensor powers of an invertible sheaf of modules agrees with itself after the symmetry constraint
of the tensor product sheaf. This was the last of the four normalisations of Tag 01CU still
outstanding.
declarations.statement:
theorem mulIso_comm (n m p : ℤ) (h : n + m = p) (h' : m + n = p) :
    mulIso O hO L n m p h =
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorSheafBraiding O hO (pow L n) (pow L m) ≪≫
        mulIso O hO L m n p h'

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.tensorPowerCoherence_exists
declarations.doc:
**The canonical multiplication on the integer tensor powers of an invertible sheaf of modules
exists and satisfies every normalisation asserted by Tag 01CU**: the two unit constraints, the
degree-`(n, 1)` normalisation by the defining iteration, naturality of that comparison,
associativity against the associativity constraint of the tensor product sheaf, and commutativity
against its symmetry constraint.

The multiplication is transported from `Stacks.MonoidalCategory.mul` by
`Stacks.MonoidalCategory.nonempty_powCoherence`, which is what absorbs the fact that the tensor
powers of Tag 01CU are built from `(Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor _).flip.obj L` while
the multiplication is built from `tensorRight`: the two functors are equal but their chosen
quasi-inverses, used by the negative exponents, have no common normal form.
declarations.statement: theorem tensorPowerCoherence_exists : Nonempty (TensorPowerCoherence O hO L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.braidingScalar_eq_id
declarations.doc:
The braiding scalar of the tensor powers of an invertible sheaf of modules is the identity,
in every degree.
declarations.statement: theorem braidingScalar_eq_id (n : ℤ) : braidingScalar O hO L n = 𝟙 _

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.mulIso_zero_left
declarations.doc:
**Multiplication by the zeroth tensor power on the left is the left unit constraint of the
tensor product sheaf.**
declarations.statement:
theorem mulIso_zero_left (n : ℤ) (h : 0 + n = n) :
    mulIso O hO L 0 n n h = Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorSheafLeftUnitor O hO (pow L n)
declarations.comment: left unit normalisation of the canonical multiplication

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.mulIso_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Associativity of the canonical multiplication, against the associativity constraint of the
tensor product sheaf.**
declarations.statement:
theorem mulIso_assoc (n m k p t s : ℤ) (h₁ : n + m = p) (h₂ : m + k = t) (h₃ : p + k = s) :
    tensorSheafMapIso O hO (mulIso O hO L n m p h₁) (Iso.refl (pow L k)) ≪≫
        mulIso O hO L p k s h₃ =
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorSheafAssociator O hO (pow L n) (pow L m) (pow L k) ≪≫
        tensorSheafMapIso O hO (Iso.refl (pow L n)) (mulIso O hO L m k t h₂) ≪≫
          mulIso O hO L n t s (by omega)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.tensorPowerMulIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical multiplication isomorphism `L^{⊗ n} ⊗_O L^{⊗ m} ≅ L^{⊗ (n + m)}`, the addition
law `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.powAdd` for the powers of `- ⊗ L` applied to the structure sheaf,
read through `powFunctorIsoTensorRight`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorPowerMulIso (n m : ℤ) :
    (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O) (forget₂
      CommRingCat RingCat) (hO)⟩).obj ((tensorPower O hO L n))).obj ((tensorPower
      O hO L m))) ≅
      tensorPower O hO L (n + m)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CU.** The `n`th tensor power `L^{⊗ n}` of an invertible sheaf `L`,
for `n` an arbitrary integer: the image of the structure sheaf under the `n`th power of the
right-tensor autoequivalence.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorPower
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [IsInvertible O hO L] (n : ℤ) :
    SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)

declarations.name: Stacks.SelfBraidingInvertible.braidingScalar_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**The braiding scalar of a tensor power of an invertible sheaf of modules is the identity**,
in every degree. By `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.tensorSheafBraiding_self_eq_refl_iff` this
is the commutativity constraint of Stacks Tag 01CU in degrees `(n, n)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem braidingScalar_eq_id (n : ℤ) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPower.braidingScalar 𝒪 h𝒪 L n = 𝟙 _

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorPowAddIso_zero_right_natCast
declarations.doc: The right unit constraint: multiplication by `L ^⊗ 0` on the right is the right unitor.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPowAddIso_zero_right_natCast (a : ℕ) :
    tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ) ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ) = ρ_ (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorPowAddIso_zero_left_natCast
declarations.doc: The left unit constraint: multiplication by `L ^⊗ 0` on the left is the left unitor.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPowAddIso_zero_left_natCast (b : ℕ) :
    tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ) (b : ℤ) ≪≫
        tensorPowNatCongrIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (Nat.zero_add b) =
      λ_ (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (b : ℤ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorPowAddIso_one_right_natCast
declarations.doc:
**The normalisation in degree one.** Multiplication by the first tensor power is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorPowOneIso` whiskered into `L ^⊗ a`, followed by the
successor step `L ^⊗ a ⊗ L = L ^⊗ (a + 1)` of the iteration which defines the powers; in
nonnegative degree that step is the identity. This is what pins the canonical multiplication
down: an associative family of multiplication isomorphisms is determined by its degree-`(a, 1)`
value.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPowAddIso_one_right_natCast (a : ℕ) :
    tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ) =
      whiskerLeftIso (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ)) (tensorPowOneIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorPowAddIso_assoc_natCast
declarations.doc:
**The associativity constraint on the multiplication of tensor powers**, which Stacks Tag
01CU asserts with the formulation omitted, in nonnegative degree and against the associator of
the monoidal structure on sheaves of modules itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPowAddIso_assoc_natCast (a b c : ℕ) :
    whiskerRightIso (tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ) (b : ℤ)) (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (c : ℤ)) ≪≫
        tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L ((a + b : ℕ) : ℤ) (c : ℤ) =
      α_ (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ)) (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (b : ℤ)) (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (c : ℤ)) ≪≫
        whiskerLeftIso (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ)) (tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (b : ℤ) (c : ℤ)) ≪≫
          tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ) ((b + c : ℕ) : ℤ) ≪≫
            tensorPowNatCongrIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (Nat.add_assoc a b c).symm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorPowAddIso_comm_natCast
declarations.doc:
**The commutativity constraint on the multiplication of tensor powers**, in nonnegative
degree.

At degrees `(1, 1)` the constraint *is* the triviality of the self-braiding of `L`, which holds
for every invertible `L` by the instance `Stacks.SelfBraidingInvertible.hasTrivialSelfBraiding`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPowAddIso_comm_natCast (a b : ℕ) :
    β_ (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ)) (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L (b : ℤ)) ≪≫
        tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (b : ℤ) (a : ℤ) =
      tensorPowAddIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (a : ℤ) (b : ℤ) ≪≫
        tensorPowNatCongrIso 𝒪 h𝒪 L (Nat.add_comm a b)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPowerCoherence_exists
declarations.doc:
**Existence of a coherent multiplication on the tensor powers.** The integer tensor powers of
an invertible sheaf of modules `L` carry coherent multiplication data
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.TensorPowerCoherence O hO L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorPowerCoherence_exists
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible O hO L] :
    Nonempty (TensorPowerCoherence O hO L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionRingStructure_exists
declarations.doc:
There is a graded ring structure on the section ring whose homogeneous product is tensor
multiplication.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionRingStructure_exists
    (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [IsInvertible O hO L] :
    Nonempty (SectionRingStructure O hO L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionModuleStructure_exists
declarations.doc:
There is a module structure of the section module over the section ring whose action on
homogeneous terms is tensor multiplication.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionModuleStructure_exists
    (L F : SheafOfModules.{w} (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [IsInvertible O hO L] :
    Nonempty (SectionModuleStructure O hO L F)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.sectionRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CV.** The *associated graded ring* `Γ_*(X, L)` of an invertible
sheaf of modules: the direct sum of the global sections of its non-negative tensor powers. Its
graded ring structure is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.homGradedRing`.
declarations.statement: abbrev sectionRing

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.twistedSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CV.** The graded module `Γ_*(X, L, F)` of a sheaf of modules `F`:
the direct sum, over all integers `n`, of the global sections of the twists `F ⊗ L^{⊗ n}`. Its
module structure over `Γ_*(X, L)` is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.twistedSectionsModule`.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.twistedSectionsGmodule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CV.** `Γ_*(X, L, F)` is a `ℤ`-graded module over the `ℕ`-graded
ring `Γ_*(X, L)`, with the action `twistedSectionsSMul` on homogeneous sections. No
commutativity of `Γ_*(X, L)` is used.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def twistedSectionsGmodule
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO)) :
    letI : GradedMonoid.GMonoid (fun n : ℕ =>
        𝟙_ (_root_.SheafOfModules.{w}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
            ⟶ tensorPower O hO L (n : ℤ)) := (tensorPowerSystem O hO L).gradedMonoid
    DirectSum.Gmodule
      (fun n : ℕ => 𝟙_ (_root_.SheafOfModules.{w}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
          ⟶ tensorPower O hO L (n : ℤ))
      (fun n : ℤ => 𝟙_ (_root_.SheafOfModules.{w}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
          ⟶ twist O hO L F n)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.homGradedCommRingOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CV: the associated graded ring
`Γ_*(X, L) = ⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, L^{⊗ n})` of an invertible sheaf of modules.** This is the
commutative graded ring on the morphism groups `𝟙 ⟶ L^{⊗ n}`, with the commutativity constraint
of Tag 01CU discharged by `tensorPowerMulIso_comm` above, so it is unconditional.

The direct sum itself needs no declaration of ours: Mathlib's `DirectSum.commRing` turns a
`DirectSum.GCommRing` on the family into a commutative ring on `⨁ n : ℕ, (𝟙 ⟶ L^{⊗ n})`, the
tensor unit *is* the structure sheaf on the nose (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorUnit_eq`) so the
summands are the global sections the tag names, and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.homToSection_sectionMul` identifies the multiplication with
the one already defined on `PresheafOfModules.sections`. This declaration alone is therefore the
covering set of the tag's first displayed object; the tag's second one, the `ℤ`-graded module
`Γ_*(X, L, F)`, is not claimed — see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homGradedCommRingOfInvertible :
    DirectSum.GCommRing (fun n : ℕ =>
      (𝟙_ (_root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O
        hO))
        ⟶ tensorPower O hO L (n : ℤ)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjTheta.sectionRingAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The two section rings of an invertible sheaf of modules have the same carrier.**

Degree by degree this is `powSectionsAddEquiv`: a morphism out of the monoidal unit into the
`natTensorPow` spelling of `L^{⊗ n}` against an honest section over `⊤_ C` of the `tensorPower`
spelling.
declarations.statement:
def sectionRingAddEquiv :
    Stacks.GradedSections.sectionRing L ≃+ Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionRing 𝒪 h𝒪 L
declarations.comment:
the repository's two realisations of the graded ring `Γ_*(X, L)` — the
`Stacks.GradedSections.sectionRing` one on morphisms out of the monoidal unit and the
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionRing` one on honest global sections — have the same carrier,
ADDITIVELY and degree by degree, and the grading corresponds
(`map_summand_eq_sectionRingGrading`). The two MULTIPLICATIONS are not identified BY THIS
DECLARATION, which is an `AddEquiv` and nothing more; they ARE identified, by
`Stacks.SectionRingProjTheta.sectionRingEquiv` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/SectionRingProjTheta/SectionRingMultiplicative.lean`, which is
this map with its multiplicativity supplied

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjTheta.sectionRingEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The two section rings of an invertible sheaf of modules are isomorphic as rings.** This is
`Stacks.SectionRingProjTheta.sectionRingAddEquiv` with its multiplicativity supplied; the
underlying function is unchanged, so every computation rule of that additive isomorphism applies
verbatim.
declarations.statement:
def sectionRingEquiv :
    Stacks.GradedSections.sectionRing L ≃+* Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionRing 𝒪 h𝒪 L
declarations.comment:
the repository's two realisations of the graded ring `Γ_*(X, L)` — the
`Stacks.GradedSections.sectionRing` one on morphisms out of the monoidal unit and the
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionRing` one on honest global sections — are isomorphic as RINGS, and
the isomorphism is graded (`sectionGradedRingHom`)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CV.** The section ring of an invertible sheaf `L`: the direct sum of
the global sections of the nonnegative tensor powers of `L`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev sectionRing (L : SheafOfModules.{w} (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [IsInvertible O hO L] : Type _

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CV.** The section module of a sheaf of modules `F`: the direct sum of
the global sections of all the twists of `F` by integer tensor powers of an invertible sheaf
`L`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev sectionModule (L F : SheafOfModules.{w} (TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    [IsInvertible O hO L] : Type _

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.homGradedRing
registrations.comment: graded ring multiplication

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.essentiallySmall_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CW.** The invertible sheaves of modules over the structure sheaf of
a ringed space have only a set of isomorphism classes: there is a set of invertible modules, of
size `max u w`, meeting every isomorphism class of invertible modules on the space.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentiallySmall_isInvertible (X : RingedSpace.{u, w}) :
    ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{max u w}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
        (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ X.presheaf
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}) X.IsSheaf))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_unique_representative_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CW.** There is a family of invertible modules over the structure
sheaf of a ringed space, indexed by a type of size `max u w`, whose members are pairwise
non-isomorphic and such that every invertible module on the space is isomorphic to the member of
exactly one index.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_representative_isInvertible (X : RingedSpace.{u, w}) :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u w)) (L : I → _root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf X.presheaf
          (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ X.presheaf
            (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}) X.IsSheaf))),
      (∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
          (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ X.presheaf
            (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}) X.IsSheaf) (L i)) ∧
      (∀ i j, Nonempty (L i ≅ L j) → i = j) ∧
      ∀ M, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
          (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ X.presheaf
            (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}) X.IsSheaf) M →
        ∃! i, Nonempty (M ≅ L i)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup
declarations.doc:
The Picard group of `O`: the group of isomorphism classes of
invertible sheaves of `O`-modules, as a small type.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def PicardGroup : Type (max (max u v) w)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.instAddCommGroupPicardGroup
declarations.doc:
The abelian group structure on the Picard group; its addition is the tensor product sheaf,
by `classOf_tensor`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instAddCommGroupPicardGroup : AddCommGroup (PicardGroup O hO)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.classOf_tensor
declarations.doc: Addition in the Picard group is the tensor product sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_tensor (L N : SheafOfModules.{w}
  (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    (hL : IsInvertible O hO L) (hN : IsInvertible O hO N)
    (hLN : IsInvertible O hO ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (hO)⟩).obj
        (L)).obj (N)))) :
    classOf O hO L hL + classOf O hO N hN =
      classOf O hO ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (hO)⟩).obj
          (L)).obj (N))) hLN

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.PicardGroup
declarations.doc:
The *Picard group* of a sheaf of rings `O` on a site: the abelian group whose elements are
the isomorphism classes of invertible sheaves of `O`-modules and whose addition is the tensor
product.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def PicardGroup : Type _

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.instAddCommGroupPicardGroup
declarations.doc:
The addition of the Picard group, induced by the tensor product of invertible sheaves of
modules.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instAddCommGroupPicardGroup : AddCommGroup (PicardGroup O hO)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc: Addition in the Picard group is the tensor product.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardClass_tensorSheaf (L N : SheafOfModules.{w}
  (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf O hO))
    (hL : IsInvertible O hO L) (hN : IsInvertible O hO N)
    (hLN : IsInvertible O hO ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (hO)⟩).obj
        (L)).obj (N)))) :
    picardClass O hO L hL + picardClass O hO N hN =
      picardClass O hO ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨O, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (O) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (hO)⟩).obj
          (L)).obj (N))) hLN

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.PicardGroup
declarations.doc:
**The Picard group of `𝒪`**, Stacks Tag 01CX: the isomorphism classes of *invertible*
sheaves of `𝒪`-modules, with multiplication induced by tensor product. It is realised as the
group of units of the monoid `ClassMonoid 𝒪 h𝒪` of all isomorphism classes; that these units
are exactly the invertible sheaves is `isInvertible_iff_isUnit`, and that every one of them is
the class of such a sheaf is `exists_classOf`.
declarations.statement: abbrev PicardGroup : Type _

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.commGroup
declarations.doc:
**The Picard group is an abelian group**, Stacks Tag 01CX. The structure is
`Units.instCommGroup` over `instCommMonoid`: no coherence law is proved by hand, because the
skeleton of a braided monoidal category is already a commutative monoid. The additive reading
the source sometimes uses is `Additive (PicardGroup 𝒪 h𝒪)`, and
`instAddCommGroupAdditivePicardGroup` records it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def commGroup : CommGroup (PicardGroup 𝒪 h𝒪)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.instAddCommGroupAdditivePicardGroup
declarations.doc: **The Picard group, written additively**, as Stacks Tag 01CX sometimes does.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instAddCommGroupAdditivePicardGroup :
    AddCommGroup (Additive (PicardGroup 𝒪 h𝒪))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.exists_classOf
declarations.doc:
**Every element of the Picard group is the class of an invertible sheaf of modules**, so
`classOf` is onto.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_classOf (x : PicardGroup 𝒪 h𝒪) :
    ∃ (M : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪)) (_ : IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 M),
      classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 M = x

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.classOf_eq_classOf_iff
declarations.doc: **Two invertible sheaves have the same Picard class exactly when they are isomorphic.**
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_eq_classOf_iff [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 N] :
    classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 L = classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 N ↔ Nonempty (L ≅ N)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.classOf_mul
declarations.doc: **Multiplication in the Picard group is tensor product**, Stacks Tag 01CX.
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_mul [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 N] :
    classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 (L ⊗ N) = classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 L * classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 N

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.classOf_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Multiplication in the Picard group is the tensor product sheaf**, Stacks Tag 01CX in the
spelling whose statement mentions no monoidal structure.
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_tensorSheaf [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 N]
    [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨𝒪, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (𝒪) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (h𝒪)⟩).obj (L)).obj
      (N)))] :
    classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
      ⟨𝒪, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (𝒪) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (h𝒪)⟩).obj (L)).obj
      (N))) = classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 L * classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 N

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.classOf_unit
declarations.doc:
**The neutral element of the Picard group is the class of the structure sheaf**, Stacks
Tag 01CX.
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_unit :
    classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪)) = 1

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.classOf_tensorInv
declarations.doc:
**The inverse of a Picard class is the class of the inverse sheaf**, Stacks Tag 01CT (2)
read in the Picard group of Stacks Tag 01CX.
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_tensorInv [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] :
    classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 (tensorInv 𝒪 h𝒪 L) = (classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 L)⁻¹

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.classOf_tensorPow
declarations.doc:
**The class of the `n`-th tensor power is the `n`-th power of the class**, for every
integer `n`. The powers are the integer tensor powers of Stacks Tag 01CU; this is the sense in
which the Picard group records them.
declarations.statement:
theorem classOf_tensorPow [IsInvertible 𝒪 h𝒪 L] (n : ℤ) :
    classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 (tensorPow 𝒪 h𝒪 L n) = classOf 𝒪 h𝒪 L ^ n

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.schemePicardGroup
declarations.doc:
**The Picard group `Pic X` of a scheme**: the isomorphism classes of invertible
`𝒪_X`-modules under tensor product.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev schemePicardGroup : Type (u + 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.schemeClassOf_eq_schemeClassOf_iff
declarations.doc:
**Two invertible `𝒪_X`-modules have the same Picard class exactly when they are
isomorphic.**
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeClassOf_eq_schemeClassOf_iff (L N : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X N] :
    schemeClassOf X L = schemeClassOf X N ↔ Nonempty (L ≅ N)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafPicardGroup.schemeClassOf_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc: **Multiplication in `Pic X` is tensor product.**
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeClassOf_tensorSheaf (L N : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X N]
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X
      ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf,
        Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
          ((Stacks.SheafInternalHom.isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf X))⟩).obj (L)).obj (N)))] :
    schemeClassOf X
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨X.presheaf,
          Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (X.presheaf) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
            ((Stacks.SheafInternalHom.isSheaf_structureRingPresheaf X))⟩).obj (L)).obj (N))) =
      schemeClassOf X L * schemeClassOf X N

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.picardClassOf_tensorObjRingedSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01CX, addition in `Pic(X)` is the tensor product**, at the spelling of the
tensor product that `K₀(Vect(X))` multiplies with.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardClassOf_tensorObjRingedSpace {X : Scheme.{u}} (L N : X.Modules)
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L)
    (hN : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 N)
    (hLN : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2
      (Scheme.Modules.tensorObjRingedSpace X L N)) :
    picardClassOf X (Scheme.Modules.tensorObjRingedSpace X L N) hLN =
      picardClassOf X L hL + picardClassOf X N hN
declarations.comment: addition in `Pic(X)` is the tensor product, read at the spelling of the tensor product that the Grothendieck ring of Tag 0FDK multiplies with

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isOpen_nonvanishingLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CY** (openness). For an invertible sheaf of modules on a ringed
space all of whose stalks are local rings, the nonvanishing locus of a global section is
open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_nonvanishingLocus
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    [IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheafRing X).property L] (s : L.sections) :
    IsOpen (nonvanishingLocus L s)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_tensorPairing_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CY** (inverse section). Let `L` be an invertible sheaf of modules on a
ringed space with local stalks, let `N` be a sheaf of modules with a trivialization
`ψ : L ⊗ N ≅ O_X`, and let `s` be a global section of `L`. Then over the nonvanishing open `X_s`
there is a section `b` of `N` with `ψ (s ⊗ b) = 1`.

Stacks states this for `N = L^{⊗ -1}`; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_tensorPairing_eq_one
    [IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheafRing X).property L] (s : L.sections) :
    ∃ b : N.val.obj (op (nonvanishingOpen L s)),
      tensorPairing ψ (nonvanishingOpen L s) (s.eval (op (nonvanishingOpen L s))) b
        = unitSection X (nonvanishingOpen L s)

declarations.name: Stacks.InverseSection.exists_tensorInv_section_pairing_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01CY, the inverse-section clause**, in the shape of the tagged statement: on the
nonvanishing open of a global section `s` of an invertible module, there is a section `t` of the
`(-1)`-st tensor power whose canonical tensor-power pairing with `s` evaluates to `1`.

The pairing is the one the tagged statement names: form the elementary tensor of `s`, read in the first
tensor power, with `t`; push it into the sheafified tensor product; apply the addition
isomorphism of Stacks Tag 01CU in degrees `1` and `-1`; reindex along `1 + (-1) = 0`. The tagged
statement then compares the result with `1` directly, its zeroth tensor power being the unit of
`SheafOfModules` on the nose; here the zeroth tensor power is the *sheafified* unit, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.tensorPowZeroIso` is inserted, and only then is the comparison
with `1 : 𝒪_X(X_s)` a statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_tensorInv_section_pairing_eq_one (s : L.sections) :
    ∃ t : (tensorPow X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L (-1)).val.obj
        (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s)),
      (tensorPowZeroIso X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L).hom.val.app
        (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s))
        ((tensorPowReindexIso X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L
            (show (1 : ℤ) + -1 = 0 by omega)).hom.val.app
          (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s))
          ((tensorPowAddIsoSheaf X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L
              1 (-1)).hom.val.app
            (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s))
            ((toSheafify X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property
                ((PresheafOfModules.tensorObj (O := X.sheaf.obj) ((powPre L 1))
                  ((powPre L (-1)))))).app
              (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s))
              ((tensorPowOneIso X.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L).inv.val.app
                  (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s))
                  (s.eval (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s)))
                ⊗ₜ[X.presheaf.obj
                    (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s))] t)))) =
      (1 : X.presheaf.obj
        (op (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X L s)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_over_nonvanishingOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01CY** (trivialization). For an invertible sheaf of modules `L` on a
ringed space all of whose stalks are local rings, and a global section `s` of `L`, the morphism
`𝒪_X ⟶ L` given by multiplication by `s` restricts to an isomorphism over the nonvanishing
locus `X_s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_over_nonvanishingOpen (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
    [IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheafRing X).property L] (s : L.sections) :
    IsIso ((L.unitHomEquiv.symm s).over (nonvanishingOpen L s))

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.Localization.isLocalization_stalk_localizationSheaf
declarations.doc:
At every point, the stalk of the sheafification of the sectionwise localization is the
localization of the original stalk at the germs of the prescribed denominators.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLocalization_stalk_localizationSheaf (D : PresheafLocalizationData.{u}) (x : D.X) :
    letI : Algebra (D.O.stalk x) ((localizationSheaf D).presheaf.stalk x) :=
      (toLocalizationSheafStalk D x).hom.toAlgebra
    IsLocalization (D.S.stalk x) ((localizationSheaf D).presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.Localization.existsUnique_lift_localizationPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01D0.** A morphism of presheaves of commutative rings which inverts every section
of the multiplicative subpresheaf `S` factors uniquely through the sectionwise localization at
`S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_localizationPresheaf (S : O.SubmonoidPresheaf) (f : O ⟶ A)
    (hf : ∀ (U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (s : S.obj U), IsUnit ((f.app U).hom (s : O.obj U))) :
    ∃! g : S.localizationPresheaf ⟶ A, S.toLocalizationPresheaf ≫ g = f

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.Localization.toLocalizationSheaf
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the sheafification of a presheaf of commutative rings to the
sheafification of its sectionwise localization.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toLocalizationSheaf (S : O.SubmonoidPresheaf) :
    (presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}).obj O ⟶
      (presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}).obj
        S.localizationPresheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.Localization.isUnit_toLocalizationSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01D0.** Every prescribed local denominator becomes invertible in the sheafified
localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnit_toLocalizationSheaf (S : O.SubmonoidPresheaf) (U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (s : S.obj U) :
    IsUnit (((toLocalizationSheaf S).hom.app U).hom
      (((toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) O).app U).hom (s : O.obj U)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.Localization.existsUnique_lift_localizationSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01D0.** A morphism out of the sheafification of `O` which inverts every prescribed
section factors uniquely through the sheafified localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_localizationSheaf (S : O.SubmonoidPresheaf) (A : X.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u})
    (f : (presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}).obj O ⟶ A)
    (hf : ∀ (U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (s : S.obj U),
      IsUnit ((f.hom.app U).hom
        (((toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) O).app U).hom (s : O.obj U)))) :
    ∃! g : (presheafToSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u}).obj
        S.localizationPresheaf ⟶ A,
      toLocalizationSheaf S ≫ g = f

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.Localization.sectionwiseLocalizedModuleIsoTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01D1, presheaf assertion.**

Any sectionwise localization of a presheaf of modules is canonically isomorphic to extension
of scalars from the original presheaf of rings to its sectionwise localization.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sectionwiseLocalizedModuleIsoTensor
    (O Oₛ : TopCat.Presheaf CommRingCat X) (α : O ⟶ Oₛ)
    (S : (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ) → Submonoid (O.obj U))
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{0} (ringPresheaf O))
    (Fₛ : PresheafOfModules.{0} (ringPresheaf Oₛ))
    (ι : F ⟶ Stacks.Sheafify.ChangeOfRingsAdjunction.restrictPresheaf O Oₛ α Fₛ)
    (hO : IsSectionwiseLocalization O Oₛ α S)
    (hF : IsSectionwiseLocalizedModule O Oₛ α S F Fₛ ι) :
    Fₛ ≅ tensorPresheafOfModules O Oₛ α F

declarations.name: Stacks.Presheaf.Localization.sheafificationSectionwiseLocalizedModuleIsoTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01D1, sheaf assertion.**

If `O` and `F` are sheaves, sheafifying a sectionwise localization `Fₛ` along a
sheafification `Oₛ ⟶ Oₛ♯` gives the tensor product of `F` with `Oₛ♯` over `O`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafificationSectionwiseLocalizedModuleIsoTensor
    (O : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat X) (Oₛ : TopCat.Presheaf CommRingCat X)
    (Oₛ' : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat X) (α : O.presheaf ⟶ Oₛ) (σ : Oₛ ⟶ Oₛ'.presheaf)
    (S : (U : (TopologicalSpace.Opens X)ᵒᵖ) → Submonoid (O.presheaf.obj U))
    (F : SheafOfModules (ringSheaf O))
    (Fₛ : PresheafOfModules (ringPresheaf Oₛ))
    (ι : F.val ⟶ Stacks.Sheafify.ChangeOfRingsAdjunction.restrictPresheaf O.presheaf Oₛ α Fₛ)
    (hO : IsSectionwiseLocalization O.presheaf Oₛ α S)
    (hF : IsSectionwiseLocalizedModule O.presheaf Oₛ α S F.val Fₛ ι)
    (hσi : Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (Stacks.Sheafify.ChangeOfRingsAdjunction.ringPresheafMap Oₛ Oₛ'.presheaf σ))
    (hσs : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (Stacks.Sheafify.ChangeOfRingsAdjunction.ringPresheafMap Oₛ Oₛ'.presheaf σ)) :
    (moduleSheafificationAlong (Stacks.Sheafify.ChangeOfRingsAdjunction.ringPresheafMap Oₛ
      Oₛ'.presheaf σ) hσi hσs).obj Fₛ ≅
      tensorSheaf O Oₛ'
        ((fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat).homEquiv.symm
          (α ≫ σ)) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01D3, part (2).** A morphism of ringed topoi: a morphism of the underlying topoi
together with a map from the structure sheaf of the target to the direct image of the structure
sheaf of the source.
declarations.statement:
structure RingedToposHom (X : RingedTopos.{v, u, w}) (Y : RingedTopos.{v', u', w'})
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w})]
    [Y.J.HasSheafCompose (forget RingCat.{w'})]
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    [Y.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w'} RingCat.{w'})]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp_assoc
declarations.doc: **Composition of morphisms of ringed topoi is associative.**
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_assoc (f : RingedToposHom X Y) (g : RingedToposHom Y Z) (h : RingedToposHom Z W) :
    h.comp (g.comp f) = (h.comp g).comp f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedTopos
declarations.doc: A site with a sheaf of commutative rings.
declarations.statement: structure RingedTopos.{v₁, u₁, w₁}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01D3, part (2).** A morphism of ringed topoi `X ⟶ Y`: a morphism of topoi
between the underlying topoi together with a map of sheaves of commutative rings
`O_Y ⟶ f_* O_X`.

The geometric morphism is presented by a continuous functor `u : Y.C ⥤ X.C` between the
underlying sites in the opposite direction, as in the source's convention for a morphism of
sites; `RingedToposSiteHom.toToposHom` produces the morphism of topoi itself as soon as `u` is a
morphism of sites. This is the generality in which the pullback of sheaves of modules of
Stacks 03D6 is available.
declarations.statement: structure RingedToposSiteHom (X : RingedTopos.{v, u, w}) (Y : RingedTopos.{v', u', w})
declarations.comment:
part (2): morphisms of ringed topoi, with the geometric morphism presented by
a continuous functor between the underlying sites rather than by an arbitrary adjoint pair;
`RingedToposHom.toToposHom` produces the underlying morphism of topoi once that functor is a
morphism of sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01D3, part (3).** Composition of morphisms of ringed topoi: the underlying
continuous functors compose, and the structure map is
`O_Z ⟶ g_* O_Y ⟶ g_* f_* O_X = (g ∘ f)_* O_X`, the last identification being the canonical
one of `CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp`.
declarations.statement: def comp (g : RingedToposSiteHom Y Z) (f : RingedToposSiteHom X Y) : RingedToposSiteHom X Z
declarations.comment: part (3): composition of morphisms of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of two morphisms of ringed topoi: the underlying morphisms of topoi compose,
and the structure map of the composite is
`O_Z ⟶ g_*O_Y ⟶ g_*f_*O_X ≅ (g ∘ f)_*O_X`, the last step being the canonical comparison of
successive direct images with the direct image of the composite.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def comp (g : RingedToposHom Y Z) (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    RingedToposHom X Z

declarations.name: AddCommGrpCat.injective_iff_divisible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01D7.** An abelian group is an injective object in the category of abelian groups
if and only if it is divisible.

Divisibility is Baer's criterion over `ℤ`: an injective group is Baer, and dividing `x` by `n`
is extending to `ℤ` the map `nℤ → J` determined by `n ↦ x`. Conversely a divisible group is
injective, which is Mathlib's `AddCommGrpCat.injective_of_divisible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem AddCommGrpCat.injective_iff_divisible (J : Type u) [AddCommGroup J] :
    Injective (C := AddCommGrpCat) (AddCommGrpCat.of J) ↔ Nonempty (DivisibleBy J ℕ)

declarations.name: CharacterModule.dualFunctor
declarations.doc:
The contravariant functor `M ↦ M^∨ = Hom_ℤ(M, ℚ/ℤ)` on modules over a commutative ring,
acting on a linear map by precomposition (`CharacterModule.dual`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualFunctor (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    (ModuleCat.{u} R)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R

declarations.name: freeModuleCoverFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor sending an `R`-module `M` to the natural epimorphism `F(M) → M`, where `F(M)` is
the free module on the underlying set of `M`. Landing in the full subcategory of the arrow
category spanned by the epimorphisms retains the surjectivity of each cover.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def freeModuleCoverFunctor (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    ModuleCat.{u} R ⥤ (MorphismProperty.epimorphisms (ModuleCat.{u} R)).Arrow ⊤ ⊤
declarations.comment: the free module on the underlying set of a module, with its natural surjection

declarations.name: CharacterModule.dualFunctor_exact
declarations.doc: The contravariant character-dual functor on modules over a commutative ring is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualFunctor_exact (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    exactFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R)ᵒᵖ (ModuleCat.{u} R) (dualFunctor R)

declarations.name: CharacterModule.eval_injective
declarations.doc:
The canonical evaluation map from an additive commutative group into its double character
module is injective.

theorem eval_injective (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] :

declarations.name: jModule_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01DC, Lemma 15.56.8.**
For every `R`-module `M` (with `R` commutative), the `R`-module `J(M) = (F(M^∨))^∨` is
injective. This is `characterModule_finsupp_injective` for the index type `M^∨`.
declarations.statement:
theorem jModule_injective (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] :
    Module.Injective R (JModule R M)

declarations.name: moduleCat_hasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01DD.** The canonical maps `M → J(M) = (F(M^∨))^∨` form a covariant
functor from `R`-modules to arrows of `R`-modules whose source projection is the identity, each
of whose components is a monomorphism, and each of whose targets is an injective module.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleCat_hasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings :
    IsFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings₁ (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (jModuleArrowFunctor R) ∧
      IsFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings₂ (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (jModuleArrowFunctor R) ∧
        IsFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings₃ (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (jModuleArrowFunctor R)

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.SheafificationTowerFactorization.exists_extension_towerIota_succ
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be an abelian sheaf and `α ≤ β` a non-maximal stage of the tower, so that
`α + 1 ≤ β` as well. Let `ι : G₁ ⟶ G₂` be an injective (i.e. monomorphic) map of abelian sheaves
and let `f : G₁ ⟶ J_α(F)` be a morphism. Then there is a morphism `g : G₂ ⟶ J_{α+1}(F)` making
the square with the transition map `ι_{α,α+1} : J_α(F) ⟶ J_{α+1}(F)` commute, i.e.
`ι ≫ g = f ≫ ι_{α,α+1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_extension_towerIota_succ (β : Ordinal.{u}) (α : Set.Iic β) (hα : ¬ IsMax α)
    (F : AbSheaf J) {G₁ G₂ : AbSheaf J} (ι : G₁ ⟶ G₂) [Mono ι]
    (f : G₁ ⟶ towerObj J β α F) :
    ∃ g : G₂ ⟶ towerObj J β (Order.succ α) F,
      ι ≫ g = f ≫ towerIota J β (Order.le_succ α) F

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.SheafificationTowerFactorization.exists_ordinal_towerFactorsThrough
declarations.doc:
Let `{G i}_{i : I}` be a set of abelian sheaves on `C`. There is an ordinal `β`, depending
only on `J` and the family `{G i}`, such that for every abelian sheaf `F`, every index `i`, and
every morphism `φ : G i → J_β(F)`, there is an ordinal `α < β` such that `φ` factors through
`J_α(F)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ordinal_towerFactorsThrough {I : Type u} (G : I → AbSheaf J) :
    ∃ β : Ordinal.{u},
      ∀ (F : AbSheaf J) (i : I) (φ : G i ⟶ towerTop J β F),
        ∃ (α : Set.Iic β) (h : (α : Ordinal) < β),
          TowerFactorsThrough J β
            (le_of_lt (show α < (⟨β, le_refl β⟩ : Set.Iic β) from h)) F (G i) φ

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.BaerCriterion.injective_of_extends_freeAbSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒥` be a sheaf of abelian groups such that for every object `X` of `C`, every abelian
subsheaf `S ⊆ Z_X^#`, and every morphism `φ : S → 𝒥`, there exists a morphism `ψ : Z_X^# → 𝒥`
extending `φ`. Then `𝒥` is an injective sheaf of abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_of_extends_freeAbSheaf
    (𝒥 : Sheaf J Ab.{u})
    (H : ∀ (X : C) (S : AbelianSubsheaf J (freeAbSheaf J X)) (φ : S.sheaf ⟶ 𝒥),
      ∃ ψ : freeAbSheaf J X ⟶ 𝒥, Extends J S φ ψ) :
    IsInjectiveSheaf J 𝒥

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.shortExact_internalHomMapLeft_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01DR] for sheaves of modules, on the ideal sequence.** For an injective sheaf
of `𝒪_Y`-modules `K` the internal Hom `𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(-, K)` carries `0 ⟶ ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ 0` to a
short exact sequence

`0 ⟶ 𝓗om(𝒪_X, K) ⟶ 𝓗om(𝒪_Y, K) ⟶ 𝓗om(ℐ, K) ⟶ 0`.

Exactness at the middle term and the left-hand monomorphism are the left exactness of internal
Hom in the first variable, [Stacks, Tag 0GMY] part (1); the right-hand epimorphism is where the
injectivity of `K` is spent, through `epi_internalHomMapLeft_ι`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma shortExact_internalHomMapLeft_of_injective
    (K : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.sheaf)) [Injective K] :
    (ShortComplex.mk
      ((internalHomMapLeftNatTrans Y.sheaf (cokernel.π I.ι)).app K)
      ((internalHomMapLeftNatTrans Y.sheaf I.ι).app K)
      (by
        rw [← NatTrans.comp_app, internalHomMapLeftNatTrans_comp, cokernel.condition,
          internalHomMapLeftNatTrans_zero]
        rfl)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: for sheaves of modules on a ringed space, against the sequence of a sheaf of ideals; the library's `Stacks.Injectives.AbelianDual.dualFunctor_shortExact_of_injective` is the statement for the abelian-sheaf internal Hom against an injective abelian sheaf instead

declarations.name: internalHom_exact_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Stacks Tag 01DR, abelian-sheaf level).**
Let `J` be an injective abelian sheaf on a site `(C, K)`. Then the contravariant
internal-Hom functor `ℋom(-, J)` is exact: for every short exact sequence
`0 → F' → F → F'' → 0` of abelian sheaves, encoded as a short complex `S` with
`S.ShortExact`, the contravariantly induced short complex
`(ℋom(-, J)) ∘ Sᵒᵖ`, i.e. `0 → ℋom(F'', J) → ℋom(F, J) → ℋom(F', J) → 0`,
is again short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHom_exact_of_injective (K : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasSheafify K Ab.{max u v}]
    (J : Sheaf K Ab.{max u v}) [Injective J]
    (S : ShortComplex (Sheaf K Ab.{max u v})) (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    (S.op.map (internalHomFunctor K J)).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.AbelianDual.dualFunctor_shortExact_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01DR (Lemma 19.8.1), the statement itself.** The functor `F ↦ F^∨`, with its
natural `O`-module structure, is exact when `J` is an injective abelian sheaf: it carries a
short exact sequence of sheaves of `O`-modules to a short exact sequence of sheaves of
`O`-modules.

The source's proof is "this because `J` is an injective abelian sheaf", and that is exactly how
this runs: exactness of the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves (Stacks 03DA) reduces the
claim to `internalHom_exact_of_injective` above, which is where the injectivity of `J` is
spent.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualFunctor_shortExact_of_injective
    [HasSheafify K Ab.{max u v}] [K.WEqualsLocallyBijective Ab.{max u v}]
    (O : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{max u v}) (J : Sheaf K Ab.{max u v}) [Injective J]
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u v} (underlyingRingSheaf O)))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    letI := (dualFunctorData O J).preservesZero
    (S.op.map (dualFunctor O J)).ShortExact
