**Stacks Project, Tag 01F5.** The canonical comparison from the derived direct image of a
composite to the composite of the derived direct images is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem higherDirectImagesComparison_isIso {X Y Z : RingedSpace.{u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (Modules X)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (Modules Y)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wZ} (Modules Z)]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    IsIso (higherDirectImagesComparison f g)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeLerayPlus.relativeLeraySpectralSequencePlus
declarations.doc:
**Relative Leray spectral sequence for bounded below complexes**, [Stacks, Tag 01F6].  For
each bounded below complex of `𝒪_X`-modules there is a bounded spectral sequence with second
page `R ᵖ g_*(H^q(R f_* K))`, vanishing in the left half plane, abutting to
`H ⁿ(R (f ≫ g)_* K)` by a finite filtration.

This is `exists_spectralSequence_relativeLerayPlus` with the spectral sequence chosen for each
complex; the four propositional clauses are the content, and all four are proved there.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeLeraySpectralSequencePlus :
    RelativeLeraySpectralSequencePlusData f g

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeLeray.exists_spectralSequence_relativeLeray
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01F6] for a bounded below complex.** For morphisms of ringed spaces
`f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` and an object `M` of `D⁺(X)` there is a filtered complex `K` of
`𝒪_Z`-modules with `H^n(K) ≅ H^n(R(g ∘ f)_* M)` in every degree, whose filtration is finite in
each degree and whose spectral sequence `E`, presented as in [Stacks, Tag 012M] by its pages
`Z_r^{p,q}/D_r^{p,q}`, has

`E₂^{p,q} ≅ R^p g_*(H^q(Rf_* M))`,

is bounded, induces a finite filtration on each `H^n(K)`, and converges to `H^*(K)`.

This is the source's *"there is a version for bounded below complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules"*, and it
is the primary form: the module statement `exists_spectralSequence_relativeLeray_obj` is this one
at `M := ℱ[0]`. It is [Stacks, Tag 015N] for the pair `(f_*, g_*)`, whose hypothesis is
`rightAcyclic_modulePushforward_obj_of_injective`, with the abutment rewritten from
`H^n(R(g_* ∘ f_*) M)` to `H^n(R(g ∘ f)_* M)` along
`Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeMayerVietoris.pushforwardCompIso`.

**The tag's functoriality in `ℱ` is not included**, which is why the attribute carries a clause;
see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_spectralSequence_relativeLeray
    (M : DerivedCategory.Plus (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    ∃ K : FilteredObject (CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Z)) ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ,
      (∀ n : ℤ, Nonempty (K.X.homology n ≅
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ n).obj
          ((modulePushforward (f ≫ g)).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj M))) ∧
      K.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite ∧
      ∀ (Fil : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ p n : ℤ, Fil p n = Subobject.mk ((K.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n))
        (Zc : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Zc r p n =
          Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (K.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (Fil (p + r) (n + 1)))
        (Dc : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Dc r p n = Zc (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
          (Subobject.«exists» (K.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Zc (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1)))
        (FH : ∀ (n _p : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.homology n))
        (_ : ∀ n p : ℤ, FH n p =
          imageSubobject (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)),
      ∃ (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Z)) 0)
        (_ : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q), (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
          cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : Dc r p n ⊓ Zc r p n ≤ Zc r p n))),
        (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty ((E.page 2 zero_le_two).X (p, q) ≅
          ((modulePushforward g).rightDerivedPlus p).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ q).obj
              ((modulePushforward f).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj M)))) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((E.page 0).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ FH n a = ⊤ ∧ FH n b = ⊥) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r), b ≤ r →
          (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) = 0) ∧
        (∀ p n : ℤ,
          IsGLB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
              Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (K.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (Fil (p + r) (n + 1)) ⊔
                Fil (p + 1) n)
            (kernelSubobject (K.X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ Fil p n ⊔ Fil (p + 1) n) ∧
          IsLUB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
              Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.«exists» (K.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Fil (p - r) (n - 1)) ⊔
                Fil (p + 1) n)
            (imageSubobject (K.X.d (n - 1) n) ⊓ Fil p n ⊔ Fil (p + 1) n))
declarations.comment: the spectral sequence for a bounded below complex, not its functoriality

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeLeray.exists_spectralSequence_relativeLeray_obj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01F6], the relative Leray spectral sequence for a module.** For morphisms of
ringed spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` and an `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` there is a spectral sequence
with

`E₂^{p,q} ≅ R^p g_*(R^q f_* ℱ)`

converging to `R^{p+q}(g ∘ f)_* ℱ`, in the presentation and convergence convention of
[Stacks, Tag 012M] and [Stacks, Tag 015N]. No hypothesis on `f`, on `g` or on `ℱ`.

This is `exists_spectralSequence_relativeLeray` at the complex `ℱ[0]`: the `E₂` term and the
abutment of that statement are *definitionally* `R^p g_*(R^q f_* ℱ)` and `R^n(g ∘ f)_* ℱ` there,
because `Functor.rightDerivedPlus i` is `singleFunctor 0 ⋙ rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
homologyFunctor i` by definition.

**The tag's functoriality in `ℱ` is not included**; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_spectralSequence_relativeLeray_obj
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    ∃ K : FilteredObject (CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Z)) ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ,
      (∀ n : ℤ, Nonempty (K.X.homology n ≅
        ((modulePushforward (f ≫ g)).rightDerivedPlus n).obj F)) ∧
      K.filtration.IsDegreewiseFinite ∧
      ∀ (Fil : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ p n : ℤ, Fil p n = Subobject.mk ((K.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n))
        (Zc : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Zc r p n =
          Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (K.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (Fil (p + r) (n + 1)))
        (Dc : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.X n))
        (_ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Dc r p n = Zc (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
          (Subobject.«exists» (K.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Zc (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1)))
        (FH : ∀ (n _p : ℤ), Subobject (K.X.homology n))
        (_ : ∀ n p : ℤ, FH n p =
          imageSubobject (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n)),
      ∃ (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Z)) 0)
        (_ : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q), (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
          cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : Dc r p n ⊓ Zc r p n ≤ Zc r p n))),
        (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty ((E.page 2 zero_le_two).X (p, q) ≅
          ((modulePushforward g).rightDerivedPlus p).obj
            (((modulePushforward f).rightDerivedPlus q).obj F))) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((E.page 0).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
        (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ FH n a = ⊤ ∧ FH n b = ⊥) ∧
        (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r), b ≤ r →
          (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) = 0) ∧
        (∀ p n : ℤ,
          IsGLB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
              Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (K.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (Fil (p + r) (n + 1)) ⊔
                Fil (p + 1) n)
            (kernelSubobject (K.X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ Fil p n ⊔ Fil (p + 1) n) ∧
          IsLUB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
              Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.«exists» (K.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Fil (p - r) (n - 1)) ⊔
                Fil (p + 1) n)
            (imageSubobject (K.X.d (n - 1) n) ⊓ Fil p n ⊔ Fil (p + 1) n))
declarations.comment: the spectral sequence for a module, not its functoriality

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeLeray.spectralSequencePlusPageTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**The second page of the relative Leray spectral sequence of a bounded below complex** is
`R ᵖ g_*(H^q(R f_* -))`, naturally in the complex.

This is `Stacks.Cohomology.LerayCard.pageTwoNatIsoDerived` for `Φ = R g_*` precomposed with
`R f_*`: the right-hand side of that isomorphism is `H^q(-)` followed by the `p`-th right derived
functor of `g_*` computed on `D⁺`, and `Stacks.DerivedIndexing.rightDerivedIso` identifies the
latter with `R ᵖ g_*` in Mathlib's `ℕ`-indexed spelling.
declarations.statement:
def spectralSequencePlusPageTwoIso (p : ℕ) (q : ℤ) :
    spectralSequencePlus f g ⋙ SpectralSequence.pageFunctor _ _ 2 2 ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.eval _ _ ((p : ℤ), q) ≅
      (modulePushforward f).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleSheaves Y) q ⋙
          (modulePushforward g).rightDerived p
declarations.comment: bounded below complexes, the second page

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeLeray.abutsTo_spectralSequencePlus
declarations.doc:
**The relative Leray spectral sequence of a bounded below complex converges to the
cohomology of the derived direct image along the composite.** For every bounded below complex
`K` of `𝒪_X`-modules, `spectralSequencePlus f g` at `K` has an infinity page at every bidegree
and the terms `E_∞^{p, n-p}` are the successive quotients of a finite decreasing filtration of
`H ⁿ(R (f ≫ g)_* K)`.

Convergence of the truncation-tower spectral sequence of a right derived functor is
`Stacks.Cohomology.LerayTruncation.abutsTo_spectralSequence_cohomologySpectralObjectFunctor_obj`,
with abutment `H ⁿ(R g_*(R f_* K))`; the identification of that with `H ⁿ(R (f ≫ g)_* K)` is
[Stacks, Tag 01F5].
declarations.statement:
theorem abutsTo_spectralSequencePlus (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleSheaves X)) :
    SpectralSequence.AbutsTo ((spectralSequencePlus f g).obj K)
      (fun n ↦ (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleSheaves Z) n).obj
        ((modulePushforward (f ≫ g)).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj K))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeLeray.spectralSequencePageTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**The second page of the relative Leray spectral sequence of a sheaf of modules** is
`R ᵖ g_*(R^q f_* -)`, naturally in the module.
declarations.statement:
def spectralSequencePageTwoIso (p q : ℕ) :
    spectralSequence f g ⋙ SpectralSequence.pageFunctor _ _ 2 2 ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.eval _ _ ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ)) ≅
      (modulePushforward f).rightDerived q ⋙ (modulePushforward g).rightDerived p
declarations.comment: sheaves of modules, the second page

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RelativeLeray.abutsTo_spectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**The relative Leray spectral sequence of a sheaf of modules converges to the higher direct
images along the composite.** For every `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, the spectral sequence has an infinity
page at every bidegree and the terms `E_∞^{p, n-p}` are the successive quotients of a finite
decreasing filtration of `R ⁿ(g ∘ f)_* ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem abutsTo_spectralSequence (M : ModuleSheaves X) :
    SpectralSequence.AbutsTo ((spectralSequence f g).obj M)
      (fun n ↦ ((modulePushforward (f ≫ g)).rightDerivedPlus n).obj M)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.toDerivedPushforwardPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01F8.**  A morphism of complexes `φ : 𝒢^• ⟶ f_* ℱ^•` from a bounded below complex
of `𝒪_Y`-modules to the termwise pushforward of a bounded below complex of `𝒪_X`-modules
induces a canonical morphism `𝒢^• ⟶ Rf_*(ℱ^•)` in `D⁺(Mod 𝒪_Y)`, namely `φ` read in the derived
category followed by the unit of the right derived functor of `f_*`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.toDerivedPushforwardPlus_comp_left
declarations.doc:
**Functoriality in the complex downstairs.**  Precomposing the morphism of complexes with
`g : 𝒢'^• ⟶ 𝒢^•` precomposes the morphism of [Stacks, Tag 01F8] with `g` read in the derived
category.
declarations.statement:
lemma toDerivedPushforwardPlus_comp_left {G G' : CochainComplex.Plus (Modules Y)}
    {F : CochainComplex.Plus (Modules X)} (g : G' ⟶ G)
    (phi : G ⟶ (pushforward f).mapCochainComplexPlus.obj F) :
    DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.map g ≫ toDerivedPushforwardPlus f phi =
      toDerivedPushforwardPlus f (g ≫ phi)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.toDerivedPushforwardPlus_comp_right
declarations.doc:
**Functoriality in the complex upstairs.**  Postcomposing the morphism of complexes with the
termwise pushforward of `k : ℱ^• ⟶ ℱ'^•` postcomposes the morphism of [Stacks, Tag 01F8] with
`Rf_*(k)`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.derivedGlobalSectionsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01F9.**  An `f`-map `φ : 𝒢 ⟶ f_* ℱ` from an `𝒪_Y`-module `𝒢` to an `𝒪_X`-module
`ℱ` induces the morphism

```
φ : RΓ(Y, 𝒢) ⟶ RΓ(X, ℱ)
```

of `D⁺(Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y))`, the target carrying its `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)`-module structure by restriction of
scalars along `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.  It is `RΓ(Y, -)` applied to the morphism
`𝒢[0] ⟶ Rf_*(ℱ[0])` of [Stacks, Tag 01F8], followed by the identification
`RΓ(Y, Rf_* ℱ) ≅ RΓ(X, ℱ)` of [Stacks, Tag 01EZ].
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedGlobalSectionsMap {G : Modules Y} {F : Modules X}
    (phi : G ⟶ (pushforward f).obj F) :
    (derivedModuleGlobalSections Y).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor (Modules Y) 0).obj G) ⟶
      (derivedModuleGlobalSectionsAlong f).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor (Modules X) 0).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.moduleCohomologyMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01FA.**  An `f`-map `φ : 𝒢 ⟶ f_* ℱ` from an `𝒪_Y`-module `𝒢` to an `𝒪_X`-module
`ℱ` induces the map on cohomology

```
φ : H^i(Y, 𝒢) ⟶ H^i(X, ℱ)
```

for every `i`, the target carrying its `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)`-module structure by restriction of scalars.
It is `H^i` applied to the arrow `RΓ(Y, 𝒢) ⟶ RΓ(X, ℱ)` of [Stacks, Tag 01F9].

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.exists_pushforwardInjectiveResolutionLift
declarations.doc:
**The commutative square labelled `(choice)` in [Stacks, Tag 01FB].** Given injective
resolutions of `F[0]`, of `G[0]` and of the pushforward of the resolution of `F[0]`, the adjoint
of an `f`-map lifts to a morphism between the latter two resolutions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pushforwardInjectiveResolutionLift {G : Modules Y} {F : Modules X}
    (φ : (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback f).obj G ⟶ F)
    (I : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules X) 0).obj F))
    (J : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules Y) 0).obj G))
    (J' : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution (modulePushforwardComplex f I.cocomplex))
    [∀ n, Mono (J.ι.f n)] :
    ∃ β : J.cocomplex ⟶ J'.cocomplex,
      J.ι ≫ β =
        (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules Y) 0).map
            (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.homEquiv f F G φ) ≫
          (HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex
              (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).inv.app F ≫
          ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map I.ι ≫ J'.ι

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.quasiIso_moduleGlobalSections_map_pushforwardResolution
declarations.doc:
**The right leg of the roof of [Stacks, Tag 01FB] is a quasi-isomorphism.** If `I⁼` is a
complex of injective sheaves of modules on `X` and `J'⁼` is an injective resolution of its
pushforward, then global sections on `Y` carry the resolution map to a quasi-isomorphism, hence
to an isomorphism in the derived category.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_moduleGlobalSections_map_pushforwardResolution {F : Modules X}
    (I : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules X) 0).obj F))
    (J' : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution (modulePushforwardComplex f I.cocomplex)) :
    QuasiIso (((moduleGlobalSections Y).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map J'.ι)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.injectiveResolutionGlobalSectionsMap
declarations.doc:
**The representative of the functorial map on derived global sections afforded by choices
of injective resolutions and a lift `β`**: it is the lower horizontal map of [Stacks, Tag 01FB]
followed by the inverse of the vertical quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def injectiveResolutionGlobalSectionsMap {G : Modules Y} {F : Modules X}
    (φ : (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback f).obj G ⟶ F)
    (I : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules X) 0).obj F))
    (J : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules Y) 0).obj G))
    (J' : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution (modulePushforwardComplex f I.cocomplex))
    (β : J.cocomplex ⟶ J'.cocomplex)
    (_hβ : J.ι ≫ β =
      (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules Y) 0).map
          (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.homEquiv f F G φ) ≫
        (HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex
            (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f)
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).inv.app F ≫
        ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map I.ι ≫ J'.ι) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj (moduleGlobalSectionsComplex Y J.cocomplex) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (moduleGlobalSectionsComplex Y (modulePushforwardComplex f I.cocomplex))
declarations.comment: the roof representing the functorial map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.derivedModuleGlobalSectionsMap_eq_injectiveResolutionGlobalSectionsMap
declarations.doc:
**The roof of [Stacks, Tag 01FB] represents the canonical functorial map of
[Stacks, Tag 01F9].** Read through the canonical identifications of `RΓ(Y, G)` with
`Γ(Y, J⁼)` and of `RΓ(X, F)`, over `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)`, with `Γ(Y, f_* I⁼)`, the morphism
`Stacks.Cohomology.derivedModuleGlobalSectionsMap` attached to the `f`-map `φ` is the roof
`Stacks.Cohomology.injectiveResolutionGlobalSectionsMap` built from a lift `β` and the inverse
of the quasi-isomorphism `Γ(Y, f_* I⁼) ⟶ Γ(Y, J'⁼)`. Both comparisons are built from `I.ι`,
`J.ι` and the derived-functor units, so neither can be replaced by an arbitrary isomorphism,
and `CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Plus.ι` displays the bounded-below objects in the
unbounded derived category in which the roof was defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedModuleGlobalSectionsMap_eq_injectiveResolutionGlobalSectionsMap
    {G : Modules Y} {F : Modules X}
    (φ : (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback f).obj G ⟶ F)
    (I : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules X) 0).obj F))
    (J : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules Y) 0).obj G))
    (J' : CochainComplex.InjectiveResolution (modulePushforwardComplex f I.cocomplex))
    (β : J.cocomplex ⟶ J'.cocomplex)
    (hβ : J.ι ≫ β =
      (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules Y) 0).map
          (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.homEquiv f F G φ) ≫
        (HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex
            (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f)
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).inv.app F ≫
        ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map I.ι ≫ J'.ι) :
    ((moduleGlobalSections Y).rightDerivedFunctorPlusInjectiveResolutionIso G J).hom ≫
        injectiveResolutionGlobalSectionsMap f φ I J J' β hβ =
      DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.map (derivedModuleGlobalSectionsMap f φ) ≫
        (derivedModuleGlobalSectionsAlongResolutionIso f I).hom
declarations.comment: identification with the canonical functorial map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechRefinement.cechToDerivedGlobalSections_naturality_of_refinement
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FD].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of ringed spaces, let `φ : f^* G ⟶ F`
be an `f`-map of sheaves of modules, let `U` be an open covering of `X`, let `V` be an open
covering of `Y` and let `c` be a refinement function, so that `U i ⊆ f⁻¹(V (c i))`. Then the
Čech refinement map `γ` of [Stacks, Tag 01FD], followed by the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 01EQ]
on `X` read over `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)`, agrees with the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 01EQ] on `Y` followed
by the functorial map on derived global sections of [Stacks, Tag 01F9].

All four corners are read in the bounded-below derived category of `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)`-modules, so the
left-hand side carries the unit `Stacks.Cohomology.scalarRestrictionUnit` of derived restriction
of scalars and the comparison `Stacks.Cohomology.derivedSectionsScalarComparison` of
[Stacks, Tag 01EZ].
declarations.statement:
theorem cechToDerivedGlobalSections_naturality_of_refinement :
    DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.map
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (cechComplexRefinementMapInt f F G φ U V hU hV c hc) :
            (CechDerived.cechComplexPlusFunctor (ringCatSheaf Y) ⊤ V hV).obj G ⟶
              (restrictGlobalScalars f).mapCochainComplexPlus.obj
                ((CechDerived.cechComplexPlusFunctor (ringCatSheaf X) ⊤ U hU).obj F)) ≫
        (scalarRestrictionUnit f
              ((CechDerived.cechComplexPlusFunctor (ringCatSheaf X) ⊤ U hU).obj F) ≫
            (restrictGlobalScalars f).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map
              ((CechDerived.cechToDerivedGlobalSections (ringCatSheaf X) ⊤ U hU).app F) ≫
            (derivedSectionsScalarComparison f).hom.app
              ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor (Modules X) 0).obj F)) =
      (CechDerived.cechToDerivedGlobalSections (ringCatSheaf Y) ⊤ V hV).app G ≫
        derivedModuleGlobalSectionsMap f φ

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechRefinement.cechCohomologyToCohomology_naturality_of_refinement
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FD] on cohomology.** The canonical maps from Čech cohomology to sheaf
cohomology of [Stacks, Tag 01EQ] commute with an `f`-map and a refinement of the inverse-image
covering: this is
`Stacks.Cohomology.CechRefinement.cechToDerivedGlobalSections_naturality_of_refinement` read
through the `p`-th homology of the bounded-below derived category. All four corners are modules
over `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)`, so the source comparison carries the derived restriction-of-scalars unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechCohomologyToCohomology_naturality_of_refinement (p : ℤ) :
    (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
            (ModuleCat ((ringCatSheaf Y).obj.obj (op ⊤))) p).map
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.map
            (ObjectProperty.homMk (cechComplexRefinementMapInt f F G φ U V hU hV c hc) :
              (CechDerived.cechComplexPlusFunctor (ringCatSheaf Y) ⊤ V hV).obj G ⟶
                (restrictGlobalScalars f).mapCochainComplexPlus.obj
                  ((CechDerived.cechComplexPlusFunctor (ringCatSheaf X) ⊤ U hU).obj F))) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
              (ModuleCat ((ringCatSheaf Y).obj.obj (op ⊤))) p).map
            (scalarRestrictionUnit f
              ((CechDerived.cechComplexPlusFunctor (ringCatSheaf X) ⊤ U hU).obj F)) ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
                (ModuleCat ((ringCatSheaf Y).obj.obj (op ⊤))) p).map
              ((restrictGlobalScalars f).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map
                ((CechDerived.cechToDerivedGlobalSections (ringCatSheaf X) ⊤ U hU).app F)) ≫
            (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
                (ModuleCat ((ringCatSheaf Y).obj.obj (op ⊤))) p).map
              ((derivedSectionsScalarComparison f).hom.app
                ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor (Modules X) 0).obj F)) =
      (CechDerived.cechCohomologyToCohomology (ringCatSheaf Y) ⊤ V hV p).app G ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
            (ModuleCat ((ringCatSheaf Y).obj.obj (op ⊤))) p).map
          (derivedModuleGlobalSectionsMap f φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleColimit.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_evaluation_of_isCompact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FF] at the module-valued spelling, in the tag's own shape.** Let `X` be a
space with a basis of quasi-compact opens whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact, let
`O_X` be a sheaf of rings on `X` and let `U` be a quasi-compact open. Then for every filtered
system `F` of `O_X`-modules and every degree `q` the canonical map
`colimᵢ Hᑫ(U, Fᵢ) ⟶ Hᑫ(U, colimᵢ Fᵢ)` of `Γ(U, O_X)`-modules is an isomorphism.

`Stacks.Cohomology.Vanishing.isIso_colimit_post_Hfunctor_of_isCompact` is the same statement
for cohomology valued in abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_evaluation_of_isCompact
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (hBasis : PrespectralSpace X) (hInter : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    (U : Opens X) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (q : ℕ)
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (F : I ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} R) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F ((_root_.SheafOfModules.evaluation R (op U)).rightDerived q))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Vanishing.isIso_colimit_post_Hfunctor_of_isCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01FF.**  Let `X` be a topological space with a basis of quasi-compact opens whose
pairwise intersections are quasi-compact, let `O_X` be a sheaf of rings on `X` and let `U` be a
quasi-compact open of `X`.  Then for every filtered system `F` of `O_X`-modules and every degree
`q` the canonical map `colimᵢ Hᑫ(U, Fᵢ) ⟶ Hᑫ(U, colimᵢ Fᵢ)` is an isomorphism.

The proof is the induction of the source on `q`, carried out for an arbitrary cohomological
δ-functor in `CategoryTheory.DeltaFunctor.isIso_colimit_post_of_isIso_zero` and specialized to
the cohomology δ-functor in
`Stacks.Cohomology.Colimit.isIso_colimit_post_Hfunctor_of_preservesColimitsOfShape`.  Its two
inputs are Stacks 009F for sheaves of modules
(`Stacks.Cohomology.Sections.preservesColimitsOfShape_secF_of_isCompact`) and the vanishing
`isZero_Hfunctor_succ_obj_colimit_of_injective` above.

The hypotheses are exactly the tag's: sheafification of abelian presheaves on the site of opens,
its characterization by local bijectivity, and enough injectives in `SheafOfModules.{u} R` are
all instances at these universes, so none of them is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_Hfunctor_of_isCompact
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (R : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (hBasis : PrespectralSpace X) (hInter : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    (U : Opens X) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (q : ℕ) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F (Hfunctor R U q))

declarations.name: CechCochains.alternatingSubgroup
declarations.doc: The alternating cochains form a subgroup `Č_alt^p ⊆ Č^p`.
declarations.statement: def alternatingSubgroup (p : ℕ) : AddSubgroup (Cochain U ℱ p)
declarations.comment: the group `Č_alt^p(𝒰, ℱ)` of alternating cochains

declarations.name: CechCochains.cechD_mem_alternating
declarations.doc:
The differential `cechD` preserves the alternating subgroup, so the latter is a
subcomplex of the full Čech complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechD_mem_alternating (p : ℕ) (s : Cochain U ℱ p) (hs : IsAlternating U ℱ s) :
    IsAlternating U ℱ (cechD U ℱ p s)
declarations.comment: `d` maps `Č_alt^p` into `Č_alt^{p+1}`, the verification the source omits

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.alternatingCechComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01FH.** The alternating Čech complex associated to an abelian presheaf and an
indexed family of open subsets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def alternatingCechComplex : CochainComplex Ab ℕ

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.alternatingCechInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01FH.** The canonical inclusion of the alternating Čech complex into the usual
Čech complex: in each degree it is the inclusion of the subgroup of alternating cochains.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def alternatingCechInclusion :
    alternatingCechComplex U ℱ ⟶ cechComplex U ℱ

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.orderedCechComplex
declarations.doc:
The ordered Čech cochain complex of an abelian presheaf with respect to a linearly
ordered family of open subsets.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def orderedCechComplex (U : I → Opens X)
    (ℱ : TopCat.Presheaf AddCommGrpCat.{w} X) :
    CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{max v w} ℕ

declarations.name: CechCochains.cAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
(3) **[Stacks, Tag 01FJ], the degreewise clause.** In every degree, `c` corestricted to the
alternating subgroup is an isomorphism of abelian groups `Č_ord^p ≃+ Č_alt^p`, with inverse the
projection `π`.

This is the degreewise statement only: it says nothing about the differentials.  That `c`
commutes with them is `c_chainMap`, and the two clauses are assembled into the isomorphism of
cochain complexes the source asserts by `Stacks.Cech.orderedIsoAlternatingCechComplex`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def cAddEquiv (p : ℕ) : OrdCochain U ℱ p ≃+ alternatingSubgroup U ℱ p

declarations.name: CechCochains.c_chainMap
declarations.doc:
(1) **[Stacks, Tag 01FJ], the chain-map clause.** `c` is a chain map: `c ∘ d = d ∘ c`.

This is the first half of what the source asserts about `c`; the degreewise bijectivity is
`cAddEquiv`, and `Stacks.Cech.orderedIsoAlternatingCechComplex` assembles the two into the
isomorphism of cochain complexes `Č_ord^• → Č_alt^•`.
declarations.statement:
theorem c_chainMap (p : ℕ) (s : OrdCochain U ℱ p) :
    c U ℱ (p + 1) (ordD U ℱ p s) = cechD U ℱ p (c U ℱ p s)
declarations.comment: c is a morphism of complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.orderedIsoAlternatingCechComplex
declarations.doc:
**The ordered Čech complex is the alternating Čech complex.** The degreewise comparison of
Stacks 01FJ is an isomorphism of cochain complexes, because `CechCochains.c` is a chain map.

This is the second assertion of the source: the degreewise isomorphism `CechCochains.cAddEquiv`
and the chain-map property `CechCochains.c_chainMap` together induce an isomorphism of the
complexes themselves.
declarations.statement:
def orderedIsoAlternatingCechComplex :
    orderedCechComplex U ℱ ≅ alternatingCechComplex U ℱ

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechProj_comp_cechDiff
declarations.doc:
The projection `π : C^• → C^•_ord` is a morphism of complexes: it commutes with the
differentials, `π ∘ d = d ∘ π`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechProj_comp_cechDiff (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w'}) (U : ι → C) (p : ℕ) :
    (Alternating.cechProj P U (p+1)).comp (Alternating.cechDiff P U p)
      = (Alternating.cechDiffOrd P U p).comp (Alternating.cechProj P U p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechProj_comp_cechComp
declarations.doc: `π` is a left inverse to the comparison map `c`: `π ∘ c = id` on the ordered cochains.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechProj_comp_cechComp (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w'}) (U : ι → C) (p : ℕ) :
    (Alternating.cechProj P U p).comp (Alternating.cechComp P U p) =
      AddMonoidHom.id (Alternating.CechCochainOrd P U p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechProjAltEquiv
declarations.doc:
The restriction of the projection to the alternating cochains, `π : C^•_alt → C^•_ord`,
is an *isomorphism* of abelian groups in each degree, with inverse the comparison map `c`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechProjAltEquiv (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w'}) (U : ι → C) (p : ℕ) :
    Alternating.CechCochainAlt P U p ≃+ Alternating.CechCochainOrd P U p

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechProjAlt_comp_cechDiffAlt
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `π : C^•_alt → C^•_ord`
commutes with the differentials, hence is an isomorphism of complexes.  Equivalently, the
comparison map `c : C^•_ord → C^•_alt` is a morphism of complexes (`c ∘ d_ord = d_alt ∘ c`),
exhibiting `c` as the inverse morphism of complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechProjAlt_comp_cechDiffAlt (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w'}) (U : ι → C)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsSubterminal (U i)) (p : ℕ) :
    (Alternating.cechProjAlt P U (p+1)).comp (Alternating.cechDiffAlt P U hU p)
      = (Alternating.cechDiffOrd P U p).comp (Alternating.cechProjAlt P U p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechProjAltComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FK] (2) as an isomorphism of complexes.**  The projection `π` from the
alternating to the ordered Čech cochains is an isomorphism of complexes.
declarations.statement:
def cechProjAltComplexIso (hU : ∀ i, IsSubterminal (U i)) :
    cechCochainComplexAlt P U hU ≅ cechCochainComplexOrd P U

declarations.name: cechProj_comp_cechDiff
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.** The projection `π : C^• → C^•_ord` is a morphism of complexes: each
`π` in degree `p` is a homomorphism of abelian groups (built into `cechProj`) and it
commutes with the differentials, `π ∘ d = d ∘ π`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechProj_comp_cechDiff (F : AbelianPresheaf X) (U : I → Opens X) (p : ℕ) :
    (cechProj F U (p+1)).comp (cechDiff F U p)
      = (cechDiffOrd F U p).comp (cechProj F U p)

declarations.name: cechProj_comp_cechComp
declarations.doc:
**Statement 3 (left inverse).** `π` is a left inverse to the comparison map `c`:
`π ∘ c = id` on the ordered complex.  (For a strictly increasing tuple the sorting
permutation is the identity, so `c(s)` agrees with `s` there.)
declarations.statement:
theorem cechProj_comp_cechComp (F : AbelianPresheaf X) (U : I → Opens X) (p : ℕ) :
    (cechProj F U p).comp (cechComp F U p) = AddMonoidHom.id (CechCochainOrd F U p)

declarations.name: cechProjAltEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2.** The restriction of the projection to the alternating subcomplex,
`π : C^•_alt → C^•_ord`, is an *isomorphism* of abelian groups in each degree, with inverse
the comparison map `c`.  (Together with Statement 2 below — that this isomorphism commutes
with the differentials — this is the asserted isomorphism of complexes.)
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechProjAltEquiv (F : AbelianPresheaf X) (U : I → Opens X) (p : ℕ) :
    CechCochainAlt F U p ≃+ CechCochainOrd F U p

declarations.name: cechProjAlt_comp_cechDiffAlt
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (isomorphism of complexes).** The isomorphism `π : C^•_alt → C^•_ord`
commutes with the differentials, hence is an isomorphism of complexes.  Equivalently, the
comparison map `c : C^•_ord → C^•_alt` is a morphism of complexes (`c ∘ d_ord = d_alt ∘ c`),
exhibiting `c` as the inverse morphism of complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechProjAlt_comp_cechDiffAlt (F : AbelianPresheaf X) (U : I → Opens X) (p : ℕ) :
    (cechProjAlt F U (p+1)).comp (cechDiffAlt F U p)
      = (cechDiffOrd F U p).comp (cechProjAlt F U p)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.CrystallineThickening.restrictCechAltInclusionHomotopyEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FM] for a restriction cover of an object of `Cris(X/S)`.**  The canonical
inclusion of the alternating Čech cochain complex of the cover into the full Čech cochain
complex is a homotopy equivalence; signed sorting is a homotopy inverse.

The family of opens is arbitrary: it need not cover the ambient scheme, exactly as at the space
level.  The hypothesis of the lifted theory is discharged by `isSubterminal_ambientOpen` and
nothing is assumed here.
declarations.statement:
def restrictCechAltInclusionHomotopyEquiv :
    HomotopyEquiv (restrictCechComplexAlt A V F) (restrictCechComplex A V F)
declarations.comment: for a restriction cover of an object of the small crystalline site

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.CrystallineThickening.restrictCechAltInclusion_homotopyEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FM] for a restriction cover of an object of `Cris(X/S)`**, in the
`homotopyEquivalences` morphism-property spelling.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictCechAltInclusion_homotopyEquivalence :
    (HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences AddCommGrpCat.{max w w'} (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
      (restrictCechAltInclusion A V F)
declarations.comment: a restriction cover's alternating inclusion lies in homotopyEquivalences

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechAltHomotopyEquivCechComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FM] in the `cechComplexFunctor` model.** The alternating Čech cochain
complex of a family of subterminal objects is homotopy equivalent to the Čech complex of the
family.
declarations.statement:
def cechAltHomotopyEquivCechComplex (hU : ∀ i, IsSubterminal (U i)) :
    HomotopyEquiv (cechCochainComplexAlt P U hU) ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj P)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechComparisonProjectionHomotopy
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FM] for a family in an arbitrary category, chain-level form.**  An
explicit homotopy from the endomorphism `c ∘ π` to the identity of the full Čech cochain
complex.  Its component from degree `j + 1` to degree `j` is `cochainHomotopy`.
declarations.statement:
def cechComparisonProjectionHomotopy (hU : ∀ i, IsSubterminal (U i)) :
    Homotopy (cechComparisonProjection P U hU) (𝟙 (cechCochainComplex P U))
declarations.comment: c after projection is homotopic to the identity

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechAltInclusionHomotopyEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FM] for a family in an arbitrary category.**  The canonical inclusion
of the alternating Čech cochain complex into the full Čech cochain complex is a homotopy
equivalence; signed sorting `c ∘ π`, corestricted to the alternating cochains, is a homotopy
inverse.  The family need not cover anything.
declarations.statement:
def cechAltInclusionHomotopyEquiv (hU : ∀ i, IsSubterminal (U i)) :
    HomotopyEquiv (cechCochainComplexAlt P U hU) (cechCochainComplex P U)
declarations.comment: the canonical inclusion is a homotopy equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.CechComplex.Alternating.cechAltInclusion_homotopyEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01FM] for a family in an arbitrary category**, in the `homotopyEquivalences`
morphism-property spelling.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechAltInclusion_homotopyEquivalence (hU : ∀ i, IsSubterminal (U i)) :
    (HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences AddCommGrpCat.{max w w'} (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
      (cechAltInclusion P U hU)
declarations.comment: the canonical inclusion lies in homotopyEquivalences

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.cechComparisonProjection_homotopic_id
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism `c ∘ π` is homotopic to the identity on the usual Čech
complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechComparisonProjection_homotopic_id :
    Nonempty (Homotopy (cechComparisonProjection U F)
      (𝟙 (cechComplex U F)))
declarations.comment: c after projection is homotopic to the identity

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.alternatingCechInclusion_homotopyEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The canonical inclusion of alternating Čech cochains into the usual Čech complex is a
homotopy equivalence: the signed-sorting projection is a homotopy inverse.
declarations.statement:
theorem alternatingCechInclusion_homotopyEquivalence
    (G : TopCat.Presheaf Ab.{max v w} X) :
    (HomologicalComplex.homotopyEquivalences AddCommGrpCat (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
      (alternatingCechInclusion U G)
declarations.comment: the canonical inclusion is a homotopy equivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.cohomologyRestriction
declarations.doc:
The restriction mapping `Hⁿ(V, ℱ) ⟶ Hⁿ(U, ℱ)`, `ξ ↦ ξ|_U`, along a morphism `f : U ⟶ V` of the
site, natural in the sheaf of `O`-modules `ℱ`. It is the map induced on cohomology by the
restriction of sections, and it is `O(V)`-linear for the `O(V)`-module structure on `Hⁿ(U, ℱ)`
through `O(V) ⟶ O(U)`.
declarations.statement:
def cohomologyRestriction (n : ℕ) {U V : C} (f : U ⟶ V) :
    (SheafOfModules.evaluation.{v} O (op V)).rightDerived n ⟶
      (SheafOfModules.evaluation.{v} O (op U)).rightDerived n ⋙
        ModuleCat.restrictScalars (O.obj.map f.op).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.cohomologyRestriction_app_eq
declarations.doc:
The restriction mapping is computed from any injective resolution `ℱ ⟶ I^•`: it is the map
induced on `Hⁿ` by the morphism of complexes `Γ(V, I^•) ⟶ Γ(U, I^•)` given by the restriction maps
of the sheaves `I^p`, followed by the identification of `Hⁿ` of the restriction of scalars of
`Γ(U, I^•)` with the restriction of scalars of `Hⁿ(U, ℱ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyRestriction_app_eq (n : ℕ) {U V : C} (f : U ⟶ V)
    {F : SheafOfModules.{v} O} (I : InjectiveResolution F) :
    (cohomologyRestriction O n f).app F =
      ((I.isoRightDerivedObj (SheafOfModules.evaluation O (op V)) n).hom ≫
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex (sectionsRestriction O f) _).app I.cocomplex) n ≫
        (I.isoRightDerivedObj (SheafOfModules.evaluation O (op U) ⋙
          ModuleCat.restrictScalars (O.obj.map f.op).hom) n).inv) ≫
      ((SheafOfModules.evaluation O (op U)).rightDerivedCompIso _ n).hom.app F

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.cohomologyPresheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor sending a sheaf of `O`-modules `ℱ` to the presheaf of `O`-modules
`H̲ⁿ(ℱ) : U ↦ Hⁿ(U, ℱ)`, defined as the `n`-th right derived functor of the inclusion of sheaves of
`O`-modules into presheaves of `O`-modules.
declarations.statement: def cohomologyPresheafFunctor (n : ℕ) : SheafOfModules.{v} O ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} O.obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso
declarations.doc:
The value of the presheaf `H̲ⁿ(ℱ)` at an object `U` of the site is the cohomology `Hⁿ(U, ℱ)`,
as an `O(U)`-module and naturally in `ℱ`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.cohomologyPresheaf_map
declarations.doc:
Under the identification of its values with the cohomology modules, the restriction map of the
presheaf `H̲ⁿ(ℱ)` along `f : U ⟶ V` is the restriction mapping `Hⁿ(V, ℱ) ⟶ Hⁿ(U, ℱ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyPresheaf_map (n : ℕ) {U V : C} (f : U ⟶ V) (F : SheafOfModules.{v} O) :
    (cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso O n V).hom.app F ≫ (cohomologyPresheaf O n F).map f.op =
      (cohomologyRestriction O n f).app F ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (O.obj.map f.op).hom).map
          ((cohomologyPresheafEvaluationIso O n U).hom.app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Locality.locality_of_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01FW (Lemma 21.7.3).** Locality of cohomology.

Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site (with `O = R : Sheaf J RingCat`), let `F` be a sheaf
of `O`-modules, let `U` be an object of `C`, let `n > 0` and let
`ξ ∈ H^n(U, F)`. Then there exists a covering `{U_i -> U}` of `U` such that the
restriction `ξ|_{U_i}` vanishes in `H^n(U_i, F)` for every member `i` of the
covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem locality_of_cohomology (R : Sheaf J RingCat) (F : SheafOfModules R)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (U : C) (ξ : cohomology R F n U) :
    ∃ S : J.Cover U, ∀ g : S.Arrow,
      (restriction R F n g.f) ξ = 0

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct
registrations.comment: the objects of `SR(C)`: families `{U_i}_{i ∈ I}` of objects of `C`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.Hom
registrations.comment: the morphisms of `SR(C)`: a map `α : I → J` and morphisms `U_i → V_{α(i)}`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.category
registrations.comment: the category structure on `SR(C)`: identities and composition of such pairs

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.yoneda
registrations.comment: the functor `F : SR(C) → PSh(C)`, `{U_i}_{i ∈ I} ↦ ∐ h_{U_i}`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.instHasBinaryProducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, products of pairs clause. If `C` has binary products, then so
does its category of formal coproducts — equivalently, the category `SR(C)` of semi-representable
objects of `C` has binary products.
declarations.statement: instance instHasBinaryProducts : HasBinaryProducts (FormalCoproduct.{w} C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.instHasEqualizers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, equalizers clause. If `C` has equalizers, then so does its
category of formal coproducts — equivalently, the category `SR(C)` of semi-representable
objects of `C` has equalizers.
declarations.statement: instance instHasEqualizers : HasEqualizers (FormalCoproduct.{w} C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.hasCoproducts_formalCoproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, coproducts clause, first half. The category of formal
coproducts of `C` — equivalently, the category `SR(C)` of semi-representable objects of `C` — has
arbitrary coproducts, indexed by types in the index universe `w`. The coproduct of a family of
families of objects is obtained by concatenating the index types.
declarations.statement: theorem hasCoproducts_formalCoproduct : HasCoproducts.{w} (FormalCoproduct.{w} C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.preservesColimitsOfShape_yoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, coproducts clause, second half. The functor
`F : SR(C) ⥤ PSh(C)`, sending a family `{U_i}` of objects of `C` to the coproduct `∐ h_{U_i}` of
the representable presheaves, commutes with coproducts.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_yoneda (J : Type v) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) (FormalCoproduct.yoneda (C := C))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.preservesLimitsOfSize_yoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, limits clause. The functor `F : SR(C) ⥤ PSh(C)`, sending a
family `{U_i}` of objects of `C` to the coproduct `∐ h_{U_i}` of the representable presheaves,
commutes with limits — of any shape, and for an arbitrary category `C`.

Limits of presheaves are computed sectionwise, and each section functor of `F` is corepresentable
by `yonedaCompEvaluationIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance preservesLimitsOfSize_yoneda :
    PreservesLimitsOfSize.{w, w'} (FormalCoproduct.yoneda (C := C))
declarations.comment: F : SR(C) → PSh(C) commutes with limits

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.hasPullbacks_formalCoproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, fibre products clause. If `C` has fibre products, then so does
its category of formal coproducts — equivalently, the category `SR(C)` of semi-representable
objects of `C` has fibre products. They are computed componentwise, the index type of
`{U_i} ×_{{V_j}} {W_k}` being the set of triples `(i, j, k)` with `j` the common image of `i` and
of `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPullbacks_formalCoproduct [HasPullbacks C] :
    HasPullbacks (FormalCoproduct.{w} C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.hasTerminal_formalCoproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, final object clause. If `C` has a final object `X`, then the
one-member family `{X}` is a final object of the category of formal coproducts of `C` —
equivalently, of the category `SR(C)` of semi-representable objects of `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTerminal_formalCoproduct [HasTerminal C] :
    HasTerminal (FormalCoproduct.{w} C)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.hasFiniteLimits_formalCoproductOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, finite limits clause for `SR(C, X)`, first half. If `C` has
fibre products then `SR(C, X)` has finite limits: it has a terminal object, namely `{X → X}`, and
it has fibre products, computed componentwise.

The second half of the clause, that `F : SR(C, X) ⥤ PSh(C)/h_X` commutes with those finite
limits, is the instance `CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.preservesLimitsOfSize_yonedaOver`
in `StacksFrontier.CategoryTheory.Sites.Localization.SemiRepresentableOver`, for limits of every
shape.
declarations.statement:
instance hasFiniteLimits_formalCoproductOver {X : C} :
    HasFiniteLimits (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.yonedaOverObjIso
declarations.doc:
**The value of `F` on a family, Stacks Project, Tag 01G2.** `F({U_i → X})` is the coproduct
`∐ h_{U_i}` of the representable presheaves of the `U_i`, equipped with the map to `h_X` whose
component on `h_{U_i}` is `h` of the structure morphism `U_i → X`. This is the source's
`F({U_i → X}) = (∐ h_{U_i} → h_X)`, and it is what makes the clauses below statements about the
source's `F`.

The proof is the source's description read backwards: `FormalCoproduct.yoneda` of `C/X` sends
`{U_i → X}` to the coproduct of the presheaves on `C/X` represented by the `U_i → X`, the
presheaf level `j_{X!}` preserves that coproduct because it is a left adjoint
(`OverShriek.presheafAdjunction`), and it takes the presheaf represented by `U_i → X` to the
presheaf represented by `U_i` over `h_X` (`OverShriek.presheafFunctorToOverYonedaIso`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def yonedaOverObjIso (A : FormalCoproduct.{v} (Over X)) :
    (yonedaOver X).obj A ≅
      Over.mk (Sigma.desc fun i : A.I ↦ CategoryTheory.yoneda.map (A.obj i).hom)
declarations.comment: the value of F: F({U_i → X}) is ∐ h_{U_i} augmented to h_X

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.hasCoproducts_formalCoproductOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, coproducts clause for `SR(C, X)`, first half. The category
`SR(C, X)` of semi-representable objects over `X` has arbitrary coproducts, obtained by
concatenating the index types of the families.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCoproducts_formalCoproductOver :
    HasCoproducts.{w} (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.preservesColimitsOfShape_yonedaOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, coproducts clause for `SR(C, X)`, second half. The functor
`F : SR(C, X) ⥤ PSh(C)/h_X` commutes with coproducts: the semi-representable Yoneda embedding of
`C/X` does, and `j_{X!} : PSh(C/X) ⥤ PSh(C)/h_X` is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_yonedaOver (J : Type v) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) (yonedaOver X)
declarations.comment: F commutes with coproducts in SR(C, X)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.FormalCoproduct.preservesLimitsOfSize_yonedaOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G2**, finite limits clause for `SR(C, X)`, second half. The functor
`F : SR(C, X) ⥤ PSh(C)/h_X` commutes with limits of every shape, with no hypothesis on `C`; this
strengthens the finite limits of the source's clause. The first half, that `SR(C, X)` has finite
limits as soon as `C` has fibre products, is
`Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.hasFiniteLimits_formalCoproductOver`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance preservesLimitsOfSize_yonedaOver :
    PreservesLimitsOfSize.{w, w'} (yonedaOver X)
declarations.comment: F : SR(C, X) → PSh(C)/h_X commutes with finite limits

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.CoveringFamilies.IsCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G3.** A morphism of semi-representable objects is covering when
every one of its fibre families is a covering family of the site. The target is allowed to be an
arbitrary formal coproduct, as it is for a matching object.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCovering (Cov : CoveringFamilies.{s, w} C) {U : SetFamily.{w} C}
    {V : FormalCoproduct.{w + 1} C} (f : U.toFormalCoproduct ⟶ V) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.CoveringFamilies.IsCoveringOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G3.** A morphism of semi-representable objects over `X` is covering
when every one of its underlying fibre families is a covering family of the site.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsCovering.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G4, part (1).** The composition of two covering morphisms of
semi-representable objects is a covering morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsCovering.comp (J : Pretopology C)
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage]
    {U V W : FormalCoproduct.{w} C} {f : U ⟶ V} {g : V ⟶ W}
    (hf : IsCovering J f) (hg : IsCovering J g) : IsCovering J (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsCoveringOver.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G4, part (1).** The composition of two covering morphisms of
semi-representable objects over `X` is a covering morphism.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsCovering.pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G4, part (2).** The base change of a covering morphism of
semi-representable objects along any morphism exists and is a covering morphism.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsCoveringOver.pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G4, part (2).** The base change of a covering morphism of
semi-representable objects over `X` along any morphism exists and is a covering morphism.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsCovering.prod_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G4, part (3).** The product of two covering morphisms of
semi-representable objects is a covering morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsCovering.prod_map (J : Pretopology C)
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage]
    [HasBinaryProducts (FormalCoproduct.{w} C)]
    {A B K L : FormalCoproduct.{w} C} {f : A ⟶ B} {g : K ⟶ L}
    (hf : IsCovering J f) (hg : IsCovering J g) : IsCovering J (prod.map f g)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsCoveringOver.prod_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G4, part (3).** The product of two covering morphisms of
semi-representable objects over `X` is a covering morphism.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.CoveringFamilies.IsHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G5.** A hypercovering of `X` for the site's covering families: the
degree-zero family is one of the covering families of `X`, and all fibres of the successive
matching morphisms are covering families of the site. The coskeleton is computed in formal
coproducts, after including the set-indexed families.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsHypercovering (Cov : CoveringFamilies.{s, w} C) {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (SetFamily.{w} (Over X))) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isCoveringOver_terminal_from_power
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G6**, condition (1) of Definition 01G5 for the Čech construction.
If the family `U` covers `X` then so does its `α`-fold power for a one-element index type `α`,
which is the degree-zero term of the Čech object of `U`: that term is `U` again, its component
at `i` being a product of one copy of the component of `U` at `i default`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoveringOver_terminal_from_power (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (U : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)) (α : Type) [Unique α] [HasProductsOfShape α (Over X)]
    (hU : IsCoveringOver J (terminal.from U)) :
    IsCoveringOver J (terminal.from (U.power α))
declarations.comment: condition (1) of Definition 01G5, for the degree-zero term of the Čech object

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsCechHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G6.** A simplicial object `K` of `SR(C, X)` is a *Čech
hypercovering* of `X` when its degree-zero family `K_0` covers `X` and `K` is the zeroth
coskeleton of `K_0`, that is, when `K` is isomorphic to `cosk₀ U` for a zero-truncated
simplicial object `U` of `SR(C, X)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCechHypercovering (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition of a Čech hypercovering

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsCechHypercovering.isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G6**, condition (2) of Definition 01G5 and the hypercovering
property. A Čech hypercovering of `X` is a hypercovering of `X`: its degree-zero family covers
`X` by definition, and each of its matching morphisms is an isomorphism, hence covering, because
`cosk₀ U` is `n`-coskeletal for every `n` (Tag 018B).
declarations.comment: condition (2) of Definition 01G5 by Tag 018B, hence the hypercovering property

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isCechHypercovering_cech
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G6.** The Čech object of a covering family of `X` is a Čech
hypercovering of `X`: its degree-zero term is the covering family again, and it is
`0`-coskeletal, hence isomorphic to the zeroth coskeleton of that term.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCechHypercovering_cech (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (A : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)) (hA : IsCoveringOver J (terminal.from A)) :
    let : HasTerminal (Over X) := Over.over_hasTerminal X
    let : HasBinaryProducts (Over X) :=
      Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback
    let : HasFiniteProducts (Over X) := hasFiniteProducts_of_has_binary_and_terminal
    IsCechHypercovering J A.cech
declarations.comment: the Čech object of a covering family is a Čech hypercovering

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isHypercovering_cech_of_isCoveringOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G6.** The Čech object of a covering family `{U_i → X}_{i ∈ I}` of `X`
is a hypercovering of `X`. Its degree-`n` term is the family of the `(n + 1)`-fold fibre products
`U_{i_0} ×_X ⋯ ×_X U_{i_n}` over `X`, indexed by `I^{n + 1}`; see `FormalCoproduct.cech_obj`,
`FormalCoproduct.power_I` and `FormalCoproduct.power_obj`. The one-member case is
`isHypercovering_cech`, Tag 0GMA.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHypercovering_cech_of_isCoveringOver (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (A : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)) (hA : IsCoveringOver J (terminal.from A)) :
    let : HasTerminal (Over X) := Over.over_hasTerminal X
    let : HasBinaryProducts (Over X) :=
      Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback
    let : HasFiniteProducts (Over X) := hasFiniteProducts_of_has_binary_and_terminal
    IsHypercovering J A.cech
declarations.comment: the Čech object of a covering family is a hypercovering

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isHypercovering_cosk_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G6**, in the `cosk₀` shape in which the source states it: the zeroth
coskeleton of a zero-truncated simplicial object of `SR(C, X)` is a hypercovering of `X` as soon
as its degree-zero family covers `X`. The degree-zero family of `cosk₀ U` is `U` up to the
isomorphism given by the counit of the coskeletal adjunction; the covering hypothesis is stated
for `cosk₀ U` itself because a covering family of a pretopology need not stay covering under an
arbitrary isomorphism of `SR(C, X)` — see the implementation notes.

This is a convenience restatement, not the tag's assertion, and its hypothesis placement is not
claimed to be optimal: the counit comparison at level `0` is a limit over a one-object,
one-morphism indexing category, so it is of the objectwise shape that
`isCoveringOver_terminal_from_of_objFun` transports, and stating the hypothesis on `U` itself is
expected to be reachable by that route — it would need an explicit description of the pointwise
right Kan extension at degree `0`, which is not developed here. For the covering family itself
as the hypothesis, use `isHypercovering_cech_of_isCoveringOver`, which carries the source's own
hypothesis and whose Čech object is `0`-coskeletal and therefore of this form.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHypercovering_cosk_zero (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)) 0)
    (hU : IsCoveringOver J
      (terminal.from (((SimplicialObject.Truncated.cosk 0).obj U).obj (op ⦋0⦌)))) :
    IsHypercovering J ((SimplicialObject.Truncated.cosk 0).obj U)
declarations.comment: the hypercovering property in the `cosk₀` form

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isLimitWidePullbackConePowerObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G6**, the terms clause read in `C`. The component at `i : α → I` of
the `α`-fold power of the family `A = {U_i → X}` is a product taken in `Over X`; its underlying
object of `C` is the fibre product over `X` of the `U_{i a}`. Precisely, the cone in `C` with
apex that underlying object, projections the underlying morphisms of the product projections of
`Over X` and base the structure morphism to `X`, is a limit of the wide cospan of the structure
morphisms `U_{i a} → X`.

Together with `FormalCoproduct.cech_obj`, `FormalCoproduct.power_I` and
`FormalCoproduct.power_obj` this is the source's formula
`K_n = {U_{i_0} ×_X ⋯ ×_X U_{i_n} → X}` indexed by `I^{n + 1}`: take `α = Fin (n + 1)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isLimitWidePullbackConePowerObj {X : C} (A : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))
    (α : Type) [Finite α] :
    let : HasTerminal (Over X) := Over.over_hasTerminal X
    let : HasBinaryProducts (Over X) :=
      Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback
    let : HasFiniteProducts (Over X) := hasFiniteProducts_of_has_binary_and_terminal
    ∀ i : α → A.I, IsLimit (WidePullbackCone.mk (f := fun a ↦ (A.obj (i a)).hom)
      ((A.power α).obj i).hom (fun a ↦ (Pi.π (A.obj ∘ i) a).left)
      fun a ↦ Over.w (Pi.π (A.obj ∘ i) a))
declarations.comment: the terms in `C`: each component is the fibre product over `X` of its factors

registrations.name: FormalCoproduct.cech_obj
registrations.comment: the terms: the degree-`n` term is the `(n + 1)`-fold power

registrations.name: FormalCoproduct.power_I
registrations.comment: the terms: the index set `I^{n + 1}`

registrations.name: FormalCoproduct.power_obj
registrations.comment: the terms: the fibre product over `X` of the indexed components

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.small_hypercoverings
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01G7.** Hypercoverings of an object of a site with
fibre products form a set.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.locallySurjective_augmentation_of_isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
The degree-zero augmentation of the simplicial presheaf associated to a hypercovering is
locally surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallySurjective_augmentation_of_isHypercovering
    (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J.toGrothendieck
      ((associatedAugmentedSimplicialPresheafOver K).hom.app
        (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0)))

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.locallySurjective_oneMatchingMap_of_isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
The map from one-simplices to the fibre product of two copies of the presheaf of vertices
over the representable presheaf of `X` is locally surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallySurjective_oneMatchingMap_of_isHypercovering
    (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J.toGrothendieck
      (oneMatchingMap (associatedAugmentedSimplicialPresheafOver K).left
        (associatedAugmentedSimplicialPresheafOver K).right
        (associatedAugmentedSimplicialPresheafOver K).hom)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.locallySurjective_higherMatchingMap_of_isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
Every higher matching map of the simplicial presheaf associated to a hypercovering is
locally surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallySurjective_higherMatchingMap_of_isHypercovering
    (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J.toGrothendieck
      (((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app
        (associatedAugmentedSimplicialPresheafOver K).left).app
          (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1))))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isZero_sheafHomology_cechNerve_of_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc:
The positive homology sheaves of the Čech nerve of a locally surjective morphism of
presheaves of sets vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma isZero_sheafHomology_cechNerve_of_isLocallySurjective (hf : IsLocallySurjective J f)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero (SimplicialObject.sheafHomology J (Arrow.mk f).cechNerve n)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isIso_cechNerveSheafHomologyZeroAugmentation
declarations.doc:
The augmentation of the Čech nerve of a locally surjective morphism induces an isomorphism
from its degree-zero homology sheaf to the free abelian sheaf on the target.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_cechNerveSheafHomologyZeroAugmentation (hf : IsLocallySurjective J f) :
    IsIso (cechNerveSheafHomologyZeroAugmentation J f)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.isIso_sheafHomologyFunctor_map_of_coskeletal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GD.** A morphism between `n`-coskeletal simplicial
presheaves which is an isomorphism in degrees below `n` and locally surjective
in degree `n` induces an isomorphism on every homology sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafHomologyFunctor_map_of_coskeletal
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    {L K : SimplicialObject (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)} (f : L ⟶ K) (n i : ℕ)
    (h_lt : ∀ j : ℕ, j < n → IsIso (f.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk j))))
    (h_surjective :
      Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J (f.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk n))))
    (hL : IsIso ((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app L))
    (hK : IsIso ((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app K)) :
    IsIso ((sheafHomologyFunctor J i).map f)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Augmented.isZero_sheafHomology_of_isLocallySurjective_matchingMaps
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GE (positive degrees).** An augmented simplicial presheaf whose
degree-zero augmentation, relation map and matching maps are all locally surjective has zero
homology sheaf in every positive degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_sheafHomology_of_isLocallySurjective_matchingMaps
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (K : SimplicialObject.Augmented (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w))
    (h₀ : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J
      (K.hom.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))))
    (h₁ : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J (edgesToFiberProduct K))
    (hmatching : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J
      (((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app K.left).app
        (op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1)))))
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    IsZero (SimplicialObject.sheafHomology J K.left i)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Augmented.sheafHomologyZeroIso_of_isLocallySurjective_matchingMaps
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GE (degree zero).** The degree-zero homology sheaf of an augmented
simplicial presheaf whose degree-zero augmentation, relation map and matching maps are all
locally surjective is the free abelian sheaf on its presheaf of augmentation points.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomologyZeroIso_of_isLocallySurjective_matchingMaps
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (K : SimplicialObject.Augmented (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w))
    (h₀ : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J
      (K.hom.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))))
    (h₁ : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J (edgesToFiberProduct K))
    (hmatching : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J
      (((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app K.left).app
        (op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1))))) :
    SimplicialObject.sheafHomology J K.left 0 ≅
      (Presheaf.freeAbelianSheaf J).obj K.right

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isZero_sheafHomology_of_isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GF (positive degrees).** The homology of the simplicial presheaf
associated to a hypercovering vanishes in every positive degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_sheafHomology_of_isHypercovering (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    IsZero (SimplicialObject.sheafHomology J.toGrothendieck
      (SectionsOver.associatedSimplicialPresheaf.{w} K) i)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.sheafHomologyZeroIso_of_isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GF (degree zero).** The degree-zero homology of the simplicial
presheaf associated to a hypercovering is the free abelian sheaf on the represented object.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomologyZeroIso_of_isHypercovering (hK : IsHypercovering J K) :
    SimplicialObject.sheafHomology J.toGrothendieck
        (SectionsOver.associatedSimplicialPresheaf.{w} K) 0 ≅
      (presheafToSheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}).obj
        (uliftYoneda.{max u w}.obj X ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.free.{max u v w})

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isHypercovering_fibreProduct
declarations.doc:
A fibre product with a hypercovering is a hypercovering when the other morphism is covering
in degree zero and on every relative matching object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHypercovering_fibreProduct (J : Pretopology C)
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage] {X : C}
    {K L M : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))} (a : K ⟶ L) (b : M ⟶ L)
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K)
    (h₀ : IsCoveringOver J (b.app (op ⦋0⦌)))
    (hmatching : ∀ n : ℕ, IsCoveringOver J
      (Limits.pullback.lift
        (f := (((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app L).app (op ⦋n + 1⦌)))
        (g := (((SimplicialObject.Truncated.cosk n).map
          ((SimplicialObject.truncation n).map b)).app (op ⦋n + 1⦌)))
        (b.app (op ⦋n + 1⦌))
        (((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app M).app (op ⦋n + 1⦌))
        (NatTrans.congr_app ((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.naturality b)
          (op ⦋n + 1⦌)))) :
    IsHypercovering J (SimplicialObject.fibreProduct a b)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsHypercovering.prod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GI.** The product of two hypercoverings of an object of a site with
fibre products is a hypercovering.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_hypercovering_map_factoring_through_covering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GJ.** A covering of the term in any fixed degree of a
hypercovering can be refined by a morphism from another hypercovering, whose component in that
degree factors through the covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hypercovering_map_factoring_through_covering
    (J : Pretopology C) [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage] {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (k : ℕ)
    {Z : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)}
    (u : Z ⟶ K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk k)))
    (hu : IsCoveringOver J u) :
    ∃ (L : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))),
      IsHypercovering J L ∧
        ∃ (f : L ⟶ K) (g : L.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk k)) ⟶ Z),
          g ≫ u = f.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk k))

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_hypercovering_map_factoring_through_locallySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GK.** A locally surjective map onto the presheaf represented by one
term of a hypercovering can be factored through after refining the hypercovering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hypercovering_map_factoring_through_locallySurjective
    (J : Pretopology C) [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage] {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{max u v w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (n : ℕ)
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u v w))
    (u : F ⟶ (associatedPresheafFunctorOver (X := X)).obj
      (K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J.toGrothendieck u] :
    ∃ (L : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{max u v w} (Over X))),
      IsHypercovering J L ∧
        ∃ (f : L ⟶ K)
          (g : (associatedPresheafFunctorOver (X := X)).obj
            (L.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))) ⟶ F),
            g ≫ u = (associatedPresheafFunctorOver (X := X)).map
              (f.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)))

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isCoveringOver_homFromSSetMap_app_zero_of_oneMoreSimplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GM.** Let `K` be a hypercovering of `X`. If the finite simplicial
set `V` is obtained from a subcomplex `U` by adjoining a single `n`-simplex `x`, with every
simplex of `V` outside `U` in degree above `n` degenerate, then the restriction morphism
`Hom(V, K)₀ ⟶ Hom(U, K)₀` is a covering in `SR(C, X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoveringOver_homFromSSetMap_app_zero_of_oneMoreSimplex (J : Pretopology C)
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage] {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K)
    (V : SSet.{max w v}) (U : V.Subcomplex)
    [SSet.Finite (U : SSet.{max w v})]
    (_hUnonempty : ∀ m : ℕ, Nonempty (U.obj (op ⦋m⦌)))
    (_hVfinite : ∀ m : ℕ, Finite (V.obj (op ⦋m⦌)))
    (_hVnonempty : ∀ m : ℕ, Nonempty (V.obj (op ⦋m⦌)))
    (n : ℕ) (x : V.obj (op ⦋n⦌))
    (hx : x ∉ Set.range (U.ι.app (op ⦋n⦌)))
    (hbelow : ∀ m < n, Function.Bijective (U.ι.app (op ⦋m⦌)))
    (hat : ∀ y : V.obj (op ⦋n⦌), y ∈ Set.range (U.ι.app (op ⦋n⦌)) ∨ y = x)
    (habove : ∀ m, n < m → ∀ y : V.obj (op ⦋m⦌),
      y ∉ Set.range (U.ι.app (op ⦋m⦌)) → y ∈ V.degenerate m)
    (HV HU : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hV : SimplicialObject.IsHomFromSSet V K HV)
    (hU : SimplicialObject.IsHomFromSSet U K HU) :
    IsCoveringOver J ((homFromSSetMap hV hU U.ι).app (op ⦋0⦌))

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isCoveringOver_homFromSSetRestriction_app_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GN.** Let `K` be a hypercovering of `X` and let `U ⊆ V` be finite
nonempty simplicial sets. Then restriction `Hom(V, K)₀ ⟶ Hom(U, K)₀` is a covering morphism in
`SR(C, X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoveringOver_homFromSSetRestriction_app_zero (J : Pretopology C)
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage] (X : C)
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))) (hK : IsHypercovering J K)
    (V : SSet.{max w v}) [V.Finite] [V.Nonempty]
    (U : V.Subcomplex) [SSet.Finite (U : SSet)] [SSet.Nonempty (U : SSet)] :
    IsCoveringOver J ((homFromSSetRestriction U.ι K).app (op ⦋0⦌))

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.boundaryIntervalRepresentable
declarations.doc:
Restriction to the two vertices of the interval is represented by the product of two copies
of a simplicial semi-representable object.
declarations.statement:
theorem boundaryIntervalRepresentable
    (L : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))) :
    Nonempty (SimplicialObject.IsHomFromSSet (SSet.boundary.{max v w} 1) L (L ⨯ L))

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.intervalEndpointMap
declarations.doc:
The fixed endpoint-evaluation morphism `Hom(Δ[1], L) ⟶ L × L`. Its two components are, in
order, the restrictions of the universal interval map to the vertices zero and one.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def intervalEndpointMap
    (L H : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hH : SimplicialObject.IsHomFromSSet Δ[1] L H) :
    { e : H ⟶ L ⨯ L //
      (∀ m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ,
        (e ≫ prod.fst).app m =
          (Functor.functorHomEquiv H L Δ[1] (hH.homEquiv (𝟙 H))).app m
            (SSet.stdSimplex.const 1 0 m)) ∧
      (∀ m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ,
        (e ≫ prod.snd).app m =
          (Functor.functorHomEquiv H L Δ[1] (hH.homEquiv (𝟙 H))).app m
            (SSet.stdSimplex.const 1 1 m)) }

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.homotopyMatchingSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GP.** The four matching objects are represented by the corresponding
simplicial sets, and the `Hom` object of the union is their fibre product. All arrows in the
fibre product square are those induced by inclusions of simplicial sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopyMatchingSquare
    (L : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (H : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hH : SimplicialObject.IsHomFromSSet Δ[1] L H) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ Q : FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X),
      let e := (intervalEndpointMap X L H hH).1;
      let m := n + 1;
      let S := SSet.boundary.{max v w} 1;
      let T := SSet.boundary.{max v w} m;
      let U := S.unionProd T;
      let F := coyoneda ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringLeft SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ
          (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)) (Type (max v w))).obj L;
      ∃ (hFull : (F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op (Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[m]))).RepresentableBy (H _⦋m⦌))
        (hTop : (F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op (Δ[1] ⊗ (T : SSet)))).RepresentableBy
          (((SimplicialObject.cosk n).obj H) _⦋m⦌))
        (hBottom : (F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op ((S : SSet) ⊗ Δ[m]))).RepresentableBy
          ((L ⨯ L) _⦋m⦌))
        (hRight : (F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op ((S : SSet) ⊗ (T : SSet)))).RepresentableBy
          (((SimplicialObject.cosk n).obj (L ⨯ L)) _⦋m⦌))
        (hUnion : (F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op (U : SSet))).RepresentableBy Q),
        let comparison := hUnion.homEquiv.symm (U.ι ≫ hFull.homEquiv (𝟙 _));
        (e.app (op ⦋m⦌) =
          hBottom.homEquiv.symm ((S.ι ▷ Δ[m]) ≫ hFull.homEquiv (𝟙 _))) ∧
        ((((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app H).app (op ⦋m⦌)) =
          hTop.homEquiv.symm ((Δ[1] ◁ T.ι) ≫ hFull.homEquiv (𝟙 _))) ∧
        ((((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app (L ⨯ L)).app (op ⦋m⦌)) =
          hRight.homEquiv.symm (((S : SSet) ◁ T.ι) ≫ hBottom.homEquiv (𝟙 _))) ∧
        ((((SimplicialObject.cosk n).map e).app (op ⦋m⦌)) =
          hRight.homEquiv.symm ((S.ι ▷ (T : SSet)) ≫ hTop.homEquiv (𝟙 _))) ∧
        (comparison ≫ hTop.homEquiv.symm
          (SSet.Subcomplex.unionProd.ι₁ S T ≫ hUnion.homEquiv (𝟙 Q)) =
          ((SimplicialObject.coskAdj n).unit.app H).app (op ⦋m⦌)) ∧
        (comparison ≫ hBottom.homEquiv.symm
          (SSet.Subcomplex.unionProd.ι₂ S T ≫ hUnion.homEquiv (𝟙 Q)) =
          e.app (op ⦋m⦌)) ∧
        IsPullback
          (hTop.homEquiv.symm (SSet.Subcomplex.unionProd.ι₁ S T ≫
            hUnion.homEquiv (𝟙 Q)))
          (hBottom.homEquiv.symm (SSet.Subcomplex.unionProd.ι₂ S T ≫
            hUnion.homEquiv (𝟙 Q)))
          (hRight.homEquiv.symm ((S.ι ▷ (T : SSet)) ≫ hTop.homEquiv (𝟙 _)))
          (hRight.homEquiv.symm (((S : SSet) ◁ T.ι) ≫ hBottom.homEquiv (𝟙 _)))

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_homotopy_after_hypercovering_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GS.** Two morphisms between hypercoverings become simplicially
homotopic after precomposition with a morphism from a further hypercovering.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopy_after_hypercovering_refinement (J : Pretopology C)
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage] {X : C}
    {K L : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))}
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (hL : IsHypercovering J L) (a b : K ⟶ L) :
    ∃ (K' : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))) (c : K' ⟶ K),
      IsHypercovering J K' ∧
