        ∃ h : K'.copower Δ[1] ⟶ L, SimplicialObject.IsHomotopy h (c ≫ a) (c ≫ b)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.nonempty_zerothCechCohomologyIsoSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GV**, the existence half. Degree-zero Čech cohomology of a
hypercovering is isomorphic to the group of sections of the coefficient sheaf on the covered
object.

This asserts only that some isomorphism exists. The canonical one, inverse to the map induced by
the augmentation of the Čech complex and natural in the sheaf, is
`zerothCechCohomologyIsoSections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_zerothCechCohomologyIsoSections (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K)
    (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) :
    Nonempty ((SectionsOver.sectionsComplex J.toGrothendieck K F).homology 0 ≅
      F.obj.obj (op X))
declarations.comment: some isomorphism Ȟ⁰(K, 𝓕) ≅ 𝓕(X) exists

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.zerothCechCohomologyFunctorIsoSections
declarations.doc:
For a hypercovering `K` of `X` the degree-zero Čech cohomology `Ȟ⁰(K, -)` is the functor of
sections on `X`, as an isomorphism of functors on the abelian sheaves, inverse to the canonical map
induced by the augmentation of the Čech complex by the sections on `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zerothCechCohomologyFunctorIsoSections (hK : IsHypercovering J K) :
    SectionsOver.sectionsComplexFunctor J.toGrothendieck K ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 ≅
      sheafToPresheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w} ⋙
        (evaluation Cᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}).obj (op X)
declarations.comment: the identification Ȟ⁰(K, 𝓕) = 𝓕(X), as functors on Ab(C)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.zerothCechCohomologyIsoSections
declarations.doc:
For a hypercovering `K` of `X` and an abelian sheaf `F`, the degree-zero Čech cohomology
`Ȟ⁰(K, F)` is the group `F(X)` of sections on `X`: the component at `F` of
`zerothCechCohomologyFunctorIsoSections`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zerothCechCohomologyIsoSections (hK : IsHypercovering J K)
    (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) :
    (SectionsOver.sectionsComplex J.toGrothendieck K F).homology 0 ≅ F.obj.obj (op X)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isIso_kernelLift_terminalAugZero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01GV] in degree zero, in canonical-map form.**  For a hypercovering `K` of an
object `X` of a site and an **arbitrary** abelian sheaf `F`, the canonical augmentation
`F(X) ⟶ ∏_{i ∈ K₀} F(K₀(i))` of the Čech complex of `K` exhibits `F(X)` as the kernel of the first
differential.

No injectivity of `F` is assumed:  the input
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Augmented.isIso_kernelLift_freeAbelianSheafAugZero` needs only
conditions (1) and (2) of a hypercovering, which
`Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isLocallySurjective_of_isHypercovering` supplies.

The terminal object of `Over X` at which the augmentation is formed is arbitrary; the proof
transports it to `Over.mk (𝟙 X)` by `terminalAugZero_eq_comp_of_isTerminal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_kernelLift_terminalAugZero (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (Limits.FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) {T : Over X} (hT : IsTerminal T)
    (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) :
    IsIso (kernel.lift ((SectionsOver.sectionsComplex J.toGrothendieck K F).d 0 1)
      (terminalAugZero K hT
        (((Functor.whiskeringLeft (Over X)ᵒᵖ Cᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}).obj
          (Over.forget X).op).obj
          ((sheafToPresheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}).obj F)))
      (terminalAugZero_comp_d K hT
        (((Functor.whiskeringLeft (Over X)ᵒᵖ Cᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}).obj
          (Over.forget X).op).obj
          ((sheafToPresheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}).obj F))))
declarations.comment: degree zero, as a kernel of the first differential of the Čech complex

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.cechCohomologyOver_isZero_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GW (positive degrees).** The positive-degree Čech cohomology of an
injective abelian sheaf on a hypercovering vanishes.

Sheafification, which the statement does not need, is supplied inside the proof from
`hasSheafify_addCommGrpCat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechCohomologyOver_isZero_of_injective (J : Pretopology C) {X : C}
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K)
    (I : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) [Injective I]
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero ((SectionsOver.sectionsComplex J.toGrothendieck K I).homology p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.cechCohomologyOverIsoOfInjective
declarations.doc:
For a hypercovering `K` of `X` and an injective abelian sheaf `I`, the Čech cohomology
`Ȟᵖ(K, I)` is the group `I(X)` of sections on `X` when `p = 0` and is zero when `p > 0`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechCohomologyOverIsoOfInjective (hK : IsHypercovering J K)
    (I : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) [Injective I] (p : ℕ) :
    (SectionsOver.sectionsComplex J.toGrothendieck K I).homology p ≅
      if p = 0 then I.obj.obj (op X) else 0

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.SemiRepresentable.sectionsComplexIsoHomFreeAbelianSheafComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GX.** The cochain complex of sections on any simplicial
semi-representable presheaf is canonically the Hom complex from its complex of free abelian
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sectionsComplexIsoHomFreeAbelianSheafComplex
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)}]
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} C))
    (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)}) :
    sectionsComplex.{q, w, v, u} J K F ≅
      homFreeAbelianSheafComplex.{q, w, v, u} J K F

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.SectionsOver.sectionsComplexIsoHomFreeAbelianSheafComplex
declarations.doc:
The complex obtained by evaluating an abelian sheaf `F` on a simplicial semi-representable
object `K` is isomorphic to the complex of morphisms from the associated complex of free abelian
sheaves into `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sectionsComplexIsoHomFreeAbelianSheafComplex {X : C}
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))
    (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) :
    sectionsComplex J K F ≅ homFreeAbelianSheafComplex J K F

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_hypercoverToDerivedSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GY.**  For a hypercovering `K` of an object `X` of a site with fibre
products there are a canonical map `ψ` from the sections on `X` to derived sections at the single
complex, and a map

`α : s(-(K)) ⟶ RΓ(X, -)`

in `D⁺(Ab)`, functorial in the abelian sheaf, compatible with the augmentation of `s(-(K))` by the
sections on `X`; and both are isomorphisms at every injective sheaf.

The last clause is what makes the statement non-vacuous: by
`StacksDraft.DerivedSectionsComparison.isZero_of_pin_zero`, `α = 0` would force `Q(s(I(K)))` to be
a zero object for every injective `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hypercoverToDerivedSections (hK : IsHypercovering J K) :
    ∃ (ψ : (sheafSectionsFunctor.{w} J X ⋙ singlePlus AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Plus.Q ⟶ derivedSectionsFunctor.{w} J X)
      (α : hypercoverDerivedFunctor.{w} J X K ⟶ derivedSectionsFunctor.{w} J X),
      Functor.whiskerRight
            (epsNat (sheafSectionsFunctor.{w} J X) (hypercoverCochainIntFunctor.{w} J X K)
              (sectionsEps.{w} J X K)
              (fun {_ _} φ ↦ sectionsEps_naturality.{w} J X K φ)
              (isZero_hypercoverCochainIntFunctor_obj_X.{w} J X K))
            DerivedCategory.Plus.Q ≫ α = ψ ∧
        (∀ F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}, Injective F → IsIso (ψ.app F)) ∧
        ∀ F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}, Injective F → IsIso (α.app F)
declarations.comment: the comparison map s(F(K)) ⟶ RΓ(X, F) in D⁺(Ab), functorial in F

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_cechCohomologyToSheafCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GY.**  The comparison map of
`exists_hypercoverToDerivedSections` induces, in every degree `i`, a natural transformation

`Ȟ^i(K, -) ⟶ H^i(X, -)`

of functors from abelian sheaves to abelian groups, and these are isomorphisms at every injective
sheaf.

The source is the `i`-th cohomology of the complex `s(-(K))` itself, i.e. the Čech cohomology of
the hypercovering, and the target is the `i`-th cohomology of `RΓ(X, -)`, i.e. sheaf cohomology on
`X`.  The invertibility at injectives is again what rules out the zero transformation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cechCohomologyToSheafCohomology (hK : IsHypercovering J K) :
    ∃ β : ∀ i : ℤ,
        (hypercoverCochainIntFunctor.{w} J X K ⋙
            HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ) i) ⟶
          (derivedSectionsFunctor.{w} J X ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w} i),
      ∀ (i : ℤ) (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}),
        Injective F → IsIso ((β i).app F)
declarations.comment: the induced natural transformations Ȟ^i(K, -) ⟶ H^i(X, -)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.hypercoverComparisonMap
declarations.doc:
**The comparison map of Stacks 01GY**: for a hypercovering `K` of `X`, the natural
transformation `s(F(K)) ⟶ RΓ(X, F)` in `D⁺(Ab)`.

It is `s(F(K)) ≅ Θ(F[0]) ⟶ RΘ(F[0]) ≅ RΓ(X, F)`: the identification of `s(F(K))` with the
hypercover total complex of `F[0]`, the unit of the right derived functor of `Θ`, and the inverse
of the comparison `RΓ(X, -) ⟶ RΘ` induced by the augmentation. It is pinned down by
`hypercoverAugDerivedSections_comp_hypercoverComparisonMap`.
declarations.statement:
def hypercoverComparisonMap (hK : IsHypercovering J K) :
    hypercoverDerivedFunctor J U K ⟶ derivedSectionsFunctor J U

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.hypercoverCohomologyComparison
declarations.doc:
The natural map from the Čech cohomology of a hypercovering `K` of `X` to sheaf cohomology in
degree `i`, induced by the comparison map `hypercoverComparisonMap`.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.hypercoverSpectralSequenceHypercoveringFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The spectral sequence of [Stacks, Tag 01GY] is functorial in the hypercovering**, which is
the last sentence of its third clause: the assignment taking a simplicial semi-representable
object `K` over `X` to the functorial spectral sequence
`hypercoverSpectralSequenceFunctor J X K` of `HypercoveringSpectralSequenceData.sequence` is a
functor on the opposite category, contravariance being the direction in which a morphism of
hypercoverings acts on Čech cochains.

Morphisms are taken to be *all* morphisms of simplicial semi-representable objects over `X`, which
is more than the source asks for: a morphism of hypercoverings is in particular one of these, the
hypercovering conditions being conditions on an object and not on a morphism.
declarations.statement:
def hypercoverSpectralSequenceHypercoveringFunctor :
    (SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)))ᵒᵖ ⥤
      (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w} ⥤
        E₂CohomologicalSpectralSequenceNat AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w})
declarations.comment: spectral sequence functorial in the hypercovering

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.hypercoveringSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**The functorial spectral sequence of a hypercovering**, with second page
`Ȟ^p(K, H̲^q(F))` and abutment `H^{p+q}(X, F)`.

This is the third clause of [Stacks, Tag 01GY]: the four fields are
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.enoughInjectives_addCommGrpCat`, `hypercoverSpectralSequenceFunctor`,
`hypercoverPageTwoIso` and `hypercoverAbutment`.  The functoriality of this spectral sequence in
the hypercovering, which is the last sentence of that clause, is
`hypercoverSpectralSequenceHypercoveringFunctor`, whose value at `K` is the `sequence` field
below.
declarations.statement:
def hypercoveringSpectralSequence (hK : IsHypercovering J K) :
    HypercoveringSpectralSequenceData.{w} J X K hK

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.hypercoveringCohomologyAbutment
declarations.doc:
**Clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01GY], the functorial abutment**: the hypercovering spectral
sequence abuts to `H^{p+q}(X, F)`, functorially in the hypercovering and in the coefficient
sheaf.

`hypercoveringFunctorialAbutment` with the cohomology of the total complex replaced by sheaf
cohomology through `hypercoverAbutmentNatIso`;
`Stacks.Cohomology.Leray.FunctorialFirstQuadrantAbutsTo.ofIsoAbutment` touches no other field --
the structure mentions the asserted abutment in `abutmentIso` alone.
declarations.statement:
def hypercoveringCohomologyAbutment :
    _root_.Stacks.Cohomology.Leray.FunctorialFirstQuadrantAbutsTo
      (hypercoveringSpectralSequence X J)
      (fun n ↦ hypercoveringCohomologyFunctor X J n)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.hypercoveringPageTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**The `pageTwoIso` of clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01GY]**: the second page of
`Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.hypercoveringSpectralSequence` at `(p, q)` is
`Ȟ^p(K, H^q(F))`, naturally in the hypercovering and in the coefficient sheaf simultaneously.
It is `hypercoverPageTwoIso` restricted along the inclusion of the full subcategory of
hypercoverings, since nothing in the second-page identification uses the hypercovering
condition -- that is needed only for the abutment.

The source is written as the whiskering rather than as
`Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.hypercoveringSpectralSequence` composed with the
page
functor. The two are the same functor -- `hypercoveringSpectralSequence` *is* that whiskering,
and composition of functors is associative definitionally -- but checking that at the ambient
heartbeat budget means unfolding `CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.natRestrictE₂Comp` inside a
functor-level defeq, which does not finish.
declarations.statement:
def hypercoveringPageTwoIso (p q : ℕ) :
    (ObjectProperty.ι (fun K : SimplicialObject (Limits.FormalCoproduct.{v} (Over X)) =>
            IsHypercovering J K)).op.prod
          (𝟭 (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{v})) ⋙
        hypercoverSpectralSequenceFunctor X J.toGrothendieck ⋙
          CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.pageFunctor _ _ 2 2 ⋙
            HomologicalComplex.eval _ _ (p, q) ≅
      pageTwoHypercovering.{v} X J p q

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.hypercoveringSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**The `sequence` of clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01GY]**: the first-quadrant `E₂` cohomological
spectral sequence of a hypercovering of `X` and a sheaf of abelian groups, functorial in the
hypercovering (contravariantly) and in the sheaf. It is the restriction of
`hypercoverSpectralSequenceFunctor` along the inclusion of the full subcategory of
hypercoverings, since nothing in the construction of the sequence itself uses the hypercovering
condition -- that is needed only for the abutment, which is not here.

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.homologyMap_hypercoverCochainNatFunctorMap_app_eq_of_isHomotopy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GZ.**  Homotopic maps of simplicial semi-representable objects over
`X` have the same effect on the Čech cohomology of an abelian sheaf: by [Stacks, Tag 019Y] their
images on the cosimplicial object of sections are homotopic, and by [Stacks, Tag 01A0] homotopic
maps of cosimplicial objects induce the same map on the cohomology of the associated cochain
complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologyMap_hypercoverCochainNatFunctorMap_app_eq_of_isHomotopy
    {K K' : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))}
    [∀ m, HasCoproduct fun _ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{t}).obj m ↦ K.obj m]
    {ψ ψ' : K ⟶ K'} {h : K.copower (Δ[1] : SSet.{t}) ⟶ K'}
    (hh : SimplicialObject.IsHomotopy h ψ ψ')
    (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) (p : ℕ) :
    HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
        ((hypercoverCochainNatFunctorMap.{w} J X ψ).app F) p =
      HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
        ((hypercoverCochainNatFunctorMap.{w} J X ψ').app F) p
declarations.comment: homotopic maps of hypercoverings have the same effect on Čech cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.whiskerRight_hypercoverCochainNatFunctorMap_eq_of_isHomotopy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GZ**, as natural transformations.  The map `Ȟ^p(K', -) ⟶ Ȟ^p(K, -)`
of Čech cohomology functors induced by a map `K ⟶ K'` depends only on its homotopy class.
declarations.comment: the induced natural transformation on Ȟ^p depends only on the homotopy class

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.cechCohomologyHypercoveringsHomotopyFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01GZ.**  `Ȟ^p(-, -) : HC(C, X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ (Ab(C) ⥤ Ab)`: the Čech cohomology
of a hypercovering of `X`, as a diagram on the hypercoverings of `X` with maps up to homotopy.

This is the diagram whose colimit [Stacks, Tag 01H0] compares with sheaf cohomology; it exists
because homotopic maps have the same effect on Čech cohomology, which is
`whiskerRight_hypercoverCochainNatFunctorMap_eq_of_isHomotopy`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechCohomologyHypercoveringsHomotopyFunctor (p : ℕ) :
    (HypercoveringsHomotopy.{w} J X)ᵒᵖ ⥤
      (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w} ⥤
        AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w})
declarations.comment: Ȟ^p(-, 𝓕) as a diagram on HC(C, X)ᵒᵖ

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.isColimit_cechCohomologyZeroCocone
declarations.doc:
For a site with fibre products and an object `X`, the functor `𝓕 ↦ H⁰(X, 𝓕)` on abelian
sheaves is the colimit over all hypercoverings `K` of `X` of the functors `𝓕 ↦ Ȟ⁰(K, H⁰(𝓕))`,
the cocone being the canonical identification of each `Ȟ⁰(K, H⁰(-))` with `H⁰(X, -)`.
declarations.statement:
def isColimit_cechCohomologyZeroCocone
    [Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition J.toPrecoverage] :
    IsColimit (cechCohomologyZeroCocone X J)
declarations.comment: the case i = 0: colim over hypercoverings of Ȟ⁰(K, H⁰(-)) is H⁰(X, -), as functors on Ab(C); the hypotheses carried are fibre products in C and stability of the pretopology under composition

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.isColimit_cechCoconeAtSheaf
declarations.doc:
For a site with fibre products, an object `X` and an abelian sheaf `𝓕`, the cohomology
`H^n(X, 𝓕)` is the colimit over the hypercoverings of `X` of the Čech cohomology groups
`Ȟ^n(K, 𝓕)`, the cocone being the canonical edge maps `hypercoveringCechEdge`. The index category
is the category of hypercoverings itself, not the homotopy quotient `HC(C, X)`.
declarations.statement:
def isColimit_cechCoconeAtSheaf (n : ℕ) (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{v}) :
    IsColimit (cechCoconeAtSheaf X J n F)
declarations.comment: the general case at a fixed abelian sheaf: colim over hypercoverings of Ȟ^i(K, 𝓕) is H^i(X, 𝓕); the index category is the hypercoverings of X themselves rather than the homotopy quotient HC(C, X), and the hypotheses carried are fibre products in C and stability of the pretopology under composition

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.isColimit_cechFunctorCocone
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a site with fibre products and `X` an object of `C`. For every `i`, the two
functors `Ab(C) ⥤ Ab` given by `𝓕 ↦ H^i(X, 𝓕)` and by `𝓕 ↦ colim_K Ȟ^i(K, 𝓕)`, the colimit
being over the hypercoverings `K` of `X`, are canonically isomorphic: the edge maps
`hypercoveringCechEdge` exhibit the functor `H^i(X, -)` as the colimit of the functors
`Ȟ^i(K, -)` in the category of functors `Ab(C) ⥤ Ab`. The index category is the category of
hypercoverings itself, not the homotopy quotient `HC(C, X)`.
declarations.statement: def isColimit_cechFunctorCocone (n : ℕ) : IsColimit (cechFunctorCocone X J n)
declarations.comment: the functor-level statement in every degree, which is the claim of the tag: the edge maps exhibit the functor 𝓕 ↦ H^i(X, 𝓕) on Ab(C) as the colimit over the hypercoverings K of X of the functors 𝓕 ↦ Ȟ^i(K, 𝓕), the colimit being taken in the category of functors Ab(C) ⥤ Ab; the index category is the hypercoverings of X themselves rather than the homotopy quotient HC(C, X), and the hypotheses carried are fibre products in C and stability of the pretopology under composition

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.iSup_eq_top_of_isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01H2.** In a hypercovering of a topological space, the opens attached
to the degree-zero indices cover the whole space.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_eq_top_of_isHypercovering {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over (⊤ : Opens X))))
    (hK : IsHypercovering (Opens.pretopology X) K) :
    (⨆ i : (K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌)).I, ((K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌)).obj i).left) = ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.inf_eq_iSup_edges
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01H3.** In a hypercovering of a topological space, the intersection of
the opens attached to two vertices is the union of the opens attached to the edges whose zeroth
and first faces are those vertices.
declarations.statement:
theorem inf_eq_iSup_edges {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over (⊤ : Opens X))))
    (hK : IsHypercovering (Opens.pretopology X) K)
    (i₀ i₁ : (K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌)).I) :
    ((K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌)).obj i₀).left ⊓
        ((K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋0⦌)).obj i₁).left =
      ⨆ i : { i : (K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋1⦌)).I //
          (K.δ (0 : Fin 2)).f i = i₀ ∧ (K.δ (1 : Fin 2)).f i = i₁ },
        ((K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋1⦌)).obj i.1).left

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.intersection_eq_union_of_isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01H4.** In a hypercovering of a topological space, the intersection of
a compatible family of `n + 3` degree-`n + 1` opens is the union of the degree-`n + 2` opens whose
faces are the prescribed family. This is the source's equation in every degree at least one.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersection_eq_union_of_isHypercovering
    (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X]
    (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over (⊤ : Opens X))))
    (hK : IsHypercovering (Opens.pretopology X) K)
    (n : ℕ)
    (i : (a : Fin (n + 3)) → (K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1)))).I)
    (hi : ∀ (a b : Fin (n + 3)) (hab : a < b),
      (K.δ (b.pred (ne_of_gt (lt_of_le_of_lt (Fin.zero_le a) hab)))).f (i a) =
        (K.δ (a.castPred (ne_of_lt (lt_of_lt_of_le hab (Fin.le_last b))))).f (i b)) :
    (⨅ a, ((K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1)))).obj (i a)).left) =
      ⨆ j : { j : (K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 2)))).I //
        ∀ a, (K.δ a).f j = i a },
        ((K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 2)))).obj j.1).left

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_hypercovering_of_isTopologicalBasis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01H6.** Every basis of a topological space supports a hypercovering all
of whose constituent open subsets belong to that basis.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hypercovering_of_isTopologicalBasis
    (B : Set (Set X)) (hB : IsTopologicalBasis B) :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{u} (Over (⊤ : Opens X))),
      IsHypercovering (Opens.pretopology X) K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ i : (K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌)).I,
          ((K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left.1 ∈ B

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_finite_hypercovering_of_isTopologicalBasis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01H7.** A quasi-compact topological space with a basis of
quasi-compact opens and quasi-compact intersections of quasi-compact opens has a hypercovering
subordinate to that basis whose index type is finite in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_hypercovering_of_isTopologicalBasis
    (B : Set (Set X)) (hB : IsTopologicalBasis B)
    (hX : IsCompact (Set.univ : Set X))
    (hBcompact : ∀ U ∈ B, IsCompact U)
    (hInter : ∀ U V : Set X, IsOpen U → IsCompact U →
      IsOpen V → IsCompact V → IsCompact (U ∩ V)) :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{u} (Over (⊤ : Opens X))),
      IsHypercovering (Opens.pretopology X) K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, Finite (K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))).I ∧
          ∀ i : (K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))).I,
            ((K.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))).obj i).left.1 ∈ B

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace
registrations.comment:
Part 1: a locally ringed space is a topological space with a sheaf of rings all
  of whose stalks are local rings.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.isLocalRing
registrations.comment:
Part 2: the local ring O_{X,x} of X at x is the stalk, which is local (the
  maximal ideal m_x is `IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal` of the stalk).

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.residueField
registrations.comment: Part 2: the residue field kappa(x) = O_{X,x}/m_x of X at x.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.Hom
registrations.comment:
Part 3: a morphism of locally ringed spaces is a morphism of ringed spaces whose
  stalk maps are local ring maps.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.isoOfSheafedSpaceIso
registrations.comment:
An isomorphism of ringed spaces between locally ringed spaces is an isomorphism
  of locally ringed spaces.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.homOfSheafedSpaceHomOfIsIso
registrations.comment: The lift of the isomorphism of ringed spaces has the same underlying morphism.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.restrictStalkIso
registrations.comment: The stalk of the restriction O_X|_U at u is the stalk of O_X at u.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.restrict
registrations.comment: (U, O_X|_U) is a locally ringed space.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.ofRestrict
registrations.comment: The morphism j : (U, O_U) → (X, O_X).

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.ofRestrict
registrations.comment: j is an open immersion.

registrations.name: LocallyRingedSpace.restrict
registrations.comment: open subspace, as the restriction along an open embedding

registrations.name: LocallyRingedSpace.ofRestrict
registrations.comment: the inclusion of the open subspace

registrations.name: LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.isoRestrict
registrations.comment: existence of the isomorphism with the open subspace on the image

registrations.name: LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.isoRestrict_hom_ofRestrict
registrations.comment: the factorization f = j ∘ f'

registrations.name: LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.mono
registrations.comment: uniqueness, as j is a monomorphism

registrations.name: LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.lift
registrations.comment: existence of the restriction, through the open immersion V → Y

registrations.name: LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac
registrations.comment: the square commutes

registrations.name: LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion.lift_uniq
registrations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.IsClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01C2.** A morphism of ringed spaces is a closed immersion when its
underlying continuous map is a closed embedding, its map on structure sheaves is surjective,
and the kernel of that map is locally generated by sections.
declarations.statement: class IsClosedImmersion {X Z : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) : Prop
declarations.comment: the same three conditions for a morphism of locally ringed spaces

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion_of_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01HL.** A morphism of ringed spaces whose restrictions over the
members of an open covering of the target are closed immersions is itself a closed immersion.

This is the Stacks statement with locally ringed spaces relaxed to ringed spaces; see
`Stacks.ClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion_toShHom_of_iSup_eq_top` for the source's own
formulation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_iSup_eq_top
    {X Z : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : Z ⟶ X) {ι : Type v} (U : ι → Opens X)
    (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (pullback.fst (X.ofRestrict (U i).isOpenEmbedding) f)) :
    IsClosedImmersion f
declarations.comment: stated for ringed spaces; the source states it for locally ringed spaces

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion_toShHom_of_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01HL.** Let `f : Z ⟶ X` be a morphism of locally ringed spaces. For
`f` to be a closed immersion it suffices that there is an open covering `X = ⋃ Uᵢ` such that
each `f : f⁻¹ Uᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ` is a closed immersion.

This is the source's formulation. It is the ringed-space statement
`Stacks.ClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion_of_iSup_eq_top` applied to the underlying morphism of
ringed spaces, since being a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces is by definition the
corresponding condition on that morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_toShHom_of_iSup_eq_top
    {X Z : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ X) {ι : Type v} (U : ι → Opens X)
    (hU : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsClosedImmersion
      (pullback.fst (X.toRingedSpace.ofRestrict (U i).isOpenEmbedding) f.toShHom)) :
    IsClosedImmersion f.toShHom

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.existsUnique_iso_closedSubspace
declarations.doc:
A closed immersion is uniquely isomorphic over its target to the closed subspace defined by
its ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_closedSubspace {X Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [hf : IsClosedImmersion f.toShHom] :
    let Z := closedSubspace Y (idealSheaf f.toShHom) (kernel.ι _) hf.kernel_locallyGenerated
    ∃! e : X ≅ Z.space, e.hom ≫ Z.inclusion = f

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.subsingleton_factorizations_closedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01HP.** A factorization of a morphism of locally ringed spaces
through the closed subspace associated to an ideal sheaf, when it exists, is unique.

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.factorsThrough_closedSubspace_iff
declarations.doc:
A morphism of locally ringed spaces factors through the closed subspace cut out by `j`
exactly when the canonical map `f^* J ⟶ 𝒪_Y` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThrough_closedSubspace_iff [Mono j] (D : ClosedSubspaceData X J j) (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (∃ g : Y ⟶ D.space, g ≫ D.inclusion = f) ↔ pullbackIdealMap f J j = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.factorsThrough_closedSubspace_of_localGenerators_iff
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of locally ringed spaces factors through the closed subspace cut out
by a sheaf of ideals `j : J ⟶ 𝒪_X` which is locally generated by sections exactly when the
canonical map `f^* J ⟶ 𝒪_Y` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThrough_closedSubspace_of_localGenerators_iff {X Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}}
    (J : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
    (j : J ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) [Mono j]
    (hJ : Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} J)) (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (∃ g : Y ⟶ (closedSubspace X J j hJ).space,
        g ≫ (closedSubspace X J j hJ).inclusion = f) ↔ pullbackIdealMap f J j = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.subsingleton_factorizations_closedSubspace_of_localGenerators
declarations.doc:
A factorization of a morphism of locally ringed spaces through the closed subspace cut out by
a sheaf of ideals which is locally generated by sections, when it exists, is unique.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_factorizations_closedSubspace_of_localGenerators
    {X Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}}
    (J : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
    (j : J ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) [Mono j]
    (hJ : Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} J)) (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    Subsingleton {g : Y ⟶ (closedSubspace X J j hJ).space //
      g ≫ (closedSubspace X J j hJ).inclusion = f}

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.pullbackIdeal_locallyGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01HQ.** The inverse-image ideal of a locally generated ideal sheaf is
locally generated. Tag 01B3 gives local generators for the pullback `f^* I`, and the inverse-image
ideal is a quotient of `f^* I`, so the images of those generators generate it.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackIdeal_locallyGenerated (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace))
    (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace))
    (hI : Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} I)) :
    Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} (pullbackIdeal f I i))

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.restrictedMap
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 01HQ.** The morphism of closed subspaces induced by `f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictedMap (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace))
    (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)) [Mono i]
    (hI : Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} I)) :
    (pullbackClosedSubspace f I i hI).space ⟶ (closedSubspace Y I i hI).space

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.restrictedMap_commutes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01HQ.** The induced map commutes with the inclusions into the ambient
spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictedMap_commutes (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace))
    (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)) [Mono i]
    (hI : Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} I)) :
    restrictedMap f I i hI ≫ (closedSubspace Y I i hI).inclusion =
      (pullbackClosedSubspace f I i hI).inclusion ≫ f

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.restrictedMap_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01HQ.** A morphism between the associated closed subspaces over `f` is
the induced one.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictedMap_unique (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace))
    (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)) [Mono i]
    (hI : Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} I))
    (g : (pullbackClosedSubspace f I i hI).space ⟶ (closedSubspace Y I i hI).space)
    (hg : g ≫ (closedSubspace Y I i hI).inclusion =
      (pullbackClosedSubspace f I i hI).inclusion ≫ f) :
    g = restrictedMap f I i hI

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.restrictedMap_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01HQ.** The restriction square is a fibre square of locally ringed
spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictedMap_isPullback (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace))
    (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace)) [Mono i]
    (hI : Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} I)) :
    IsPullback (pullbackClosedSubspace f I i hI).inclusion (restrictedMap f I i hI) f
      (closedSubspace Y I i hI).inclusion

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Cech.exists_isStandardOpenCoverOfSpectrum_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Any open covering of an affine open of a scheme is refined by a finite standard open
covering of it.** This is the scheme-level form of [Stacks, Tag 01HS] part (2), and it is
condition (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01EW] for the system of finite standard open coverings of affine
opens: the returned family `g` of sections over `U` satisfies the standard-covering condition of
[Stacks, Tag 01HT], its ambient basic opens cover `U`, and each of them is contained in a member
of the given family.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isStandardOpenCoverOfSpectrum_refinement {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    {ι : Type v} (W : ι → X.Opens) (hW : U ≤ ⨆ i, W i) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : Fin n → Γ(X, U)) (a : Fin n → ι),
      PrimeSpectrum.IsStandardOpenCoverOfSpectrum g ∧ (⨆ j, X.basicOpen (g j)) = U ∧
        ∀ j, X.basicOpen (g j) ≤ W (a j)
declarations.comment: part (2), for an affine open of a scheme

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.ringRestrictionMap
declarations.doc: The canonical `R`-algebra map `R_f → R_g` attached to an inclusion `D(g) ⊆ D(f)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ringRestrictionMap {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (f g : R)
    (hfg : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g ≤ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) :
    Localization.Away f →ₐ[R] Localization.Away g

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.ringRestrictionMap_unique
declarations.doc:
The restriction map is canonical: it is the unique `R`-algebra
homomorphism from `R_f` to `R_g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringRestrictionMap_unique {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (f g : R)
    (hfg : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g ≤ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)
    (φ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[R] Localization.Away g) :
    φ = ringRestrictionMap f g hfg

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical `R_f`-linear restriction map `M_f → M_g` associated to an inclusion
`D(g) ⊆ D(f)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleRestrictionMap {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f g : R)
    (hfg : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g ≤ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) :
    let φ := ringRestrictionMap f g hfg
    letI := Module.compHom (R := Localization.Away g) (S := Localization.Away f)
      (LocalizedModule.Away (R := R) g M) φ.toRingHom
    LocalizedModule.Away (R := R) f M →ₗ[Localization.Away f]
      LocalizedModule.Away (R := R) g M

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMap_mk
declarations.doc:
The module restriction map agrees with the canonical localization maps on
elements of `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleRestrictionMap_mk {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f g : R)
    (hfg : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g ≤ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) (m : M) :
    moduleRestrictionMap f g hfg
        (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M m) =
      LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers g) M m

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMap_unique
declarations.doc:
An `R_f`-linear map `M_f → M_g` which agrees with the localization maps
from `M` is the canonical module restriction map.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleRestrictionMap_unique {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f g : R)
    (hfg : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g ≤ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)
    (F :
      let φ := ringRestrictionMap f g hfg
      letI := Module.compHom (R := Localization.Away g) (S := Localization.Away f)
        (LocalizedModule.Away (R := R) g M) φ.toRingHom
      LocalizedModule.Away (R := R) f M →ₗ[Localization.Away f]
        LocalizedModule.Away (R := R) g M)
    (hF : ∀ m : M,
      F (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M m) =
        LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers g) M m) :
    F = moduleRestrictionMap f g hfg

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_le_iSup_iff_span_algebraMap_eq_top
declarations.doc:
A standard open `D(f)` is contained in the union of the standard opens `D(g i)` if and only
if the images of the `g i` generate the unit ideal after localizing away from `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem basicOpen_le_iSup_iff_span_algebraMap_eq_top
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {ι : Type w} (f : R) [IsLocalization.Away f S] (g : ι → R) :
      PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⨆ i, PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (g i) ↔
      Ideal.span (Set.range fun i ↦ algebraMap R S (g i)) = ⊤

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement
declarations.doc:
Every open cover of a standard open in the prime spectrum has a finite
refinement by standard opens.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R]
    {ι : Type*} (f : R) (U : ι → Opens (PrimeSpectrum R))
    (hU : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f ≤ ⨆ i, U i) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : Fin n → R) (a : Fin n → ι),
      PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f = ⨆ j, PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (g j) ∧
        ∀ j, PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (g j) ≤ U (a j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.basicOpen_map
declarations.doc:
Under the canonical localization identifications, the map on sections
over a standard open induced by a module map is its localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem basicOpen_map {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {M N : ModuleCat.{u} R}
    (f : M ⟶ N) (a : R) (m : LocalizedModule.Away (R := R) a M) :
    ((modulesSpecToSheaf.map (tilde.map f)).1.app
        (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen a)))
      ((IsLocalizedModule.iso (Submonoid.powers a)
        (tilde.toOpen M (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen a)).hom) m) =
      (IsLocalizedModule.iso (Submonoid.powers a)
        (tilde.toOpen N (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen a)).hom)
        (IsLocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers a)
          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers a) M)
          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers a) N) f.hom m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.toStalk_map
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification of the stalk of an associated sheaf with
localization at a prime is natural in the module.
declarations.statement:
theorem toStalk_map {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {M N : ModuleCat.{u} R}
    (f : M ⟶ N) (x : PrimeSpectrum.Top R)
    (m : (tilde M).presheaf.stalk x) :
    ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map
      (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf (tilde.map f))) m =
      IsLocalizedModule.map x.asIdeal.primeCompl
        (tilde.toStalk M x).hom (tilde.toStalk N x).hom f.hom m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.StructureSheaf.map_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
Under the canonical identifications of sections on standard opens with localizations,
restriction in the structure sheaf is the canonical map `R_f → R_g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_basicOpen {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (f g : R)
    (hfg : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g ≤ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) :
    ((AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.structureSheaf R).obj.map (homOfLE hfg).op).hom.comp
        (IsLocalization.algEquiv (Submonoid.powers f) (Localization.Away f)
          ((AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.structureSheaf R).obj.obj
            (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)))).toRingHom =
      (IsLocalization.algEquiv (Submonoid.powers g) (Localization.Away g)
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.structureSheaf R).obj.obj
          (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g)))).toRingHom.comp
        (PrimeSpectrum.ringRestrictionMap f g hfg).toRingHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.map_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
Sections of the associated sheaf on `D(f)` and `D(g)` are canonically isomorphic to `M_f`
and `M_g`. The isomorphisms identify sheaf restriction with the canonical map `M_f → M_g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_basicOpen {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (f g : R)
    (hfg : PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g ≤ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) :
    ∀ x : LocalizedModule.Away (R := R) f M,
      (modulesSpecToSheaf.obj (tilde M)).presheaf.map (homOfLE hfg).op
          ((IsLocalizedModule.iso (Submonoid.powers f)
            (tilde.toOpen M (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)).hom) x) =
        (IsLocalizedModule.iso (Submonoid.powers g)
          (tilde.toOpen M (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen g)).hom)
            (PrimeSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMap f g hfg x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isoSpec_hom_base_apply_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a locally ringed space, let `Y` be an affine scheme and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of locally ringed spaces. Given `x : X`, consider the ring maps

    Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y) --f^♯--> Γ(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ 𝒪_{X,x}

and let `p ⊆ Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)` be the inverse image of the maximal ideal `m_x`. Let `y ∈ Y` be the
corresponding point. Then `f x = y`.

The point `y` of the affine scheme `Y` corresponding to a prime of `Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)` is named by
transporting along `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isoSpec`, the identification of `Y` with
`Spec Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)`: the statement here is that `Y.isoSpec.hom` sends `f x` to `p`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.base_eq_isoSpec_inv_base_of_isAffine` is the same thing written as `f x = y`.
The prime `p` is spelled as the inverse image along `f^♯` of the inverse image along
`Γ(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ 𝒪_{X,x}` of the maximal ideal, which is the inverse image along the composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoSpec_hom_base_apply_of_isAffine (X : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}) (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [IsAffine Y] (f : X ⟶ Y.toLocallyRingedSpace) (x : X) :
    Y.isoSpec.hom.base (f.base x) =
      PrimeSpectrum.comap (LocallyRingedSpace.Γ.map f.op).hom
        (PrimeSpectrum.comap (X.presheaf.Γgerm x).hom
          (IsLocalRing.closedPoint (X.presheaf.stalk x)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeAssociatedSheafNatIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison between the affine construction `M ↦ M̃` on `Spec R` and tensor
sheafification along `R → Γ(Spec R, 𝒪)`: a natural isomorphism of the two functors, together
with the equation that on global sections it sends `m` to `1 ⊗ m`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tildeAssociatedSheafNatIso (R : CommRingCat.{u}) :
    { e : tilde.functor R ≅
        associatedSheafFunctor (Spec R).toRingedSpace
          (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom //
      ∀ (M : ModuleCat R) (m : M),
        (e.hom.app M).val.app (op ⊤) (tilde.toOpen M ⊤ m) =
          tensorUnitSection (X := (Spec R).toRingedSpace)
            (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom M (op ⊤) m }

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineExteriorPower.tildeExteriorPowerIso
declarations.doc:
**The affine exterior-power comparison.** The associated sheaf of the `n`-th exterior power
of `M` is the `n`-th exterior power of `M̃`.

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineExteriorPower.tildeExteriorPowerIso_natural
declarations.doc:
**The affine exterior-power comparison is natural.** It respects every unital homomorphism of
exterior algebra sheaves extending the map `M̃ ⟶ Ñ` of generating module sheaves on the
degree-one generators; the universal property of the exterior algebra makes such a homomorphism
unique, so this determines the degree-`n` square.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeExteriorPowerIso_natural (n : ℕ)
    (A : SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥(Spec R)) (tilde M))
    (B : SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥(Spec R)) (tilde N))
    (g : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.UnitalHom A.exterior B.exterior)
    (hg : A.exteriorGenerator ≫ g.app 1 = tilde.map f ≫ B.exteriorGenerator) :
    tilde.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (R := R)
          (X := ModuleCat.of ↥R ↥(⋀[↥R]^n ↥M)) (Y := ModuleCat.of ↥R ↥(⋀[↥R]^n ↥N))
          (exteriorPower.map n f.hom)) ≫ (tildeExteriorPowerIso N B n).hom =
      (tildeExteriorPowerIso M A n).hom ≫ g.app (n : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineExteriorPower.tildeExteriorPowerIso_hom_ιMulti
declarations.doc:
**The affine exterior-power comparison on a wedge of global sections.** The global section of
`(⋀ⁿ_R M)~` attached to `m₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ mₙ` is carried to the ordered product, in `⋀(M̃)`, of the
degree-one generators at the global sections of `M̃` attached to the `mᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeExteriorPowerIso_hom_ιMulti
    (A : SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥(Spec R)) (tilde M)) (s : Fin n → ↥M) :
    (((tilde.adjunction (R := R)).homEquiv (ModuleCat.of ↥R ↥(⋀[↥R]^n ↥M))
          (A.exteriorPower n)) (tildeExteriorPowerIso M A n).hom).hom
        (exteriorPower.ιMulti ↥R n s) =
      A.exterior.toPresheafGradedAlgebra.homogeneousProd (specGlobalOpen R) n
        (fun i => A.exteriorGenerator.val.app (specGlobalOpen R)
          ((tilde.toOpen M ⊤).hom (s i)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SymGraded.tildeSymmetricPowerIso
declarations.doc:
**The affine symmetric-power comparison.** The associated sheaf of the `n`-th symmetric
power of `M` is the `n`-th symmetric power of `M̃`.

declarations.name: Stacks.SymGraded.tildeSymmetricPowerIso_unit
declarations.doc:
**In degree zero the comparison takes the algebraic unit to the unit of the symmetric
algebra sheaf.**
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeSymmetricPowerIso_unit :
    let x : SymPow.symmetricPower 0 R M := ⟨1, one_mem_gradedPiece (R := R) M⟩
    (((tilde.adjunction (R := R)).homEquiv
      (ModuleCat.of R (SymPow.symmetricPower 0 R M))
      (A.symmetricPower 0))
      (tildeSymmetricPowerIso M A 0).hom).hom x =
        A.symmetric.one.eval (.op (⊤ : Opens (Spec R).carrier))

declarations.name: Stacks.SymGraded.tildeSymmetricPowerIso_generator
declarations.doc:
**In degree one the comparison takes an algebraic generator to the corresponding generator
of the symmetric algebra sheaf.**
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeSymmetricPowerIso_generator (m : M) :
    let x : SymPow.symmetricPower 1 R M :=
      ⟨SymmetricAlgebra.ι R M m, ι_mem_gradedPiece_one (R := R) M m⟩
    (((tilde.adjunction (R := R)).homEquiv
      (ModuleCat.of R (SymPow.symmetricPower 1 R M))
      (A.symmetricPower 1))
      (tildeSymmetricPowerIso M A 1).hom).hom x =
        (A.symmetricGenerator.val.app (.op (⊤ : Opens (Spec R).carrier)))
          ((tilde.toOpen M ⊤).hom m)

declarations.name: Stacks.SymGraded.tildeSymmetricPowerIso_mul_generator
declarations.doc:
**The comparison in degree `n + 1` takes multiplication by an algebraic degree-one generator
to multiplication by the corresponding sheaf generator.** Together with the degree-one
normalization this fixes the canonical comparison in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeSymmetricPowerIso_mul_generator (n : ℕ) (m : M)
    (x : SymPow.symmetricPower n R M) :
    HEq
      ((((tilde.adjunction (R := R)).homEquiv
        (ModuleCat.of R (SymPow.symmetricPower (n + 1) R M))
        (A.symmetricPower (n + 1)))
        (tildeSymmetricPowerIso M A (n + 1)).hom).hom
          (SymPow.symMulMap n (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[R] M) (m ⊗ₜ[R] x)))
      ((A.symmetric.mul 1 (n : ℤ)).app (.op (⊤ : Opens (Spec R).carrier))
        (A.symmetricGenerator.val.app (.op (⊤ : Opens (Spec R).carrier))
          ((tilde.toOpen M ⊤).hom m))
        ((tildeSymmetricPowerIso M A n).hom.val.app (.op (⊤ : Opens (Spec R).carrier))
          ((tilde.toOpen (ModuleCat.of R (SymPow.symmetricPower n R M)) ⊤).hom x)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SymGraded.tildeSymmetricPowerIso_natural
declarations.doc:
**The affine symmetric-power comparison is natural.** It respects every unital homomorphism
of symmetric algebra sheaves extending the map of generating module sheaves; the universal
property of the symmetric algebra makes such a homomorphism unique.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeSymmetricPowerIso_natural (n : ℕ)
    (A : SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥(Spec R)) (tilde M))
    (B : SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥(Spec R)) (tilde N))
    (g : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.UnitalHom A.symmetric B.symmetric)
    (hg : A.symmetricGenerator ≫ g.app 1 = tilde.map f ≫ B.symmetricGenerator) :
    tilde.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (R := R)
          (X := ModuleCat.of R (SymPow.symmetricPower n R M))
          (Y := ModuleCat.of R (SymPow.symmetricPower n R N)) (SymPow.symMap n f.hom)) ≫
        (tildeSymmetricPowerIso N B n).hom =
      (tildeSymmetricPowerIso M A n).hom ≫ g.app (n : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.SymGraded.tildeSymmetricPowerIso_natural_symMap
declarations.doc:
**The affine symmetric-power comparison is natural, for the canonical induced map.** This is
`Stacks.SymGraded.tildeSymmetricPowerIso_natural` instantiated at `symmetricAlgebraHom`, the
unital homomorphism the universal property of the symmetric algebra provides, so that the square
is stated against a canonical map rather than a hypothesised one. The left-hand map is the
associated sheaf of `SymPow.symMap`, the `n`-th symmetric power of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeSymmetricPowerIso_natural_symMap (n : ℕ)
    (A : SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥(Spec R)) (tilde M))
    (B : SheafOfModules.TensorExteriorSymmetricAlgebras
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥(Spec R)) (tilde N)) :
    tilde.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (R := R)
          (X := ModuleCat.of R (SymPow.symmetricPower n R M))
          (Y := ModuleCat.of R (SymPow.symmetricPower n R N)) (SymPow.symMap n f.hom)) ≫
        (tildeSymmetricPowerIso N B n).hom =
      (tildeSymmetricPowerIso M A n).hom ≫ (symmetricAlgebraHom f A B).app (n : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.InternalHomTildeIso
declarations.doc:
An isomorphism from an affine internal Hom to the associated sheaf of the module of linear
maps, together with the characterization that makes the isomorphism canonical.

The inverse sends the global section associated to `f : M ⟶ N` to the section of the internal
Hom represented by the sheaf morphism `tilde.map f`. This is the content of
[Stacks, Tag 01I8].
declarations.statement:
structure InternalHomTildeIso (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (H : SheafHom (Spec R).sheaf (tilde M) (tilde N))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.internalHomTildeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01I8 (`internal_hom`).**

Let `M` and `N` be modules over a commutative ring `R`, with `M` finitely presented. The
internal Hom between the associated sheaves of `M` and `N` on `Spec R` is canonically
isomorphic to the sheaf associated to the `R`-module `Hom_R(M, N)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def internalHomTildeIso (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M]
    (H : SheafHom (Spec R).sheaf (tilde M) (tilde N)) :
    InternalHomTildeIso R M N H

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.internalHomTildeIsoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01I8 (`internal_hom`).**

The affine internal-Hom isomorphism itself: for `M` finitely presented, the internal Hom of the
associated sheaves of `M` and `N` on `Spec R` is isomorphic to the associated sheaf of the
`R`-module `Hom_R(M, N)`. This is the `iso` field of `internalHomTildeIso`, named so that the
isomorphism asserted by the tag is readable as a type. It is canonical by
`internalHomTildeIsoIso_inv_app_toOpen`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def internalHomTildeIsoIso (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M]
    (H : SheafHom (Spec R).sheaf (tilde M) (tilde N)) :
    H.obj ≅ tilde (ModuleCat.of R (M ⟶ N))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.internalHomTildeIsoIso_inv_app_toOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01I8 (`internal_hom`).** The affine internal-Hom isomorphism is
canonical: its inverse sends the global section associated to `f : M ⟶ N` to the section of the
internal Hom represented by the sheaf morphism `tilde.map f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomTildeIsoIso_inv_app_toOpen (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M]
    (H : SheafHom (Spec R).sheaf (tilde M) (tilde N)) (f : M ⟶ N) :
    H.sectionsEquiv ⊤
        ((internalHomTildeIsoIso R M N H).inv.val.app (op ⊤)
          (tilde.toOpen (ModuleCat.of R (M ⟶ N)) ⊤ f)) =
      (tilde.map f).over ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.internalHomTildeIso_natural_right
declarations.doc:
The affine internal-Hom comparison is natural in the target module: a morphism of internal
Homs exhibited as post-composition with `tilde.map u` is carried to the associated sheaf of
post-composition with `u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomTildeIso_natural_right (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (M N N' : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M]
    (H : SheafHom (Spec R).sheaf (tilde M) (tilde N))
    (H' : SheafHom (Spec R).sheaf (tilde M) (tilde N'))
    (u : N ⟶ N') (m : H.obj ⟶ H'.obj)
    (hm : SheafHom.IsPostcomp (Spec R).sheaf (tilde.map u) H H' m) :
    m ≫ (internalHomTildeIso R M N' H').iso.hom =
      (internalHomTildeIso R M N H).iso.hom ≫ tilde.map (ModuleCat.homPostcomp M u)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.internalHomTildeIso_natural_left
declarations.doc:
The affine internal-Hom comparison is contravariantly natural in the source module: a
morphism of internal Homs exhibited as pre-composition with `tilde.map β` is carried to the
associated sheaf of pre-composition with `β`.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomTildeIso_natural_left (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (M M' N : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M] [Module.FinitePresentation R M']
    (H : SheafHom (Spec R).sheaf (tilde M) (tilde N))
    (H' : SheafHom (Spec R).sheaf (tilde M') (tilde N))
    (β : M' ⟶ M) (m : H.obj ⟶ H'.obj)
    (hm : SheafHom.IsPrecomp (Spec R).sheaf (tilde.map β) H H' m) :
    m ≫ (internalHomTildeIso R M' N H').iso.hom =
      (internalHomTildeIso R M N H).iso.hom ≫ tilde.map (ModuleCat.homPrecomp N β)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeTensorPowerIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01I8 (tensor-power part).** The associated sheaf of a tensor power is
canonically the tensor power of the associated sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tildeTensorPowerIso (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    (n : ℕ) → (tilde (ModuleCat.of R (TensorPower R n M)) ≅ specTildeTensorPower R M n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeTensorPowerIso_hom_tprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01I8 (tensor-power part).** The canonical affine tensor-power
comparison carries a pure tensor to the tensor product of its associated global sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeTensorPowerIso_hom_tprod (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (n : ℕ)
    (a : Fin n → M) :
    (tildeTensorPowerIso R M n).hom.val.app (specGlobalOpen R)
        ((tilde.toOpen (ModuleCat.of R (TensorPower R n M)) ⊤).hom
          (PiTensorProduct.tprod R a)) =
      tildeTensorPowerSection R M n a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeTensorPowerIso_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01I8 (tensor-power part).** Naturality of the affine tensor-power
comparison. The right-hand map is the degree-`n` component of a unital graded-algebra map
extending `tilde.map f` on degree-one generators; the universal property of the tensor algebra
makes such a map unique, so quantifying over it is a statement about the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeTensorPowerIso_natural
    (hg : (specTildeAlgebras R M).tensorGenerator ≫ g.app 1 =
      tilde.map f ≫ (specTildeAlgebras R N).tensorGenerator) (n : ℕ) :
    tilde.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin n => f.hom))) ≫
        (tildeTensorPowerIso R N n).hom =
      (tildeTensorPowerIso R M n).hom ≫ ((specTildeAlgebras R M).tensorPieceIso n).inv ≫
        g.app (n : ℤ) ≫ ((specTildeAlgebras R N).tensorPieceIso n).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeTensorPowerIso_natural_piTensorProductMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01I8 (tensor-power part).** Naturality of the affine tensor-power
comparison against the canonical induced map, rather than against a hypothesised one: this is
`tildeTensorPowerIso_natural` instantiated at `specTildeTensorAlgebraMap`, the unital
graded-algebra map the universal property of the tensor algebra provides. The left-hand map is
the associated sheaf of `PiTensorProduct.map`, the `n`-fold tensor power of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeTensorPowerIso_natural_piTensorProductMap (n : ℕ) :
    tilde.map (ModuleCat.ofHom (PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ : Fin n => f.hom))) ≫
        (tildeTensorPowerIso R N n).hom =
      (tildeTensorPowerIso R M n).hom ≫ ((specTildeAlgebras R M).tensorPieceIso n).inv ≫
        (specTildeTensorAlgebraMap R f).app (n : ℤ) ≫
          ((specTildeAlgebras R N).tensorPieceIso n).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeTensorIso
declarations.doc:
For modules `M` and `N` over `R`, there is a canonical isomorphism
`(M ⊗[R] N)~ ≅ M~ ⊗_{𝒪_(Spec R)} N~`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tildeTensorIso (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    tilde (M ⊗ N) ≅
      specTensorSheaf R (tilde M) (tilde N)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeTensorIso_hom_tmul
declarations.doc:
The canonical isomorphism sends a pure tensor, under the
tilde--global-sections adjunction, to the section obtained by tensoring the two
canonical global sections and applying the sheafification unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeTensorIso_hom_tmul (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (m : M) (n : N) :
    (((tilde.adjunction (R := R)).homEquiv (M ⊗ N)
      (specTensorSheaf R (tilde M) (tilde N))) (tildeTensorIso R M N).hom).hom
        (TensorProduct.tmul R m n) =
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.toSheafify (Spec R).presheaf
        (isSheaf_specStructureRingPresheaf R)
        (specTensorPresheaf R (tilde M) (tilde N))).app (.op ⊤)).hom
        (TensorProduct.tmul ((Spec R).presheaf.obj (.op ⊤))
          ((tilde.toOpen M ⊤).hom m) ((tilde.toOpen N ⊤).hom n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeTensorIso_eq_of_hom_tmul
declarations.doc:
The comparison is canonical: it is the *only* isomorphism `(M ⊗ N)~ ≅ M~ ⊗ N~` satisfying
the pure-tensor equation `tildeTensorIso_hom_tmul`, so `tildeTensorIso` does not depend on the
choice `Classical.choose` makes to produce it.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeTensorIso_eq_of_hom_tmul (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (e : tilde (M ⊗ N) ≅ specTensorSheaf R (tilde M) (tilde N))
    (he : ∀ (m : M) (n : N),
      (((tilde.adjunction (R := R)).homEquiv (M ⊗ N)
        (specTensorSheaf R (tilde M) (tilde N))) e.hom).hom
          (TensorProduct.tmul R m n) =
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.toSheafify (Spec R).presheaf
          (isSheaf_specStructureRingPresheaf R)
          (specTensorPresheaf R (tilde M) (tilde N))).app (.op ⊤)).hom
          (TensorProduct.tmul ((Spec R).presheaf.obj (.op ⊤))
            ((tilde.toOpen M ⊤).hom m) ((tilde.toOpen N ⊤).hom n))) :
    e = tildeTensorIso R M N

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tildeTensorIso_natural
declarations.doc: The canonical tensor comparison is natural in both modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildeTensorIso_natural (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    {M M' N N' : ModuleCat.{u} R} (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N') :
    tilde.map (f ⊗ₘ g) ≫ (tildeTensorIso R M' N').hom =
      (tildeTensorIso R M N).hom ≫ tildeTensorSheafMap R f g

declarations.name: Stacks.AssociatedSheaf.associatedSheafTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Construction (3) carries the tensor product of `R`-modules to the tensor product of
sheaves of modules:** `ℱ_{M ⊗_R N} ≅ ℱ_M ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℱ_N`, on an arbitrary ringed space.

This is the clause of Tag 01I8 that the determinant argument of Tag 0FJN needs on the
trivialising open of Tag 08BL rather than on an affine scheme.
declarations.statement:
def associatedSheafTensorIso (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    associatedSheaf X α (M ⊗ N) ≅
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨X.presheaf, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ X.presheaf
          (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) (structureSheafRing X).property⟩).obj
        (associatedSheaf X α M)).obj (associatedSheaf X α N)
declarations.comment: construction (3) commutes with the tensor product, on an arbitrary ringed space

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBaseChange.tilde_map_comp_pushforwardTildeIso_inv
declarations.doc:
The associated sheaf of a map of `R`-modules `R ⟶ S` sending `1` to `1`, followed by the
inverse of the comparison identifying the direct image along `Spec φ` of the associated sheaf of
`S` with the associated sheaf of `S` restricted to an `R`-module, is the structure morphism
`𝒪_{Spec R} ⟶ (Spec φ)_* 𝒪_{Spec S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tilde_map_comp_pushforwardTildeIso_inv
    (u : ModuleCat.of R R ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ.hom).obj (ModuleCat.of S S))
    (hu : u.hom (1 : R) = (1 : S)) :
    (tilde.functor R).map u ≫ ((pushforwardTildeIso R S φ).app (ModuleCat.of S S)).inv =
      structureUnitHom (Spec.map φ)
declarations.comment:
affine_pushforward_tilde at the ring itself: the comparison carries the
structure map of φ to the structure morphism of Spec φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackTildeIso
declarations.doc:
Pullback along the map of affine schemes induced by `f : R ⟶ S` carries the associated sheaf
of an `R`-module to the associated sheaf of its extension of scalars to `S`, naturally in the
module.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackTildeIso_hom_app_unit_toOpen
declarations.doc:
The canonical affine pullback comparison sends the pullback of the global
section represented by `m` to the global section represented by `1 ⊗ m`.
Here the first map is the pullback--pushforward adjunction unit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pullbackTildeIso_hom_app_unit_toOpen
    (R S : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : R ⟶ S) (M : ModuleCat R) (m : M) :
    ((pullbackTildeIso R S f).hom.app M).val.app (.op ⊤)
      (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (Spec.map f)).unit.app
        (tilde M)).val.app (.op ⊤) (tilde.toOpen M ⊤ m)) =
    tilde.toOpen ((ModuleCat.extendScalars f.hom).obj M) ⊤
      ((1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R, f.hom] m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushforwardTildeIso
declarations.doc:
Pushforward along the map of affine schemes induced by `φ : R ⟶ S` carries the associated
sheaf of an `S`-module to the associated sheaf of its restriction of scalars along `φ`, naturally
in the module.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushforwardTildeIso_hom_app_toOpen
declarations.doc:
The canonical affine pushforward comparison is normalized by the canonical identifications of
a module with the global sections of its associated sheaf: its component at `N` sends the global
section represented by `n` on `Spec S` to the global section represented by the same element of
the restricted `R`-module on `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pushforwardTildeIso_hom_app_toOpen
    (R S : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : R ⟶ S) (N : ModuleCat S) (n : N) :
    ((pushforwardTildeIso R S φ).hom.app N).val.app (Opposite.op (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))
      (tilde.toOpen N (⊤ : (Spec S).Opens) n) =
    tilde.toOpen ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ.hom).obj N) (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens) n

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.SectionsSheaf.tildePullbackIso_id_hom_app
declarations.doc:
**The affine base-change comparison of [Stacks, Tag 01I9] at the identity ring map.** The
isomorphism `(Spec (𝟙 A))^* M̃ ≅ (A ⊗_A M)~` is the identity law for pullback followed by the
associated sheaf of the unit `m ↦ 1 ⊗ m` of extension of scalars.

Neither factor is an identity: `A ⊗_A M` is not `M` and `(Spec (𝟙 A))^*` is an abstract left
adjoint. What the statement says is that the comparison, which is built by uniqueness of left
adjoints and so has no formula, *is* the composite of the two canonical maps that are available.

The proof is the uniqueness itself:
`CategoryTheory.Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app` evaluates the comparison after the unit
of `tildePullbackAdjunction (𝟙 A)`, and `eq_of_unit_comp` says that this determines a morphism
out of `(tilde.functor A ⋙ (Spec (𝟙 A))^*).obj M`; the four lemmas above evaluate the
right-hand side there.
declarations.statement:
theorem tildePullbackIso_id_hom_app (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) :
    (tildePullbackIso (𝟙 A)).hom.app M =
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (Spec.map_id A)).hom.app ((tilde.functor A).obj M) ≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId (Spec A)).hom.app ((tilde.functor A).obj M)) ≫
        (tilde.functor A).map (extendUnitId M)
declarations.comment:
the affine base-change comparison at the identity ring map: the pullback of the
associated sheaf along Spec of the identity ring map is the identity law for pullback followed
by the associated sheaf of m ↦ 1 ⊗ m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quotientPrime_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01IG.** The point `p / I` of `Spec(R / I)` maps to
the point `p` of `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotientPrime_comap {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (hIp : I ≤ p) :
    PrimeSpectrum.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (quotientPrime I p hIp) =
      (⟨p, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkMap_quotient_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01IG.** The map on stalks induced by
`Spec(R / I) → Spec R` at `p / I` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stalkMap_quotient_surjective {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (I p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (hIp : I ≤ p) :
    Function.Surjective
      ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).stalkMap
        (quotientPrime I p hIp)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkMap_quotient_ker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01IG.** The kernel of the map on stalks induced by
`Spec(R / I) → Spec R` at `p / I` is the extended ideal `I R_p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stalkMap_quotient_ker {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (I p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (hIp : I ≤ p) :
    RingHom.ker
        ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).stalkMap
          (quotientPrime I p hIp)).hom =
      Ideal.map
        (StructureSheaf.toStalk R
          (PrimeSpectrum.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (quotientPrime I p hIp))).hom I

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion_specMap_quotientMk
declarations.doc:
For an ideal `I` of a ring `R` the morphism `Spec (R ⧸ I) ⟶ Spec R` is a closed immersion
of locally ringed spaces, in the sense of Definition 01HK: a closed embedding on spaces whose
structure-sheaf map is surjective with kernel locally generated by sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_specMap_quotientMk :
    IsClosedImmersion
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).toLRSHom.toShHom

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.isClosedEmbedding_specMap_quotientMk
declarations.doc:
The map `Spec (R ⧸ I) → Spec R` is a homeomorphism of `Spec (R ⧸ I)` onto a closed subset
of `Spec R`.

    Topology.IsClosedEmbedding ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).base

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.existsUnique_iso_tildeSubspace
declarations.doc:
`Spec (R ⧸ I)` is the closed subspace of `Spec R` cut out by the quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals `I^~`: there is a unique isomorphism of locally ringed spaces from `Spec (R ⧸ I)` to that
closed subspace commuting with the two morphisms to `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_tildeSubspace :
    ∃! t : (Spec (CommRingCat.of (↑R ⧸ I))).toLocallyRingedSpace ≅ tildeSubspace I,
      t.hom ≫ tildeSubspaceInclusion I =
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).toLRSHom

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.existsUnique_ideal_iso_quotientSpec
declarations.doc:
A closed immersion of locally ringed spaces into `Spec R` is, over `Spec R`, the spectrum of
the quotient by a unique ideal of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_ideal_iso_quotientSpec {Z : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ (Spec R).toLocallyRingedSpace) [IsClosedImmersion i.toShHom] :
    ∃! I : Ideal ↑R, ∃ e : Z ≅ (Spec (CommRingCat.of (↑R ⧸ I))).toLocallyRingedSpace,
      i = e.hom ≫ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).toLRSHom

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.exists_ideal_iso_quotient_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
Over an affine open `U` of a scheme `X`, a closed immersion of locally ringed spaces
`i : Z ⟶ X` is, compatibly with the canonical presentation of `U` as `Spec Γ(X, U)`, the spectrum
of a quotient of `Γ(X, U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_iso_quotient_of_isAffineOpen (X : Scheme.{u}) (Z : LocallyRingedSpace.{u})
    (i : Z ⟶ X.toLocallyRingedSpace) [hi : IsClosedImmersion i.toShHom]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    ∃ (I : Ideal Γ(X, U)) (e : pullback i U.ι.toLRSHom ≅
        (Spec (CommRingCat.of (Γ(X, U) ⧸ I))).toLocallyRingedSpace),
      pullback.snd i U.ι.toLRSHom ≫ hU.isoSpec.hom.toLRSHom =
        e.hom ≫ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).toLRSHom

theorem exists_scheme_of_isClosedImmersion (X : Scheme.{u}) (Z : LocallyRingedSpace.{u})
    (i : Z ⟶ X.toLocallyRingedSpace) [IsClosedImmersion i.toShHom] :
    ∃ Z' : Scheme.{u}, Z'.toLocallyRingedSpace = Z

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.exists_scheme_of_closedSubspace
declarations.doc:
The closed subspace of a scheme cut out by a locally generated ideal sheaf carries a scheme
structure on its underlying locally ringed space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_scheme_of_closedSubspace (X : Scheme.{u})
    (J : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace))
    (j : J ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace))
    [Mono j] (hJ : Nonempty (SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u} J)) :
    ∃ Z : Scheme.{u}, Z.toLocallyRingedSpace =
      (closedSubspace X.toLocallyRingedSpace J j hJ).space

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.exists_ideal_idealSheaf_restrict_iso_tilde_of_locallyRingedSpace
declarations.doc:
The affine-local description of the ideal sheaf for a closed immersion of locally ringed
spaces `i : Z ⟶ X` into a scheme: over an affine open `U = Spec R` of `X` there is an ideal
`I ⊆ R = Γ(X, U)` presenting the fibre over `U` as `Spec (R ⧸ I)`, and the kernel `ℐ` of
`𝒪_X ⟶ i_* 𝒪_Z` restricts on `U` to `I^~`.

The source `Z` is a scheme by `Stacks.ClosedImmersion.sourceScheme`, so `i` is a morphism of
schemes `Stacks.ClosedImmersion.sourceSchemeHom` with the same ideal sheaf, and this is
`Stacks.ClosedImmersion.exists_ideal_idealSheaf_restrict_iso_tilde` for that morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_idealSheaf_restrict_iso_tilde_of_locallyRingedSpace (X : Scheme.{u})
    (Z : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X.toLocallyRingedSpace)
    [hi : IsClosedImmersion i.toShHom] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    ∃ (I : Ideal Γ(X, U)) (e : pullback (sourceSchemeHom X Z i) U.ι ≅
        Spec (CommRingCat.of (Γ(X, U) ⧸ I))),
      pullback.snd (sourceSchemeHom X Z i) U.ι ≫ hU.isoSpec.hom =
          e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ∧
        ∃ φ : (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj (idealSheaf i.toShHom) ≅
            (modulePullback hU.isoSpec.hom.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
              (tilde (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U) I)),
          φ.hom ≫ (modulePullback hU.isoSpec.hom.toLRSHom.toShHom).map
                (tildeIdealι Γ(X, U) I) ≫
              (Stacks.IdealSheafRestrict.pullbackUnitIso hU.isoSpec.hom).hom =
            (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).map
                (kernel.ι (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit
                  (structureSheafHom i.toShHom))) ≫
              (Scheme.Modules.restrictUnitIso U.ι).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isStandardOpenCover_basicOpen_eq_of_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Every affine open has a finite standard open cover each of whose members is also a standard
open in a member of a given affine open cover of the ambient scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isStandardOpenCover_basicOpen_eq_of_iSup_eq_top
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {ι : Type v} (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hUcover : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤)
    (V : X.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → Γ(X, V)) (i : Fin n → ι)
      (g : ∀ j, Γ(X, U (i j))),
      PrimeSpectrum.IsStandardOpenCoverOfSpectrum f ∧
        (⨆ j, X.basicOpen (f j)) = V ∧
        ∀ j, X.basicOpen (f j) = X.basicOpen (g j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_valuationRing_with_spectrum_chain
declarations.doc:
There is a valuation ring whose spectrum is a countable strictly increasing chain
of prime ideals, with one further maximal ideal above all of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_valuationRing_with_spectrum_chain :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (ring : CommRing R),
      letI : CommRing R := ring
      ∃ (domain : IsDomain R),
        letI : IsDomain R := domain
        ∃ (localRing : IsLocalRing R),
          letI : IsLocalRing R := localRing
          IsValuationRing R ∧
            ∃ p : ℕ → PrimeSpectrum R,
              ((p 0).asIdeal = ⊥) ∧
                (∀ n, (p n).asIdeal < (p (n + 1)).asIdeal) ∧
                (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum R,
                  (q = IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) ∨ (∃ n, q = p n))
declarations.comment: valuation ring with the specified prime spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.puncturedSpectrum_no_closed_points
declarations.doc:
Removing the unique closed point from a local spectrum with the indicated
unbounded chain of other primes gives an open subscheme without closed points.
declarations.statement:
theorem puncturedSpectrum_no_closed_points
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (p : ℕ → PrimeSpectrum R)
    (hchain : ∀ n, (p n).asIdeal < (p (n + 1)).asIdeal)
    (hexhaust : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum R,
      (q = IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) ∨ (∃ n, q = p n)) :
    ∀ x : Scheme.Opens.toScheme
      (⟨({IsLocalRing.closedPoint R} : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))ᶜ,
        (IsLocalRing.isClosed_singleton_closedPoint R).isOpen_compl⟩ :
        (Spec (.of R)).Opens),
      ¬ IsClosed ({x} : Set _)
declarations.comment: the punctured spectrum has no closed points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_scheme_without_closed_points
declarations.doc: A nonempty scheme may have no closed points.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_scheme_without_closed_points :
    ∃ X : Scheme.{u}, Nonempty X ∧ ∀ x : X, ¬ IsClosed ({x} : Set X)
declarations.comment: existence of a scheme without closed points

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_stalk_of_isReduced

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk

declarations.doc: A reduced closed subscheme structure on a closed subset is its vanishing-ideal structure.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
registrations.comment: canonical construction
