declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.reduction
declarations.doc:
The **reduction** `X_red` of a scheme `X`: the closed subscheme cut out by the nilradical
ideal sheaf, that is the reduced induced closed subscheme structure on all of `X`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def reduction : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.reducedInduced
declarations.doc:
**The reduced induced scheme structure on a closed subset `Z` of `X`:** the closed subscheme
cut out by the vanishing ideal sheaf of `Z`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def reducedInduced {X : Scheme.{u}} (Z : Closeds X) : X.SchemeStructure Z
declarations.comment: the reduced induced scheme structure on Z

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.SchemeStructure
registrations.comment: scheme structure on Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_valuation_ring_of_specializes
declarations.doc:
A specialization of points of a scheme is witnessed by a valuation ring.  The valuation
ring may be chosen so that the residue-field extension at its generic point is any prescribed
extension.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_valuation_ring_of_specializes (S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u})
    {s' s : S} (h : s' ⤳ s) (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (i : S.residueField s' ⟶ CommRingCat.of K) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsDomain A) (_ : ValuationRing A)
      (f : AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
      (e : (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of A)).residueField
        (genericPoint (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of A))) ≅ CommRingCat.of K)
      (hη : f (genericPoint (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of A))) = s'),
      f (closedPoint A) = s ∧
        (S.residueFieldCongr hη).inv ≫
          f.residueFieldMap (genericPoint (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of A))) ≫ e.hom = i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pointsEquivFieldValuedPointClasses
declarations.doc: Points of a scheme correspond bijectively to equivalence classes of field-valued points.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointsEquivFieldValuedPointClasses (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    X ≃ Quotient (FieldValuedPoint.setoid X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FieldValuedPoint.hasCommonExtension_iff_point_eq
declarations.doc:
Two field-valued points have a common field-valued extension if and only if they have the same
image point.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCommonExtension_iff_point_eq {X : Scheme.{u}} (p q : FieldValuedPoint X) :
    p.HasCommonExtension q ↔ p.point = q.point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FieldValuedPoint.canonical_isSmallest
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism `Spec(κ(x)) ⟶ X` is the smallest representative of the equivalence
class corresponding to `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonical_isSmallest {X : Scheme.{u}} (x : X) :
    (canonical X x).IsSmallest

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FieldValuedPoint.uniqueIso_of_isSmallest
declarations.doc: Any two smallest representatives of the same point are uniquely isomorphic over `X`.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField
registrations.comment: morphisms from the spectrum of a fixed field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPushout_opens_ι_of_sup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
A scheme covered by two opens is glued from them: the square formed by the two inclusions of
the intersection and the two inclusions into the ambient scheme is a pushout square.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPushout_opens_ι_of_sup_eq_top {S : Scheme.{u}} {U V : S.Opens} (h : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    IsPushout (S.homOfLE inf_le_left) (S.homOfLE inf_le_right) U.ι V.ι
declarations.comment: the two-chart glueing as a pushout square of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_comp_ι_eq_of_sup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
The mapping property for morphisms out of a glueing with two charts: if the opens `U, V` of a
scheme `S` satisfy `U ⊔ V = ⊤`, then a morphism out of `S` is the same thing as a pair of
morphisms out of `U` and out of `V` agreeing on `U ⊓ V`.
declarations.comment: the two-chart case of the mapping property for morphisms out of a glueing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.opensRange_pushout_inl_sup_opensRange_pushout_inr
declarations.doc:
The two charts of the scheme obtained by glueing `X` and `Y` along a span of open immersions
cover it.
declarations.statement:
theorem opensRange_pushout_inl_sup_opensRange_pushout_inr :
    (pushout.inl f g).opensRange ⊔ (pushout.inr f g).opensRange = ⊤
declarations.comment: the two-chart case of part (1): the charts cover the glued scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_opensRange_pushout_inl
declarations.doc:
Inside the second chart of the scheme obtained by glueing `X` and `Y` along a span of open
immersions, the overlap with the first chart is exactly the image of the span's vertex.
declarations.statement:
theorem preimage_opensRange_pushout_inl :
    (pushout.inr f g) ⁻¹ᵁ (pushout.inl f g).opensRange = g.opensRange
declarations.comment: the two-chart case of part (2): the overlap of the two charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_pushout_inl_inr
declarations.doc:
The pushout square of a span of open immersions of schemes is also cartesian: the span's
vertex is the intersection of the two charts of the glued scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_pushout_inl_inr :
    IsPullback f g (pushout.inl f g) (pushout.inr f g)
declarations.comment: the two-chart case of part (2), as a cartesian square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.range_overlap
declarations.doc:
The prescribed overlap `V i j`, viewed inside the chart `U i` through `D.f i j`, is exactly
the part of that chart lying over the chart `U j`: `φ i '' U i j = U i ∩ U j` in the glued
space, stated as an equality of subsets of `U i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_overlap (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u}) (i j : D.J) :
    Set.range (D.f i j).base = (D.ι i).base ⁻¹' Set.range (D.ι j).base
declarations.comment: part (2): the overlap is the intersection of two charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.t_f_eq_restrictOverlapIso_comp
declarations.doc:
The transition map is `φ j⁻¹ ∘ φ i` on the overlap: for any morphism `s : U i ∩ U j ⟶ U j`
with `s ≫ φ j` the inclusion of `U i ∩ U j` (the restriction of `φ j⁻¹` to `U i ∩ U j`), the
map `φ i j`, read in the chart `U j`, is `s` composed with the restriction isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem t_f_eq_restrictOverlapIso_comp (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u}) (i j : D.J)
    (s : pullback (D.ι i) (D.ι j) ⟶ D.U j)
    (hs : s ≫ D.ι j = pullback.fst (D.ι i) (D.ι j) ≫ D.ι i) :
    D.t i j ≫ D.f j i = (D.restrictOverlapIso i j).hom ≫ s
declarations.comment: part (3): the transition map is the restriction of φ j⁻¹ ∘ φ i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.homOutEquiv
declarations.doc:
The mapping property for morphisms *out of* a gluing: a morphism `D.glued ⟶ Y` is the same
thing as a family of morphisms `D.U i ⟶ Y` agreeing on the prescribed overlaps, the agreement
being read through the transition maps. The bijection sends a morphism to the family of its
restrictions `D.ι i ≫ h`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homOutEquiv
    (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u}) (Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}) :
    (D.glued ⟶ Y) ≃
      { f : ∀ i, D.U i ⟶ Y //
          ∀ i j, D.f i j ≫ f i = D.t i j ≫ D.f j i ≫ f j }
declarations.comment: the mapping property for morphisms out of the glueing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.hom_pullbackCharts_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
The pullbacks of the canonical charts along a morphism into the glued space jointly cover its
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_pullbackCharts_jointlySurjective (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u})
    {Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ D.glued) (y : Y) :
    ∃ (i : D.J) (x : pullback (C := LocallyRingedSpace) g (D.ι i)),
      (pullback.fst g (D.ι i)).base x = y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.hom_pullbackCharts_preimage_overlap
declarations.doc:
On the inverse-image chart indexed by `i`, the inverse image of `V i j` is exactly its
intersection with the chart indexed by `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_pullbackCharts_preimage_overlap (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u})
    {Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ D.glued) (i j : D.J) :
    (pullback.snd g (D.ι i)).base ⁻¹' Set.range (D.f i j).base =
      Set.range
        (pullback.fst (pullback.fst g (D.ι i))
          (pullback.fst g (D.ι j))).base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.hom_pullbackCharts_transition
declarations.doc:
The local morphisms on the inverse-image charts are related on intersections by the
prescribed transition map.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_pullbackCharts_transition (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u})
    {Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ D.glued) (i j : D.J) :
    ∃! k : pullback (pullback.fst g (D.ι i)) (pullback.fst g (D.ι j)) ⟶ D.V (i, j),
      k ≫ D.f i j =
          pullback.fst (pullback.fst g (D.ι i)) (pullback.fst g (D.ι j)) ≫
            pullback.snd g (D.ι i) ∧
        k ≫ D.t i j ≫ D.f j i =
          pullback.snd (pullback.fst g (D.ι i)) (pullback.fst g (D.ι j)) ≫
            pullback.snd g (D.ι j)
declarations.comment: transition compatibility for morphisms into the gluing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.existsUnique_hom_of_openCover
declarations.doc:
Morphisms of locally ringed spaces glue over an open covering of the source: a family of
morphisms out of the members of the covering which agree on the pairwise overlaps comes from a
unique morphism out of the covered space.

This is the locally ringed space counterpart of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`,
and the reason it is available here is that the covered space is the gluing of its own covering
(`openCoverFromGlued_isIso`), so the morphism is obtained from the universal property of the
multicoequalizer.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_hom_of_openCover
    {I : Type u} {Y Z : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}}
    {V : I → LocallyRingedSpace.{u}} (v : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Y)
    [∀ i, LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion (v i)]
    (hv : ∀ y : Y, ∃ i x, (v i).base x = y)
    (h : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Z)
    (hcompat : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (v i) (v j) ≫ h i = pullback.snd (v i) (v j) ≫ h j) :
    ∃! f : Y ⟶ Z, ∀ i, v i ≫ f = h i
declarations.comment: morphisms of locally ringed spaces glue over an open covering of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.existsUnique_hom_to_glued_of_compatibleCharts
declarations.doc:
Compatible morphisms from an open covering of a locally ringed space to the pieces of a
gluing datum determine a unique morphism to the glued space. The two equations for
`transitionLift` say that on `V i ×_Y V j` the maps are related by the transition `D.t i j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_hom_to_glued_of_compatibleCharts
    (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u}) (Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u})
    (V : D.J → LocallyRingedSpace.{u}) (v : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Y)
    (v_open : ∀ i, LocallyRingedSpace.IsOpenImmersion (v i))
    (v_jointly_surjective : ∀ y : Y, ∃ (i : D.J) (x : V i), (v i).base x = y)
    (g : ∀ i, V i ⟶ D.U i)
    (transitionLift : ∀ i j, pullback (v i) (v j) ⟶ D.V (i, j))
    (transitionLift_f : ∀ i j,
      transitionLift i j ≫ D.f i j = pullback.fst (v i) (v j) ≫ g i)
    (transitionLift_t_f : ∀ i j,
      transitionLift i j ≫ D.t i j ≫ D.f j i = pullback.snd (v i) (v j) ≫ g j) :
    ∃! f : Y ⟶ D.glued, ∀ i, v i ≫ f = g i ≫ D.ι i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.hom_chartDatumOfHom
declarations.doc:
The mapping property for morphisms *into* a glueing: a morphism `g : Y ⟶ D.glued` is
recovered from the descent datum it induces, so that passing from a morphism to its chart datum
and back is the identity. Combined with
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.existsUnique_hom_to_glued`, which says that every
chart datum determines a unique morphism, this identifies `Mor(Y, D.glued)` with the set of
descent data arising from morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_chartDatumOfHom (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u})
    {Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ D.glued) :
    ∀ f : Y ⟶ D.glued,
      (∀ i, (D.chartDatumOfHom g).v i ≫ f = (D.chartDatumOfHom g).g i ≫ D.ι i) → f = g
declarations.comment: the mapping property for morphisms into the glueing

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.ChartDatum.chartIso_hom_fst_and_snd
declarations.doc:
The other half of the round trip for morphisms *into* a glueing: a descent datum is carried
isomorphically, chart by chart and compatibly with both the covering maps and the local
morphisms, onto the descent datum induced by the morphism it determines — whose charts, covering
maps and local morphisms are `pullback f (D.ι i)`, `pullback.fst f (D.ι i)` and
`pullback.snd f (D.ι i)` by `chartDatumOfHom_V`, `chartDatumOfHom_v` and `chartDatumOfHom_g`.
Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.hom_chartDatumOfHom` this identifies
`Mor(Y, D.glued)` with the descent data of the statement.
declarations.comment: a descent datum is its own inverse-image covering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.homIntoEquiv
declarations.doc:
The mapping property for morphisms *into* a gluing, as a bijection: a morphism `Y ⟶ D.glued` is
the same thing as a descent datum on `Y`, namely an open covering of `Y` together with compatible
morphisms from its members to the pieces of the gluing datum. The bijection sends `f` to the
covering by the inverse images `f ⁻¹' (U i)` and the factorisations of `f` through the charts.
This is the counterpart for morphisms into the gluing of
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.homOutEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homIntoEquiv (D : LocallyRingedSpace.GlueData.{u})
    (Y : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}) : (Y ⟶ D.glued) ≃ D.ChartDatumOpens Y
declarations.comment: Mor(Y, X) is the set of descent data on an open covering of Y

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.glued
registrations.comment: the glued scheme

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData.isoLocallyRingedSpace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineSpaceWithDoubledZero
declarations.doc:
Affine `n`-space over `k` with its origin doubled, obtained by gluing two copies along the
complements of their origins via the coordinate identification.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev affineSpaceWithDoubledZero (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coordinateMorphismData
declarations.doc:
The coordinate maps on the two charts of affine space with doubled origin glue to a scheme
morphism to affine space, restricting to the identity on each chart.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coordinateMorphismData (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) :
    { f : affineSpaceWithDoubledZero k n ⟶
        Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) //
      ∀ i : Fin 2,
        chartInclusion k n i ≫ f = 𝟙 _ }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coordinateMorphism_map_origin
declarations.doc:
The coordinate morphism maps the origin of each affine chart to the origin of affine
space.
declarations.statement:
theorem coordinateMorphism_map_origin (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ)
    (i : Fin 2) :
    coordinateMorphism k n
        (chartInclusion k n i
          (affineOrigin k n)) = affineOrigin k n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.intersection_iso_puncturedAffinePlane
declarations.doc:
In dimension two, the overlap of the two affine charts of the doubled-origin scheme is the
punctured affine plane.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersection_iso_puncturedAffinePlane (S : PuncturedAffinePlane.{u}) :
    Nonempty (((chartInclusion S.k 2 0).opensRange ⊓
      (chartInclusion S.k 2 1).opensRange).toScheme ≅ S.puncturedScheme)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_isAffineOpen_chartIntersection
declarations.doc:
For dimension greater than one, the two affine charts of affine space with doubled origin have
a non-affine intersection.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isAffineOpen_chartIntersection (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ)
    (hn : 1 < n) :
    ¬ IsAffineOpen ((chartInclusion k n 0).opensRange ⊓
      (chartInclusion k n 1).opensRange)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpens_nonaffine_inf
declarations.doc: The intersection of two affine opens in a scheme need not be affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpens_nonaffine_inf :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (U V : X.Opens),
      IsAffineOpen U ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧ ¬ IsAffineOpen (U ⊓ V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.infinite_irreducibleClosed_closures
declarations.doc:
In dimension greater than one, infinitely many irreducible closed subsets of affine space with
doubled origin are closures of nonclosed points in its first affine chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem infinite_irreducibleClosed_closures (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
    Set.Infinite
      { T : Set (affineSpaceWithDoubledZero k n) |
        IsClosed T ∧ IsIrreducible T ∧
          ∃ x : Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)),
            ¬ IsClosed ({x} : Set (Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)))) ∧
              T = closure ({(chartInclusion k n 0).base x} :
                Set (affineSpaceWithDoubledZero k n)) }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_origin_iff_mem_origin
declarations.doc:
Apart from the two singleton origins, an irreducible closed subset of affine space with
the origin doubled contains either both origins or neither.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_origin_iff_mem_origin (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ)
    (T : Set (affineSpaceWithDoubledZero k n))
    (hT : IsIrreducible T) (hT_closed : IsClosed T)
    (hT₀ : T ≠ {chartInclusion k n 0 (affineOrigin k n)})
    (hT₁ : T ≠ {chartInclusion k n 1 (affineOrigin k n)}) :
    (chartInclusion k n 0 (affineOrigin k n) ∈ T ↔
      chartInclusion k n 1 (affineOrigin k n) ∈ T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_coordinateMorphism_globalSections
declarations.doc:
In positive dimension, every global function on affine space with doubled origin is induced
uniquely by a polynomial via the coordinate morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coordinateMorphism_globalSections (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))).inv ≫
      (coordinateMorphism k n).appTop)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_isAffine_affineSpaceWithDoubledZero
declarations.doc: Affine space of positive dimension with its origin doubled is not affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isAffine_affineSpaceWithDoubledZero (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ¬ IsAffine (affineSpaceWithDoubledZero k n)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineOpen_opensRange
registrations.comment: affine_open_charts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineInversionIso
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `φ₁₂` of the gluing datum: the automorphism of the punctured affine line
induced by `T ↦ T⁻¹`, which is the identification `y = 1/x` of the two coordinates on the
overlap.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def projectiveLineInversionIso :
    Spec (.of (LaurentPolynomial k)) ≅ Spec (.of (LaurentPolynomial k))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineGluingData
declarations.doc:
The gluing datum for the projective line: two copies of `Spec k[X]`, glued along
`D(X) = Spec k[T,T⁻¹]` by inversion.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def projectiveLineGluingData : Scheme.GlueData.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLine
declarations.doc: The projective line over `k`, constructed by gluing its two standard affine charts.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev projectiveLine : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineZero
declarations.doc: The point `0` of the projective line, namely the point `(X)` in the `x`-chart.
declarations.statement: def projectiveLineZero [IsDomain k] : projectiveLine k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineInfinity
declarations.doc: The point `∞` of the projective line, namely the point `(X)` in the `y`-chart.
declarations.statement: def projectiveLineInfinity [IsDomain k] : projectiveLine k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineLineOne
declarations.doc: The point `1` of an affine-line chart, represented by the prime ideal `(X - 1)`.
declarations.statement: def affineLineOne : Spec (.of (Polynomial k))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineOne
declarations.doc: The point `1` of the projective line, namely the point `(x - 1)` in the `x`-chart.

declarations.doc: The point `1` is *also* the point `(y - 1)` of the second chart.

    projectiveLineYChart k (affineLineOne k) = projectiveLineOne k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineSChart
declarations.doc:
The third chart of the projective line: the affine line with coordinate
`s = 1/(x-1) = y/(1-y)`, mapping onto the complement of the point `1`.
declarations.statement: def projectiveLineSChart : Spec (.of (Polynomial k)) ⟶ projectiveLine k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineSXPiece_comp_projectiveLineSChart
declarations.doc:
On `D(x-1) ⊂ X₁` the third chart is the inclusion of that open into the first chart;
equivalently, `s` restricts to `1/(x-1)` there.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLineSXPiece_comp_projectiveLineSChart :
    projectiveLineSXPiece k ≫ projectiveLineSChart k =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (Polynomial k) (affineLineAwayOne k))) ≫
        projectiveLineXChart k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineSYPiece_comp_projectiveLineSChart
declarations.doc:
On `D(y-1) ⊂ X₂` the third chart is the inclusion of that open into the second chart;
equivalently, `s` restricts to `y/(1-y)` there.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLineSYPiece_comp_projectiveLineSChart :
    projectiveLineSYPiece k ≫ projectiveLineSChart k =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (Polynomial k) (affineLineAwayOne k))) ≫
        projectiveLineYChart k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.range_projectiveLineSChart
declarations.doc: The image of the third chart is exactly the complement of the point `1`: `U = ℙ¹ \ {1}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_projectiveLineSChart :
    Set.range (projectiveLineSChart k).base = {projectiveLineOne k}ᶜ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineOpen_projectiveLineSChart
declarations.doc: `U = ℙ¹ \ {1}` is an affine open.
declarations.statement:

    IsAffineOpen (projectiveLineSChart k).opensRange

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineInfinity_mem_opensRange_projectiveLineSChart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLineSChartIso
declarations.doc: `U = ℙ¹ \ {1}` is isomorphic to `Spec k[s]`, and so `Γ(U, O_U) = k[s]`.

declarations.doc:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_range_projectiveLinePuncturedChart_iff
declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_openCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01JJ for the big fppf site over `S`.** A sheaf on the big fppf site over `S`
which admits a jointly locally surjective family of relatively representable open immersions
from representable presheaves is representable, by an object of that site.

This is the statement Mathlib's
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.isRepresentable` does not give: Mathlib glues
in `Scheme` with no size control, so its representing object need not satisfy the site's size
cutoff. The hypothesis on the index type is one set-theoretic condition which makes the glued
scheme an object of the site; an at most countable family satisfies it automatically, since
uncountable cofinality of the cutoff is a field of `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite`. It is not
the weakest such condition:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_openCover_of_contains` asks only that the glued
scheme lie in the site, however that is established.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_openCover (hι : #ι < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    [HasCoproduct fun i => yoneda.obj (X i)]
    (hsurj : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Sigma.desc f)) :
    G.obj.IsRepresentable
declarations.comment: big fppf site over a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lrsRepresentableByScheme
declarations.doc:
A Zariski sheaf on locally ringed spaces, covered by subfunctors represented
by schemes and relatively represented by open immersions, is itself represented
by a scheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem lrsRepresentableByScheme
    (F : LocallyRingedSpace.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf lrsZariskiTopology F)
    {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I] (H : I → Subfunctor F)
    (hrep : ∀ i, ∃ S : Scheme.{u}, Nonempty ((H i).toFunctor.RepresentableBy
      S.toLocallyRingedSpace))
    (hopen : ∀ i, (MorphismProperty.presheaf
      lrsIsOpenImmersion.{u}) (H i).ι)
    (hcover : Covers LocallyRingedSpace.forgetToTop
      lrsIsOpenImmersion.{u} F H) :
    ∃ S : Scheme.{u}, Nonempty (F.RepresentableBy S.toLocallyRingedSpace)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pullback.isAffine_openCoverOfBase_bind_openCoverOfLeftRight
declarations.doc:
Every member of the open cover of a fibre product assembled from affine open covers over an
affine open cover of the base is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_openCoverOfBase_bind_openCoverOfLeftRight
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (𝒰 : Scheme.OpenCover.{v} S)
    (𝒱 : ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, Scheme.OpenCover.{w} (pullback f (𝒰.f i)))
    (𝒲 : ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, Scheme.OpenCover.{t} (pullback g (𝒰.f i)))
    (h𝒰 : ∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i))
    (h𝒱 : ∀ i j, IsAffine ((𝒱 i).X j))
    (h𝒲 : ∀ i k, IsAffine ((𝒲 i).X k)) :
    ∀ a : ((Scheme.Pullback.openCoverOfBase 𝒰 f g).bind fun i =>
      Scheme.Pullback.openCoverOfLeftRight (𝒱 i) (𝒲 i)
        (pullback.snd f (𝒰.f i)) (pullback.snd g (𝒰.f i))).I₀,
      IsAffine (((Scheme.Pullback.openCoverOfBase 𝒰 f g).bind fun i =>
        Scheme.Pullback.openCoverOfLeftRight (𝒱 i) (𝒲 i)
          (pullback.snd f (𝒰.f i)) (pullback.snd g (𝒰.f i))).X a)

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.existsUnique_idealSheaf_pullbackSnd_iso_pullbackIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01JU, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a closed immersion of schemes
corresponding to the sheaf of ideals `i : I ⟶ 𝒪_S`, and let `g : Y ⟶ S` be any morphism of
schemes. Then the base change `X ×_S Y ⟶ Y`, which is a closed immersion by
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.isStableUnderBaseChange`, corresponds to the inverse-image
ideal `Im(g^* I ⟶ 𝒪_Y)`: its ideal sheaf is that ideal, by a unique isomorphism compatible with
the two inclusions into `𝒪_Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_idealSheaf_pullbackSnd_iso_pullbackIdeal {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (g : Y ⟶ S) [hcl : AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion f]
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace))
    (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (structureSheafRing S.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace))
    (e : I ≅ idealSheaf f.toLRSHom.toShHom)
    (he : e.hom ≫ kernel.ι (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit
      (structureSheafHom f.toLRSHom.toShHom)) = i) :
    ∃! e' : idealSheaf (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom ≅ pullbackIdeal g.toLRSHom I i,
      e'.hom ≫ pullbackIdealInclusion g.toLRSHom I i =
        kernel.ι (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit
          (structureSheafHom (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.structureMorphism
declarations.doc:
The structure morphism of infinite-dimensional affine space with doubled
origin, restricting on both charts to the canonical affine-space morphism.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def structureMorphism {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
    (D : DoubledOriginData k) :
    { f : D.scheme ⟶ Spec (.of k) //
      ∀ i : Fin 2,
        D.chart i ≫ f = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPolynomial.C :
          k →+* MvPolynomial ℕ k)) }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.diagonal_preimage_mixedCharts
declarations.doc:
The diagonal inverse image of the product of the two affine charts is the punctured
affine space, embedded in the doubled-origin scheme through its first chart.
declarations.statement:
public theorem diagonal_preimage_mixedCharts {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
    (D : DoubledOriginData k) {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : D.scheme ⟶ S) :
    (pullback.diagonal f) ⁻¹'
        ((pullback.fst f f) ⁻¹' Set.range (D.chart 0) ∩
          (pullback.snd f f) ⁻¹' Set.range (D.chart 1)) =
      Set.range ((puncturedInfiniteAffineSpace k).ι ≫ D.chart 0)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparated_iff_isCompact_inf
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is quasi-separated if and only if for every pair of affine opens `U`,
`V` of `X` which map into a common affine open `W` of `S`, the intersection `U ∩ V` is
quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiSeparated_iff_isCompact_inf {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    QuasiSeparated f ↔
      ∀ (W : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → ∀ U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W, ∀ V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W,
        IsAffineOpen U → IsAffineOpen V → IsCompact ((U ⊓ V : X.Opens) : Set X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparated_iff_finite_iSup_affineOpens
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is quasi-separated if and only if for every pair of affine opens `U`,
`V` of `X` which map into a common affine open of `S`, the intersection `U ∩ V` is a finite union
of affine opens of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiSeparated_iff_finite_iSup_affineOpens {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    QuasiSeparated f ↔
      ∀ (W : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → ∀ U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W, ∀ V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W,
        IsAffineOpen U → IsAffineOpen V →
        ∃ s : Set X.affineOpens, s.Finite ∧ (U ⊓ V : X.Opens) = ⨆ i ∈ s, (i : X.Opens)
declarations.comment: condition (2), as a finite union of affine opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparated_of_openCover
declarations.doc:
Given an affine open covering `𝒰` of `S` and, for each `i`, an affine open covering `𝒱 i` of
`f ⁻¹ U i`, if every fibre product `V j ×_{U i} V k` is quasi-compact then `f` is
quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiSeparated_of_openCover {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (𝒰 : Scheme.OpenCover.{v} S) [∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i)]
    (𝒱 : ∀ i, Scheme.OpenCover.{w} (pullback f (𝒰.f i))) [∀ i j, IsAffine ((𝒱 i).X j)]
    (h : ∀ i j k, CompactSpace (pullback ((𝒱 i).f j) ((𝒱 i).f k) : Scheme.{u})) :
    QuasiSeparated f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparated_of_isOpenCover
declarations.doc:
Given an affine open covering `S = ⋃ i, W i` and for each `i` an affine open covering
`f ⁻¹ (W i) = ⋃ j, V i j`, if each intersection `V i j ∩ V i k` is quasi-compact then `f` is
quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiSeparated_of_isOpenCover {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    {ι : Type*} (W : ι → S.Opens) (hW : IsOpenCover W) (hWaff : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (W i))
    {κ : ι → Type*} (V : ∀ i, κ i → X.Opens) (hV : ∀ i, ⨆ j, V i j = f ⁻¹ᵁ W i)
    (hVaff : ∀ i j, IsAffineOpen (V i j))
    (hVcompact : ∀ i j k, IsCompact ((V i j ⊓ V i k : X.Opens) : Set X)) :
    QuasiSeparated f
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies (1), for families of opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenCover_of_quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
A quasi-separated morphism admits an affine open covering of the base and an affine open
covering of each preimage whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact; one may take all the
affine opens there are.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpenCover_of_quasiSeparated {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [QuasiSeparated f] :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (W : ι → S.Opens), IsOpenCover W ∧ (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (W i)) ∧
      ∃ (κ : ι → Type u) (V : ∀ i, κ i → X.Opens),
        (∀ i, ⨆ j, V i j = f ⁻¹ᵁ W i) ∧ (∀ i j, IsAffineOpen (V i j)) ∧
        (∀ i j k, IsCompact ((V i j ⊓ V i k : X.Opens) : Set X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sectionTensorMap_surjective_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
For a separated morphism, the tensor product of sections surjects onto
sections of the intersection of compatible affine opens.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sectionTensorMap_surjective_of_isSeparated {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f] (U V : X.Opens)
    (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (W : S.Opens) (hW : IsAffineOpen W)
    (hUW : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W) (hVW : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W) :
    Function.Surjective (sectionTensorMap X U V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_affine_intersections
declarations.doc:
Affine neighborhoods of every pair of points in a fiber, with affine
intersection and surjective tensor map on sections, imply separatedness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSeparated_of_affine_intersections {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S)
    (h : ∀ x₁ x₂ : X, f.base x₁ = f.base x₂ →
      ∃ (U V : X.Opens) (W : S.Opens),
        x₁ ∈ U ∧ x₂ ∈ V ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧
        IsAffineOpen W ∧ U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W ∧ V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ W ∧
        IsAffineOpen (U ⊓ V) ∧ Function.Surjective (sectionTensorMap X U V)) :
    IsSeparated f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineOpen_inf_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01KW.** For a separated morphism `f : X ⟶ S` over a separated scheme `S`, the
intersection of two affine opens of `X` is affine. The hypotheses make `X` separated over the
terminal scheme, so its absolute diagonal is affine.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_prodLift_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01KW.** Under the hypotheses, `U ∩ V` is a closed subscheme of the absolute
product `U × V`, the product being taken over the terminal scheme.

The map exhibiting it is the canonical `prod.lift` of the two inclusions `U ⊓ V ⟶ U` and
`U ⊓ V ⟶ V`. It is obtained from the base change `pullback U.ι V.ι ⟶ pullback (U.ι ≫ 𝟙_)
(V.ι ≫ 𝟙_)` of the absolute diagonal of `X`, which is a closed immersion because `X` is a
separated scheme, by transporting along `(isPullback_opens_inf U V).isoPullback` on the source
and `prodIsoPullback` on the target.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedImmersion_prodLift_of_isSeparated {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [S.IsSeparated] (U V : X.Opens) :
    IsClosedImmersion (prod.lift (X.homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ V ≤ U))
      (X.homOfLE (inf_le_right : U ⊓ V ≤ V)))
declarations.comment: closed subscheme of the absolute product

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FunctorialityQcoh.isQuasicoherent_iff_forall_isAffineOpen_exists_tilde
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01LA], item (1).** A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `F` is quasi-coherent if and
only if the restriction of `F` to each affine open `U = Spec Γ(X, U)` is of the form `M^~` for
some `Γ(X, U)`-module `M`.

Forwards, the module is `Γ(F, U)` and the isomorphism is
`Stacks.Modules.tildeIsoRestrictFromSpec`. Backwards, `M^~` is quasi-coherent, hence so is the
restriction of `F` to `Spec Γ(X, U)`; transporting along `hU.isoSpec.hom ≫ hU.fromSpec = U.ι`
makes the restriction of `F` to `U` quasi-coherent, and quasi-coherence is local on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_iff_forall_isAffineOpen_exists_tilde (F : X.Modules) :
    F.IsQuasicoherent ↔
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U),
        ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U),
          Nonempty (tilde (R := Γ(X, U)) M ≅ F.restrict hU.fromSpec)
declarations.comment: the section's item (1): a sheaf of modules is quasi-coherent exactly when its restriction to each affine open `U = Spec Γ(X, U)` is the sheaf associated to a `Γ(X, U)`-module

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FunctorialityQcoh.isQuasicoherent_iff_forall_restrict
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01LA], item (2).** A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `F` is quasi-coherent if and
only if the restriction of `F` to each of the members of an affine open covering of `X` is
quasi-coherent.

Forwards this is restriction along an open immersion, which preserves quasi-coherence;
backwards it is `Stacks.Modules.isQuasicoherent_of_restrict`, the locality of
quasi-coherence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_iff_forall_restrict {I : Type w} (F : X.Modules)
    (U : I → X.affineOpens) (hU : ⨆ i, (U i : X.Opens) = ⊤) :
    F.IsQuasicoherent ↔ ∀ i, (F.restrict (U i : X.Opens).ι).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the section's item (2): a sheaf of modules is quasi-coherent exactly when its restriction to each member of an affine open covering is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FunctorialityQcoh.isQuasicoherent_X₁_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01LA], item (6), the kernel case.** Let
`0 ⟶ F₁ ⟶ F₂ ⟶ F₃ ⟶ 0` be a short exact sequence of `𝒪_X`-modules on an arbitrary scheme `X`.
If `F₂` and `F₃` are quasi-coherent then so is `F₁`, being the kernel of `F₂ ⟶ F₃`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_X₁_of_shortExact (S : ShortComplex X.Modules)
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (h₂ : S.X₂.IsQuasicoherent) (h₃ : S.X₃.IsQuasicoherent) :
    S.X₁.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the section's item (6), the kernel case on an arbitrary scheme: in a short exact sequence, if the last two terms are quasi-coherent then so is the first

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeMayerVietoris.pushforward_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01LC].** The direct image of a quasi-coherent module along a quasi-compact
quasi-separated morphism of schemes is quasi-coherent.

The statement is local on the target: over an affine open `V` of `S` the restriction of `f_* F` is
the direct image along `f ∣_ V` of the restriction of `F` to `f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, and `f ∣_ V` is again
quasi-compact and quasi-separated with affine target.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforward_isQuasicoherent (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LC.** Pushforward along a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphism of schemes preserves quasi-coherence.
declarations.statement:
public instance pushforward_isQuasicoherent
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.BasisGluingData.exists_isPullback_res_comp
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme and `B` a basis for its topology. Given a scheme `D.obj U` over `U` for
every `U ∈ B`, together with morphisms `D.res : D.obj V ⟶ D.obj U` for `V ⊆ U` in `B`
identifying `D.obj V` with the part of `D.obj U` over `V` and satisfying the cocycle condition,
there is a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` and charts `i U : D.obj U ⟶ X` identifying `D.obj U`
with the part of `X` over `U`, compatibly with the restriction morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPullback_res_comp (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) (D : BasisGluingData S B) :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ S) (i : ∀ U : B, D.obj U ⟶ X),
      (∀ U : B, IsPullback (D.proj U) (i U) U.1.ι f) ∧
        ∀ {V U : B} (h : V.1 ≤ U.1), D.res h ≫ i U = i V
declarations.comment:
existence of the glued scheme, with the charts identifying each piece with the
part of it lying over the corresponding member of the basis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.BasisGluingData.existsUnique_isoOver
declarations.doc:
The glued scheme of a gluing datum over a basis of the topology of `S` is unique up to unique
isomorphism over `S`: between any two solutions of the gluing problem there is exactly one
isomorphism compatible with the charts, and it is a morphism over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isoOver (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) (D : BasisGluingData S B)
    {X X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {f' : X' ⟶ S}
    {i : ∀ U : B, D.obj U ⟶ X} {i' : ∀ U : B, D.obj U ⟶ X'}
    (hi : ∀ U : B, IsPullback (D.proj U) (i U) U.1.ι f)
    (hi' : ∀ U : B, IsPullback (D.proj U) (i' U) U.1.ι f')
    (hres : ∀ {V U : B} (h : V.1 ≤ U.1), D.res h ≫ i U = i V)
    (hres' : ∀ {V U : B} (h : V.1 ≤ U.1), D.res h ≫ i' U = i' V) :
    ∃! e : X ≅ X', (∀ U : B, i U ≫ e.hom = i' U) ∧ e.hom ≫ f' = f
declarations.comment: the glued scheme is unique up to unique isomorphism over the base

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeSheafGluing.RelativeSheafGluingData.exists_glued_and_existsUnique_pairIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LI, both of its assertions as one statement.**  Let `𝒰` be a locally
directed open cover of a scheme `S`, let `d` be a relative gluing datum over it, and let `D` be a
compatible family of quasi-coherent modules on the schemes of `d`.  Then:

* *existence of the whole package.*  There is a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`, morphisms
  `i a : X a ⟶ X` exhibiting each `X a` as the part of `X` lying over the `a`-th member of the
  cover and compatible with the transition morphisms of `d`, and a quasi-coherent module `F` on
  `X` together with isomorphisms `θ a : F a ≅ (i a)^* F` under which the prescribed transition
  isomorphisms of the `F a` are the ones induced by `F`.
* *uniqueness.*  The pair `(X, F)` is unique up to unique isomorphism over `S`: any two glued
  pairs are related by exactly one isomorphism of pairs.

The two conjuncts are
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeSheafGluing.RelativeSheafGluingData.exists_isPullback_localIso`
and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeSheafGluing.RelativeSheafGluingData.existsUnique_pairIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_glued_and_existsUnique_pairIso :
    (∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ S) (i : ∀ a, d.functor.obj a ⟶ X)
      (_ : ∀ a, IsPullback (d.natTrans.app a) (i a) (𝒰.f a) f)
      (hi : ∀ {a b : 𝒰.I₀} (hab : a ⟶ b), d.functor.map hab ≫ i b = i a)
      (F : X.Modules), F.IsQuasicoherent ∧
        ∃ θ : ∀ a, D.obj a ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (i a)).obj F,
          ∀ {a b : 𝒰.I₀} (hab : a ⟶ b),
            (D.transitionIso hab).hom ≫ (θ a).hom =
              (Scheme.Modules.pullback (d.functor.map hab)).map (θ b).hom ≫
                (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (d.functor.map hab) (i b)).hom.app F ≫
                  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (hi hab)).hom.app F) ∧
      ∀ (H H' : Gluing d) (R : D.RealizationOn H) (R' : D.RealizationOn H'),
        ∃ p : D.PairIso R R', ∀ q : D.PairIso R R', q = p
declarations.comment:
both assertions of the tag as one statement: existence of the glued package — the
morphism f, the charts i_U, the quasi-coherent module F, the identifications θ_U and their two
compatibilities — and uniqueness of the pair (X, F) up to unique isomorphism over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CompatibleRelativeGluingData.colimMap_localHom_toBase
declarations.doc: The morphism induced on the glued schemes is a morphism over the common base.
declarations.statement:
public lemma colimMap_localHom_toBase :
    colimMap D.localHom ≫ D.target.toBase = D.source.toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.BasisGluingData.existsUnique_hom_of_compatible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LK: functoriality for the data of Lemma 01LH.** Let `S` be a scheme
and `B` a basis for its topology, and let `D` and `D'` be gluing data over `B` as in Tag 01LH,
with local schemes `D.obj U ⟶ U` and `D'.obj U ⟶ U` and restriction morphisms `D.res` and
`D'.res`. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a scheme glued from `D`, with charts `i U`, and `g : Y ⟶ S` one
glued from `D'`, with charts `j U`. A family of morphisms `h U : D.obj U ⟶ D'.obj U` over `U`
compatible with the restriction morphisms gives rise to a morphism `k : X ⟶ Y` over `S` which
restricts back to the `h U`, and `k` is the only such morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_hom_of_compatible (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) (D D' : BasisGluingData S B)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : Y ⟶ S}
    {i : ∀ U : B, D.obj U ⟶ X} {j : ∀ U : B, D'.obj U ⟶ Y}
    (hi : ∀ U : B, IsPullback (D.proj U) (i U) U.1.ι f)
    (hj : ∀ U : B, IsPullback (D'.proj U) (j U) U.1.ι g)
    (hires : ∀ {V U : B} (h : V.1 ≤ U.1), D.res h ≫ i U = i V)
    (hjres : ∀ {V U : B} (h : V.1 ≤ U.1), D'.res h ≫ j U = j V)
    (h : ∀ U : B, D.obj U ⟶ D'.obj U)
    (hover : ∀ U : B, h U ≫ D'.proj U = D.proj U)
    (hcompat : ∀ {V U : B} (hVU : V.1 ≤ U.1), D.res hVU ≫ h U = h V ≫ D'.res hVU) :
    ∃! k : X ⟶ Y, (∀ U : B, i U ≫ k = h U ≫ j U) ∧ k ≫ g = f
declarations.comment: scheme_morphism, for the gluing data over a basis of Tag 01LH

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeSheafGluing.exists_pullbackHom_of_transitionCompatible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LK.** *Functoriality of relative gluing for quasi-coherent sheaves.*
Let `𝒰` be a locally directed open cover of a scheme `S` and let `dX`, `dY` be relative gluing
data over it, carrying compatible families of quasi-coherent modules realized by `ℱ` on the glued
scheme `X` and `𝒢` on the glued scheme `Y`. Given a family of morphisms `hᵢ : Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ` commuting
with the restriction maps — hence the morphism `h = colimMap` of glued schemes — and morphisms
`τᵢ : hᵢ⁎𝒢ᵢ ⟶ ℱᵢ` compatible with the transition isomorphisms of the two families, there is a
morphism `h⁎𝒢 ⟶ ℱ` whose inverse image on the `i`-th chart is `τᵢ`, read through the canonical
identifications.

The companion half of the remark — that `h` is a morphism over `S` restricting to the given `hᵢ`
— is `CategoryTheory.Limits.ι_colimMap` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.CompatibleRelativeGluingData.colimMap_localHom_toBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pullbackHom_of_transitionCompatible (hom : dX.functor ⟶ dY.functor)
    (A : DX.Realization) (B : DY.Realization)
    (τ : ∀ i, (Scheme.Modules.pullback (hom.app i)).obj (DY.obj i) ⟶ DX.obj i)
    (hτ : IsTransitionCompatible hom DX DY τ) :
    ∃ ψ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (colimMap hom)).obj B.sheaf ⟶ A.sheaf, ∀ i,
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (colimit.ι dX.functor i)).map ψ =
        pullbackChartHom hom A B τ i

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.colimMap
registrations.comment: scheme_morphism

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.ι_colimMap
registrations.comment: scheme_morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.RelativeSpecSituation
declarations.doc:
A scheme equipped with a quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative
algebras over its structure sheaf.
declarations.statement: structure RelativeSpecSituation

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.isPullback_specMap_restriction
declarations.doc:
For nested affine opens `U ⊆ U'` of the base of a relative spectrum situation, the square
formed by the spectra of the sections of the quasi-coherent algebra, the two open subschemes,
and their canonical restriction morphisms is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_specMap_restriction (s : RelativeSpecSituation.{u})
    (U U' : s.base.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hU' : IsAffineOpen U') (h : U ≤ U') :
    IsPullback
      (Spec.map (s.algebra.right.obj.map (homOfLE h).op))
      (Spec.map (s.algebra.hom.hom.app (.op U)) ≫ hU.isoSpec.inv)
      (Spec.map (s.algebra.hom.hom.app (.op U')) ≫ hU'.isoSpec.inv)
      (s.base.homOfLE h)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.specMap_restriction_comp
declarations.doc:
For opens `U ⊆ U' ⊆ U''` of the base of a relative spectrum situation, the composition of
the morphisms `Spec A(U) ⟶ Spec A(U')` and `Spec A(U') ⟶ Spec A(U'')` of
`Stacks.RelativeSpec.isPullback_specMap_restriction` is the morphism `Spec A(U) ⟶ Spec A(U'')`
of the same lemma.
declarations.statement:
theorem specMap_restriction_comp (s : RelativeSpecSituation.{u}) {U U' U'' : s.base.Opens}
    (h : U ≤ U') (h' : U' ≤ U'') :
    Spec.map (s.algebra.right.obj.map (homOfLE h).op) ≫
        Spec.map (s.algebra.right.obj.map (homOfLE h').op) =
      Spec.map (s.algebra.right.obj.map (homOfLE (h.trans h')).op)
declarations.comment: the composite of the restriction morphisms of spectra of sections is the restriction morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LP**, existence. The affine spectra of the sections of a
quasi-coherent algebra glue to a scheme over the base, with the prescribed inverse images and
the prescribed transition morphisms.

The glued scheme and its structure morphism are
`Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.relativeSpec` and
`Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.relativeSpecToBase`; the content added here is that its
charts satisfy properties (1) and (2) of the tag.
declarations.statement: def relativeSpectrum : RelativeSpectrum s

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.existsUnique_relativeSpectrumIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LP**, uniqueness. Any two relative spectra of the same
quasi-coherent algebra admit a unique isomorphism over the base compatible with all the
charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_relativeSpectrumIso (X Y : RelativeSpectrum s) :
    ∃! e : X.scheme ≅ Y.scheme,
      (e.hom ≫ Y.toBase = X.toBase) ∧ ∀ U, X.chart U ≫ e.hom = Y.chart U

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.gluedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LP, parts (1) and (2).** The affine spectra of the sections of a
quasi-coherent algebra glue to a scheme over the base, with the prescribed inverse images and
transition open immersions.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gluedSpectrum (s : RelativeSpecSituation.{u}) : GluedSpectrum s

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.existsUnique_gluedSpectrumIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LP, uniqueness.** Any two schemes over the base carrying the affine
charts of the relative spectrum admit a unique isomorphism over the base that respects all the
charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.Stacks.RelativeSpec.existsUnique_gluedSpectrumIso
    (s : RelativeSpecSituation.{u}) (X Y : GluedSpectrum s) :
    ∃! e : X.scheme ≅ Y.scheme,
      (e.hom ≫ Y.toBase = X.toBase) ∧ (∀ U, X.chart U ≫ e.hom = Y.chart U)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctor
declarations.doc:
The contravariant functor sending a test scheme `T` to the pairs
`(f : T ⟶ X, φ : A ⟶ f_* 𝒪_T)` and a morphism of test schemes to pullback of such pairs.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeSpecFunctor (s : RelativeSpecSituation.{u}) :
    Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.algebraPullback_nonempty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** Extension of scalars of a quasi-coherent algebra sheaf along
any morphism of schemes exists and is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement: theorem algebraPullback_nonempty : Nonempty (AlgebraPullback s g)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctorPullbackToOriginal_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** On a test scheme, the canonical map composes the structural
morphism with the base-change morphism.
declarations.comment: base component of the canonical map to the original functor

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctorPullbackToOriginal_algebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** The algebra component of the canonical map is obtained from
the transpose of `g⁻¹A ⟶ g⁺A`, then pushed forward along the test-scheme map.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeSpecFunctorPullbackToOriginal_algebra {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : RelativeSpecPair (pullbackAlgebra s g).situation T) :
    HEq ((relativeSpecFunctorPullbackToOriginal s g).app (.op T) p).2.right
      (((TopCat.Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction CommRingCat g.base).homEquiv
          s.algebra.right (pullbackAlgebra s g).algebra.right
          (pullbackAlgebra s g).map).hom ≫
        (TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward CommRingCat g.base).map p.2.right)
declarations.comment: algebra component of the canonical map to the original functor

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctor_pullback_iso_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** Formation of the relative spectrum functor commutes with
arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeSpecFunctor_pullback_iso_pullback :
    relativeSpecFunctor (pullbackAlgebra s g).situation ≅
      pullback (yoneda.map g) (relativeSpecFunctorToBase s)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctor_pullback_iso_pullback_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** The first component of the canonical base-change isomorphism
remembers the map from a test scheme to the new base.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeSpecFunctor_pullback_iso_pullback_fst :
    (relativeSpecFunctor_pullback_iso_pullback s g).hom ≫
        pullback.fst (yoneda.map g) (relativeSpecFunctorToBase s) =
      relativeSpecFunctorToBase (pullbackAlgebra s g).situation
declarations.comment: first component of the canonical isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctor_pullback_iso_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** The second component of the isomorphism is the canonical
transformation induced by the algebra pullback map.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeSpecFunctor_pullback_iso_pullback_snd :
    (relativeSpecFunctor_pullback_iso_pullback s g).hom ≫
        pullback.snd (yoneda.map g) (relativeSpecFunctorToBase s) =
      relativeSpecFunctorPullbackToOriginal s g
declarations.comment: second component of the canonical isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.RelativeSpecSituation.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** The relative-spectrum situation obtained from `(S, A)` by base
change along `g : S' ⟶ S`: the base is `S'` and the algebra is `A' = g^*A`, the pullback
`g⁻¹A ⊗_{g⁻¹𝒪_S} 𝒪_{S'}` of `A` as an algebra sheaf, which is again quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
def RelativeSpecSituation.baseChange (s : RelativeSpecSituation.{u}) {S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : S' ⟶ s.base) : RelativeSpecSituation.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.baseChangeToOriginal_app_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** The morphism to `S` underlying the image of a pair under the
canonical transformation `F' ⟶ F` is the morphism to `S'` of the pair, composed with `g`.
declarations.comment: base component of the canonical map to the original functor

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.baseChangeToOriginal_app_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** The algebra map of the image of a pair under the canonical
transformation `F' ⟶ F` is the direct image along `g` of the pair's algebra map, precomposed
with the adjunct of the canonical map `g⁻¹A ⟶ g^*A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChangeToOriginal_app_right {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : RelativeSpecPair (s.baseChange g) T) :
    ((baseChangeToOriginal s g).app (.op T) p).2.right =
      ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction CommRingCat g.base).homEquiv
          s.algebra.right ((algebraPullback g).obj s.algebra).right
          ((algebraPullbackMap g).app s.algebra)).hom ≫
        (TopCat.Presheaf.pushforward CommRingCat g.base).map p.2.right
declarations.comment: algebra component of the canonical map to the original functor

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctorBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** Formation of the relative-spectrum functor commutes with
arbitrary base change: the functor attached to `(S', g^*A)` is canonically the fibre product
`h_{S'} ×_{h_S} F` of the functor of points of `S'` and the functor attached to `(S, A)` over
the functor of points of `S`.

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctorBaseChangeIso_hom_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** The first component of the base-change isomorphism is the
structural map of `F'` to the functor of points of the new base.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeSpecFunctorBaseChangeIso_hom_fst :
    (relativeSpecFunctorBaseChangeIso s g).hom ≫
        pullback.fst (yoneda.map g) (relativeSpecFunctorToBase s) =
      relativeSpecFunctorToBase (s.baseChange g)
declarations.comment: first component of the canonical isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctorBaseChangeIso_hom_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LS.** The second component of the base-change isomorphism is the
canonical transformation `F' ⟶ F` induced by the base-change map of algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeSpecFunctorBaseChangeIso_hom_snd :
    (relativeSpecFunctorBaseChangeIso s g).hom ≫
        pullback.snd (yoneda.map g) (relativeSpecFunctorToBase s) =
      baseChangeToOriginal s g
declarations.comment: second component of the canonical isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.relativeSpecIsoSpecSections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01LT] at the level of schemes.** Over an affine base the relative spectrum
of a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras is the spectrum of the ring of global sections of the
algebra:

`Spec_S(A) ≅ Spec Γ(S, A)`.

`Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctor_representableBy` is the same tag in its
functor-of-points form; this is the identification with the glued relative spectrum
`Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.relativeSpec`.

It is an isomorphism of schemes; no compatibility with the structure morphism to `S` is
claimed.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def relativeSpecIsoSpecSections [IsAffine S] :
    relativeSpec A ≅ Spec (A.right.obj.obj (op (⊤ : S.Opens)))
declarations.comment: the scheme-level form: over an affine base the relative spectrum is the spectrum of the ring of global sections of the algebra

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctor_representableBy
declarations.doc:
If the base is affine, the functor of relative-spectrum pairs associated to a quasi-coherent
algebra is represented by the spectrum of the algebra's ring of global sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeSpecFunctor_representableBy (s : RelativeSpecSituation.{u}) [IsAffine s.base] :
    Nonempty ((relativeSpecFunctor s).RepresentableBy
      (Spec (s.algebra.right.obj.obj (.op (⊤ : s.base.Opens)))))

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecFunctor_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
The functor associated to a quasi-coherent algebra on a scheme is representable by a
scheme.
declarations.statement: theorem relativeSpecFunctor_isRepresentable : (relativeSpecFunctor s).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecRepresentableBy
declarations.doc:
The glued relative spectrum represents the relative spectrum functor, with universal element
the structure morphism together with the universal algebra map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeSpecRepresentableBy :
    (relativeSpecFunctor s).RepresentableBy (gluedSpectrum s).scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.gluedSpectrumIso_hom_toBase
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison between the glued relative spectrum and a scheme representing the
relative spectrum functor is a morphism over the base, where the representing scheme carries the
structure morphism of its universal element.

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.relativeSpecRepresentableBy
declarations.doc:
The glued relative spectrum represents the relative spectrum functor, with universal element
the structure morphism together with the universal algebra map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeSpecRepresentableBy :
    (relativeSpecFunctor s).RepresentableBy (gluedSpectrum s).scheme
declarations.comment: the relative spectrum with its universal algebra map

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.isAffineOpen_preimage_relativeSpecToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LX(1).** The preimage of an affine open of the base in the relative
spectrum is affine.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineOpen_preimage_relativeSpecToBase (U : S.affineOpens) :
    IsAffineOpen (relativeSpecToBase A ⁻¹ᵁ (U : S.Opens))

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.pushforwardAlgebraIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LX(3).** The isomorphism of sheaves of `𝒪_S`-algebras
`(relativeSpecToBase A)_* 𝒪 ≅ A`. Its inverse is the universal map
`A ⟶ (relativeSpecToBase A)_* 𝒪` of the relative spectrum, so this says that the universal map
is an isomorphism; it is also the essential surjectivity of the pushforward functor.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def pushforwardAlgebraIso : pushforwardAlgebra (relativeSpecToBase A) ≅ A

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.relativeSpecBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01LX part (2).** For a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_S`-algebras `A` and
an arbitrary morphism of schemes `g : T ⟶ S`, the fibre product
`\underline{Spec}_S(A) ×_S T` is the relative spectrum over `T` of the base change `g^*A`:
```
T ×_S \underline{Spec}_S(A) = \underline{Spec}_T(g^*A).
```
The base change `g^*A` is quasi-coherent by
`Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.isQuasicoherent_algebraPullback_obj`, which is what makes the
right-hand side meaningful.
declarations.comment: part (2): Spec_S(A) ×_S T = Spec_T(g^*A) for an arbitrary morphism g : T → S

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.AlgebraSheaf.isQuasicoherent_pushforwardAlgebra
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`, the sheaf of
`𝒪_S`-algebras `f_* 𝒪_X` is quasi-coherent.

This is Tag 01LC for the structure sheaf of `X`: the `𝒪_S`-module underlying `f_* 𝒪_X` is the
direct image of the unit module over `𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
instance AlgebraSheaf.isQuasicoherent_pushforwardAlgebra [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] :
    AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent (pushforwardAlgebra f)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.toRelativeSpec
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism `can : X ⟶ Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)` from the source of a quasi-compact,
quasi-separated morphism to the relative spectrum of the direct image of its structure sheaf. It
is the morphism classified by the identity map of `f_* 𝒪_X` under the representing bijection of
Tag 01LV.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toRelativeSpec : X ⟶ (gluedSpectrum (pushforwardSituation f)).scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.toRelativeSpec_toBase
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism to the relative spectrum of `f_* 𝒪_X` is a morphism of schemes over
`S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toRelativeSpec_toBase :
    toRelativeSpec f ≫ (gluedSpectrum (pushforwardSituation f)).toBase = f

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.ι_toRelativeSpec
declarations.doc:
Over an affine open `U` of the base, the canonical morphism to the relative spectrum of
`f_* 𝒪_X` restricts on `f⁻¹(U)` to the canonical morphism `f⁻¹(U) ⟶ Spec Γ(f⁻¹(U), 𝒪_X)`,
followed by the chart of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ι_toRelativeSpec (U : S.affineOpens) :
    (f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1).ι ≫ toRelativeSpec f =
      (f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1).toSpecΓ ≫ (gluedSpectrum (pushforwardSituation f)).chart U

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineSpace.affineNSpace
declarations.doc:
**Affine `n`-space over a scheme.** For a scheme `S` and an integer `n ≥ 0`, affine `n`-space
`𝐀ⁿ_S = Spec_S(𝒪_S[T_1, …, T_n])` over `S` is the relative spectrum of the quasi-coherent sheaf
of `𝒪_S`-algebras `𝒪_S[T_1, …, T_n]`, as a scheme over `S`. For `S = Spec R` this is affine
`n`-space `𝐀ⁿ_R` over `R`.

Here `𝒪_S[T_1, …, T_n]` is the sheaf associated to the presheaf `U ↦ 𝒪_S(U)[T_1, …, T_n]`,
whose sections over an affine open `U` are `𝒪_S(U)[T_1, …, T_n]`
(`Stacks.AffineSpace.bijective_toSheafify_app`), and the result is Mathlib's `𝔸(n; S)` over `S`
by `Stacks.AffineSpace.affineSpaceIso`.
declarations.statement: abbrev affineNSpace (n : ℕ) : Over S
declarations.comment: affine n-space over S, the relative spectrum of the polynomial algebra O_S[T_1, ..., T_n], as a scheme over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.vectorBundle
declarations.doc:
**The vector bundle `𝐕(ℰ) = Spec_S(Sym(ℰ))` associated to a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module
`ℰ`**: the relative spectrum of the symmetric algebra of `ℰ`.

Following EGA II, Definition 1.7.8, `ℰ` is not assumed finite locally free.
declarations.statement: def vectorBundle [E.IsQuasicoherent] : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjStandardOpenStatement.tag01M4
declarations.statement:
theorem tag01M4 (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] {f : A} {d : ℕ}
    (hfd : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (hd : 0 < d) :
    -- part (1)
    (∀ (g : A) (e : ℕ) (hge : g ∈ 𝒜 e) (he : 0 < e)
        (hfg : ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 g ≤ ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 f),
        -- (a) `f` is invertible in `A[1/g]`, and `f ^ deg g / g ^ deg f` is invertible in `A₍g₎`
        (IsUnit (algebraMap A (Localization.Away g) f) ∧
          IsUnit (Away.isLocalizationElem hge hfd)) ∧
        -- (b) a positive power of `g` is a homogeneous multiple of `f`
        (∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ ∃ a : A, SetLike.IsHomogeneousElem 𝒜 a ∧ g ^ k = a * f) ∧
        -- (c) the canonical, and only, `A`-algebra map `A[1/f] → A[1/g]`
        ((∀ x : A,
            ProjectiveSpectrum.localizedRingMap 𝒜 f g ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg
                (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f) x) = algebraMap A (Localization.Away g) x) ∧
          Subsingleton (Localization.Away f →ₐ[A] Localization.Away g)) ∧
        -- (d) the canonical `𝒜 0`-algebra map `A₍f₎ → A₍g₎`, compatible with the map of (c),
        -- and the only `𝒜 0`-algebra map compatible with it
        ((∀ x : Away 𝒜 f,
            (ProjectiveSpectrum.degreeZeroRingMap 𝒜 f g ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg x).val =
              ProjectiveSpectrum.localizedRingMap 𝒜 f g ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg x.val) ∧
          ∀ ψ : Away 𝒜 f →ₐ[𝒜 0] Away 𝒜 g,
            (∀ x : Away 𝒜 f, (ψ x).val =
              ProjectiveSpectrum.localizedRingMap 𝒜 f g ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg x.val) →
            ψ = ProjectiveSpectrum.degreeZeroRingMap 𝒜 f g ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg) ∧
        -- (e) that map exhibits `A₍g₎` as `A₍f₎` localized at `g ^ deg f / f ^ deg g`
        (letI : Algebra (Away 𝒜 f) (Away 𝒜 g) :=
          (ProjectiveSpectrum.degreeZeroRingMap 𝒜 f g
            ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).toRingHom.toAlgebra
         IsLocalization.Away
           (Away.mk 𝒜 hfd e (g ^ d) (by simpa [mul_comm] using SetLike.pow_mem_graded d hge))
           (Away 𝒜 g)) ∧
        -- (f) the commutative diagram of topological spaces, with horizontal arrows
        -- homeomorphisms and vertical arrows open immersions
        (letI := gradedRingTwistAway 𝒜 hfd
         letI := gradedRingTwistAway 𝒜 hge
         IsHomeomorph (gradedPrimeToBasicOpen 𝒜 hge he) ∧
           IsHomeomorph (gradedPrimesAwayToSpec 𝒜 hge) ∧
           IsHomeomorph (gradedPrimeToBasicOpen 𝒜 hfd hd) ∧
           IsHomeomorph (gradedPrimesAwayToSpec 𝒜 hfd) ∧
           Topology.IsOpenEmbedding (basicOpenInclusion 𝒜 hfg) ∧
           Topology.IsOpenEmbedding
             (gradedPrimesVertical 𝒜 hfd hge ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg) ∧
           Topology.IsOpenEmbedding (specDegreeZeroVertical 𝒜 f g d e hd he hfd hge hfg) ∧
           (∀ q : gradedPrimes (twistAway 𝒜 g e),
             basicOpenInclusion 𝒜 hfg (gradedPrimeToBasicOpen 𝒜 hge he q) =
               gradedPrimeToBasicOpen 𝒜 hfd hd
                 (gradedPrimesVertical 𝒜 hfd hge ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg q)) ∧
           (∀ q : gradedPrimes (twistAway 𝒜 g e),
             specDegreeZeroVertical 𝒜 f g d e hd he hfd hge hfg
                 (gradedPrimesAwayToSpec 𝒜 hge q) =
               gradedPrimesAwayToSpec 𝒜 hfd
                 (gradedPrimesVertical 𝒜 hfd hge ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg q))) ∧
        -- (g) and (h), for an arbitrary graded `A`-module `M`
        (∀ {M : Type w} {τ : Type t} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [SetLike τ M]
            [AddSubgroupClass τ M] (𝒨 : ℤ → τ) [DirectSum.Decomposition 𝒨]
            [SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒜 𝒨],
          -- (g) compatible maps `M_f → M_g` and `M₍f₎ → M₍g₎`, induced by the identity of `M`,
          -- each the only such map
          ((∀ m : M,
              (ProjectiveSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMaps 𝒜 𝒨 f g
                    ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).localizedMap
                  (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M m) =
                LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers g) M m) ∧
            (∀ x : GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization 𝒜 𝒨 f,
              (((ProjectiveSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMaps 𝒜 𝒨 f g
                      ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).degreeZeroMap x :
                    GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization 𝒜 𝒨 g) :
                  LocalizedModule.Away (R := A) g M) =
                (ProjectiveSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMaps 𝒜 𝒨 f g
                  ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).localizedMap x) ∧
            (∀ L :
                letI := Module.compHom (R := Localization.Away g) (S := Localization.Away f)
                  (LocalizedModule.Away (R := A) g M)
                  (ProjectiveSpectrum.localizedRingMap 𝒜 f g
                    ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).toRingHom
                LocalizedModule.Away (R := A) f M →ₗ[Localization.Away f]
                  LocalizedModule.Away (R := A) g M,
              (∀ m : M, L (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M m) =
                LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers g) M m) →
              L = (ProjectiveSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMaps 𝒜 𝒨 f g
                ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).localizedMap) ∧
            (∀ N :
                letI := Module.compHom (R := Localization.Away f)
                  (LocalizedModule.Away (R := A) f M)
                  (algebraMap (Away 𝒜 f) (Localization.Away f))
                letI := Module.compHom (R := Localization.Away g)
                  (LocalizedModule.Away (R := A) g M)
                  (algebraMap (Away 𝒜 g) (Localization.Away g))
                letI := Module.compHom (R := Away 𝒜 g)
                  (GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization 𝒜 𝒨 g)
                  (ProjectiveSpectrum.degreeZeroRingMap 𝒜 f g
                    ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).toRingHom
                GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization 𝒜 𝒨 f →ₗ[Away 𝒜 f]
                  GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization 𝒜 𝒨 g,
              (∀ x : GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization 𝒜 𝒨 f,
                (N x : LocalizedModule.Away (R := A) g M) =
                  (ProjectiveSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMaps 𝒜 𝒨 f g
                    ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).localizedMap x) →
              N = (ProjectiveSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMaps 𝒜 𝒨 f g
                ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).degreeZeroMap)) ∧
          -- (h) `M₍g₎` is `M₍f₎` localized at `g ^ deg f / f ^ deg g`
          (letI : Algebra (Away 𝒜 f) (Away 𝒜 g) :=
             (ProjectiveSpectrum.degreeZeroRingMap 𝒜 f g
               ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).toRingHom.toAlgebra
           letI := Module.compHom (R := Away 𝒜 g)
             (GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization 𝒜 𝒨 g)
             (ProjectiveSpectrum.degreeZeroRingMap 𝒜 f g
               ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).toRingHom
           IsLocalizedModule
             (Submonoid.powers
               (Away.mk 𝒜 hfd e (g ^ d) (by simpa [mul_comm] using SetLike.pow_mem_graded d hge)))
             (ProjectiveSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMaps 𝒜 𝒨 f g
               ⟨d, hd, hfd⟩ ⟨e, he, hge⟩ hfg).degreeZeroMap))) ∧
    -- part (2)
    (∀ {ι : Type s} (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens (ProjectiveSpectrum 𝒜)),
        ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 f ≤ ⨆ i, U i →
        ∃ (n : ℕ) (g : Fin n → A) (e : Fin n → ℕ),
          (∀ i, 0 < e i ∧ g i ∈ 𝒜 (e i)) ∧
          ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 f = ⨆ i, ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 (g i) ∧
          ∀ i, ∃ j, ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 (g i) ≤ U j) ∧
    -- part (3)
    (∀ {ι : Type s'} (g : ι → A) (e : ι → ℕ) (hg : ∀ i, g i ∈ 𝒜 (e i)) (_he : ∀ i, 0 < e i),
        AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f ≤ ⨆ i, AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (g i) ↔
          Ideal.span (Set.range fun i => Away.isLocalizationElem hfd (hg i)) = ⊤)
declarations.comment: the ten assertions of the tag in one statement: part (1)(a)-(h) for a standard open D+(g) contained in D+(f), part (2) the finite refinement of an open covering of D+(f) by standard opens, part (3) the unit-ideal criterion

declarations.name: ProjectiveSpectrum.IsStandardOpenCover
declarations.doc:
A finite family of positive-degree homogeneous elements `gᵢ` gives a standard open
covering of the projective standard open `D₊(f)` when their standard opens have union
exactly `D₊(f)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv_restrict
declarations.doc:
The standard-open identification `Γ(D₊(f), M̃) = M₍f₎` intertwines the restriction map of
`M̃` with the canonical degree-zero restriction map `M₍f₎ → M₍g₎`, for any two positive-degree
homogeneous elements with `D₊(g) ⊆ D₊(f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv_restrict (f g : S) {d e : ℕ}
    (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (hd : 0 < d) (hg : g ∈ 𝒜 e) (he : 0 < e)
    (hfg : ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 g ≤ ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 f)
    (s : (associatedModuleSheaf 𝒜 𝒨).val.obj (op (ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 f))) :
    associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv 𝒜 𝒨 hg he
        ((associatedModuleSheaf 𝒜 𝒨).val.map (homOfLE hfg).op s) =
      (ProjectiveSpectrum.moduleRestrictionMaps 𝒜 𝒨 f g
          ⟨d, hd, hf⟩ ⟨e, he, hg⟩ hfg).degreeZeroMap
        (associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv 𝒜 𝒨 hf hd s)
declarations.comment: part (3), the standard-open identification intertwines the restriction map of the associated sheaf with the degree-zero restriction map of Tag 01M4

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.coe_associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The standard-open identification `Γ(D₊(f), M̃) = M₍f₎` is linear for the action of
`Γ(P, D₊(f))` read through `AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.awayToSection`, the action on the target being
multiplication by the fraction inside `M_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coe_associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv_smul {f : S} {d : ℕ} (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d)
    (hd : 0 < d) (r : HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f)
    (s : (associatedModuleSheaf 𝒜 𝒨).val.obj (op (ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 f))) :
    ((associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv 𝒜 𝒨 hf hd
          ((ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f).hom r • s) :
        LocalizedModule.Away f M)) =
      HomogeneousLocalization.val r •
        ((associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv 𝒜 𝒨 hf hd s : LocalizedModule.Away f M))
declarations.comment: part (3), the scalar action in the standard-open identification, written out on the underlying elements of the localization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.associatedModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
The actual sheaf associated to a graded module. Its sections are locally homogeneous
fractions of degree zero, and its restrictions are restrictions of dependent functions.
declarations.comment: part (3), the sheaf associated to a graded module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical linear identification of sections on `D₊(f)` with `M_(f)`.
Its inverse is evaluation of a degree-zero fraction in every homogeneous-prime fiber.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleSheafStandardOpenEquiv {f : S} {d : ℕ}
    (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (hd : 0 < d) :
    (associatedModuleSheaf 𝒜 𝒨).val.obj (.op (ProjectiveSpectrum.basicOpen 𝒜 f))
      ≃ₗ[HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 f]
        GradedModuleDegreeZeroLocalization 𝒜 𝒨 f
declarations.comment: part (3), canonical linear identification on standard opens
