declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a scheme `X` the following are equivalent: `X` is a Jacobson space; `X` is locally
Jacobson in the sense of Definition 01OQ; the ring of sections over every affine open of `X` is
Jacobson; there is an affine open covering of `X` whose rings of sections are Jacobson; there is
an open covering of `X` by Jacobson open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      JacobsonSpace X,
      IsLocally (fun (R : Type u) [CommRing R] => IsJacobsonRing R) X,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, IsJacobsonRing Γ(X, (U : X.Opens)),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        IsOpenCover (fun i ↦ (U i : X.Opens)) ∧
          ∀ i, IsJacobsonRing Γ(X, (U i : X.Opens)),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        IsOpenCover U ∧ ∀ i, JacobsonSpace (U i).toScheme]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of the five conditions (1)–(5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_open
declarations.doc: Every open subscheme of a Jacobson scheme is Jacobson.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobsonSpace_open {X : Scheme.{u}} (hX : JacobsonSpace X) (U : X.Opens) :
    JacobsonSpace U.toScheme
declarations.comment: the final assertion: every open subscheme of a Jacobson scheme is Jacobson

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalizedModule_restriction_basicOpen_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
On a quasi-compact, quasi-separated open, restriction of sections of a quasi-coherent
module to a principal open is localization at the defining function.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalizedModule_restriction_basicOpen_of_qcqs {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules)
    [M.IsQuasicoherent] {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsCompact U.1) (hU' : IsQuasiSeparated U.1)
    (f : Γ(X, U)) :
    letI : Module Γ(X, U) Γ(M, X.basicOpen f) :=
      Module.compHom Γ(M, X.basicOpen f)
        (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le f)).op).hom
    IsLocalizedModule.Away f
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictionLinearMap M (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le f)))

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalization_basicOpen_of_qcqs
registrations.comment: the structure sheaf, for a quasi-compact quasi-separated open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_toSpecΓ_restrict_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01P8.** If `X` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
and its basic open defined by `f` is affine, then the canonical morphism to
`Spec Γ(X, ᵊ_X)` restricts to an isomorphism from that basic open onto the
standard open defined by `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_toSpecΓ_restrict_basicOpen (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (f : Γ(X, ⊤)) (hf : IsAffineOpen (X.basicOpen f)) :
    IsIso (X.toSpecΓ ∣_ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isQuasiAffine_iff_quasiCompact_and_isOpenImmersion_toSpecΓ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01P9.** A scheme `X` is quasi-affine if and only if the canonical morphism
`X ⟶ Spec Γ(X, ⊤)` is a quasi-compact open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffine_iff_quasiCompact_and_isOpenImmersion_toSpecΓ (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    X.IsQuasiAffine ↔ QuasiCompact X.toSpecΓ ∧ IsOpenImmersion X.toSpecΓ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tilde_isFiniteType_iff
declarations.doc:
An associated sheaf on `Spec R` is of finite type precisely when its module of global
sections is finite over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tilde_isFiniteType_iff {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    (tilde M).IsFiniteType ↔ Module.Finite R M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tilde_isFinitePresentation_iff
declarations.doc:
The quasi-coherent sheaf on `Spec R` associated to an `R`-module `M` is of finite
presentation if and only if `M` is a finitely presented module.
declarations.statement:
theorem tilde_isFinitePresentation_iff {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    (tilde M).IsFinitePresentation ↔ Module.FinitePresentation R M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_quasicoherent_restrict_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PE.** A quasi-coherent module on a quasi-compact open subscheme
extends to a quasi-coherent module on the ambient scheme: the pushforward along the open immersion
is quasi-coherent, and its restriction is isomorphic to the given module.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_quasicoherent_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PE.** A morphism from a quasi-coherent module on a quasi-compact
open subscheme to the restriction of a quasi-coherent module extends to a morphism of
quasi-coherent modules on the whole scheme.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_quasicoherent_extension
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (G : U.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] (φ : G ⟶ F.restrict j) :
    ∃ (H : X.Modules) (_ : H.IsQuasicoherent)
      (ψ : H ⟶ F) (e : H.restrict j ≅ G),
      e.hom ≫ φ = (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor j).map ψ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_quasicoherentSubobject_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PE.** A quasi-coherent submodule of the restriction of a
quasi-coherent module to a quasi-compact open subscheme extends to a quasi-coherent submodule
of the ambient module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasicoherentSubobject_restrict {U X : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (G : Subobject (F.restrict j)) (hG : (G : U.Modules).IsQuasicoherent) :
    ∃ H : Subobject F, (H : X.Modules).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      ∃ e : (H : X.Modules).restrict j ≅ (G : U.Modules),
        e.hom ≫ G.arrow = (restrictFunctor j).map H.arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag01PFAffineExtend.exists_isFiniteType_submodule_restrictTo_eq_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PF.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`U ⊆ X` be a quasi-compact open, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `G ⊆ F|_U` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_U`-submodule which is of finite type. Then there exists a quasi-coherent
submodule `G' ⊆ F` which is of finite type such that `G'|_U = G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteType_submodule_restrictTo_eq_of_qcqs
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (G : (F.restrict U.ι).Submodule)
    (hqc : (G.toSheafOfModules : U.toScheme.Modules).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hft : (G.toSheafOfModules : U.toScheme.Modules).IsFiniteType) :
    ∃ N : F.Submodule, (N.toSheafOfModules : X.Modules).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      (N.toSheafOfModules : X.Modules).IsFiniteType ∧ restrictTo U.ι N = G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_extension
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, `F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, `U` a
quasi-compact open and `G` a quasi-coherent subobject of `F|_U` of finite type. Then `G` extends to
a quasi-coherent subobject of `F` of finite type: there is a quasi-coherent subobject `G'` of `F`
of finite type and an isomorphism of `G'|_U` with `G` compatible with the inclusions into `F|_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_extension
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact U.1)
    (G : CategoryTheory.Subobject (F.restrict U.ι))
    [(G : U.toScheme.Modules).IsQuasicoherent]
    [(G : U.toScheme.Modules).IsFiniteType] :
    ∃ (G' : CategoryTheory.Subobject F), (G' : X.Modules).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      (G' : X.Modules).IsFiniteType ∧
      ∃ e : (G' : X.Modules).restrict U.ι ≅ (G : U.toScheme.Modules),
        (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).map G'.arrow = e.hom ≫ G.arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag01PGColimitClose.isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PG (colimit).** On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, a
quasi-coherent module is the colimit of the canonical diagram of all its quasi-coherent finite
type submodules.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PG.** On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, a quasi-coherent
module is the colimit of the canonical diagram of all its quasi-coherent finite type submodules.

This is the colimit half of the tag; the other half, that the diagram is filtered — so that the
colimit is a *directed* one — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_isFiltered`. Together the two are the tag's
assertion, so the tag is attached to both.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsColimit (finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_isFiltered
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PG.** The category of quasi-coherent finite type submodules of a
quasi-coherent module is filtered.

This is the directedness half of the tag; the other half, that the canonical cocone over this
diagram is a colimit cocone, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isColimit_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobjectCocone`. Together the two are the
tag's assertion that a quasi-coherent module is the directed colimit of its quasi-coherent
submodules of finite type, so the tag is attached to both.
declarations.statement:
instance finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_isFiltered {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsFiltered (FiniteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject F)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_isFiltered
registrations.comment: directedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFiniteType_idealSheafData_support_eq_compl
declarations.doc:
**A quasi-compact open of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is the complement of the
vanishing locus of a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteType_idealSheafData_support_eq_compl
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) :
    ∃ I : X.IdealSheafData, I.IsFiniteType ∧ (I.support : Set X) = (U : Set X)ᶜ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompact_iff_exists_finset_affineOpens
declarations.doc:
**An open of a scheme is quasi-compact exactly when it is a finite union of affine
opens.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompact_iff_exists_finset_affineOpens (U : X.Opens) :
    IsCompact (U : Set X) ↔ ∃ s : Finset X.affineOpens, U = s.sup fun V => (V : X.Opens)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompact_of_isFiniteType_idealSheafData
declarations.doc:
**An open subscheme of a quasi-compact scheme whose complement is the vanishing locus of a
finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals is quasi-compact.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompact_of_isFiniteType_idealSheafData [CompactSpace X] (U : X.Opens)
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (hI : I.IsFiniteType)
    (hsupp : (I.support : Set X) = (U : Set X)ᶜ) : IsCompact (U : Set X)

registrations.name: QuasiSeparatedSpace.isRetrocompact_iff_isCompact
registrations.comment: retrocompact iff quasi-compact

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompact_iff_finite_and_eq_biUnion_affineOpens
registrations.comment: quasi-compact iff finite union of affine opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finitePresentation_extension_of_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PI.**  Extension of a finitely presented module from a
quasi-compact open.  Let `X` be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme, `U` a quasi-compact
open, `F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and `φ : G ⟶ F|_U` a morphism from a finitely presented
`𝒪_U`-module.  Then `φ` is the restriction of a morphism `G' ⟶ F` from a finitely presented
`𝒪_X`-module `G'` restricting to `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_extension_of_hom [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact U.1)
    (G : U.toScheme.Modules) [G.IsFinitePresentation] (φ : G ⟶ F.restrict U.ι) :
    ∃ (G' : X.Modules) (_ : G'.IsFinitePresentation)
      (φ' : G' ⟶ F) (e : G'.restrict U.ι ≅ G),
      e.hom ≫ φ = (restrictFunctor U.ι).map φ'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_filtered_diagram_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme is a filtered colimit of
finitely presented modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_filtered_diagram_of_isFinitePresentation (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (inst : SmallCategory I),
      let _ := inst
      ∃ (_ : IsFiltered I) (D : CategoryTheory.Functor I X.Modules)
        (φ : NatTrans D ((Functor.const I).obj F)),
        (∀ i, (D.obj i).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
          Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk F φ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_directed_system_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme is a directed colimit of
finitely presented modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directed_system_of_isFinitePresentation (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
      (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (D : I ⥤ X.Modules)
      (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj F),
      (∀ i, (D.obj i).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
        Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk F φ))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.canonicalMapToSectionsData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PM (`canonical_map`).** The canonical map
`colim_n Hom_A(I ^ n, M) → Γ(Spec(A) \ V(I), M̃)`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def canonicalMapToSectionsData : CanonicalMapToSectionsData A I M

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.canonicalMapToSections
declarations.doc: The canonical map, with its local evaluation rule supplied by the construction.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def canonicalMapToSections :
    colimit (idealPowersHom A I M) ⟶ sectionsOnComplement A I M

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.canonicalMapToSections_restrict_ι
declarations.doc:
On every basic open `D(f)` with `f ∈ I`, a colimit representative `φ` has image
`φ(fⁿ)/fⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalMapToSections_restrict_ι (n : ℕ)
    (φ : (I ^ n : Ideal A) →ₗ[A] M) (f : A) (hf : f ∈ I) :
    restrictToBasicOpen A I M f hf
      (canonicalMapToSections A I M (colimit.ι (idealPowersHom A I M) n φ)) =
        basicOpenFraction A M f n (φ ⟨f ^ n, Ideal.pow_mem_pow hf n⟩)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.canonicalMapToSections_injective_of_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PM (`injective`).** The canonical map
`colim_n Hom_A(I ^ n, M) → Γ(Spec(A) \ V(I), M̃)` is injective when `I` is finitely generated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalMapToSections_injective_of_fg (hI : I.FG) :
    Function.Injective (canonicalMapToSections A I M)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.canonicalMapToSections_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Surjectivity in the torsion-free case.** If `I` is finitely generated and annihilates no
nonzero element of `M`, the canonical map `colim_n Hom_A(I ^ n, M) ⟶ Γ(Spec(A) \ V(I), M̃)` is
surjective.
declarations.comment: surjectivity when no nonzero element of M is annihilated by I

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.canonicalMapToSections_injective
declarations.doc:
For a finitely generated ideal `I` the canonical map
`colim_n Hom_A(I ^ n, M) → Γ(Spec(A) \ V(I), M̃)` is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalMapToSections_injective (hI : I.FG) :
    Function.Injective (canonicalMapToSections A I M)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.isIso_canonicalMapToSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PM (`torsionfree_isomorphism`).** Let `I` be a finitely generated
ideal of `A`. If no nonzero element of `M` is annihilated by all of `I`, then the canonical map
`colim_n Hom_A(I ^ n, M) → Γ(Spec(A) \ V(I), M̃)` is an isomorphism.

The hypothesis is the vanishing of `Submodule.torsionBySet A M I`, the submodule of elements
annihilated by every element of `I`; in the source it is used exactly to see that all of the
submodules `Mₙ` vanish, so that the general isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 01PM] reduces to the
canonical map itself.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.canonicalMapModuloAnnihilator_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PM (`general_isomorphism`).** For a finitely generated ideal `I`
the canonical map from the direct limit of `Hom_A(I ^ n, M / Mₙ)` to the sections of `M̃` on
`Spec(A) \ V(I)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public lemma canonicalMapModuloAnnihilator_bijective (hI : I.FG) :
    Function.Bijective (canonicalMapModuloAnnihilator A I M)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.idealPowersHomModuloAnnihilatorColimitIsoSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PM (`general_isomorphism`).** For a finitely generated ideal `I`,
the direct limit of `Hom_A(I ^ n, M / Mₙ)` is canonically isomorphic to the sections of `M̃`
on `Spec(A) \ V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def idealPowersHomModuloAnnihilatorColimitIsoSections (hI : I.FG) :
    colimit (idealPowersHomModuloAnnihilator A I M) ≅ sectionsOnComplement A I M

registrations.name: Submodule.torsionBySet
registrations.comment: i_power_annihilator_submodules

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PrincipalIdealCounterexample.fractionSection
declarations.doc: The fraction `y/x`, as a section of `𝒪` on the complement of `V(x)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fractionSection :
    sectionsOnComplement (counterexampleRing k) (principalIdeal k) (counterexampleRing k)
declarations.comment: first example: the section y/x on Spec(A) minus V(x), A = k[x,y,z_n]/(x^n z_n)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PrincipalIdealCounterexample.fractionSection_restrict
declarations.doc: On `D(x)`, which is all of the complement of `V(x)`, the section is the fraction `y/x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fractionSection_restrict :
    restrictToBasicOpen (counterexampleRing k) (principalIdeal k) (counterexampleRing k)
        (x k) (x_mem_principalIdeal k) (fractionSection k) =
      basicOpenFraction (counterexampleRing k) (counterexampleRing k) (x k) 1 (y k)
declarations.comment: first example: that section restricts on D(x) to the fraction y/x

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PrincipalIdealCounterexample.fractionSection_not_mem_range
declarations.doc: The fraction `y/x` is not obtained from a map out of any power of `(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fractionSection_not_mem_range :
    fractionSection k ∉ Set.range (canonicalMapToSections (counterexampleRing k)
      (principalIdeal k) (counterexampleRing k))
declarations.comment: first example: y/x is not in the range of the map from colim_n Hom_A((x)^n, A)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PrincipalIdealCounterexample.canonicalMapToSections_not_surjective
declarations.doc: The canonical map is not surjective for the principal ideal `(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSections_not_surjective :
    ¬ Function.Surjective (canonicalMapToSections (counterexampleRing k)
      (principalIdeal k) (counterexampleRing k))
declarations.comment: first example: the canonical map for I = (x) is not surjective

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PrincipalIdealCounterexample.canonicalMapToSections_not_isIso
declarations.doc: The canonical map is not an isomorphism for the principal ideal `(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSections_not_isIso :
    ¬ IsIso (canonicalMapToSections (counterexampleRing k)
      (principalIdeal k) (counterexampleRing k))
declarations.comment: first example: the canonical map for I = (x) is not an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TwoGeneratorCounterexample.gluedFractionSection
declarations.doc: The section on `D(f) ∪ D(g)` to which the fractions `x/f` and `y/g` glue.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gluedFractionSection :
    sectionsOnComplement (counterexampleRing k) (twoGeneratorIdeal k)
      (counterexampleRing k)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TwoGeneratorCounterexample.gluedFractionSection_f
declarations.doc: `f` times the glued section is `x`, i.e. the section restricts to `x/f` on `D(f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gluedFractionSection_f :
    f k • gluedFractionSection k =
      toComplement (counterexampleRing k) (twoGeneratorIdeal k)
        (counterexampleRing k) (x k)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TwoGeneratorCounterexample.gluedFractionSection_g
declarations.doc: `g` times the glued section is `y`, i.e. the section restricts to `y/g` on `D(g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gluedFractionSection_g :
    g k • gluedFractionSection k =
      toComplement (counterexampleRing k) (twoGeneratorIdeal k)
        (counterexampleRing k) (y k)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TwoGeneratorCounterexample.gluedFractionSection_not_mem_range
declarations.doc: The glued fraction section is not obtained from a map out of any power of `(f,g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gluedFractionSection_not_mem_range :
    gluedFractionSection k ∉ Set.range (canonicalMapToSections (counterexampleRing k)
      (twoGeneratorIdeal k) (counterexampleRing k))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TwoGeneratorCounterexample.canonicalMapToSections_not_isIso
declarations.doc: The canonical map is not an isomorphism for the ideal `(f,g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSections_not_isIso :
    ¬ IsIso (canonicalMapToSections (counterexampleRing k)
      (twoGeneratorIdeal k) (counterexampleRing k))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AnnihilatorQcoh.isAnnihilatorSubsheaf_sSup
declarations.doc:
**The subsheaf of [Stacks, Tag 01PO]: the largest submodule sheaf of `F` that `I`
annihilates, and its sections.** The supremum is taken in the complete lattice of submodule
sheaves of `F`, and the conclusion unfolds to the statement that a section over `U` belongs to
it exactly when every restriction of it is annihilated by the sections of `I` there.

That this supremum is the *only* submodule sheaf with those sections is
`IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf.unique`, and `isAnnihilatorSubsheaf_annihilatorSubmodule` exhibits a
second, explicit model of it. Neither quasi-coherence nor finiteness is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAnnihilatorSubsheaf_sSup
    (I : (SheafOfModules.unit.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).Submodule) (F : X.Modules) :
    IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf I F
      (sSup {N : F.Submodule | ∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : Γ(F, U)),
        s ∈ N.toSubmodule.obj (op U) →
          ∀ a : Γ(X, U), a ∈ I.toSubmodule.obj (op U) → a • s = 0})

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AnnihilatorQcoh.IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf.mem_iff_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01PO].** Over an affine open `U`, the sections of the annihilator
subsheaf are exactly the sections of `F` annihilated by `Γ(I, U)`; no restriction has to be
tested.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf.mem_iff_of_isAffineOpen {N : F.Submodule}
    (hN : IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf I F N) [I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent]
    {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (s : Γ(F, U)) :
    s ∈ N.toSubmodule.obj (op U) ↔
      ∀ a : Γ(X, U), a ∈ I.toSubmodule.obj (op U) → a • s = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AnnihilatorQcoh.IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf.isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 01PO].** The subsheaf of sections of a quasi-coherent module
annihilated by a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf of finite type is quasi-coherent.

Such a subsheaf exists for every `I` and `F` (`isAnnihilatorSubsheaf_annihilatorSubmodule`) and
is unique (`IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf.unique`), so the hypothesis `hN` is not a restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf.isQuasicoherent (hN : IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf I F N)
    [I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent] [I.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    N.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AnnihilatorQcoh.IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf.exists_stalk_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01PO].** A germ of `F` at `x` lies in the image of the stalk of
the annihilator subsheaf exactly when every section of `I` over a neighbourhood of `x`
annihilates every representative of that germ, to first order at `x`.

Quasi-coherence of `F` is not needed: the forward implication uses no hypothesis beyond the
sheaf axiom, and the backward one goes through the affine description of the sections of `N`,
which needs only `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf.exists_stalk_eq_iff (hN : IsAnnihilatorSubsheaf I F N)
    [I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent] [I.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    (x : X) (s : F.presheaf.stalk x) :
    (∃ t : (Scheme.Modules.presheaf N.toSheafOfModules).stalk x,
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab.{u} x).map
          (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf N.ι) t = s) ↔
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (t : Γ(F, U)), F.presheaf.germ U x hx t = s →
        ∀ r : Γ(X, U), r ∈ I.toSubmodule.obj (op U) →
          F.presheaf.germ U x hx (r • t) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.isQuasicoherent_idealAnnihilator
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01PO] (1).** For a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `I` of finite type on a
scheme and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the subsheaf of sections annihilated by `I` is
quasi-coherent.

Assertion (2) of the tag is `mem_idealAnnihilator_affineOpen` below.  Assertion (3), the
description of the stalks, is not proved, so this is a clause tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_idealAnnihilator (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (hFG : ∀ U : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal U).FG) :
    (idealPowerAnnihilator I.unitSubmodule F 1).toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.mem_idealAnnihilator_affineOpen
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01PO] (2).** On an affine open `U` the subsheaf of sections annihilated by `I`
consists of the sections of `F` over `U` annihilated by `I(U)`.

No finiteness hypothesis is needed for this half: it is
`mem_idealPowerAnnihilator_affineOpen` at `n = 1`, and `idealPower_unitSubmodule_one` identifies
the ideal sheaf being annihilated with `I` rather than its first power.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_idealAnnihilator_affineOpen (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules)
    (V : X.affineOpens) (s : Γ(F, V.1)) :
    s ∈ (idealPowerAnnihilator I.unitSubmodule F 1).toSubmodule.obj (op V.1) ↔
      ∀ a ∈ (I.ideal V : Ideal Γ(X, V.1)), a • s = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_annihilatorSubsheaf_iff
declarations.doc:
Membership in the annihilator subsheaf means that, on every smaller open,
every section of the ideal annihilates the restricted section.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_annihilatorSubsheaf_iff [Mono i] (U : X.Opens) (s : Γ(F, U)) :
    s ∈ (annihilatorSubsheaf I F i).toSubmodule.obj (op U) ↔
      ∀ (V : X.Opens) (f : V ⟶ U) (r : Γ(I, V)),
        (show Γ(X, V) from i.app V r) • F.presheaf.map f.op s = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_annihilatorSubsheaf_iff_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 01PO (2).** On an affine open it suffices to test annihilation by the sections
of the ideal over that open itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_annihilatorSubsheaf_iff_of_isAffine [I.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.affineOpens)
    (s : Γ(F, U.1)) :
    s ∈ (annihilatorSubsheaf I F i).toSubmodule.obj (op U.1) ↔
      ∀ r : Γ(I, U.1), (show Γ(X, U.1) from i.app U.1 r) • s = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.annihilatorSubsheaf_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 01PO (1).** The subsheaf of sections annihilated by a quasi-coherent ideal
sheaf of finite type is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem annihilatorSubsheaf_isQuasicoherent [I.IsQuasicoherent] [I.IsFiniteType]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (annihilatorSubsheaf I F i).toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_range_stalk_annihilatorSubsheaf_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 01PO (3).** The germs of the annihilator subsheaf at a point are exactly the
germs of `F` annihilated by the stalk of the ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_range_stalk_annihilatorSubsheaf_iff [I.IsQuasicoherent] [I.IsFiniteType]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (x : X) (s : F.presheaf.stalk x) :
    (∃ t : (Scheme.Modules.presheaf (annihilatorSubsheaf I F i).toSheafOfModules).stalk x,
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab x).map
        (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf (annihilatorSubsheaf I F i).ι)).hom t = s) ↔
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (t : Γ(F, U)), F.presheaf.germ U x hx t = s →
        ∀ r : Γ(I, U), F.presheaf.germ U x hx ((show Γ(X, U) from i.app U r) • t) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.annihilatorSubsheaf
declarations.doc:
The subsheaf of `F` whose sections are annihilated by the ideal sheaf `I`: the largest
submodule all of whose sections are killed by the sections of `I` over the same open.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def annihilatorSubsheaf [Mono i] : F.Submodule
declarations.comment: the subsheaf of sections annihilated by I

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSections
declarations.doc: The canonical map `colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F) ⟶ Γ(X \ V(I), F)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalMapToSections (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) :
    Limits.colimit (idealPowHomSystem I F) ⟶ Γ(F, (I.support.compl : X.Opens))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSections_injective
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact scheme `X`, a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `I` of finite type and a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the canonical map `colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F) → Γ(X \ V(I), F)`
is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSections_injective [CompactSpace X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hFT : ∀ V : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal V).FG) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Function.Injective (canonicalMapToSections I F)
declarations.comment: injective: the FIRST display colim Hom(Iⁿ, F) → Γ(U, F) is injective; X quasi-compact, I quasi-coherent of finite type, F quasi-coherent. The second display is canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_bijective

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F/F_n) ⟶ Γ(X \ V(I), F)`, where `F_n` is the
subsheaf of sections annihilated by `Iⁿ`, sending the class of `φ` to the section of `F`
corresponding to `φ(1)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient :
    Limits.colimit (idealPowHomQuotientSystem I F) ⟶ Γ(F, (I.support.compl : X.Opens))
declarations.comment: canonical map of the second display, colim Hom(Iⁿ, F/F_n) → Γ(U, F)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_injective
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact scheme `X`, a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `I` of finite type and a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the canonical map
`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F/F_n) → Γ(X \ V(I), F)` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_injective [CompactSpace X] :
    Function.Injective (canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient I F hFG)
declarations.comment:
second display colim Hom(Iⁿ, F/F_n) → Γ(U, F) is injective; X quasi-compact,
I of finite type; surjectivity is canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_surjective

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PQ, second display, surjectivity.** For a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme `X`, a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `I` of finite type and a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the canonical map
`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F/F_n) → Γ(X ∖ V(I), F)` is surjective.

Quasi-separatedness of `X` is used exactly here, as in the source: it is what makes the pairwise
intersections of a finite affine covering again finitely covered by affine opens, hence what
bounds the exponent needed for the local morphisms to agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_surjective [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hFG : ∀ V : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal V).FG) :
    Function.Surjective (canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient I F hFG)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PQ, clause (c).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme, let `I ⊂ 𝒪_X` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type, let `Z = V(I)` and
`U = X ∖ Z`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `F_n ⊂ F` be the subsheaf of
sections annihilated by `Iⁿ`.  Then the canonical map

`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F/F_n) ⟶ Γ(U, F)`

is an isomorphism.

Injectivity is `canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_injective` and needs only quasi-compactness;
surjectivity is `canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_surjective` and is where quasi-separatedness
enters.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_bijective [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hFG : ∀ V : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal V).FG) :
    Function.Bijective (canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient I F hFG)
declarations.comment:
clause (c): the second display colim Hom(Iⁿ, F/F_n) → Γ(U, F) is an isomorphism;
X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, I quasi-coherent of finite type, F quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.isIso_canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PQ, clause (c), categorically.** The canonical map
`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F/F_n) ⟶ Γ(X ∖ V(I), F)` is an isomorphism of abelian groups, for `X`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `I` quasi-coherent of finite type and `F` quasi-coherent.

This is `canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_bijective` read in `AddCommGrpCat`, where a bijective
morphism is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hFG : ∀ V : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal V).FG) :
    IsIso (canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient I F hFG)
declarations.comment:
clause (c): the second display colim Hom(Iⁿ, F/F_n) → Γ(U, F) is an isomorphism in
AddCommGrpCat; X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, I quasi-coherent of finite type,
F quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSections_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PQ (`surjective`), the case `F_N = 0`.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact
scheme, let `I` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type and let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module with **no `I`-power torsion**, that is, with
`F_N = 0` for every `N`.  Then the canonical map
`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F) → Γ(X \ V(I), F)` is surjective.

Together with `canonicalMapToSections_injective` this is the second assertion of Tag 01PQ in the
case `F_N = 0`, where `F/F_N = F`; the general assertion, which needs the quotient sheaves
`F/F_N`, is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSectionsQuotient_bijective` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Coherent/HomColimit/QuotientSurjectivity.lean`.  Note that
quasi-separatedness of `X` is not needed for the torsion-free case proved here: the source
glues the local morphisms over a finite cover of the pairwise intersections, whereas here the
local sections to be glued are *unique*, by the absence of torsion, so no comparison over the
intersections is required.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSections_surjective [CompactSpace X] (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hFT : ∀ V : X.affineOpens, (I.ideal V).FG) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hTF : NoIdealTorsion I F) :
    Function.Surjective (canonicalMapToSections I F)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.canonicalMapToSections_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PQ (injectivity).** The canonical map from the colimit of
homomorphisms out of the powers of a finite-type ideal sheaf on a quasi-compact scheme to the
sections of a quasi-coherent module on the complement of the support is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalMapToSections_injective {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [((idealPowerMultiple I 1 (unitModule X)).toModules).IsFiniteType] :
    Function.Injective (canonicalMapToSections I F).1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.idealPowerAnnihilator
declarations.doc:
The subsheaf of `F` whose local sections are annihilated by the `n`-th power of the
ideal subsheaf `I`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def idealPowerAnnihilator
    (I : (SheafOfModules.unit.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).Submodule) (F : X.Modules) (n : ℕ) :
    F.Submodule

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple
declarations.doc:
An invertible sheaf of modules on a scheme is *ample* if the scheme is quasi-compact and
every point has an affine nonvanishing locus for some global section of a tensor power of
positive exponent.
declarations.statement: public def IsAmple : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.AmplePositivePower.isAmple_iff_isAmple_tensorPowModule
declarations.doc:
An invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` is ample if and only if its tensor power `L ^⊗ d` is ample,
for any `d ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_iff_isAmple_tensorPowModule (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    IsAmple X L ↔ IsAmple X (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAmple_iff_tensorPower_isAmple
declarations.doc:
An invertible sheaf is ample if and only if any of its positive tensor
powers is ample.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_iff_tensorPower_isAmple (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L ↔
    Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X
        (Invertible.tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isAmple_pullback_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PU.** The restriction of an ample invertible sheaf of modules to a
closed subscheme is ample. The closed immersion is affine, and its source is quasi-compact
because its target is.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAmple_pullback_of_isClosedImmersion [IsClosedImmersion f] (h : IsAmple Y L) :
    IsAmple X ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isAffineOpen_inf_nonvanishingOpen
declarations.doc:
For an invertible module `L` on a scheme `X` and a global section `s` of `L`, every affine
open `U ⊆ X` meets the nonvanishing locus `X_s` in an affine open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineOpen_inf_nonvanishingOpen {X : Scheme.{u}} (L : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L]
    (s : L.sections) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    IsAffineOpen (U ⊓ nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toRingedSpace) L s)

declarations.name: Stacks.NonvanishingAffineIntersection.isAffineOpen_inf_nonvanishingOpen
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme, `M` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `s` a global section of `M`. For every
affine open `U` of `X`, the intersection `U ∩ X_s` of `U` with the nonvanishing locus of `s` is
affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineOpen_inf_nonvanishingOpen {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    IsAffineOpen (U ⊓ Stacks.NonvanishingOpen.nonvanishingOpen X M s)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionLocalizationMap_injective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01PW] part (1).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact scheme, let `L` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module, let `s` be a global section of `L` and let `ℱ` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module.
The comparison map of Tag 0B5L
`(⨁_n Γ(X, ℱ ⊗ L^{⊗ n}))_{(s)} ⟶ Γ(X_s, ℱ|_{X_s})` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionLocalizationMap_injective [CompactSpace X] [F.IsQuasicoherent] (s : L.sections) :
    Function.Injective (sectionLocalizationMap X L F s)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sectionLocalizationMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01PW] part (2).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, let `s` be a global section of `L` and let `ℱ` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module. The comparison map of Tag 0B5L
`(⨁_n Γ(X, ℱ ⊗ L^{⊗ n}))_{(s)} ⟶ Γ(X_s, ℱ|_{X_s})` is bijective.

Both chart-local steps of the source's proof are theorems here, so the statement asks only for
the quasi-coherence of `ℱ` and the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `X`:
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasTwistedChartExtension` is Tag 01P7 on an affine chart trivializing
`L`, and `Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasTwistedCompactAnnihilation` is part (1) over a quasi-compact
open.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionLocalizationMap_bijective [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (s : L.sections) :
    Function.Bijective (sectionLocalizationMap X L F s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isBasis_affine_nonvanishingOpens
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PX.** If the nonvanishing opens of global sections of the positive
tensor powers of an invertible sheaf form a basis of the topology, then the affine ones among
them already form a basis.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBasis_affine_nonvanishingOpens
    (hBasis : Opens.IsBasis
      {U : X.Opens | ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧
        ∃ s : (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)).sections,
          U = nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)
            (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
              (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)) s}) :
    Opens.IsBasis
      {U : X.Opens | (∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧
        ∃ s : (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)).sections,
          U = nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)
            (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
              (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)) s) ∧
          IsAffineOpen U}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isSeparated_of_affine_nonvanishingOpen_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01PY.** A scheme carrying an invertible sheaf of modules such that
every point lies in an *affine* nonvanishing open of a global section of some positive tensor
power is separated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSeparated_of_affine_nonvanishingOpen_cover
    (h : ∀ x : X, ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧
      ∃ s : (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)).sections,
        x ∈ nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)
          (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
            (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)) s ∧
        IsAffineOpen (nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)
          (tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
            (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)) s)) :
    Scheme.IsSeparated X

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleNonvanishing.isSeparated_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**A scheme carrying an ample invertible module is separated**, at the predicate
`Stacks.Ample.IsAmple`. This is [Stacks, Tag 01PY], available as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple.isSeparated` for the other of the two ampleness
predicates of [Stacks, Tag 01PS], transported along the hypothesis-free
`Stacks.AmpleBridge.isAmple_iff_isAmple`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isAmple (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : IsAmple X L) : Scheme.IsSeparated X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_exists_affine_nonvanishingOpen
declarations.doc:
A scheme is separated as soon as every point lies in an affine nonvanishing open of a global
section of some positive tensor power of an invertible sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_exists_affine_nonvanishingOpen
    (h : ∀ x : X, ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧
      ∃ s : (Invertible.tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)).sections,
        x ∈ nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toRingedSpace)
            (Invertible.tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
              (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)) s ∧
          IsAffineOpen (nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toRingedSpace)
            (Invertible.tensorPower X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
              (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L (n : ℤ)) s)) :
    Scheme.IsSeparated X

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHom
declarations.doc:
**The canonical morphism `⋃ X_a ⟶ Proj Γ_*(X, L)` of Stacks Tag 01PZ.** It is glued from the
charts `Stacks.SectionRingChartMap.chartHom` over the cover of `⋃ X_a` by the nonvanishing opens
of the homogeneous elements of positive degree; the overlap condition is
`Stacks.SectionRingChartOpen.chartHomOn_eq`, which says that the chart at `a` and the chart at `b`
agree on `X_a ∩ X_b`.

For `L` ample the source is all of `X` (`Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHomOfIsAmple`); in
general `⋃ X_a` is the largest open on which the construction makes sense, and that is where the
Stacks project's statement puts it as well.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def projHom : (nvUnion L).toScheme ⟶ Proj (grading L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.homOfLE_projHom
declarations.doc:
**On `X_a` the canonical morphism is the chart at `a`.** This is the second half of the
characterisation of the morphism of Stacks Tag 01PZ, not one of the tag's numbered clauses. For
`a` homogeneous of positive degree, the restriction of the canonical morphism to `X_a` is the
morphism `X_a ⟶ Proj Γ_*(X, L)` determined by the degree-zero part of the localization of
`Γ_*(X, L)` at `a`, namely `Stacks.SectionRingChartMap.chartHom`.
declarations.comment: the restriction to a nonvanishing open is the chart

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHom_preimage_projBasicOpen
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks Tag 01PZ: the preimage of a basic open.** For every homogeneous element
`a` of `Γ_*(X, L)` of positive degree, the canonical morphism pulls the chart `D₊(a)` of
`Proj Γ_*(X, L)` back to the nonvanishing open `X_a`.

The identity is checked on the cover: on the piece `X_b` the composite is the chart at `b`, and
`Stacks.SectionRingChartOpen.chartHomOn_preimage_projBasicOpen` computes its preimage of `D₊(a)`
as `X_b ∩ X_a`, which is also what the right-hand side restricts to.
declarations.comment: the preimage of a basic open

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.image_projHom_preimage_projBasicOpen
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks Tag 01PZ, read as an open of `X`.** The image in `X` of the preimage of
`D₊(a)` is the nonvanishing open `X_a` itself, which is the shape the Stacks project's statement
takes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem image_projHom_preimage_projBasicOpen {d : ℕ} (a : powSections L d) (hd : 0 < d) :
    (nvUnion L).ι ''ᵁ
        (projHom L ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen (grading L) (DirectSum.of (powSections L) d a))
      = nvOpen L a
declarations.comment: the preimage of a basic open, as an open of X

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.Theta.homOfLE_projHom_eq_glued
declarations.doc:
**The canonical morphism `Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHom` is the morphism `r_{L, ψ}` of
[Stacks, Tag 01NK] at `ψ` the identity map of `Γ_*(X, L)`**, with no hypothesis on `L`: the two
morphisms have the same source `U(ψ) = ⋃_a X_a`
(`Stacks.SectionRingGluedComparison.coveringOpen_canonicalSections`) and agree there.
declarations.statement:
theorem homOfLE_projHom_eq_glued :
    X.homOfLE (coveringOpen_canonicalSections L).le
        ≫ Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHom L
      = (canonicalSections L).glued
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism is the morphism r_{L,psi} of Tag 01NK at psi the identity map of the section ring, with no hypothesis on L; this is what the clauses below are clauses about

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.Theta.glued_preimage_projBasicOpen
declarations.doc:
`f^{-1}(D₊(s)) = X_s` for every homogeneous `s ∈ S_+`, where `f` is `r_{L, ψ}` at `ψ` the
identity map of `S = Γ_*(X, L)`. Both sides are opens of the source `U(ψ) = ⋃_a X_a` of `f`, the
right-hand side being `X_s`, which lies inside it.
declarations.statement:
theorem glued_preimage_projBasicOpen {d : ℕ} (a : powSections L d) (hd : 0 < d) :
    (canonicalSections L).glued ⁻¹ᵁ
        AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpen (grading L) (DirectSum.of (powSections L) d a)
      = (canonicalSections L).coveringOpen.ι ⁻¹ᵁ nvOpen L a
declarations.comment: clause (1): f^{-1}(D_+(s)) = X_s for every homogeneous s in S_+, for the morphism f = r_{L,psi} that clauses (2), (3) and (4) are stated at, as opens of its source U(psi)

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.Theta.projTheta
declarations.doc:
**The `𝒪_X`-module maps `f^*𝒪_Y(n) ⟶ L^{⊗ n}`, compatible with the multiplication maps of
Constructions, Equation 01MO.** All degrees at once, as a homomorphism of sheaves of `ℤ`-graded
`𝒪_X`-algebras `f^*(⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_Y(n)) ⟶ ⨁_{n ∈ ℤ} L^{⊗ n}`: its component in degree `n` is the map
`f^*𝒪_Y(n) ⟶ L^{⊗ n}`, and its `map_mul` field is exactly the compatibility, the multiplication
maps of the two graded algebras being those of Equation 01MO on the source and the tensor product
of sections on the target. It is `θ` of [Stacks, Tag 01NK] at `ψ` the identity map of `Γ_*(X, L)`,
taken along `f = r_{L, ψ}`.
declarations.statement:
def projTheta : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.Hom
    (Stacks.Conormal.gradedPullback (canonicalSections L).glued
      (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjConeTwist.integerTwistAlgebra (grading L)))
    (laurentRestrict (grading L) (canonicalSections L))
declarations.comment: clause (2): the O_X-module maps f^*O_Y(n) -> L^{tensor n} for all n in Z, as a homomorphism of sheaves of Z-graded algebras, whose map_mul is their compatibility with the multiplication maps of Constructions Equation 01MO

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.Theta.projTheta_app_top_degreeSection
declarations.doc:
**The composite `S_d ⟶ Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y(d)) ⟶ Γ(X, L^{⊗ d})` is the identity map.** For a homogeneous
element `z` of `S = Γ_*(X, L)` of degree `d`, the first map sends `z` to the global section of
`𝒪_Y(d)` attached to it by [Stacks, Tag 01MP], the second pulls that back along `f` and applies the
degree-`d` component of `projTheta`, and the result is `z` itself: the global section of `L^{⊗ d}`
that the degree-`d` component `z d` of `z` names.

Both sides are sections of `L^{⊗ d}` over `⋃_a X_a`, where `f` is defined, with `L^{⊗ d}` read in
the family `Stacks.AmpleProjectiveImmersion.tensorPowerModule` and compared with the iterated
tensor power by `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentMulSections.powCompare`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projTheta_app_top_degreeSection (d : ℕ) {z : sectionRing L} (hz : z ∈ grading L d) :
    ((projTheta L).app (d : ℤ)).val.app (op ⊤)
        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackSection (canonicalSections L).glued
          (twistM (grading L) (d : ℤ)) ⊤ ⊤ (fun _ _ => trivial)
          (degreeSection (grading L) d ⟨z, hz⟩))
      = resTop (tensorPowerModule X L (d : ℤ))
          ((powCompare L d).hom.app ⊤ (globalSection X (natTensorPow L d) (z d)))
          ((canonicalSections L).coveringOpen.ι ''ᵁ ⊤)
declarations.comment: clause (3): the composite S_d -> Gamma(Y, O_Y(d)) -> Gamma(X, L^{tensor d}) is the identity map, read on the open where the canonical morphism is defined

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.Theta.exists_isIso_pullback_projTheta_app_intMul
declarations.doc:
Every point of `⋃_a X_a` has an integer `d ≥ 1` and an open neighbourhood `U` on which
`f^*𝒪_Y(d n)|_U ⟶ L^{⊗ d n}|_U` is an isomorphism **for all `n ∈ ℤ`**.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIso_pullback_projTheta_app_intMul {x : X}
    (hx : x ∈ (canonicalSections L).coveringOpen) :
    ∃ (e : ℕ) (_ : 0 < e) (V : X.Opens) (_ : x ∈ V) (hVU : V ≤ (canonicalSections L).coveringOpen),
      ∀ n : ℤ,
        IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hVU)).map
          ((projTheta L).app ((e : ℤ) * n)))
declarations.comment: clause (4): every point of the open where the canonical morphism is defined has an integer d >= 1 and an open neighbourhood U of it on which f^*O_Y(dn) -> L^{tensor dn} is an isomorphism for all n in Z, positive, zero and negative; d is the degree of a homogeneous element of the section ring not vanishing at the point and U is the nonvanishing open of that element

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjQuasiCompact.quasiCompact_projHomOfCovers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01Q0, the quasi-compactness.** Under clause (a) of Stacks Tag 01PZ — the `X_s`
cover `X` — and `X` quasi-compact, the canonical morphism `f : X ⟶ Proj Γ_*(X, L)` of Stacks Tag
01PZ is quasi-compact.

`Proj` of any graded ring is quasi-separated
(`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjQuasiSeparated.quasiSeparatedSpace_proj`), so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_compactSpace`, which is Stacks Tag 01KO.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiCompact_projHomOfCovers [CompactSpace X]
    (hcov : Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.nvUnion L = ⊤) :
    QuasiCompact (Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHomOfCovers L hcov)
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism of 01PZ is quasi-compact, under (a) the X_s cover X and (b) X quasi-compact

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjQuasiCompact.denseRange_projHomOfCovers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01Q0, the dense image.** Under clause (a) of Stacks Tag 01PZ — the `X_s` cover
`X` — and `X` quasi-compact, the canonical morphism `f : X ⟶ Proj Γ_*(X, L)` of Stacks Tag 01PZ
has dense image.

A nonempty open of `Proj Γ_*(X, L)` missing the image would contain a nonempty `D₊(a)` with `a`
homogeneous of positive degree, whose preimage `X_a` would then be empty; but then `a` is
nilpotent and `D₊(a) = ∅`.
declarations.statement:
theorem denseRange_projHomOfCovers [CompactSpace X]
    (hcov : Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.nvUnion L = ⊤) :
    DenseRange (Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHomOfCovers L hcov).base
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism of 01PZ has dense image, under (a) the X_s cover X and (b) X quasi-compact

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjImmersion.isOpenImmersion_projHomOfIsAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01Q1, the open immersion.** For `L` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module, the
canonical morphism `X ⟶ Proj Γ_*(X, L)` of Stacks Tag 01PZ is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_projHomOfIsAmple (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    IsOpenImmersion (Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHomOfIsAmple L hL)

declarations.name: Stacks.SectionRingProjImmersion.denseRange_projHomOfIsAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01Q1, the dense image.** For `L` an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module, the canonical
morphism `X ⟶ Proj Γ_*(X, L)` of Stacks Tag 01PZ has dense image.

This is Stacks Tag 01Q0 (`Stacks.SectionRingProjQuasiCompact.denseRange_projHomOfCovers`), which
the source cites here: ampleness gives both of that tag's hypotheses, that the `X_s` cover `X`
(`Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.nvUnion_eq_top_of_isAmple`) and that `X` is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem denseRange_projHomOfIsAmple (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    DenseRange (Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHomOfIsAmple L hL).base

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjAmpleTwist.exists_isAmple_pullback_twistingSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01Q2.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact scheme and `S` a graded ring, and
assume there is an open immersion `j : X ⟶ Proj(S)`. Then `j^* 𝒪(d)` is an invertible ample
`𝒪_X`-module for some `d > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_pullback_twistingSheaf {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    (j : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Proj 𝒮) [IsOpenImmersion j] :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ ∃ h : IsInvertibleModule X
        ((modulePullback j.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (twistingSheaf 𝒮 (d : ℤ))),
      @IsAmple X ((modulePullback j.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (twistingSheaf 𝒮 (d : ℤ))) h

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.exists_nvUnion_eq_top_and_isOpenImmersion_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3]** — the clause labelled 01Q5: for `L` ample the open sets
`X_s`, with `s ∈ S₊` homogeneous, cover `X`, and the associated morphism `X ⟶ Proj S` is an open
immersion.

The covering is `Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.nvUnion_eq_top_of_isAmple`; it is also what makes
the morphism `Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHomOfCovers` of Stacks Tag 01PZ exist at all. The
open immersion is Stacks Tag 01Q1,
`Stacks.SectionRingProjImmersion.isOpenImmersion_projHomOfIsAmple`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nvUnion_eq_top_and_isOpenImmersion_of_isAmple (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    ∃ h : Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.nvUnion L = ⊤,
      IsOpenImmersion (Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHomOfCovers L h)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_isOpenImmersion_projHomOfCovers
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (1).** If the opens `X_s` cover the
quasi-compact scheme `X` and the resulting morphism `j : X ⟶ Proj Γ_*(X, L)` is an open immersion,
then `L` is ample.

This is the source's implication `(2) ⇒ (4) ⇒ (1)` in one step: the basic opens `D₊(a)` of the
homogeneous elements of positive degree are a basis of `Proj S` and are affine, so every point of
`X` has one of them around its image inside the (open) range of `j`; its preimage is `X_a`, is
affine because `j` is an open immersion, and contains the point. That is clause (1) of Stacks
Tag 01PS verbatim.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_of_isOpenImmersion_projHomOfCovers [CompactSpace X]
    (h : Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.nvUnion L = ⊤)
    (hj : IsOpenImmersion (Stacks.SectionRingProjMorphism.projHomOfCovers L h)) :
    IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_isBasisNonvanishing_and_isBasisAffineNonvanishing
declarations.doc:
**Clauses (3) and (4) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] imply clause (1)** — the converse of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.exists_sections_mem_nonvanishingOpen_le_of_isAmple`, which is the
implication `(1) ⇒ (3) ∧ (4)`.

Either clause alone suffices on a quasi-compact scheme: clause (4) applied at the ambient open `⊤`
is condition (2) of Stacks Tag 01PS, and clause (3) yields clause (4) by Stacks Tag 01PX, which is
unconditional here because Tag 01PV is proved. Both are stated so that the conjunction the forward
implication produces can be fed back verbatim.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_of_isBasisNonvanishing_and_isBasisAffineNonvanishing [CompactSpace X]
    (h : Stacks.AmpleTheory.IsBasisNonvanishing X L ∧
      Stacks.AmpleTheory.IsBasisAffineNonvanishing X L) :
    IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_isBasisNonvanishing
declarations.doc:
**Clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (1)**, from clause (3) alone: on a
quasi-compact scheme, an invertible `L` whose nonvanishing opens `X_s` — for `s` a global section
of a positive tensor power of `L` — form a basis for the topology is ample.

This is the implication the conjunction above does not give, since that one consumes only its
clause (4) conjunct. Stacks Tag 01PX supplies the step clause (3) ⇒ clause (4): the affine opens
are themselves a basis, so the prescribed open may be shrunk to an affine one before clause (3) is
applied, and the resulting `X_s`, sitting inside an affine open, is affine by Stacks Tag 01PV.
Clause (4) at the ambient open `⊤` is then condition (2) of Stacks Tag 01PS.

The implication was already proved, as the `mpr` of
`Stacks.SectionExtension.isAmple_iff_compactSpace_and_isBasisNonvanishing`, and that is what is
invoked here rather than a second derivation; what this declaration adds is the standalone
statement of the clause, and its registration, beside the other clauses of the tag. Tag 01PX is
likewise already proved and registered — as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isBasis_affine_nonvanishingOpens`, in the Tag 01PS vocabulary —
and in the vocabulary these clauses are stated in it is
`Stacks.NonvanishingAffineIntersection.isBasisAffineNonvanishing_of_isBasisNonvanishing`, which
carries no hypothesis beyond invertibility because Tag 01PV is proved
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isAffineOpen_inf_nonvanishingOpen`).

The hypotheses are exactly clause (3) and the quasi-compactness standing over the whole source
Proposition; nothing is assumed about affineness of the `X_s`, which is precisely what clause (3)
as the tag states it leaves out.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_of_isBasisNonvanishing [CompactSpace X]
    (h : Stacks.AmpleTheory.IsBasisNonvanishing X L) :
    IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Clause (9) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3]** — the clause labelled 01QC: `X` is quasi-separated, and
every sheaf of ideals of finite type on `X` is a quotient of a direct sum of `k` copies of
`L ^⊗ (-n)` for some `n > 0` and `k ≥ 0`.

A sheaf of ideals is presented as a module `J` together with a monomorphism `J ⟶ 𝒪_X`, which is
what "sheaf of ideals" means; `k` is the cardinality of the finite index type `ι`, a direct sum
over a finite index type being a direct sum of `Nat.card ι` copies.

The clause is read with its ideals **quasi-coherent**, as clause (6) of the source states them
explicitly, and this is forced rather than chosen: a quotient of a direct sum of quasi-coherent
modules is quasi-coherent, so the clause would be false for a sheaf of ideals that is not. It is
also what makes the source's "the implication (8) ⇒ (9) is trivial" true, and it is the generality
in which clause (8) is registered
(`Stacks.AmpleLocalGeneration.quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isAmple`).

The proof is exactly the source's: clause (9) is clause (8) with its quantifier restricted, so
clause (8) applied to `J` is the whole content.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal_of_isAmple (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ unitModule X), Mono j →
      J.IsQuasicoherent → SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} J →
        ∃ (n : ℤ) (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι), 0 < n ∧
          ∃ (b : CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone fun _ : ι => tensorPowModule X L (-n))
            (_ : b.IsBilimit) (p : b.pt ⟶ J), CategoryTheory.Epi p

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.iSup_range_twistHom_eq_top_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3]** — the clause labelled 01Q8: for every quasi-coherent
sheaf `F` on `X` the sum of the images of the canonical maps
`Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗ n}) ⊗_𝐙 L^{⊗ -n} ⟶ F`, over `n ≥ 1`, equals `F`.

The `n`-th canonical map is the sum over `m ∈ Γ(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗ n})` of the maps
`Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.twistHom L F n m`, a tensor product over `𝐙` with a free abelian
group being the direct sum; so the sum of the images of the canonical maps is the sum of the
images of the `twistHom L F n m`, which is what is written.

**The equality of subsheaves is read on stalks**, as `Stacks.AmpleLocalGeneration.IsFinGenOn` and
every other generation statement in this repository is. For sheaves of modules the two readings
agree: the stalk functor is exact and commutes with the filtered colimit defining a sum of
subsheaves, and a submodule of `F` whose stalks are all of `F` is `F`. What is proved is in fact
stronger than the clause and is what the source's proof gives — every germ lies in the image of a
*single* one of the maps, by `Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.exists_mem_range_twistHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_range_twistHom_eq_top_of_isAmple (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent → ∀ x : X,
      (⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ n) (m : Γ(F ⊗ tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ), ⊤)),
        LinearMap.range (Stacks.ModuleStalk.map (twistHom L F (n : ℤ) m) x)) = ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.iSup_range_twistHom_ideal_eq_top_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Clause (6) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3]** — the clause labelled 01Q9: clause (5) with `F` ranging
over the quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals of `X`.

A sheaf of ideals is a module `J` with a monomorphism into `𝒪_X`. The clause is clause (5) with
its quantifier restricted, which is why the source proves it by the single word "clearly"; the
restriction is recorded here rather than left implicit because clauses (6) and (9) are the two
the source's cycle re-enters ampleness through.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_range_twistHom_ideal_eq_top_of_isAmple (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ Stacks.Ample.unitModule X), Mono j → J.IsQuasicoherent →
      ∀ x : X, (⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ n) (m : Γ(J ⊗ tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ), ⊤)),
        LinearMap.range (Stacks.ModuleStalk.map (twistHom L J (n : ℤ) m) x)) = ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.iSup_range_twistHom_ideal_eq_top_of_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal
declarations.doc:
**Clause (9) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (6)**, by the source's own argument through
[Stacks, Tag 01PG] rather than through ampleness.

Given a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `j : ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_X`, a point `x` and a germ `u ∈ ℐ_x`: the germ
comes from a section of `ℐ` over an affine open `V ∋ x`, and Tag 01PG in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteTypeQuasicoherentSubobject_section` — where quasi-separatedness
is used — puts that section inside a quasi-coherent subobject `G ⊆ ℐ` of finite type. Then
`G.arrow ≫ j` is a monomorphism, so clause (9) applies to `G` and writes it as a quotient of a
finite direct sum of copies of `L ^⊗ (-n)` with `n > 0`; the germ of `G` decomposes as a finite
sum of germs from the summands (`Stacks.ModuleBicone.exists_germ_sum_of_epi`), and pushing the
decomposition forward along `G.arrow` writes `u` as a finite sum of images of morphisms
`L ^⊗ (-n) ⟶ ℐ`, each of which is one of the maps of clause (6) by
`Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.exists_twistHom_eq`.

The other proof of this implication, `Stacks.AmpleCharacterization`
`.iSup_range_twistHom_ideal_eq_top_of_quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal`, goes
`(9) ⇒ (1) ⇒ (6)` instead; both are kept, as the tag's implication and as the route the
nine-clause equivalence was first closed along.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_range_twistHom_ideal_eq_top_of_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal [CompactSpace X]
    (h : QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ unitModule X), Mono j →
      J.IsQuasicoherent → SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} J →
        ∃ (n : ℤ) (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι), 0 < n ∧
          ∃ (b : Bicone fun _ : ι => tensorPowModule X L (-n)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
            (p : b.pt ⟶ J), Epi p) :
    ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ unitModule X), Mono j → J.IsQuasicoherent →
      ∀ x : X, (⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ n) (m : Γ(J ⊗ tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ), ⊤)),
        LinearMap.range (Stacks.ModuleStalk.map (twistHom L J (n : ℤ) m) x)) = ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_iSup_range_twistHom_ideal
declarations.doc:
**Clause (6) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (1)** — the implication the source's cycle
re-enters ampleness through. If for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of the quasi-compact
scheme `X` the sum of the images of the canonical maps
`Γ(X, ℐ ⊗ L^{⊗ n}) ⊗_𝐙 L^{⊗ -n} ⟶ ℐ`, `n ≥ 1`, is all of `ℐ`, then `L` is ample.

This is the source's argument verbatim. Given `x`, choose an affine open `U ∋ x` and apply the
hypothesis to the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `Stacks.ComplementIdeal.sheaf` of the reduced
closed subscheme on `X ∖ U` (Schemes, Section 01IZ, i.e. [Stacks, Tag 01J3]). Its stalk at `x`
contains the germ of `1`, so some single map `L ^⊗ (-n) ⟶ ℐ` composed with the inclusion
`ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_X` has image at `x` outside `𝔪_x`. That composite is multiplication by a global section
`s` of `L ^⊗ n` (`Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.exists_twistUnitHom_eq`); `s` does not vanish at
`x`, and it vanishes along `X ∖ U` because the composite factors through `ℐ`, so `X_s ⊆ U` and
`X_s` is affine by [Stacks, Tag 01PV].
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_of_iSup_range_twistHom_ideal [CompactSpace X]
    (h : ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ unitModule X), Mono j → J.IsQuasicoherent →
      ∀ x : X, (⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ n) (m : Γ(J ⊗ tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ), ⊤)),
        LinearMap.range (Stacks.ModuleStalk.map (twistHom L J (n : ℤ) m) x)) = ⊤) :
    IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_iSup_range_twistHom
declarations.doc:
**Clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (1)**: clause (5) is clause (6) with its
quantifier widened from the quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals to all quasi-coherent sheaves, so
this is `Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_iSup_range_twistHom_ideal` with the hypothesis
restricted.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_of_iSup_range_twistHom [CompactSpace X]
    (h : ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent → ∀ x : X,
      (⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ n) (m : Γ(F ⊗ tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ), ⊤)),
        LinearMap.range (Stacks.ModuleStalk.map (twistHom L F (n : ℤ) m) x)) = ⊤) :
    IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isGeneratedByGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**Clause (7) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (8), at clause (7)'s own strength.** The
clause asks only that `F ⊗ L ^⊗ n` be *globally generated* for every `n ≥ n₀` — generated by
*some* family of global sections, [Stacks, Tag 03DE] (3), with no finiteness demanded of that
family — and that is the hypothesis carried here. The quasi-compactness of `X` is the standing
hypothesis of the tag and nothing else is added.

The finiteness clause (8) asks for is supplied by that quasi-compactness, which is where the
source puts it too. `F ⊗ L ^⊗ n` is of finite type (`isFiniteType_tensor`: `F` is of finite type
by the clause's own hypothesis and `L ^⊗ n` is of finite type, being invertible), and on a
quasi-compact scheme a module of finite type generated by global sections is generated by
finitely many of them — Modules, Lemma 17.9.7 ([Stacks, Tag 01BB]), available as
`Stacks.AmpleEventualGeneration.isFinGen_of_generatingSections`. From there the step is the one
`Stacks.AmpleLocalGeneration.quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isAmple` runs: a
finite family of global sections generating `F ⊗ L ^⊗ n` for one `n ≥ 1` is exactly an
epimorphism onto `F` from a finite direct sum of copies of `L ^⊗ (-n)`, by
`Stacks.AmpleGlobalGeneration.exists_epi_biproduct_of_epi_free`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isGeneratedByGlobalSections
    [CompactSpace X]
    (h : QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent →
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F →
        ∃ n₀ : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n₀ ≤ n →
          _root_.SheafOfModules.IsGeneratedByGlobalSections.{u, u, u}
            ((F ⊗ tensorPowModule X L n : X.Modules))) :
    QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent →
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F →
        ∃ (n : ℤ) (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι), 0 < n ∧
          ∃ (b : Bicone fun _ : ι => tensorPowModule X L (-n)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
            (p : b.pt ⟶ F), Epi p

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isEventuallyGloballyGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Clause (7) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (8)**, from the *strengthened* hypothesis
that the twists are generated by **finitely many** global sections — which is more than clause
(7) says, and so is not the tag's implication; that one is
`quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isGeneratedByGlobalSections` above, and it is
what the equivalences below rest on. This variant is kept because it needs no quasi-compactness:
it is the proof
`Stacks.AmpleLocalGeneration.quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isAmple` runs with
ampleness replaced by the strengthened clause, a finite family of global sections generating
`F ⊗ L ^⊗ n` for one `n ≥ 1` being exactly an epimorphism onto `F` from a finite direct sum of
copies of `L ^⊗ (-n)`, by
`Stacks.AmpleGlobalGeneration.exists_epi_biproduct_of_epi_free`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isEventuallyGloballyGenerated
    (h : QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent →
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F →
        ∃ n₀ : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n₀ ≤ n →
          ∃ σ : (F ⊗ tensorPowModule X L n).GeneratingSections, Finite σ.I) :
    QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent →
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F →
        ∃ (n : ℤ) (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι), 0 < n ∧
          ∃ (b : Bicone fun _ : ι => tensorPowModule X L (-n)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
            (p : b.pt ⟶ F), Epi p
declarations.comment: clause (7) implies (8), under the strengthened hypothesis that the twists are generated by finitely many global sections; the tag's own implication is `quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_of_isGeneratedByGlobalSections` above

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal_of_exists_epi_biproduct
declarations.doc:
**Clause (8) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (9)**, the source's "trivial" step: clause
(9) is clause (8) with its quantifier restricted to the sheaves of ideals.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal_of_exists_epi_biproduct
    (h : QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsQuasicoherent →
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F →
        ∃ (n : ℤ) (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι), 0 < n ∧
          ∃ (b : Bicone fun _ : ι => tensorPowModule X L (-n)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
            (p : b.pt ⟶ F), Epi p) :
    QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ unitModule X), Mono j →
      J.IsQuasicoherent → SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} J →
        ∃ (n : ℤ) (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι), 0 < n ∧
          ∃ (b : Bicone fun _ : ι => tensorPowModule X L (-n)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
            (p : b.pt ⟶ J), Epi p

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal
declarations.doc:
**Clause (9) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (1)** — the step the source's second cycle
re-enters ampleness through, and with the two implications above the last link of the
nine-clause equivalence.

The argument is the source's, with [Stacks, Tag 01PG] where the source puts it. Fix `x`, choose
an affine open `U ∋ x` and let `Z = X ∖ U` with its reduced closed subscheme structure. Its
sheaf of ideals `ℐ_Z` is the unit ideal on some affine open `V ∋ x`, so Tag 01PG — in its
ideal-sheaf form `Stacks.IdealSheaf.exists_fg_le_of_mem`, which is what quasi-separatedness is
used for — produces a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊆ ℐ_Z`, finitely generated on every
affine open and still containing the unit section over `V`. Being finitely generated affine-
locally it is of finite type (`Stacks.IdealSheafModules.isFiniteType_sheaf`), so clause (9)
applies to it: `ℐ` is a quotient of a finite direct sum of copies of `L ^⊗ (-n)` with `n > 0`.

The germ at `x` of that unit section is not in `𝔪_x · (𝒪_X)_x`, and
`Stacks.ModuleBicone.exists_germ_sum_of_epi` writes it as a finite sum of germs coming from the
summands; since `𝔪_x · (𝒪_X)_x` is a submodule, one summand `i` already escapes it. Its
composite `L ^⊗ (-n) ⟶ ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_X` is multiplication by a global section `σ` of `L ^⊗ n`
(`Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.exists_twistUnitHom_eq`), and from here the argument is the one
`Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_iSup_range_twistHom_ideal` runs: `σ` does not vanish at
`x`, and it vanishes at every point of `Z` — which is in the support of `ℐ` because `ℐ ⊆ ℐ_Z` —
so `X_σ ⊆ U` and `X_σ` is affine by [Stacks, Tag 01PV].
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_of_quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal [CompactSpace X]
    (h : QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ unitModule X), Mono j →
      J.IsQuasicoherent → SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} J →
        ∃ (n : ℤ) (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι), 0 < n ∧
          ∃ (b : Bicone fun _ : ι => tensorPowModule X L (-n)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
            (p : b.pt ⟶ J), Epi p) :
    IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.iSup_range_twistHom_ideal_eq_top_of_quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal
declarations.doc:
**Clause (9) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (6)**, the implication the source's cycle
runs through. It is clause (9) implies clause (1)
(`Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isAmple_of_quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal`)
followed by clause (6) from ampleness, rather than the source's direct argument; the ingredient
the source uses for the direct route, [Stacks, Tag 01PG], is the ingredient used there.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_range_twistHom_ideal_eq_top_of_quasiSeparatedSpace_and_exists_epi_biproduct_ideal
    [CompactSpace X]
    (h : QuasiSeparatedSpace X ∧ ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ unitModule X), Mono j →
      J.IsQuasicoherent → SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} J →
        ∃ (n : ℤ) (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι), 0 < n ∧
          ∃ (b : Bicone fun _ : ι => tensorPowModule X L (-n)) (_ : b.IsBilimit)
            (p : b.pt ⟶ J), Epi p) :
    ∀ (J : X.Modules) (j : J ⟶ unitModule X), Mono j → J.IsQuasicoherent →
      ∀ x : X, (⨆ (n : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ n) (m : Γ(J ⊗ tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ), ⊤)),
        LinearMap.range (Stacks.ModuleStalk.map (twistHom L J (n : ℤ) m) x)) = ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCharacterization.isBasisNonvanishing_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 01Q3] implies clause (3)** — the clause labelled 01Q6: for `L`
ample the opens `X_s`, with `s ∈ S₊` homogeneous, form a basis for the topology of `X`.

The clause is written out rather than named, and in the `Stacks.Ample.IsAmple` vocabulary the
other eight clauses of the tag are stated in. The content is
`Stacks.SectionExtension.isBasisNonvanishing_of_isAmple`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBasisNonvanishing_of_isAmple (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    ∀ (x : X) (U : X.Opens), x ∈ U → ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧
      ∃ s : Γ(tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ), ⊤),
        x ∈ powNonvanishingOpen X L n s ∧ powNonvanishingOpen X L n s ≤ U
