declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.rationalFunctions
declarations.doc: A rational function on a scheme is a rational map to the affine line over the integers.
declarations.statement: abbrev Scheme.rationalFunctions (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalFunctionsRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01RU.** The ring structure on rational maps to the affine line is the one induced
by the ring operations on sections on every dense open: there is a commutative ring structure on
`R(X)` for which, for every dense open `U ⊆ X`, the map sending a section `s ∈ Γ(X, U)` to the
rational function it represents is a ring homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalFunctionsRing (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ R : CommRing (rationalFunctions X),
      letI := R
      ∀ U : DenseOpen X,
        ∃ φ : Γ(X, U.1) →+* rationalFunctions X,
          ∀ s, φ s = ofSection X U s

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalFunctionsEquivStalks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01RV.** The rational functions of a scheme with finitely many irreducible
components are the product of the local rings at the generic points of those components; the
identification sends a section on a dense open to its family of germs.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalFunctionsEquivResidueFields
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01RV.** On a reduced scheme the generic local rings are the residue fields at the
generic points, so the rational functions are their product.
declarations.statement:
def rationalFunctionsEquivResidueFields (X : Scheme.{u}) [Finite (irreducibleComponents X)]
    [IsReduced X] :
    { e : rationalFunctions X ≃+*
        (∀ Z : irreducibleComponents X, X.residueField Z.2.1.genericPoint) //
      ∀ (U : DenseOpen X) (s : Γ(X, U.1)) (Z : irreducibleComponents X)
        (h : Z.2.1.genericPoint ∈ U.1),
        e (ofSection X U s) Z = X.evaluation U.1 Z.2.1.genericPoint h s }

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalFunctionsEquivFunctionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01RV.** On an integral scheme the rational functions are the function field, that
is, the stalk at the generic point.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalFunctionsEquivResidueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01RV.** On an integral scheme the rational functions are the residue field of the
generic point.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.isField_rationalFunctions
declarations.doc: **Stacks 01RV.** The ring of rational functions of an integral scheme is a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_rationalFunctions (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] :
    IsField (rationalFunctions X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.functionFieldOfRationalFunctions
declarations.doc:
The *function field*, or *field of rational functions*, of an integral scheme `X`: the ring
`R(X)` of rational functions on `X`, which is a field because `X` is integral.
declarations.statement: abbrev functionFieldOfRationalFunctions (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] : Type u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PseudoMap
declarations.doc:
A pseudo-map from `X` to `Y` is a morphism into `Y` defined on a scheme-theoretically dense
open subscheme of `X`. This is the variant of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PartialMap` in which the
domain of definition is required to be scheme-theoretically dense.
declarations.statement: structure PseudoMap (X Y : Scheme.{u})
declarations.comment:
the pseudo-maps: morphisms into `Y` defined on scheme-theoretically dense opens
of `X`, the objects whose equivalence classes the remark calls pseudo-morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PseudoMap.equiv
declarations.doc:
Two pseudo-maps are equivalent if they agree after restriction to a scheme-theoretically
dense open subscheme.
declarations.statement: protected noncomputable def equiv (f g : X.PseudoMap Y) : Prop
declarations.comment:
the equivalence relation on pseudo-maps: agreement after restriction to a
scheme-theoretically dense open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PseudoMap.equivalence_rel
declarations.doc: Equivalence of pseudo-maps is an equivalence relation.
declarations.statement: lemma equivalence_rel : Equivalence (@Scheme.PseudoMap.equiv X Y)
declarations.comment:
equivalence relation, via stability of scheme-theoretic density under
intersection (Tag 01RF)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PseudoMorphism
declarations.doc:
A pseudo-morphism from `X` to `Y` is an equivalence class of pseudo-maps, where two
pseudo-maps are equivalent if they agree on a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def PseudoMorphism (X Y : Scheme.{u}) : Type u
declarations.comment: the pseudo-morphisms from `X` to `Y`: the equivalence classes of pseudo-maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PseudoMorphism.IsOver
declarations.doc:
A pseudo-morphism is an `S`-pseudo-morphism if some pseudo-map in the equivalence class is
an `S`-morphism.
declarations.statement: class PseudoMorphism.IsOver [X.Over S] [Y.Over S] (f : X.PseudoMorphism Y) : Prop
declarations.comment:
the `S`-pseudo-morphisms: the analogue for pseudo-morphisms of part (3) of the
definition of an `S`-rational map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PseudoMorphism.equivRationalMap
declarations.doc:
If `X` is reduced, pseudo-morphisms from `X` to `Y` are the same thing as rational maps from
`X` to `Y`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def PseudoMorphism.equivRationalMap : X.PseudoMorphism Y ≃ X.RationalMap Y
declarations.comment: agreement of pseudo-morphisms with rational maps for reduced `X`

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyInjective
registrations.comment: (1) universally injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_of_subsingleton_of_section
declarations.doc:
**A morphism of schemes whose source is a subsingleton and which admits a section is
universally injective.**  This is condition (3) of **Stacks 01S4**: injectivity on points is the
subsingleton hypothesis, and at a point `x` of the source the residue field map is an
isomorphism because `x` coincides with the image under the section of its own image.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_subsingleton_of_section {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton X]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (s : Y ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = 𝟙 Y) : UniversallyInjective f
declarations.comment: a morphism with a subsingleton source and a section is universally injective

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.of_isAffineHom
registrations.comment: separated

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.instQuasiCompactOfIsAffineHom
registrations.comment: quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_iff_forall_exists_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01S8, equivalence of (1) and (2).** A morphism of schemes
`f : X ⟶ S` is affine if and only if every point of `S` has an affine open neighbourhood
whose inverse image under `f` is affine.
declarations.statement:
lemma isAffineHom_iff_forall_exists_isAffineOpen {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsAffineHom f ↔
      ∀ x : S, ∃ U : S.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ IsAffineOpen (f ⁻¹ᵁ U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeSpecPushforwardAlgebraIso
declarations.doc:
For an affine morphism `f : X ⟶ S`, the source is, over `S`, the relative spectrum of the
pushforward `f_* 𝒪_X` of its structure sheaf, which is a quasi-coherent sheaf of
`𝒪_S`-algebras.
declarations.comment: the source is the relative spectrum of the pushforward algebra

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_iff_exists_relativeSpecIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01S8, equivalence of (1) and (3).** A morphism of schemes is affine if
and only if it is isomorphic, as an object over its target, to the structure morphism of the
relative spectrum of a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras on the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_iff_exists_relativeSpecIso (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsAffineHom f ↔
      ∃ (A : AlgebraSheaf S) (hA : AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A),
        Nonempty (Over.mk f ≅ Over.mk (@relativeSpecToBase S A hA))

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.overRelativeSpecIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01S8, the final statement.** For an affine morphism `f : X ⟶ S` there
is an isomorphism `X ≅ \underline{Spec}_S(f_* 𝒪_X)` of schemes over `S`.
declarations.comment: the final statement: X = Spec_S(f_* O_X) for an affine morphism f : X → S

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.isAffineHom_iff_exists_quasicoherentAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01S8, part (3).** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is affine if and
only if there is a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_S`-algebras `A` and an isomorphism
`X ≅ \underline{Spec}_S(A)` of schemes over `S`.

The forward direction takes `A = f_* 𝒪_X` and is `overRelativeSpecIso`; the converse is
`isAffineHom_relativeSpecToBase` together with `isAffineHom_of_overIso`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineHom_iff_exists_quasicoherentAlgebra {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsAffineHom f ↔ ∃ A : QuasicoherentAlgebra S,
      letI := A.property
      Nonempty ((Over.mk f : Over S) ≅ Over.mk (relativeSpecToBase A.obj))
declarations.comment: part (3): f is affine iff X is a relative spectrum over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_of_iSup_eq_top_of_isAffineOpen_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01S9.** If `S = ⋃ⱼ Wⱼ` is an affine open covering such that each
`f⁻¹(Wⱼ)` is affine, then `f : X ⟶ S` is affine.
declarations.statement:
lemma isAffineHom_of_iSup_eq_top_of_isAffineOpen_preimage {ι : Type*} (W : ι → S.Opens)
    (hW : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (W j)) (hcov : ⨆ j, W j = ⊤)
    (hfW : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (f ⁻¹ᵁ W j)) :
    IsAffineHom f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraPullbackQcoh.affineEquivalenceAlgebras
declarations.doc:
**All nine clauses of [Stacks, Tag 01SA].**  The canonical anti-equivalence between the
schemes affine over a base and the quasi-coherent sheaves of commutative algebras on that base,
compatible with arbitrary base change.

The tag is registered by a single unqualified attribute on this nine-field structure.
declarations.statement: def affineEquivalenceAlgebras : AffineAlgebraAntiEquivalence.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01SA, the base-change clause.** The anti-equivalence between the
schemes affine over `S` and the quasi-coherent sheaves of `𝒪_S`-algebras is compatible with
arbitrary base change, unconditionally: the one assertion on which
`Stacks.AffineAlgebraEquivalence.antiEquivalenceOfQuasicoherentAlgebraPullback` was left standing
is `isQuasicoherentAlgebraPullback`, proved above.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def affineAlgebraAntiEquivalence : AffineAlgebraAntiEquivalence.{u}
declarations.comment: compatibility of the anti-equivalence with arbitrary base change

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineQcohUnit.isEquivalence_affineQuasicoherentPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01SB, first assertion.**  For an affine morphism `f : X ⟶ S`, direct
image induces an equivalence from quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules to quasi-coherent modules over
`f_* 𝒪_X`, with quasi-inverse `𝒢 ↦ f^*𝒢 ⊗_{f^*f_*𝒪_X} 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_affineQuasicoherentPushforward [IsAffineHom f] :
    (affineQuasicoherentPushforward f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.QcohLimits.affine_isQuasicoherent_restrictScalars_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01SB, second assertion.** An `f_* 𝒪_X`-module is quasi-coherent as an
`𝒪_S`-module if and only if it is quasi-coherent as an `f_* 𝒪_X`-module.

This is the whole of the tag's final statement ("Moreover, an `𝒜`-module is quasi-coherent as an
`𝒪_S`-module if and only if it is quasi-coherent as an `𝒜`-module").  The tag's other assertion,
the equivalence of categories, is not proved here, so the attribute is clause-qualified.
declarations.statement:
theorem affine_isQuasicoherent_restrictScalars_iff (f : X ⟶ S) [IsAffineHom f]
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (AffineQcohPushforward.pushforwardRing f.base X.ringCatSheaf)) :
    ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars f.toRingCatSheafHom).obj G).IsQuasicoherent ↔
      G.IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineHom.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The base change of an affine morphism is affine: if `f : X ⟶ S` is affine and
`g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` is a cartesian square, then the base change `f' : X' ⟶ S'` of `f` along
`g : S' ⟶ S` is affine.

declarations.name: Stacks.NonvanishingAffineIntersection.isAffineOpen_inf_nonvanishingOpen
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme, `M` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `s` a global section of `M`. For every
affine open `U` of `X`, the intersection `U ∩ X_s` of `U` with the nonvanishing locus of `s` is
affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineOpen_inf_nonvanishingOpen {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    IsAffineOpen (U ⊓ Stacks.NonvanishingOpen.nonvanishingOpen X M s)
declarations.comment: affineness of the inclusion j : X_s -> X, i.e. preimages of affine opens under j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_of_isAffineHom_of_isAffineHom_diagonal
declarations.doc:
Let `g : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes over `S`. If `X` is affine over `S` and the diagonal
`Y ⟶ Y ×_S Y` is affine, then `g` is affine.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_of_isAffineHom_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `g : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes over `S`. If `X` is affine over `S` and `Y` is
separated over `S`, then `g` is affine.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineHom_of_isAffineHom_of_isSeparated (g : X ⟶ Y) {a : X ⟶ S} (b : Y ⟶ S)
    (hab : g ≫ b = a) [IsAffineHom a] [IsSeparated b] : IsAffineHom g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_of_isAffine_of_isAffineHom_diagonal
declarations.doc:
A morphism from an affine scheme to a scheme with affine
diagonal is affine.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineHom_of_isAffine_of_isAffineHom_diagonal (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffine X]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from Y))] : IsAffineHom g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_of_isAffine_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc: A morphism from an affine scheme to a separated scheme is affine.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineHom_of_isAffine_of_isSeparated (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffine X]
    [Y.IsSeparated] : IsAffineHom g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_of_isArtinianRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01SI.** Every morphism from the spectrum of an
Artinian ring to a scheme is affine.
declarations.statement:
lemma isAffineHom_of_isArtinianRing {A : CommRingCat.{u}} [IsArtinianRing A]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : Spec A ⟶ S) : IsAffineHom f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is quasi-affine if the inverse image of every affine open subscheme of
the target is a quasi-affine scheme.
declarations.statement: class IsQuasiAffineHom {X S : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc: A quasi-affine morphism of schemes is separated.
declarations.statement:
instance isSeparated_of_isQuasiAffineHom {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsQuasiAffineHom f] : IsSeparated f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc: A quasi-affine morphism of schemes is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
instance quasiCompact_of_isQuasiAffineHom {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsQuasiAffineHom f] : QuasiCompact f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_toSpecΓ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01SM, part (4), over an affine base.** A morphism to an affine scheme
is quasi-affine if and only if the canonical morphism from its source to the spectrum of its
global sections — the relative spectrum of the pushforward of the structure sheaf — is a
quasi-compact open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_toSpecΓ [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom f ↔ IsOpenImmersion X.toSpecΓ ∧ QuasiCompact X.toSpecΓ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_exists_isOpenCover
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is quasi-affine if and only if there exists an affine open covering of
the target all of whose members have quasi-affine inverse image.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_exists_isOpenCover {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom f ↔ ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → S.affineOpens),
      IsOpenCover (fun i ↦ (U i : S.Opens)) ∧
        ∀ i, Scheme.IsQuasiAffine (f ⁻¹ᵁ (U i : S.Opens)).toScheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_canonicalMorphism
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated — so that `f_* 𝒪_X` is a
quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_S`-algebras and the canonical morphism `X ⟶ Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)` exists —
is quasi-affine if and only if that canonical morphism is a quasi-compact open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_canonicalMorphism :
    IsQuasiAffineHom f ↔
      IsOpenImmersion (canonicalMorphism f) ∧ QuasiCompact (canonicalMorphism f)
declarations.comment: (1) ↔ (4) over a general base, carrying the quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses that make `f_* 𝒪_X` quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_canonicalMorphism
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism from the source of a quasi-affine morphism to the relative spectrum of
the pushed-forward structure sheaf is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
instance isOpenImmersion_canonicalMorphism (f : X ⟶ S) [IsQuasiAffineHom f] :
    IsOpenImmersion (canonicalMorphism f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_canonicalMorphism
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism from the source of a quasi-affine morphism to the relative spectrum of
the pushed-forward structure sheaf is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
instance quasiCompact_canonicalMorphism (f : X ⟶ S) [IsQuasiAffineHom f] :
    QuasiCompact (canonicalMorphism f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_exists_relativeSpec
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is quasi-affine if and only if there is a quasi-coherent
sheaf `A` of `𝒪_S`-algebras and a quasi-compact open immersion `X ⟶ Spec_S(A)` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_exists_relativeSpec (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom f ↔
      ∃ (A : AlgebraSheaf S) (hA : AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A)
        (g : X ⟶ @relativeSpec S A hA),
        IsOpenImmersion g ∧ QuasiCompact g ∧ g ≫ @relativeSpecToBase S A hA = f
declarations.comment: (1) ↔ (3) over a general base, no hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_of_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01SM, (1) is equivalent to (2).** A morphism of schemes is
quasi-affine if and only if the preimages of the members of one affine open covering of the
target are quasi-affine schemes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_isStableUnderComposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01SN.** A composition of quasi-affine morphisms of schemes is
quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasiAffineHom_isStableUnderComposition :
    MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition
      (@IsQuasiAffineHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01SO.** Quasi-affine morphisms of schemes are stable under arbitrary
base change.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasiAffineHom_isStableUnderBaseChange :
    MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (@IsQuasiAffineHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_quasiCompact
declarations.doc: A morphism from an affine scheme is quasi-affine if and only if it is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_quasiCompact {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X]
    (f : X ⟶ S) : IsQuasiAffineHom f ↔ QuasiCompact f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiAffineHom_of_isQuasiAffine_of_quasiSeparatedSpace
declarations.doc: Every morphism from a quasi-affine scheme to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
instance isQuasiAffineHom_of_isQuasiAffine_of_quasiSeparatedSpace
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [Scheme.IsQuasiAffine X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) : IsQuasiAffineHom f

declarations.name: RingHom.StacksPropertyIsLocal
declarations.doc:
A property of commutative-ring homomorphisms is local if it is preserved
by simultaneous principal localization, passes from a map `R_f → A` to the
composite `R → A_a`, and can be checked on a finite principal open cover of
the target.
declarations.statement:
structure StacksPropertyIsLocal
    (P : ∀ {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S], (R →+* S) → Prop) : Prop

registrations.name: RingHom.IsStableUnderBaseChange
registrations.comment: (2) stable under base change, in the pushout formulation

registrations.name: RingHom.StableUnderComposition
registrations.comment: (3) stable under composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfType
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is locally of type `P` if every point of its source lies in
an affine open mapping into an affine open of the target on whose rings of sections
the induced homomorphism satisfies `P`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev locallyOfType (P : ∀ {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S],
    (R →+* S) → Prop) : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.appLE_of_locallyOfType
declarations.doc:
If `f` is locally of type `P` for a local property `P`, then `P` holds for the ring map
`𝒪_S(V) → 𝒪_X(U)` of any affine opens `U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ S` with `f(U) ⊆ V`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfType_resLE
declarations.doc:
If `f` is locally of type `P` for a local property `P`, then so is its restriction
`U → V` to any opens `U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ S` with `f(U) ⊆ V`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfType_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a local property `P`, being locally of type `P` can be checked on all pairs of affine
opens, on open coverings of target and preimages, or on affine such coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfType_tfae (hP : RingHom.StacksPropertyIsLocal P) (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      locallyOfType P f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1), P (f.appLE V U e).hom,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, locallyOfType P (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1, P (f.appLE V U e).hom]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfType_tfae_and_resLE
declarations.doc:
The whole statement: for a local property `P`, the four characterizations of being locally
of type `P` agree, and being locally of type `P` passes to restrictions to open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfType_tfae_and_resLE (hP : RingHom.StacksPropertyIsLocal P) (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      locallyOfType P f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1), P (f.appLE V U e).hom,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, locallyOfType P (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1, P (f.appLE V U e).hom] ∧
    (locallyOfType P f → ∀ (U : X.Opens) (V : S.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
      locallyOfType P (f.resLE V U e))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfType_comp
declarations.doc:
For a local property `P` stable under composition, a composition of morphisms locally of
type `P` is locally of type `P`.

declarations.name: RingHom.isOpenImmersion_localizationAwayPreserves
declarations.doc:
Locality condition (1)(a): the affine open-immersion criterion is preserved by
simultaneous principal localization. This is base change along `R → R_r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_localizationAwayPreserves :
    RingHom.LocalizationAwayPreserves
      (fun {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] (φ : R →+* A) ↦ φ.IsOpenImmersion)
declarations.comment: part (2) (open immersion), locality condition (1)(a) of 01SR only: the criterion is preserved by simultaneous principal localization. Part (2) itself is false; see not_stacksPropertyIsLocal_isOpenImmersion

declarations.name: RingHom.isOpenImmersion_compPrincipalLocalizations
declarations.doc:
Locality condition (1)(b): if `R_f → A` satisfies the affine open-immersion criterion then
so does the induced composite `R → A_a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_compPrincipalLocalizations
    {R A Rf Aa : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing Rf] [CommRing Aa] (f : R) (a : A)
    [Algebra R Rf] [IsLocalization.Away f Rf] [Algebra A Aa] [IsLocalization.Away a Aa]
    (g : Rf →+* A) (hg : g.IsOpenImmersion) :
    ((algebraMap A Aa).comp (g.comp (algebraMap R Rf))).IsOpenImmersion
declarations.comment: part (2) (open immersion), locality condition (1)(b) of 01SR only: `P (R_f → A) ⟹ P (R → A_a)`. Part (2) itself is false; see not_stacksPropertyIsLocal_isOpenImmersion

declarations.name: RingHom.not_ofLocalizationFiniteSpanTarget_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
The affine open-immersion criterion does not descend from a finite principal open cover of
the target: this is the third locality condition of `RingHom.StacksPropertyIsLocal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_ofLocalizationFiniteSpanTarget_isOpenImmersion :
    ¬ RingHom.OfLocalizationFiniteSpanTarget
      (fun {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) ↦ φ.IsOpenImmersion)
declarations.comment: refutation of part (2) (open immersion): locality condition (1)(c) of 01SR fails for the criterion, the witness being the diagonal `k → k × k` of a field, whose two localizations at the coordinate idempotents are bijective while the diagonal itself is not a principal localization

declarations.name: RingHom.not_stacksPropertyIsLocal_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
The affine open-immersion criterion is not a local property of commutative-ring
homomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_stacksPropertyIsLocal_isOpenImmersion :
    ¬ RingHom.StacksPropertyIsLocal
      (fun {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) ↦ φ.IsOpenImmersion)
declarations.comment: refutation of part (2) (open immersion): the criterion is NOT a local property of ring maps, so part (2) is false as stated. Conditions (1)(a) and (1)(b) of 01SR do hold and are the two carriers above; (1)(c) fails by not_ofLocalizationFiniteSpanTarget_isOpenImmersion. Parts (1), (3), (4) and (5) of the tag are true and carried in LocalRingIso, ReducedFibers, FiberDimension and NoetherianTarget

declarations.name: RingHom.fiberDimensionLE_propertyIsLocal
declarations.doc:
A uniform bound on the Krull dimensions of the fibres is a local property of
commutative-ring homomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiberDimensionLE_propertyIsLocal (n : ℕ) :
    RingHom.StacksPropertyIsLocal
      (fun {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) =>
        letI : Algebra R S := f.toAlgebra
        ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], ringKrullDim (p.Fiber S) ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞))

declarations.name: RingHom.localRingHom_bijective_propertyIsLocal
declarations.doc:
Having isomorphisms on the local rings at every prime of the target is a
local property of ring homomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingHom_bijective_propertyIsLocal :
    RingHom.StacksPropertyIsLocal
      (fun {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) ↦
        ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
          Function.Bijective
            (Localization.localRingHom (Ideal.comap f q) q f rfl))

declarations.name: RingHom.noetherianTarget_propertyIsLocal
declarations.doc: Having Noetherian target is local for commutative-ring homomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherianTarget_propertyIsLocal :

      (fun {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (_ : R →+* S) =>
        IsNoetherianRing S)

declarations.name: RingHom.reducedFibers_propertyIsLocal
declarations.doc: Having reduced fibres is local for ring homomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem reducedFibers_propertyIsLocal :
    RingHom.StacksPropertyIsLocal (fun f => RingHom.ReducedFibers f)

declarations.name: RingHom.isOpenImmersion_isStableUnderBaseChange

declarations.name: RingHom.isOpenImmersion_stableUnderComposition

Being an isomorphism on some principal neighborhood of each target prime

declarations.name: RingHom.localRingHom_bijective_stableUnderComposition

The property that all induced maps on local rings are isomorphisms is

declarations.statement:
theorem localRingHom_bijective_stableUnderComposition :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparated_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc: A morphism locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
instance quasiSeparated_of_locallyOfFiniteType {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian S] : QuasiSeparated f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01T8.** If a composite of morphisms of schemes is locally of finite
type, then so is its first factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem LocallyOfFiniteType.of_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z}
    (h : LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ g)) : LocallyOfFiniteType f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteType_specField_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01TA.** For a morphism from the spectrum of a field, being of finite
type, being locally of finite type, admitting a finite affine coordinate-ring map around its
image, and having closed image with finite residue field extension are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteType_specField_tfae {k : Type u} [Field k] {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f,
      LocallyOfFiniteType f,
      ∃ (U : S.affineOpens)
          (hU : (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1),
        ((f.appLE U ⊤ hU) ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).hom).hom.Finite,
      ∃ (U : S.affineOpens)
          (_hU : (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)
          (x : U.1),
        (x : S) = ((Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField k S) f).1 ∧
          IsClosed ({x} : Set U.1) ∧
          letI := ((Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField k S) f).2.hom.toAlgebra
          Module.Finite (S.residueField ((Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField k S) f).1) k]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteTypePoint_of_isClosed_singleton
declarations.doc:
A closed point of a scheme is a finite type point: the morphism from the spectrum of its
residue field is a closed immersion
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_singleton_iff_isClosedImmersion`), hence both locally of finite
type and quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteTypePoint_of_isClosed_singleton {X : Scheme.{u}} {x : X}
    (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) : IsFiniteTypePoint x
declarations.comment: closed points are finite type points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_finiteTypePoints_tfae
declarations.doc:
A scheme is Jacobson exactly when its finite type points are its closed points; equivalently,
closed points under every locally finite type morphism to it have closed image, and the induced
residue field extensions are finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem jacobsonSpace_finiteTypePoints_tfae (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      JacobsonSpace S,
      S.finiteTypePoints = {s | IsClosed ({s} : Set S)},
      ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (t : T),
        IsClosed ({t} : Set T) → IsClosed ({f t} : Set S),
      ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (t : T),
        IsClosed ({t} : Set T) → (
          IsClosed ({f t} : Set S) ∧
            letI := (f.residueFieldMap t).hom.toAlgebra
            Module.Finite (S.residueField (f t)) (T.residueField t))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is quasi-finite at `x` if it is of finite type at `x` and its
stalk map at `x` is quasi-finite.
declarations.statement: public abbrev quasiFiniteAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt_iff_exists_affineOpens
declarations.doc:
Quasi-finiteness at a point is equivalently witnessed on compatible affine
neighbourhoods by a finite-type ring map which is quasi-finite at the corresponding
prime.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiFiniteAt_iff_exists_affineOpens
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    quasiFiniteAt f x ↔
      ∃ (U : S.affineOpens) (V : X.affineOpens) (hxV : x ∈ V.1)
        (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1),
        (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.FiniteType ∧
          (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.QuasiFiniteAt
            (V.2.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hxV⟩).asIdeal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.forall_quasiFiniteAt_iff
declarations.doc:
A morphism is quasi-finite at every point exactly when it is locally of finite type
and locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem forall_quasiFiniteAt_iff {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    (∀ x, quasiFiniteAt f x) ↔
      (AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFinite_conditions_iff_isDiscrete_fibers
declarations.doc:
The conditions defining a quasi-finite morphism can be expressed either by local
quasi-finiteness or by discreteness of every set-theoretic fiber.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiFinite_conditions_iff_isDiscrete_fibers
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    ((LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f) ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite f) ↔
      ((LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ QuasiCompact f) ∧
        ∀ s, IsDiscrete (f ⁻¹' {s}))

registrations.comment: the local finite-type condition in parts (2) and (3)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_asFiber_of_isAlgebraic_residueField
declarations.doc: A point whose residue field is algebraic over that of its image is closed in its fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosed_asFiber_of_isAlgebraic_residueField (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    (h : letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsAlgebraic (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) :
    IsClosed ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_of_isAlgebraic_residueField
declarations.doc:
If the image of a point is closed and its residue field extension is algebraic, then the
point is closed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosed_of_isAlgebraic_residueField (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    (h : letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsAlgebraic (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x))
    (hs : IsClosed ({f x} : Set S)) : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_asFiber_iff_finite_residueField
declarations.doc:
A point of a fibre of a locally finite type morphism is closed exactly when its residue
field is finite over the residue field of its image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosed_asFiber_iff_finite_residueField (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) :
    IsClosed ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x))) ↔
      letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
      Module.Finite (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.finite_residueField_of_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
At a point where a morphism of schemes is quasi-finite, the residue field of the source is a
finite extension of the residue field of the image: the stalk map is quasi-finite, the residue
field of the source is a quotient of the source stalk, and a quasi-finite algebra over a field is
finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.finite_residueField_of_quasiFiniteAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    (h : f.QuasiFiniteAt x) :
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    Module.Finite (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)
declarations.comment:
the hypothesis is the stalk half `Scheme.Hom.QuasiFiniteAt` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt`, so the finite-type half is not used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01TH.** For a morphism locally of finite type, quasi-finiteness at a
point is equivalent to isolation of that point in the fibre, to the corresponding closedness
and specialization condition, and to quasi-finiteness at the corresponding prime for every
compatible pair of affine open neighbourhoods.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiFiniteAt_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) :
    List.TFAE [
      quasiFiniteAt f x,
      IsIsolatedPoint (f.asFiber x),
      IsClosed ({f.asFiber x} : Set (f.fiber (f x))) ∧
        (¬ ∃ x' : f.fiber (f x),
          x' ≠ f.asFiber x ∧ x' ⤳ f.asFiber x),
      ∀ (U : S.affineOpens) (V : X.affineOpens) (hxV : x ∈ V.1)
        (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1),
        (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.QuasiFiniteAt
          (V.2.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hxV⟩).asIdeal]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_quasiFiniteLocus_iff
declarations.doc:
A point belongs to the locally quasi-finite locus exactly when the morphism is quasi-finite
at that point. In particular, the set of such points is open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_quasiFiniteLocus_iff {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    x ∈ quasiFiniteLocus f ↔ quasiFiniteAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_quasiFiniteLocus
declarations.doc: The restriction to the quasi-finite locus is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
public instance locallyOfFiniteType_quasiFiniteLocus {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType ((quasiFiniteLocus f).ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: the induced morphism, local finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_quasiFiniteLocus
declarations.doc:
The restriction to the quasi-finite locus is locally quasi-finite in Mathlib's
fiber-isolation sense.
declarations.statement:
public instance locallyQuasiFinite_quasiFiniteLocus {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    LocallyQuasiFinite ((quasiFiniteLocus f).ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_conditions_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01TK.** Local quasi-finiteness can be checked on all pairs of affine
opens, on open coverings of the target and of the preimages, or on affine such coverings; on
affine opens it is the condition that the ring map be quasi-finite, that is of finite type and
quasi-finite at every prime.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyQuasiFinite_conditions_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.FiniteType ∧ (f.appLE V U e).hom.QuasiFinite,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V,
          LocallyOfFiniteType (f.resLE V U e) ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1,
          (f.appLE V U e).hom.FiniteType ∧ (f.appLE V U e).hom.QuasiFinite]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_conditions_resLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01TK.** If `f` is locally quasi-finite then so is its restriction
`U → V` to any opens `U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ S` with `f(U) ⊆ V`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyQuasiFinite_conditions_resLE {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    (hf : LocallyOfFiniteType f ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite f) (V : S.Opens) (U : X.Opens)
    (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (f.resLE V U e) ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite (f.resLE V U e)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_conditions_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01TL.** The composition of two locally quasi-finite morphisms is
locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_conditions_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [LocallyQuasiFinite g] :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ g) ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFinite_conditions_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01TL.** The composition of two quasi-finite morphisms is
quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFinite_conditions_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] [LocallyQuasiFinite g] :
    (LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ g) ∧ QuasiCompact (f ≫ g)) ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite (f ≫ g)

morphism.

declarations.statement: public abbrev FinitePresentationAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is of finite presentation if it is locally of finite
presentation, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated.
declarations.statement: public abbrev FinitePresentation {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_resLE
declarations.doc:
If `f` is locally of finite presentation then so is its restriction `U → V` to any opens
`U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ S` with `f(U) ⊆ V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_resLE {f : X ⟶ S} (hf : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f)
    (V : S.Opens) (U : X.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f.resLE V U e)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_tfae
declarations.doc:
Being locally of finite presentation can be checked on all pairs of affine opens, on open
coverings of target and preimages, or on affine such coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_tfae (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.FinitePresentation,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1,
          (f.appLE V U e).hom.FinitePresentation]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_tfae_and_resLE
declarations.doc:
The whole statement: the four characterizations of being locally of finite presentation
agree, and being locally of finite presentation passes to restrictions to open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_tfae_and_resLE (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.FinitePresentation,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1,
          (f.appLE V U e).hom.FinitePresentation] ∧
    (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f → ∀ (U : X.Opens) (V : S.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f.resLE V U e))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOver_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlatOver_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F,
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (V : S.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
        (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
        let : Module Γ(S, V) Γ(F, U) :=
          Module.compHom Γ(F, U) (f.appLE V U hUV).hom
        Module.Flat Γ(S, V) Γ(F, U),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            ∀ i, IsFlatOver
              (f.resLE (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)).toLRSHom.toShHom
              (F.restrict (U i).ι),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i,
                let hUV : U i ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V j := (le_iSup U i).trans hU.le
                let : Module Γ(S, V j) Γ(F, U i) :=
                  Module.compHom Γ(F, U i) (f.appLE (V j) (U i) hUV).hom
                Module.Flat Γ(S, V j) Γ(F, U i)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_tfae
declarations.doc:
Flatness of a morphism of schemes can be checked on all pairs of affine opens, on open
coverings of target and preimages, or on affine such coverings.

The source defines flatness of `f` by flatness of the local ring maps
`𝒪_{S, f(x)} → 𝒪_{X, x}`; this agrees with `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_tfae (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      Flat f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.Flat,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, Flat (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1,
          (f.appLE V U e).hom.Flat]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_tfae_and_resLE
declarations.doc:
The whole statement: the four characterizations of flatness agree, and flatness passes to
restrictions to open subschemes.

The source defines flatness of `f` by flatness of the local ring maps
`𝒪_{S, f(x)} → 𝒪_{X, x}`; this agrees with `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_tfae_and_resLE (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      Flat f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.Flat,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, Flat (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1,
          (f.appLE V U e).hom.Flat] ∧
    (Flat f → ∀ (U : X.Opens) (V : S.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), Flat (f.resLE V U e))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SyntomicAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is *syntomic at* `x : X` if there are affine open
neighbourhoods `U` of `x` and `V` of `f(x)`, with `f(U) ⊆ V`, for which the induced map
`Γ(S, V) → Γ(X, U)` is syntomic.
declarations.statement: def SyntomicAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Syntomic
declarations.doc: A morphism of schemes is syntomic if it is syntomic at every point of its source.
declarations.statement: abbrev Syntomic {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardSyntomic
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : X ⟶ S` of affine schemes is **standard syntomic** if the induced ring map
`Γ(S, ⊤) → Γ(X, ⊤)` is a relative global complete intersection. Via the canonical isomorphisms of
affine schemes with the spectra of their global sections, this says precisely that `f` is
isomorphic to the spectrum of a relative global complete intersection.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsStandardSyntomic {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField
declarations.doc:
A scheme over a field is a **local complete intersection over the field** if its structure
morphism to the spectrum of the field is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomic_tfae
declarations.doc:
The four characterizations of a syntomic morphism: the global condition, the condition on
every compatible pair of affine opens, an open-covering criterion, and an affine-open-covering
criterion on rings of sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomic_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      Syntomic f,
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (V : S.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
        (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
        letI : Algebra Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U) := (f.appLE V U hUV).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.Syntomic Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            ∀ i, Syntomic (f.resLE (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i,
                let hUV : U i ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V j := (le_iSup U i).trans hU.le
                letI : Algebra Γ(S, V j) Γ(X, U i) := (f.appLE (V j) (U i) hUV).hom.toAlgebra
                Algebra.Syntomic Γ(S, V j) Γ(X, U i)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomicAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `x : X` map to `s : S`, and let `V` be an affine open neighbourhood of `s`. Then the
following are equivalent:

1. `f` is syntomic at `x`;
2. some affine open neighbourhood `U` of `x`, mapping into `V`, makes the
   restricted morphism `U ⟶ V` standard syntomic;
3. `f` is of finite presentation at `x`, its map on local rings is flat, and
   its local fibre ring at `x` is a complete intersection over `κ(s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomicAt_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    (V : S.affineOpens) (_hxV : f x ∈ V.1) :
    List.TFAE [
      SyntomicAt f x,
      ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1) (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        IsStandardSyntomic (f.resLE V.1 U.1 hUV),
      AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentationAt f x ∧
        (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        (let A := S.presheaf.stalk (f x)
         let B := X.presheaf.stalk x
         letI : Algebra A B := (f.stalkMap x).hom.toAlgebra
         IsCompleteIntersection (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
           (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A ⊗[A] B))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomic_of_lci_fibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01UF.** A flat morphism of schemes which is locally of finite
presentation and whose every fibre is a local complete intersection over the residue field of
its base point is syntomic.
declarations.statement:
theorem syntomic_of_lci_fibers {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hlci : ∀ s : S, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s)) :
    Syntomic f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.localCompleteIntersection_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01UG.** For a scheme locally of finite type over a field, being a
local complete intersection is equivalent to the existence of affine neighbourhoods with
global-complete-intersection coordinate rings, and to all local rings being complete
intersections over the field.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCompleteIntersection_tfae (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    let globalCI := fun U : X.Opens ↦
      letI : Algebra k Γ(X, U) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ U (by simp)).hom.toAlgebra
      IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k Γ(X, U)
    let localCI := fun x : X ↦
      letI : Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
          X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x (by simp)).hom.toAlgebra
      IsCompleteIntersection k (X.presheaf.stalk x)
    List.TFAE [
      IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOverField f,
      ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, x ∈ U.1 ∧ globalCI U.1,
      ∀ x : X, localCI x]

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.SquareZeroExtension.sectionsEquivDerivations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01UP.** Relative derivations into the square-zero kernel act simply transitively
on the algebra sections of the extension. Under the resulting bijection, the derivation
corresponding to `t` is the pointwise difference `t - s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionsEquivDerivations {X : TopCat.{u}}
    {B O A : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{max u v} X}
    (α : B ⟶ O) (β : B ⟶ A) (π : A ⟶ O)
    (s : AlgebraSection α β π)
    (I : SheafOfModules.{max u v w} (underlyingRingSheaf O))
    (hI : SquareZeroKernel α β π s I) :
    ∃ e : AlgebraSection α β π ≃ SheafDerivation α I,
      ∀ (t : AlgebraSection α β π) (U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (a : O.obj.obj U),
        hI.ι U ((e t).d a) = t.hom.hom.app U a - s.hom.hom.app U a

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.cotangentDerivation
declarations.doc:
The universal `S`-derivation `d_{X/S} : 𝒪_X ⟶ Ω_{X/S}` that the sheaf of differentials of a
morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is equipped with: the universal derivation of the underlying
morphism of ringed spaces, read as a relative derivation over the structural map
`f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X` of `f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cotangentDerivation :
    SheafOfModules.SheafDerivation (inverseImageStructureMap f) (cotangentSheaf f)
declarations.comment: the universal S-derivation d_{X/S} that the sheaf of differentials `Stacks.Smooth.cotangentSheaf` of a morphism of schemes is equipped with

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.cotangentSheaf
declarations.doc:
The sheaf of relative differentials `Ω_{X/S}` of a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`, as a
sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules: the module of differentials of the morphism of sheaves of rings
`f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X`, which is how Stacks Project, Tag 01UM defines it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def cotangentSheaf {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : X.Modules
declarations.comment: the sheaf of differentials of a morphism of schemes, namely the differentials of the underlying morphism of ringed spaces; the universal S-derivation d_{X/S} it is equipped with is `Stacks.Smooth.cotangentDerivation`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.universalDerivation_isUniversal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 08RM.** Postcomposition with the universal
derivation gives the unique morphism from the module of relative
differentials to any coefficient sheaf.
declarations.comment: postcomposition with the universal derivation is bijective onto the derivations

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DifferentialsRestrict.existsUnique_relativeDifferentials_restrict
declarations.doc:
Restricting a morphism of schemes to compatible open subschemes identifies the
restriction of its sheaf of relative differentials with the sheaf of relative differentials
of the restricted morphism, and this is the unique identification carrying the restricted
universal derivation to the universal derivation.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_relativeDifferentials_restrict :
    ∃! i : Scheme.Modules.restrict (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f) U.ι ≅
        Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials (f.resLE V U e),
      ∀ (W : U.toScheme.Opens) (x : Γ(U.toScheme, W)),
        (i.hom.val.app (.op W)).hom
            ((Scheme.Modules.restrictAppIso U.ι
                (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f) W).inv.hom
              ((Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation f).d (((U.ι.appIso W).inv).hom x))) =
          (Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation (f.resLE V U e)).d x

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineDifferentialsIso.existsUnique_sectionsIso
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of the comparison of global differentials.** There is exactly one isomorphism
of `A`-modules from `Ω[A⁄R]` to the global differentials of `Spec φ` compatible with the
universal derivations.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_sectionsIso :
    ∃! e : CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential φ ≅
        moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials (Spec.map φ)),
      ∀ a : A, e.hom.hom (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d a) =
        (Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation (Spec.map φ)).d ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).inv a)
declarations.comment: affine case in the coordinate rings: the global differentials of Spec φ are Ω[A⁄R]

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineDifferentialsIso.existsUnique_tildeKaehlerIso
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of the comparison of sheaves.** There is exactly one isomorphism from the
quasi-coherent sheaf associated to `Ω[A⁄R]` to the sheaf of relative differentials of `Spec φ`
carrying the global section determined by the universal differential of `a : A` to the
universal relative differential of the global section of `𝒪_{Spec A}` corresponding to `a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_tildeKaehlerIso :
    ∃! e : (tilde.functor A).obj (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential φ) ≅
        Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials (Spec.map φ),
      ∀ a : A,
        (tilde.toTildeΓNatIso.hom.app (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential φ) ≫
            moduleSpecΓFunctor.map e.hom).hom (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d a) =
          (Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation (Spec.map φ)).d
            ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).inv a)
declarations.comment: affine case as a sheaf comparison: Ω_{Spec A/Spec R} is the sheaf of Ω[A⁄R]

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineDifferentialsIso.existsUnique_affineDifferentialsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01UT.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let `V` be an
affine open of `S` and let `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V` be an affine open of `X`. The sections of the sheaf
of relative differentials of `f` on `U` are *uniquely* isomorphic to the Kähler differentials
of `Γ(S, V) ⟶ Γ(X, U)`, compatibly with the universal derivations.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_affineDifferentialsIso (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    ∃! e : (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).val.obj (.op U) ≅
        CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential (f.appLE V U hUV),
      ∀ a : Γ(X, U), e.hom.hom ((Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation f).d a) =
        CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d a

declarations.name: Stacks.Smooth.existsUnique_linearEquiv_universalD
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes. For any pair of affine opens `Spec A = U ⊆ X` and
`Spec R = V ⊆ S` with `f(U) ⊆ V` there is a unique isomorphism

`Ω[A⁄R] ≃ₗ[A] Γ(Ω_{X/S}, U)`

compatible with `d_{X/S}` and with `d : A → Ω[A⁄R]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_linearEquiv_universalD (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
    letI := algebraAppLE f hUV
    ∃! e : Ω[Γ(X, U)⁄Γ(S, V)] ≃ₗ[Γ(X, U)] Γ(cotangentSheaf f, U),
      ∀ b : Γ(X, U), e (KaehlerDifferential.D Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U) b) = universalD f U b
declarations.comment: unique isomorphism Γ(U, Ω_{X/S}) = Ω_{A/R} compatible with the differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isBasis_affineOpensOver
declarations.doc:
**The affine opens over affine opens form a basis.** The affine opens of `X` mapping into
an affine open of `S` form a basis of the topology of `X`.
declarations.statement: theorem isBasis_affineOpensOver : Opens.IsBasis f.affineOpensOver
declarations.comment: the affine opens mapping into an affine open of the base form a basis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver
declarations.doc:
**The ansatz `Γ(U, Ω_{X/S}) = Ω_{A/R}`.** The presheaf of modules on the basis
`f.affineOpensOver`, over the restriction of `𝒪_X`, with sections the Kähler differentials
`Ω_{A/R}` over `U = Spec A` lying over `V = Spec R`. Its restriction maps are described by
`kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver_map_d`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver :
    _root_.PresheafOfModules.{u} (restrictRingSheafToBasis
      f.isBasis_affineOpensOver X.ringCatSheaf).obj
declarations.comment: the presheaf on the basis with sections the Kähler differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver_map_d
declarations.doc:
**The restriction maps.** For `U' ⊆ U` in the basis, the restriction map
`Ω_{A/R} ⟶ Ω_{A'/R'}` sends `d a` to `d (a|_{U'})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver_map_d
    {U U' : BasisCat f.affineOpensOver} (i : U' ⟶ U)
    (a : Γ(X, U.obj)) :
    (f.kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver.map i.op).hom (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d a) =
      CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d
        (X.presheaf.map ((basisInclusion _).map i).op a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isSheaf_kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver
declarations.doc: **The sheaf condition.** The presheaf with sections `Ω_{A/R}` is a sheaf on the basis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (basisGrothendieckTopology f.isBasis_affineOpensOver)
      f.kaehlerOnAffineOpensOver.presheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.restrictRelativeDifferentialsIso
declarations.doc:
**The construction gives `Ω_{X/S}`.** The restriction of the sheaf of relative
differentials to the basis `f.affineOpensOver` is the sheaf with sections `Ω_{A/R}`; on
sections it is the identification of Stacks 01UT
(`restrictRelativeDifferentialsIso_hom_app_d`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictRelativeDifferentialsIso :
    (restrictModuleSheaf.{u, u} f.isBasis_affineOpensOver
      X.ringCatSheaf).obj (relativeDifferentials f) ≅ f.kaehlerSheafOnAffineOpensOver
declarations.comment: the sheaf on the basis is the restriction of the sheaf of differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.nonempty_iso_relativeDifferentials_iff
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf on the basis determines `Ω_{X/S}`.** A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules is isomorphic to
the sheaf of relative differentials if and only if its restriction to the basis
`f.affineOpensOver` is isomorphic to the sheaf with sections `Ω_{A/R}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_relativeDifferentials_iff (M : X.Modules) :
    Nonempty (M ≅ relativeDifferentials f) ↔
      Nonempty ((restrictModuleSheaf.{u, u} f.isBasis_affineOpensOver
        X.ringCatSheaf).obj M ≅ f.kaehlerSheafOnAffineOpensOver)
declarations.comment: the sheaf on the basis determines the sheaf of differentials

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.existsUnique_relativeDifferentialsMap
declarations.doc:
A commutative square of schemes induces a unique morphism `f^* Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X'/S'}`
carrying the universal differential of every local section to the universal differential of
its pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_relativeDifferentialsMap {X' X S' S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (p : X ⟶ S) (p' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (hcomm : f ≫ p = p' ≫ g) :
    ∃! c : (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj (relativeDifferentials p) ⟶
      relativeDifferentials p', IsRelativeDifferentialsMap f p p' c

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isRelativeDifferentialsMap_iff_eq
declarations.doc:
Compatibility with the universal derivations characterizes the canonical morphism on
relative differentials associated to a commutative square of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeDifferentialsMap_iff_eq {X' X S' S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (p : X ⟶ S) (p' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (hcomm : f ≫ p = p' ≫ g)
    (c : (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj (relativeDifferentials p) ⟶
      relativeDifferentials p') :
    IsRelativeDifferentialsMap f p p' c ↔ c = relativeDifferentialsMap f p p' g hcomm

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedSpaceDifferentials.differentialMap_comp
declarations.doc:
Functoriality, composition: the comparison map of a vertical composite of two commutative
diagrams of ringed spaces is the composite of the comparison maps, after the canonical
identification `(f' ≫ f)^* ⟶ f'^* (f^*)`. This is the relation `c_{f ∘ f'} = c_{f'} ∘ (f')^* c_f`
of Tag 01UW.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialMap_comp :
    differentialMap (f' ≫ f) h h'' (g' ≫ g) hcomm''
      = modulePullbackComparison f f' (moduleOfDifferentials h) ≫
        ((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.modulePullback f').map
            (differentialMap f h h' g hcomm) ≫ differentialMap f' h' h'' g' hcomm')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toRelativeDifferentials_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01UX.** The canonical map `Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y}` of a composable pair of
morphisms of schemes is an epimorphism; equivalently, the canonical sequence
`f^* Ω_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0` is exact at `Ω_{X/Y}`. For the underlying ringed spaces
this is Stacks Project, Tag 0H79.
declarations.statement:
theorem toRelativeDifferentials_epi (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) :
    Epi (f.toRelativeDifferentials g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toRelativeDifferentials_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01UX.** For morphisms of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ S` the
canonical maps of relative differentials, both obtained from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsMap`, form a complex
`f^* Ω_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y}` which is exact at `Ω_{X/S}`. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toRelativeDifferentials_epi` this is the exactness of
`f^* Ω_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X/Y} ⟶ 0`. For the underlying ringed spaces this is Stacks
Project, Tag 0H79.
declarations.statement:
theorem toRelativeDifferentials_exact (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) :
    ∃ h : relativeDifferentialsMap f g (f ≫ g) (𝟙 S) (Category.comp_id (f ≫ g)).symm ≫
        f.toRelativeDifferentials g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk _ _ h).Exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isZero_relativeDifferentials_of_mono
declarations.doc: The sheaf of relative differentials of a monomorphism of schemes is a zero object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_relativeDifferentials_of_mono (f : X ⟶ S) [Mono f] :
    IsZero (relativeDifferentials f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isZero_relativeDifferentials_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc: The sheaf of relative differentials of an immersion of schemes is a zero object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_relativeDifferentials_of_isImmersion (f : X ⟶ S) [IsImmersion f] :
    IsZero (relativeDifferentials f)
declarations.comment: the immersion case named in the first clause of the statement

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.differentialsMapOver_epi
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01UZ], exactness at the right term.** For an immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of
schemes over `S`, the canonical map `i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S}` of [Stacks, Tag 01UV] is an
epimorphism, so the conormal sequence of `i` ends in zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem differentialsMapOver_epi (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] (p : X ⟶ S) :
    Epi (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsMap i p (i ≫ p) (𝟙 S) (by simp))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.conormalDifferential
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01UZ], the first arrow.** For an immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of schemes over `S`,
the canonical morphism `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S}` induced by `d_{X/S}`: the adjoint transpose of
the map carrying a section `f` of the defining ideal sheaf of the closed factor to `1 ⊗ d f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalDifferential :
    (conormalSheaf i : Z.Modules) ⟶
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials p)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.equationDifferentialsComplexOver_exact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01UZ], exactness at the middle term.** For an immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of schemes
over `S` cut out by global sections `f j` of `𝒪_X`, the conormal sequence is exact at
`i^*Ω_{X/S}`: the kernel of the canonical map `i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S}` of [Stacks, Tag 01UV] is
generated by the pulled-back differentials `d (f j)`, which generate the image of the conormal
module of the immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem equationDifferentialsComplexOver_exact (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i] (p : X ⟶ S)
    {I : Type u} (f : I → Γ(X, ⊤)) (hf : IsCutOutBy i f) :
    (equationDifferentialsComplex i p (by simp) f hf).Exact

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.conormalShortComplex_exact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01UZ], exactness at the middle term of the conormal sequence,
unconditionally.** For an immersion of schemes `i : Z ⟶ X` over `p : X ⟶ S` the conormal
sequence `𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S} ⟶ 0` is exact at `i^*Ω_{X/S}`: the image of the
conormal differential is the kernel of the canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 01UV].

No hypothesis beyond `IsImmersion i` is used, and the sequence is the canonical one rather than
a presentation by equations. Injectivity of the first arrow, which would make the sequence short
exact, is false in general and holds under the smoothness hypothesis of [Stacks, Tag 06AA]; see
`Stacks.ConormalSequenceRight.conormalShortComplex_shortExact`.
declarations.statement: theorem conormalShortComplex_exact (p : X ⟶ S) : (conormalShortComplex i p).Exact
declarations.comment:
exactness at the middle term of the sequence 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ i^*Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{Z/S},
for an arbitrary immersion and with the conormal sheaf itself at the left-hand end

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsMap
registrations.comment: the functorial second arrow

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isIso_relativeDifferentialsMap_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01V0.** For a cartesian square of schemes with left edge `f' : X' ⟶ S'`,
right edge `f : X ⟶ S` and top edge `g' : X' ⟶ X`, the canonical map
`g'^* Ω_{X/S} ⟶ Ω_{X'/S'}` of Tag 01UV is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_relativeDifferentialsMap_of_isPullback {X' X S' S : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (f' : X' ⟶ S') (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (h : IsPullback g' f' f g) :
    IsIso (relativeDifferentialsMap g' f f' g h.w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isIso_biprodDesc_relativeDifferentialsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01V1.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` and `g : Y ⟶ S` be morphisms of schemes with
the same target and let `p : W ⟶ X`, `q : W ⟶ Y` be the projections of a fibre product of `f` and
`g`. The two canonical maps of Tag 01UV give an isomorphism
`p^* Ω_{X/S} ⊕ q^* Ω_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω_{W/S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_biprodDesc_relativeDifferentialsMap {W X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (p : W ⟶ X) (q : W ⟶ Y)
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (h : IsPullback p q f g) :
    IsIso (biprod.desc
      (relativeDifferentialsMap p f (p ≫ f) (𝟙 S) (Category.comp_id (p ≫ f)).symm)
      (relativeDifferentialsMap q g (p ≫ f) (𝟙 S)
        (h.w.symm.trans (Category.comp_id (p ≫ f)).symm)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isFiniteType_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01V2.** The sheaf of relative differentials of a morphism of schemes
which is locally of finite type is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite type.
declarations.statement:
instance Scheme.Hom.isFiniteType_relativeDifferentials (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).IsFiniteType

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isFinitePresentation_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01V3.** The sheaf of relative differentials of a morphism of schemes
which is locally of finite presentation is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
instance Scheme.Hom.isFinitePresentation_relativeDifferentials (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).IsFinitePresentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardSmooth
declarations.doc:
A morphism of affine schemes is standard smooth if the corresponding ring homomorphism on
global sections is standard smooth.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsStandardSmooth {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}}
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine X] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

registrations.comment: smooth_at_point

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth
registrations.comment: smooth_morphism

declarations.name: RingHom.Smooth.stacksPropertyIsLocal
declarations.doc: Smoothness of ring maps is a local property.
declarations.statement: theorem Smooth.stacksPropertyIsLocal : StacksPropertyIsLocal RingHom.Smooth
declarations.comment: smoothness of ring maps is local

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_resLE
declarations.doc:
If `f` is smooth then so is its restriction `U → V` to any opens `U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ S` with
`f(U) ⊆ V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_resLE {f : X ⟶ S} (hf : Smooth f) (V : S.Opens) (U : X.Opens)
    (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) : Smooth (f.resLE V U e)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_tfae
declarations.doc:
Smoothness of a morphism of schemes can be checked on all pairs of affine opens, on open
coverings of target and preimages, or on affine such coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_tfae (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      Smooth f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.Smooth,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, Smooth (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1,
          (f.appLE V U e).hom.Smooth]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_tfae_and_resLE
declarations.doc:
The whole statement: the four characterizations of smoothness agree, and smoothness passes
to restrictions to open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_tfae_and_resLE (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE [
      Smooth f,
      ∀ (V : S.affineOpens) (U : X.affineOpens) (e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        (f.appLE V U e).hom.Smooth,
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.Opens, sSup 𝒱 = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.Opens, sSup 𝒰 = f ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V, Smooth (f.resLE V U e),
      ∃ 𝒱 : Set S.affineOpens, (⨆ V ∈ 𝒱, V.1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝒱, ∃ 𝒰 : Set X.affineOpens,
        (⨆ U ∈ 𝒰, U.1) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1 ∧ ∀ U ∈ 𝒰, ∃ e : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1,
          (f.appLE V U e).hom.Smooth] ∧
    (Smooth f → ∀ (U : X.Opens) (V : S.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), Smooth (f.resLE V U e))

declarations.name: InfinitesimalLifting.smoothAt_iff_exists_affine_isStandardSmooth
declarations.doc:
Smoothness at a point is equivalent to standard smoothness on a suitable affine
neighbourhood lying over any prescribed affine neighbourhood of the image point.
declarations.statement:
public lemma smoothAt_iff_exists_affine_isStandardSmooth
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) (V : S.Opens)
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hxV : x ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
    InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x ↔
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : x ∈ U)
        (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
        @AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardSmooth
          U.toScheme V.toScheme hU hV (f.resLE V U hUV)

declarations.name: Stacks.FiberCotangentAssembly.fiberDifferentialsTensorIdentification
declarations.doc:
The fibre of the sheaf of relative differentials at `x` is canonically identified with the
fibre of the relative differentials of the scheme-theoretic fibre.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fiberDifferentialsTensorIdentification :
    FiberDifferentialsTensorIdentification f x

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag01V9NumericalCriterion.smoothAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a morphism locally of finite presentation, the following
are equivalent: smoothness at `x`; flatness of the local-ring map together with smoothness of the
scheme-theoretic fibre; either of the two numerical differential criteria; a standard smooth
affine neighbourhood; and an affine presentation whose chosen Jacobian determinant does not
vanish at `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smoothAt_tfae [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    List.TFAE [
      InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x,
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (f x)) (f.asFiber x),
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        (let B := X.presheaf.stalk x
         let Ω := relativeDifferentialStalk f x
         letI := relativeDifferentialStalkModule f x
         GeneratedByAtMost B Ω (topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x))),
      (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat ∧
        (let k := X.residueField x
         GeneratedByAtMost k (relativeCotangentSpace f x)
           (topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x))),
      ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : S.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1)
          (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardSmooth (f.resLE V.1 U.1 hUV),
      ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : S.affineOpens) (hxU : x ∈ U.1)
          (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        letI : Algebra Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, U.1) := (f.appLE V U hUV).hom.toAlgebra
        ∃ (n c : ℕ) (P : Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation
            Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, U.1) (Fin n) (Fin c)),
          P.jacobian ∉ (U.2.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hxU⟩).asIdeal]
