declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VH.** An invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` is *ample relative to* `f : X ⟶ S` when
`f` is quasi-compact and, for every affine open `V` of `S`, the restriction of `L` to the open
subscheme `f⁻¹(V)` is ample. The restriction is the module pullback along the open immersion of
`f⁻¹(V)`, whose invertibility is Stacks Tag 0B8L, and ampleness is Stacks Tag 01PS.
declarations.statement:
def IsRelativelyAmple {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsRelativelyAmple.isSeparated
declarations.doc: A morphism of schemes admitting a relatively ample invertible sheaf is separated.

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple.quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VJ, clause (5), the quasi-separatedness assertion.** A morphism carrying a
relatively ample invertible module is quasi-separated. It is in fact separated, which is
[Stacks, Tag 01VI] and is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsRelativelyAmple.isSeparated`; a separated
morphism is quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRelativelyAmple.quasiSeparated {X S : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {L : X.Modules}
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsRelativelyAmple f L) : QuasiSeparated f
declarations.comment: (5), the quasi-separatedness assertion: a morphism carrying a relatively ample invertible module is quasi-separated

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.isQuasicoherent_gradedDirectImage_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**The pieces of `𝒜` in nonnegative degree are quasi-coherent**, for a relatively ample `L`:
both hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 01LC] are then available, quasi-compactness from
[Stacks, Tag 01VH] and quasi-separatedness from
`Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple.quasiSeparated`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_gradedDirectImage_of_isRelativelyAmple
    (hL : IsRelativelyAmple f L) (d : ℕ) :
    (gradedDirectImage f L (d : ℤ)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: (5), the homogeneous pieces of the graded algebra A = f_*(⨁_{d ≥ 0} L^{⊗ d}) of the clause: their quasi-coherence in nonnegative degree (the step the source attributes to Schemes 26.24.1) and their vanishing in negative degree. The graded algebra A itself, with its multiplication, is Stacks.RelativeAmple.directImageAlgebra; see the module docstring

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.iSup_nonvanishingOpenOn_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VJ, clause (5), the assertion `U(ψ) = X`.** For `L` ample relative to `f`,
the nonvanishing opens of the sections of positive degree of `𝒜 = f_*(⨁_{d ≥ 0} L^{⊗ d})` cover
`X`.

The supremum is over triples of an affine open `V` of `S`, a degree `d ≥ 1`, and a section of
`𝒜_d` over `V`; `U(ψ)` is the union of exactly these nonvanishing opens, since the degree-`d`
component of the adjunction map `ψ` is the identity on sections over `V` under
`sections_gradedDirectImage`. See the section "Why `U(ψ) = X` is the supremum below" of the
module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem iSup_nonvanishingOpenOn_eq_top (hL : IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    (⨆ p : Σ' (V : S.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (d : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ d),
        Γ(gradedDirectImage f L (d : ℤ), V),
      nonvanishingOpenOn (tensorPowModule X L (p.2.2.1 : ℤ)) (f ⁻¹ᵁ p.1) p.2.2.2.2) = ⊤
declarations.comment: (5), the assertion U(psi) = X: for L ample relative to f, the nonvanishing opens of the positive-degree sections of A = f_*(⨁_{d ≥ 0} L^{⊗ d}) cover X

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmpleLocalOnBase.isRelativelyAmple_of_forall_exists_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VJ, clause (3) implies clause (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact
morphism of schemes and `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. If every point of `S` has an affine open
neighbourhood `V` with `L|_{f⁻¹V}` ample, then `L` is ample relative to `f`, that is, `L|_{f⁻¹V}`
is ample for *every* affine open `V ⊆ S`.

For an affine open `W ⊆ S` the preimage `f⁻¹W` is covered by the preimages of basic opens of `W`
lying inside members of the given covering, and on each of those the restriction of `L` is ample
by [Stacks, Tag 0B3E]; those preimages are the basic opens of the pullbacks to `f⁻¹W` of the
cutting functions, so
`Stacks.RelativeAmpleLocalOnBase.isAmple_of_basicOpen_cover` assembles them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_of_forall_exists_isAmple {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hf : QuasiCompact f)
    (hcov : ∀ x : S, ∃ V : S.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧
      IsAmple (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme (Stacks.AmpleLocallyClosed.pullbackModule (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι L)) :
    Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L
declarations.comment: (3) implies (1): relative ampleness may be checked on an affine open covering

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmpleLocalOnBase.exists_affine_isAmple_cover_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VJ, clause (1) implies clause (3).** A relatively ample module restricts to an
ample module on the preimage of *some* affine open neighbourhood of every point of the base,
because the affine opens of the base are a basis of its topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_isAmple_cover_of_isRelativelyAmple {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) (x : S) :
    ∃ V : S.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧
      IsAmple (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme (Stacks.AmpleLocallyClosed.pullbackModule (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι L)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3): the affine opens of the base are such a covering

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple.isOpenImmersion_globalMorphism
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01VJ], (1) implies the open-immersion assertion of (5).** For `L` ample relative
to `f`, with `𝒜 = f_*(⨁_{d ≥ 0} L^{⊗ d})` and `ψ` the adjunction map, the morphism
`r_{L, ψ} : U(ψ) ⟶ Proj_S(𝒜)` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRelativelyAmple.isOpenImmersion_globalMorphism (hL : IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    haveI := hL.quasiCompact
    haveI := hL.quasiSeparated
    IsOpenImmersion
      ((directImagePowerMap f L).globalMorphism (relativeProj (directImageAlgebra f L)))
declarations.comment: (1) implies (5), the assertion that r_{L,psi} is an open immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.isRelativelyAmple_of_isImmersion_globalMorphism
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01VJ], (6) implies (1).** Let `f` be quasi-compact, `𝒜` a quasi-coherent
graded `𝒪_S`-algebra and `ψ : f^*𝒜 ⟶ ⨁_{d ≥ 0} L^{⊗ d}` a graded map with `U(ψ) = X` such that
`r_{L, ψ} : X ⟶ Proj_S(𝒜)` is an immersion. Then `L` is ample relative to `f`.

Over an affine open `V` of `S` the morphism is an immersion `f⁻¹V ⟶ Proj 𝒜(V)` by
`globalMorphism_iff`, and `isAmple_of_isImmersion_glued` gives ampleness of `L|_{f⁻¹V}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_of_isImmersion_globalMorphism (hf : QuasiCompact f)
    {A : SheafGradedAlgebra.{u} S} (P : GradedPowerMap A f) (e : P.L ≅ L)
    (hU : P.coveringOpen = ⊤) (hP : IsImmersion (P.globalMorphism (relativeProj A))) :
    IsRelativelyAmple f L

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.isRelativelyAmple_of_isOpenImmersion_globalMorphism
declarations.doc: **[Stacks, Tag 01VJ], (4) implies (1)**: an open immersion is an immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_of_isOpenImmersion_globalMorphism (hf : QuasiCompact f)
    {A : SheafGradedAlgebra.{u} S} (P : GradedPowerMap A f) (e : P.L ≅ L)
    (hU : P.coveringOpen = ⊤) (hP : IsOpenImmersion (P.globalMorphism (relativeProj A))) :
    IsRelativelyAmple f L

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.isRelativelyAmple_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_tfae (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules)
    [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsRelativelyAmple f L,
      ∀ x : S, ∃ V : S.Opens, x ∈ V ∧
        IsRelativelyAmple (f ∣_ V) (Stacks.AmpleLocallyClosed.pullbackModule (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι L),
      ∀ x : S, ∃ V : S.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧
        Stacks.Ample.IsAmple (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme
          (Stacks.AmpleLocallyClosed.pullbackModule (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι L),
      ∃ (A : SheafGradedAlgebra.{u} S) (P : GradedPowerMap A f), Nonempty (P.L ≅ L) ∧
        P.coveringOpen = ⊤ ∧ IsOpenImmersion (P.globalMorphism (relativeProj A)),
      ∃ h : QuasiSeparated f,
        haveI := h
        (directImagePowerMap f L).coveringOpen = ⊤ ∧ IsOpenImmersion
          ((directImagePowerMap f L).globalMorphism (relativeProj (directImageAlgebra f L))),
      ∃ (A : SheafGradedAlgebra.{u} S) (P : GradedPowerMap A f), Nonempty (P.L ≅ L) ∧
        P.coveringOpen = ⊤ ∧ IsImmersion (P.globalMorphism (relativeProj A))]

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmpleRestrictBase.isRelativelyAmple_morphismRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VJ, clause (1) implies clause (2).** If `L` is ample relative to `f : X ⟶ S`
then, for *every* open `V ⊆ S`, the restriction `L|_{f⁻¹V}` is ample relative to the restricted
morphism `f ∣_ V : f⁻¹V ⟶ V`. In particular every open covering of `S` — for instance the
one-member covering `{S}` — witnesses clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01VJ].

Quasi-compactness of `f ∣_ V` holds because quasi-compactness of a morphism is local on the
target. For an affine open `A ⊆ V` the image `W = V.ι ''ᵁ A` is an affine open of `S`, where
clause (1) gives ampleness of `L|_{f⁻¹W}`, and
`Stacks.RelativeAmpleRestrictBase.isAmple_preimage_morphismRestrict_iff` moves it onto
`(f ∣_ V)⁻¹A`.

This also records that `Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple` restricts to an open of the
base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_morphismRestrict
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) (V : S.Opens) :
    Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple (f ∣_ V) (pullbackModule (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι L)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2): relative ampleness is inherited by the restriction of the morphism over an arbitrary open of the base, so every open covering witnesses clause (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmpleRestrictBase.isRelativelyAmple_of_forall_exists_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VJ, clause (2) implies clause (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be quasi-compact and `L`
invertible. If every point of `S` has an open neighbourhood `V` such that `L|_{f⁻¹V}` is ample
relative to `f ∣_ V : f⁻¹V ⟶ V`, then `L` is ample relative to `f`.

The affine opens of `S` are a basis, so each `V` contains an affine open `W` around the given
point, and `V.ι⁻¹W` is then an affine open of `V`. Relative ampleness over `V` gives ampleness
on `(f ∣_ V)⁻¹(V.ι⁻¹W)`, which
`Stacks.RelativeAmpleRestrictBase.isAmple_preimage_morphismRestrict_iff` turns into ampleness of
`L|_{f⁻¹W}`. That is an affine open covering of the kind
`Stacks.RelativeAmpleLocalOnBase.isRelativelyAmple_of_forall_exists_isAmple` — clause (3) implies
clause (1) — consumes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_of_forall_exists_isRelativelyAmple (hf : QuasiCompact f)
    (hcov : ∀ x : S, ∃ V : S.Opens, x ∈ V ∧ Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple (f ∣_ V)
      (pullbackModule (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι L)) :
    Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1): relative ampleness over the members of an arbitrary open covering of the base implies relative ampleness

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmpleAffineBase.isRelativelyAmple_iff_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VK.** Over an affine base, an invertible `𝒪_X`-module is ample relative to
`f : X ⟶ S` if and only if it is ample on `X`.

Both implications are `Stacks.AmplePullback.isAmple_modulePullback_of_isAffineHom`, the
unconditional case of Stacks Tag 0B3E for an affine morphism. Forwards, at `V = ⊤`: the hypothesis
gives ampleness of the restriction of `L` to `f⁻¹(⊤) = ⊤`, and
`Stacks.RelativeAmpleAffineBase.isAmple_of_isAmple_modulePullback` descends it along the
isomorphism `⊤ ⟶ X`. Backwards: quasi-compactness of `f` over an affine base is quasi-compactness
of `X`, and on each affine open `V` of `S` the open immersion of `f⁻¹V` is an affine morphism by
`Stacks.RelativeAmpleAffineBase.isAffineHom_preimage_ι`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_iff_isAmple {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] :
    Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L ↔ IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VM: relative very ampleness.** An invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` is *very ample
relative to* `f : X ⟶ S` when there are a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `E` and an immersion
`i : X ⟶ 𝐏(E) = Proj_S(Sym(E))` over `S` with `L ≅ i^* 𝒪_{𝐏(E)}(1)`.
declarations.statement:
def IsRelativelyVeryAmple {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.isRelativelyAmple_of_isRelativelyVeryAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VN** (EGA II, Proposition 4.6.2). Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and
`L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. If `f` is quasi-compact and `L` is very ample relative to `f`,
then `L` is ample relative to `f`.

Relative very ampleness is [Stacks, Tag 01VM] at the named twist of the projective bundle:
an immersion `i : X ⟶ 𝐏(E)` over `S` into the projective bundle of a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module `E`, with `L ≅ i^* 𝒪_{𝐏(E)}(1)`. Relative ampleness is [Stacks, Tag 01VH]:
quasi-compactness of `f` together with ampleness of `L|_{f⁻¹V}` for every affine open `V ⊆ S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_of_isRelativelyVeryAmple {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] (hf : QuasiCompact f)
    (hL : Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f L) :
    IsRelativelyAmple f L

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjEvenPowerRoots.instGradedAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**The graded-algebra structure on `A`**, the decomposition of the quotient by the homogeneous
relation ideal.
declarations.statement: public instance instGradedAlgebra : _root_.GradedAlgebra (grading k)
declarations.comment: the graded algebra of the example

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjEvenPowerRoots.sup_basicOpen_eq_top
declarations.doc: **`X = Proj A` is covered by the two standard opens `D₊(U)` and `D₊(V)`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem sup_basicOpen_eq_top :
    Proj.basicOpen (grading k) (uGen k) ⊔ Proj.basicOpen (grading k) (vGen k) = ⊤
declarations.comment: the two-chart cover of the example

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjEvenPowerRoots.isInvertible_twistingSheaf
declarations.doc: **Every twist `𝒪_X(n)` is invertible**, although `A` is not generated in degree one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInvertible_twistingSheaf (n : ℤ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (grading k)).toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (grading k)).toRingedSpace).property
      (twistingSheaf (grading k) n)
declarations.comment: invertibility of the twists on the example

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjEvenPowerRoots.isIso_twistMultiplicationMap
declarations.doc:
**The multiplication `𝒪_X(n) ⊗ 𝒪_X(m) → 𝒪_X(n + m)` is an isomorphism**, so each `𝒪_X(n)` is
the `n`-th tensor power of `𝒪_X(1)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_twistMultiplicationMap (n m : ℤ) :
    IsIso (twistMultiplicationMap (grading k) n m)
declarations.comment: the twists are tensor powers of the first twist

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjEvenPowerRoots.isAmple_twistingModule_one
declarations.doc: **`𝒪_X(1)` is an ample invertible sheaf on `X = Proj A`.**
declarations.comment: the ample invertible sheaf on the example

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjEvenPowerRoots.not_isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPowModule
declarations.doc:
**No power `𝒪_X(1)^{⊗ n}` with `n ≥ 1` is `f`-relatively very ample**, for `f : X ⟶ Spec k`
the structure morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_isRelativelyVeryAmple_tensorPowModule (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    letI := isInvertible_twistingSheaf k 1
    ¬ Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple (structureMorphism k)
      (Stacks.Ample.tensorPowModule (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (grading k))
        (Stacks.ProjTwistSection.twistingModule (grading k) 1) (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: no power of `𝒪_X(1)` is `f`-relatively very ample

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjEvenPowerRoots.isRelativelyAmple_twistingModule_one
declarations.doc: **`𝒪_X(1)` is `f`-ample** for the structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`.

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjHyperellipticDoubleCover.instGradedAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**The graded-algebra structure on `A_d`.** It is constructed: the relation ideal is
homogeneous because the relation is weighted homogeneous, and the grading is the decomposition of
the quotient by a homogeneous ideal.
declarations.statement: public instance instGradedAlgebra : _root_.GradedAlgebra (grading k d lam)
declarations.comment: the graded algebra of the example

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjHyperellipticDoubleCover.sup_basicOpen_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**`X_d = Proj A_d` is covered by the two standard opens `D₊(U)` and `D₊(V)`.** The three
variables generate `A_d` over `(A_d)₀ = k`, so their standard opens cover, and `D₊(Z)` is
contained in the union of the other two.
declarations.comment: the two-chart cover of the example

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjHyperellipticDoubleCover.isInvertible_twistingSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Every twist `𝒪_{X_d}(n)` is invertible.** For `d ≥ 2` the algebra `A_d` is not generated in
degree one, so this does not come from degree-one generation; the two-chart cover is what
supplies it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInvertible_twistingSheaf (hd : 0 < d) (n : ℤ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (grading k d lam)).toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (grading k d lam)).toRingedSpace).property
      (twistingSheaf (grading k d lam) n)
declarations.comment: invertibility of the twists on the example

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjHyperellipticDoubleCover.isIso_twistMultiplicationMap
declarations.doc:
**The multiplication `𝒪_{X_d}(n) ⊗ 𝒪_{X_d}(m) → 𝒪_{X_d}(n + m)` is an isomorphism**, so each
`𝒪_{X_d}(n)` is the `n`-th tensor power of `𝒪_{X_d}(1)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_twistMultiplicationMap (hd : 0 < d) (n m : ℤ) :
    IsIso (twistMultiplicationMap (grading k d lam) n m)
declarations.comment: the twists are tensor powers of the first twist

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjHyperellipticDoubleCover.isAmple_twistingModule_one
declarations.doc:
**`𝒪_{X_d}(1)` is an ample invertible sheaf on `X_d = Proj A_d`** — the positive assertion of
the example. `X_d` is quasi-compact and every point lies in the affine standard open of one of
the degree-one elements `U`, `V`.
declarations.comment: the ample invertible sheaf on the example

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjHyperellipticDoubleCover.bijective_degreeSection_binaryForm
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01VP]: `Γ(X_d, 𝒪_{X_d}(n)) = k[U, V]_n` for `0 ≤ n < d`.** The map sending a
binary form `p` of degree `n` to the global section `p / 1` of `𝒪_{X_d}(n)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_degreeSection_binaryForm (hd : 0 < d) {n : ℕ} (hn : n < d) :
    Function.Bijective fun p : homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n =>
      AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.degreeSection (grading k d lam) n
        ⟨binaryForm k d lam p, binaryForm_mem k d lam ((mem_homogeneousSubmodule _ _).mp p.2)⟩
declarations.comment: the global sections of the twists of degree less than d

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjHyperellipticDoubleCover.le_of_isRelativelyVeryAmple
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01VP]: if `𝒪_{X_d}(n)` is very ample, then `n ≥ d`.** Here very ample is
relative to any morphism from `X_d` to an affine scheme, the case of the structure morphism
`X_d → Spec k` included.

The proof is the source's. Very ampleness gives an immersion `α : X_d → 𝐏(E)` with
`𝒪_{X_d}(n) ≅ α^* 𝒪(1)`, and over an affine base `𝐏(E)` is the `Proj` of a graded ring generated
in degree one. For `n < d` every global section of `𝒪(n)` is a form in `U`, `V` alone near the
branch point `(λ₁ : 1 : 0)` — this is `Γ(X_d, 𝒪(n)) = k[U, V]_n` — so the two `k[ε]`-points
`Z ↦ ε` and `Z ↦ 0` at the branch point, which agree on `U` and `V`, have the same image under
`α`. An immersion is a monomorphism, and the two points are different.
declarations.statement:
public theorem le_of_isRelativelyVeryAmple (hd : 0 < d) {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
    (f : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (grading k d lam) ⟶ S) (n : ℤ)
    (h : @Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple _ _ f
      (Stacks.ProjTwistSection.twistingModule (grading k d lam) n)
      (isInvertible_twistingSheaf k d lam hd n)) :
    (d : ℤ) ≤ n
declarations.comment: very ampleness of a twist forces its degree to be at least d

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag01VMRelativeVeryAmple.isSeparated_of_isRelativelyVeryAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VQ: a morphism admitting a relatively very ample invertible sheaf is
separated.**

Relative very ampleness gives an immersion `i : X ⟶ 𝐏(E)` over the base. The structure morphism
of `𝐏(E) = relativeProj (symAlgebra E)` is separated, an immersion is a monomorphism and hence
separated, and separatedness is stable under composition; the composite is `f`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.tfae_isRelativelyVeryAmple
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isRelativelyVeryAmple (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] :
    List.TFAE [IsRelativelyVeryAmple f L, IsRelativelyVeryAmpleLocallyOnBase f L,
      HasImmersionToRelativeProj f L, IsImmersionDirectImageBundle f L]

declarations.name: Stacks.StalkwiseGeneration.exists_immersion_projectiveSpaceOver_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01VS].** For `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type and `L` an ample invertible
`𝒪_X`-module there is a `d₀ ≥ 1` such that every degree `d ≥ d₀` admits an immersion
`i : X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` over `S` pulling the twisting sheaf `𝒪(1)` back to `L ^⊗ d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_immersion_projectiveSpaceOver_of_isAmple {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsAmple X L) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    ∃ d₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ d₀ ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOver n S),
        IsImmersion i ∧
        i ≫ pullback.fst (terminal.from S)
          (terminal.from (projectiveSpaceAtUniverse.{u} n)) = f ∧
        Nonempty (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ) ≅
          (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj (projectiveSpaceTwistingSheaf n S))

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.tfae
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01VT], conditions (1), (2), (5) and (6), unconditionally.** For `f : X ⟶ S`
of finite type with `S` affine and `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, the following are equivalent:

1. `L` is ample on `X`;
2. `L` is ample relative to `f`;
3. (the source's (5)) `L ^⊗ d` is `𝒪(1)` pulled back along an immersion `X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` over `S`, for
   some `d ≥ 1`;
4. (the source's (6)) the same, for every sufficiently large `d`.

The cycle is (1) ⟹ (4) ⟹ (3) ⟹ (2) ⟹ (1). The first step is [Stacks, Tag 01VS] at the single
situation `(X, S, f, L)` — no covering of the base and no glueing, which is what affineness of
`S` buys — the second is dropping the lower bound on the degree, the third is [Stacks, Tag 01VN]
together with [Stacks, Tag 02NN], and the last two are the two halves of [Stacks, Tag 01VK].

The source's conditions (3) and (4), relative very ampleness, are not among the four; they join
them in `Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.tfae_six`, in the sibling module
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.VeryAmple`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsAmple X L,
      Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L,
      ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ HasImmersionTwistOver f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ)),
      ∃ d₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ d₀ ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
        HasImmersionTwistOver f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ))]
declarations.comment: conditions (1), (2), (5) and (6) of the six; conditions (3) and (4), relative very ampleness, are stated together with these four by `Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.tfae_six`, and (5), (6) are taken with no lower bound on `n`, which `Stacks.AmpleProjectiveImmersion.hasImmersionTwistOverPos_iff` shows is the source's `n ≥ 1` clause

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.tfae_six
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_six [IsAffine S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsAmple X L,
      Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L,
      ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
        Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ)),
      ∃ d₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ d₀ ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
        Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ)),
      ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ HasImmersionTwistOver f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ)),
      ∃ d₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ d₀ ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
        HasImmersionTwistOver f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ))]
declarations.comment: all six conditions, with no named input: ampleness, `f`-ampleness, relative very ampleness of some and of every sufficiently high tensor power, and the two immersion clauses; the immersion clauses are taken with no lower bound on the dimension `n` of the projective space, where the source writes `n ≥ 1` — the two agree by `Stacks.AmpleProjectiveImmersion.hasImmersionTwistOverPos_iff`, and `Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.tfae_six_pos` is the list with the source's clauses

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.isAmple_iff_exists_isRelativelyVeryAmple
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of (1) and (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01VT]**: `L` is ample exactly when some
tensor power `L ^⊗ d` with `d ≥ 1` is very ample relative to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_iff_exists_isRelativelyVeryAmple [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    IsAmple X L ↔ ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
      Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (3): ampleness and relative very ampleness of some positive tensor power

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.isAmple_iff_eventually_isRelativelyVeryAmple
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of (1) and (4) of [Stacks, Tag 01VT]**: `L` is ample exactly when every
sufficiently high tensor power of `L` is very ample relative to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_iff_eventually_isRelativelyVeryAmple [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    IsAmple X L ↔ ∃ d₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ d₀ ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
      Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (4): ampleness and relative very ampleness of every sufficiently high tensor power

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.tfae_six_pos
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01VT], all six conditions, with the source's own immersion clauses.** The
immersion clauses (5) and (6) are
`Stacks.AmpleProjectiveImmersion.HasImmersionTwistOverPos`, which writes `∃ n ≥ 1` as the source
does, rather than `Stacks.AmpleProjectiveImmersion.HasImmersionTwistOver`'s `∃ n : ℕ`.

The two agree — `Stacks.AmpleProjectiveImmersion.hasImmersionTwistOverPos_iff` — because an
immersion into `ℙⁿ_S` composed with the linear embedding `ℙⁿ_S ↪ ℙᴺ_S` is an immersion into
`ℙᴺ_S` carrying the same hyperplane sheaf, so a witness at `n` gives one at `max n 1`. This is
therefore `Stacks.AmpleRelativeFiniteType.tfae_six` with two clauses rewritten, and the tag's
six conditions hold verbatim.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_six_pos [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsAmple X L,
      Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L,
      ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
        Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ)),
      ∃ d₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ d₀ ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
        Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ)),
      ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ HasImmersionTwistOverPos f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ)),
      ∃ d₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ d₀ ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d₀ ≤ d →
        HasImmersionTwistOverPos f (tensorPowModule X L (d : ℤ))]
declarations.comment: all six conditions verbatim and with no named input: ampleness, `f`-ampleness, relative very ampleness of some and of every sufficiently high tensor power, and the two immersion clauses with the source's lower bound `n ≥ 1` on the dimension of the projective space

declarations.name: Stacks.VeryAmplePowersQuasiCompactBase.existsVeryAmplePower_of_eventuallyVeryAmplePower
declarations.doc:
If every sufficiently high tensor power of `L` is very ample relative to `f`, then some
positive tensor power of `L` is very ample relative to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsVeryAmplePower_of_eventuallyVeryAmplePower (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (h : EventuallyVeryAmplePower f L) : ExistsVeryAmplePower f L

declarations.name: Stacks.VeryAmplePowersQuasiCompactBase.isRelativelyAmple_of_existsVeryAmplePower
declarations.doc:
If some positive tensor power of `L` is very ample relative to a quasi-compact `f`, then `L` is
ample relative to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_of_existsVeryAmplePower (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hf : QuasiCompact f) (h : ExistsVeryAmplePower f L) :
    Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L

declarations.name: Stacks.VeryAmplePowersQuasiCompactBase.isRelativelyAmple_of_eventuallyVeryAmplePower
declarations.doc:
If every sufficiently high tensor power of `L` is very ample relative to a quasi-compact `f`,
then `L` is ample relative to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyAmple_of_eventuallyVeryAmplePower (f : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hf : QuasiCompact f) (h : EventuallyVeryAmplePower f L) :
    Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L

declarations.name: Stacks.VeryAmplePowersQuasiCompactBase.eventuallyVeryAmplePower_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type with `S` quasi-compact and let `L` be ample
relative to `f`. Then `L^{⊗ d}` is very ample relative to `f` for every sufficiently large `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventuallyVeryAmplePower_of_isRelativelyAmple (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] [CompactSpace S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hL : Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    EventuallyVeryAmplePower f L

declarations.name: Stacks.VeryAmplePowersQuasiCompactBase.tfae
declarations.doc:
For `f : X ⟶ S` of finite type with `S` quasi-compact and `L` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, the
three conditions

1. `L` is `f`-relatively ample,
2. `L^{⊗ d}` is `f`-relatively very ample for some `d ≥ 1`, and
3. `L^{⊗ d}` is `f`-relatively very ample for every sufficiently large `d`

are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae (f : X ⟶ S)
    (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] [CompactSpace S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hf : QuasiCompact f) :
    List.TFAE [Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L, ExistsVeryAmplePower f L,
      EventuallyVeryAmplePower f L]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsHQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01VW.** A quasi-compact immersion into relative
finite-dimensional projective space.  This is `Stacks.HProjective.IsHQuasiProjective`, which
states the same thing with the structure morphism of `ℙⁿ_S` spelled `↘`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsHQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01VW.** A morphism quasi-projective after restriction over an open
cover of the base.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is *quasi-projective* when it is of finite type — locally of finite type
and quasi-compact — and the source carries an invertible sheaf that is ample relative to it.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01VX, quasi-projective case.** A quasi-projective morphism is locally
of finite type; here this is part of the definition.
declarations.statement: public theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : IsQuasiProjective f) : LocallyOfFiniteType f

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01VX, quasi-projective case.** A quasi-projective morphism is
quasi-compact; here this is part of the definition.
declarations.statement: public theorem quasiCompact (h : IsQuasiProjective f) : QuasiCompact f

declarations.doc: An H-quasi-projective morphism of schemes is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement: theorem locallyOfFiniteType (hf : IsHQuasiProjective f) : LocallyOfFiniteType f

declarations.doc: A quasi-projective morphism of schemes is separated.
declarations.statement: theorem isSeparated (hf : IsQuasiProjective f) : IsSeparated f

declarations.doc: A locally quasi-projective morphism of schemes is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement: theorem locallyOfFiniteType (hf : IsLocallyQuasiProjective f) : LocallyOfFiniteType f

declarations.doc: A locally quasi-projective morphism of schemes is quasi-compact.

declarations.doc: A locally quasi-projective morphism of schemes is separated.

declarations.name: Stacks.HProjective.isQuasiProjective_of_isHQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VY: an H-quasi-projective morphism is quasi-projective.** Let
`i : X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` be a quasi-compact immersion with `i ≫ (ℙⁿ_S ↘ S) = f`. Then `f` is of finite
type, because `i` is an immersion and `ℙⁿ_S ⟶ S` is proper, and `i^* 𝒪(1)` is an invertible
module ample relative to `f` by [Stacks, Tag 01VN], `𝒪(1)` being ample relative to
`ℙⁿ_S ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_of_isHQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hf : IsHQuasiProjective f) : IsQuasiProjective f

declarations.name: Stacks.HProjective.isLocallyQuasiProjective_of_exists_openCover_isHQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VZ, the implication (2) ⟹ (1).** If the base carries an open covering over
whose members `f` is H-quasi-projective, then `f` is locally quasi-projective.

This is [Stacks, Tag 01VY] applied over each member of the covering, which is the source's own
proof of this implication.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiProjective_of_exists_openCover_isHQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (h : ∃ 𝒰 : Scheme.OpenCover.{u} S, ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀,
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsHQuasiProjective (pullback.snd f (𝒰.f i))) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyQuasiProjective f
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1): H-quasi-projective over a cover of the base

declarations.name: Stacks.HProjective.exists_openCover_isHQuasiProjective_of_isLocallyQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VZ, the implication (1) ⟹ (2).** A locally quasi-projective morphism admits an
open covering of the base over whose members it is H-quasi-projective.

Local quasi-projectivity gives a covering `𝒰` of the base over whose members `f` becomes
quasi-projective. Refining `𝒰` to an affine covering —
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.affineRefinement`, whose members are the affine covers of the
members of `𝒰` — reduces to an affine base, where
`Stacks.HProjective.isHQuasiProjective_pullbackSnd_of_isQuasiProjective` applies. The refinement's
base change is identified with the iterated one by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.pullbackCoverAffineRefinementObjIso_inv_pullbackHom`, and
H-quasi-projectivity travels across that identification by
`Stacks.HProjective.isHQuasiProjective_of_iso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_openCover_isHQuasiProjective_of_isLocallyQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyQuasiProjective f) :
    ∃ 𝒰 : Scheme.OpenCover.{u} S, ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀,
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsHQuasiProjective (pullback.snd f (𝒰.f i))
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2): a cover of the base over which f is H-quasi-projective

declarations.name: Stacks.HProjective.isLocallyQuasiProjective_iff_exists_openCover_isHQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VZ.** A morphism of schemes is locally quasi-projective if and only if the base
has an open covering over whose members it is H-quasi-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiProjective_iff_exists_openCover_isHQuasiProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyQuasiProjective f ↔
      ∃ 𝒰 : Scheme.OpenCover.{u} S, ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀,
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsHQuasiProjective (pullback.snd f (𝒰.f i))
declarations.comment: (1) iff (2): the equivalence the tag states

declarations.name: Stacks.HProjective.exists_opens_isHQuasiProjective_of_isLocallyQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01VZ, condition (2) in the source's own phrasing.** A locally quasi-projective
`f : X ⟶ S` admits a family of opens `Vⱼ` of `S` with `S = ⋃ Vⱼ` such that every
`f⁻¹(Vⱼ) ⟶ Vⱼ` is H-quasi-projective.

The opens are the images of the covering produced by
`Stacks.HProjective.exists_openCover_isHQuasiProjective_of_isLocallyQuasiProjective`; they cover
`S` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.OpenCover.iSup_opensRange`, and over each of them the base
change and the restriction are isomorphic as arrows by
`AlgebraicGeometry.morphismRestrictOpensRange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_isHQuasiProjective_of_isLocallyQuasiProjective
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyQuasiProjective f) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (V : ι → S.Opens), (⨆ j, V j) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ j, AlgebraicGeometry.IsHQuasiProjective (f ∣_ V j)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2), with the cover as opens Vⱼ of S and f⁻¹(Vⱼ) → Vⱼ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_iff_exists_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01W2].** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is proper if and only if there is
an open covering `S = ⋃ V j` such that every restriction `f⁻¹(V j) ⟶ V j` is proper. The index
type of the covering may live in any universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_iff_exists_iSup_eq_top {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsProper f ↔ ∃ (ι : Type*) (V : ι → S.Opens), iSup V = ⊤ ∧ ∀ j, IsProper (f ∣_ V j)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.stableUnderComposition
registrations.comment: the composition of proper morphisms is proper

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_isStableUnderComposition
registrations.comment: the composition of universally closed morphisms is universally closed

declarations.name: Stacks.ProperAlgebraBaseChange.universallyClosed_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01W4, second statement.** The base change of a universally closed
morphism is universally closed: in a cartesian square

```
Y' --f'--> Y
|          |
g'         g
v          v
X ---f---> S
```

if `g` is universally closed then so is `g'`.
declarations.comment: the base change of a universally closed morphism is universally closed

declarations.name: Stacks.ProperAlgebraBaseChange.isProper_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01W4, first statement.** The base change of a proper morphism is
proper: in a cartesian square

```
Y' --f'--> Y
|          |
g'         g
v          v
X ---f---> S
```

if `g` is proper then so is `g'`.
declarations.comment: the base change of a proper morphism is proper

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
A closed immersion of schemes is proper: it is a finite morphism, and a finite morphism is
separated, universally closed and locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
lemma isProper_of_isClosedImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion f] :
    IsProper f

registrations.comment: a closed immersion is universally closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_of_universallyClosed_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01W6] part (1).** Let `X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` be a commutative triangle with `Y`
separated over `S`. If `X ⟶ S` is universally closed, then so is `X ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma universallyClosed_of_universallyClosed_of_isSeparated (h : g ≫ q = p) [IsSeparated q]
    [UniversallyClosed p] : UniversallyClosed g
declarations.comment: (1), in the triangle form of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_isProper_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01W6] part (2).** Let `X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` be a commutative triangle with `Y`
separated over `S`. If `X` is proper over `S`, then `X ⟶ Y` is proper.
declarations.statement:
lemma isProper_of_isProper_of_isSeparated (h : g ≫ q = p) [IsSeparated q] [IsProper p] :
    IsProper g
declarations.comment: (2), in the triangle form of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_range_of_universallyClosed_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**The final clause of [Stacks, Tag 01W6].** In a commutative triangle `X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` with `Y`
separated over `S` and `X` universally closed over `S`, the image of `X` in `Y` is closed: the
morphism `X ⟶ Y` is universally closed, hence a closed map, and its image is the image of the
whole space.
declarations.statement:
lemma isClosed_range_of_universallyClosed_of_isSeparated (h : g ≫ q = p) [IsSeparated q]
    [UniversallyClosed p] : IsClosed (Set.range g.base)
declarations.comment: the final clause: the image of X in Y is closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01W8, first condition.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is *projective* if
`X` is isomorphic, as a scheme over `S`, to a closed subscheme of the projective bundle
`𝐏(ℰ) = Proj_S(Sym(ℰ))` of some quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `ℰ` of finite type — equivalently,
if there is a closed immersion `i : X ⟶ 𝐏(ℰ)` with `i` followed by the projection equal to
`f`.
declarations.statement: def IsProjective (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01W8, third condition.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is *locally
projective* if the base is covered by opens over each of which the restriction of `f` is
projective.
declarations.statement: def IsLocallyProjective (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjectiveMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01W8 (H-projective).** A morphism `f : X ⟶ S` is H-projective if
for some `n` there is a closed immersion `X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` over `S`.
declarations.statement: def IsProjectiveMorphism (f : X ⟶ S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjectiveMorphism.isHQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01W9, first clause.** An H-projective morphism is
H-quasi-projective: the closed immersion into `ℙⁿ_S` witnessing H-projectivity is an immersion,
and it is quasi-compact because a closed immersion is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsProjectiveMorphism.isHQuasiProjective (hf : IsProjectiveMorphism f) :
    IsHQuasiProjective f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjectiveMorphism.isProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01W9, second clause.** An H-projective morphism is projective.

Projective `n`-space over `S` is the projective bundle of the free module `𝒪_S^{n+1}`, which is
quasi-coherent and of finite type; so the closed immersion `X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` over `S` witnessing
H-projectivity becomes, after composing with the inverse of the isomorphism
`𝐏(𝒪_S^{n+1}) ≅ ℙⁿ_S` of [Stacks, Tag 01OE], a closed immersion of `X` into that projective
bundle over `S`.
declarations.statement: theorem IsProjectiveMorphism.isProjective (hf : IsProjectiveMorphism f) : IsProjective f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_isProjectiveMorphism_of_isHQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WA.** An H-quasi-projective morphism factors as an open immersion
followed by an H-projective morphism.

H-quasi-projectivity gives a quasi-compact immersion `i : X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` over `S`. Being
quasi-compact, `i` is an open immersion onto its scheme-theoretic image `X'` by
[Stacks, Tag 01RG], which is the only place the quasi-compactness is used; and `X'` is a closed
subscheme of `ℙⁿ_S`, so its structure morphism `X' ⟶ S` is H-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isProjectiveMorphism_of_isHQuasiProjective
    (hf : IsHQuasiProjective f) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (j : X ⟶ X') (p : X' ⟶ S),
      IsOpenImmersion j ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism p ∧ j ≫ p = f

declarations.name: Stacks.LocallyProjectiveHProjective.isLocallyProjectiveMorphism_of_isLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WB, the implication (1) ⟹ (2).** A locally projective morphism is
H-projective over the members of an open covering of its base.

Over each member `U` of the covering witnessing local projectivity the morphism is projective,
so over each affine open `V` of `U` it is H-projective; and the images of those affine opens,
over all members of the covering, cover the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyProjectiveMorphism_of_isLocallyProjective (hf : IsLocallyProjective f) :
    IsLocallyProjectiveMorphism f

declarations.name: Stacks.LocallyProjectiveHProjective.isLocallyProjective_iff_isLocallyProjectiveMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WB.** A morphism of schemes is locally projective if and only if its
base is covered by opens over which it is H-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyProjective_iff_isLocallyProjectiveMorphism :
    IsLocallyProjective f ↔ IsLocallyProjectiveMorphism f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyProjective_of_isLocallyProjectiveMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WB, the implication (2) ⟹ (1).** If the base is covered by opens
over each of which `f` is H-projective, then `f` is locally projective.

The opens are the ranges of the maps of the covering, which cover the base; over each of them
the base change of `f` is isomorphic, as an arrow, to the restriction of `f`, so the restriction
is H-projective, hence projective by the second clause of [Stacks, Tag 01W9].
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyProjective_of_isLocallyProjectiveMorphism (hf : IsLocallyProjectiveMorphism f) :
    IsLocallyProjective f
declarations.comment: the implication from a local H-projective cover

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_isLocallyProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WC.** A locally projective morphism is proper.

Tag 01WB turns local projectivity into local H-projectivity, and a locally H-projective
morphism is proper.
declarations.statement: theorem isProper_of_isLocallyProjective (hf : IsLocallyProjective f) : IsProper f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Segre.isClosedImmersion_segreMorphism
declarations.doc: **The Segre morphism of the integral models is a closed immersion.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_segreMorphism (n m : ℕ) :
    IsClosedImmersion (segreMorphism.{u} n m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Segre.hasSegreEmbeddingSharp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01WD] over an arbitrary base.** For every scheme `S` and all `n m`, there is a
closed immersion `ℙⁿ_S ×_S ℙᵐ_S ⟶ ℙ^{nm + n + m}_S` over `S`.
declarations.statement: theorem hasSegreEmbeddingSharp (S : Scheme.{u}) : HasSegreEmbeddingSharp S

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.SegreProdIso.exists_segreEmbedding
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01WD.**  Over an arbitrary base scheme `S` the product `ℙⁿ_S ×_S ℙᵐ_S` admits a
closed immersion into `ℙ^{nm+n+m}_S` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_segreEmbedding (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ f : pullback ((projectiveSpaceOver n S) ↘ S) ((projectiveSpaceOver m S) ↘ S) ⟶
        projectiveSpaceOver (n * m + n + m) S,
      IsClosedImmersion f ∧
        f ≫ ((projectiveSpaceOver (n * m + n + m) S) ↘ S) =
          pullback.fst ((projectiveSpaceOver n S) ↘ S) ((projectiveSpaceOver m S) ↘ S) ≫
            ((projectiveSpaceOver n S) ↘ S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjectiveMorphism.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WE. A composition of H-projective morphisms is H-projective.**

Closed immersions `i : X ⟶ ℙⁿ_Y` over `Y` and `j : Y ⟶ ℙᵐ_Z` over `Z` are composed as follows.
The identification `ℙⁿ_Z ×_Z Y ≅ ℙⁿ_Y` turns `i` into a closed immersion of `X` into
`ℙⁿ_Z ×_Z Y`; base changing `j` along `ℙⁿ_Z ⟶ Z` embeds that closed into `ℙⁿ_Z ×_Z ℙᵐ_Z`; and the
Segre embedding of [Stacks, Tag 01WD] embeds the product closed into `ℙ^{nm+n+m}_Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} (hf : IsProjectiveMorphism f)
    (hg : IsProjectiveMorphism g) : IsProjectiveMorphism (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjectiveMorphism.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WF. H-projectivity is stable under base change.** A closed
immersion `X ⟶ ℙⁿ_S` over `S` base changes to a closed immersion
`X ×_S T ⟶ ℙⁿ_S ×_S T ≅ ℙⁿ_T` over `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange {f : X ⟶ S} (hf : IsProjectiveMorphism f) {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) :
    IsProjectiveMorphism (pullback.snd f g)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.IsLocallyPrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WR (1).** A closed subscheme of `S` is *locally principal* when its
sheaf of ideals is locally generated by a single element: every point of `S` has an affine open
neighbourhood on which the defining ideal is principal.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyPrincipal {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WR (2).** An *effective Cartier divisor* on `S` is a closed
subscheme `D ⊆ S` whose ideal sheaf `ℐ_D ⊆ 𝒪_S` is an invertible `𝒪_S`-module.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsEffectiveCartierDivisor {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.CartierAffineLocalConverse.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_iff_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WS.** A closed subscheme `D ⊆ X` is an effective Cartier divisor if
and only if every point of `D` has an affine open neighbourhood `U` in `X` on which `D` is cut
out by a nonzerodivisor `f ∈ Γ(X, U)`.

The forward direction is `Stacks.CartierAffineLocal.exists_affineOpen_isRegular`, which proves
the stronger statement with the quantifier over all of `X`; the reverse direction is
`isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_affineLocal`.

The right-hand side renders the source's `D ∩ U = Spec(A/fA)` as the equation
`I.ideal U = Ideal.span {f}` between ideals of `A = Γ(X, U)`: `I.ideal U` *is* the ideal cutting
`D` out on `U`, so the two say the same thing. The scheme-level packaging as an isomorphism
`D ×_X U ≅ Spec (A ⧸ (f))` compatible with the closed immersions is not produced here; see the
module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_iff_isRegular (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ↔
      ∀ x ∈ I.supportSet, ∃ V : X.affineOpens, x ∈ (V : Set X) ∧
        ∃ f : Γ(X, V.1), IsRegular f ∧ I.ideal V = Ideal.span {f}

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_iff_affineLocal
declarations.doc:
A closed subscheme is an effective Cartier divisor if and only if it is locally, on affine
neighbourhoods of its support, the zero scheme of a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_iff_affineLocal :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I ↔
      ∀ x ∈ I.supportSet,
        ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U),
          x ∈ (U : Set X) ∧
            ∃ f : Γ(X, U), IsRegular f ∧
              ∃ e : pullback I.subschemeι U.ι ≅
                  Spec (.of (Γ(X, U) ⧸ Ideal.span {f})),
                pullback.snd I.subschemeι U.ι ≫ hU.isoSpec.hom =
                  e.hom ≫ Spec.map
                    (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {f})))

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_forall_mem_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WS, the direction (2) ⇒ (1).** A closed subscheme which near every
point of its support is cut out, on an affine open, by a single nonzerodivisor is an effective
Cartier divisor.

The hypothesis is clause (2) of the tag: the points of `I.support` are the points of `D`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.range_subschemeι`, and `I.ideal U = (f)` says that
`U ∩ D = Spec(Γ(X, U)/(f))`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι_app`.

Near such a point the generator gives a rank-one dual basis of the ideal sheaf
(`Stacks.Divisors.dualBasisOneOfPrincipal`), and off the support the ideal is the unit ideal,
generated by the nonzerodivisor `1`; the resulting dual bases cover `X`, so
`Stacks.Divisors.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_forall_exists_dualBasisOne` applies.

The converse direction (1) ⇒ (2) is not proved: it needs that an invertible sheaf of modules is
locally free of rank one, which is the descent step
`StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Invertible` records as missing.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_forall_mem_support (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (h : ∀ x ∈ I.support, ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (f : Γ(X, (U : X.Opens))),
      x ∈ (U : Set X) ∧ I.ideal U = Ideal.span {f} ∧
        f ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, (U : X.Opens))) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WU.**  The sum of two effective Cartier divisors on a scheme, that
is, the closed subscheme cut out by the product of their ideal sheaves, is again an effective
Cartier divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_mul (I J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I) (hJ : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor J) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (I * J)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.IsPullbackDefined
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WV.** The pullback of an effective Cartier divisor is defined
exactly when its scheme-theoretic inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsPullbackDefined
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (D : Y.IdealSheafData) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.comap_mul
declarations.doc:
**Scheme-theoretic inverse image commutes with products of ideal sheaves.**  For a morphism
of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` and quasi-coherent ideal sheaves `I`, `J` on `Y`, the inverse image of
`I * J` is the product of the inverse images.  In divisor language: the pullback of a sum of
effective Cartier divisors is the sum of their pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem comap_mul {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (I J : Y.IdealSheafData) :
    (I * J).comap f = I.comap f * J.comap f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullbackDefined_mul
declarations.doc:
If the pullbacks of two effective Cartier divisors along a morphism of schemes are defined,
then so is the pullback of their sum.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullbackDefined_mul {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (I J : Y.IdealSheafData)
    (hI : IsPullbackDefined f I) (hJ : IsPullbackDefined f J) :
    IsPullbackDefined f (I * J)

declarations.doc:

`D ⊆ X`: its sheaf of ideals.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev negativeTwist' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)

declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev invertibleSheaf' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (1).** The sheaf `𝒪_X(D)` of an effective Cartier divisor is
invertible: the evaluation pairing `𝒪_X(D) ⊗ ℐ_D ⟶ 𝒪_X` trivializes it.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleSheaf_isInvertible [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property (invertibleSheaf' D)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (2).** The canonical section `1_D` of `𝒪_X(D)`: the global
section corresponding to the inclusion of the ideal sheaf `ℐ_D` into `𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def canonicalSection' : (invertibleSheaf' D).sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheafIsoInverseIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (1).** The sheaf `𝒪_X(D)` of an effective Cartier divisor is the
inverse tensor power `ℐ_D^{⊗ -1}` of its ideal sheaf: both are tensor inverses of `ℐ_D`, and a
tensor inverse is unique up to a canonical isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def invertibleSheafIsoInverseIdeal [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower X.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property (negativeTwist' D) (-1) ≅
      invertibleSheaf' D

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.negativeTwistIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (3).** The sheaf `𝒪_X(-D) = ℐ_D` is the inverse tensor power
`𝒪_X(D)^{⊗ -1}`, which is the sense in which `𝒪_X(-D)` is the inverse of `𝒪_X(D)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def negativeTwistIso [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower X.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property (invertibleSheaf' D) (-1) ≅
      negativeTwist' D

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.differenceTwist'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (4).** The sheaf
`𝒪_X(D - D') = 𝒪_X(D) ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X(-D')` attached to a pair of closed subschemes.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev differenceTwist' : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.negativeTwist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (3).** The sheaf `𝒪_S(-D)` *is* the ideal sheaf `ℐ_D` of the
closed subscheme `D ⊆ S`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev negativeTwist : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (1).** The sheaf `𝒪_S(D) = SheafHom_{𝒪_S}(ℐ_D, 𝒪_S)` associated
to a closed subscheme `D ⊆ S`: the dual of its ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev invertibleSheaf : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.differenceTwist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (4).** The difference twist
`𝒪_S(D - D') = 𝒪_S(D) ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝒪_S(-D')`. The expression `D - D'` has no geometric meaning on
its own; this is the definition of the sheaf it names.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev differenceTwist : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isInvertible_invertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (1).** The sheaf `𝒪_S(D)` of an effective Cartier divisor is
invertible, which is what the tag's wording "the invertible sheaf `𝒪_S(D)`" asserts.

This is Tag 0B8K (2) ⟹ (1) applied to the evaluation pairing: no trivializing cover is
constructed, and no rank-one dual basis is assumed.
declarations.statement:
instance isInvertible_invertibleSheaf :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property (invertibleSheaf D)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheafIsoNegativeTensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (1):** `𝒪_S(D) = ℐ_D^{⊗ -1}`. The dual of the ideal sheaf is its
negative first tensor power, by uniqueness of tensor inverses; the identification is the one
normalized by `invertibleSheafPairing`, not an arbitrary isomorphism. That normalization needs
no restatement here: this *is*
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isoTensorPowerNegOne` at that pairing, so
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isoTensorPowerNegOne_hom_tensor` applies to it directly and
says that tensoring this isomorphism with `ℐ_D` carries the canonical trivialization of
`ℐ_D^{⊗ -1} ⊗ ℐ_D` back to `invertibleSheafPairing`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def invertibleSheafIsoNegativeTensorPower :
    invertibleSheaf D ≅ Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property (negativeTwist D) (-1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.negativeTwistIsoNegativeTensorPower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (3):** `𝒪_S(-D) = 𝒪_S(D)^{⊗ -1}`. Together with the definition
of `negativeTwist` this is the tag's full chain `𝒪_S(-D) = 𝒪_S(D)^{⊗ -1} = ℐ_D`. The
identification is normalized by `invertibleSheafPairing'`, through the same
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.isoTensorPowerNegOne_hom_tensor`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def negativeTwistIsoNegativeTensorPower :
    negativeTwist D ≅ Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPower X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property (invertibleSheaf D) (-1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01WX (2).** The canonical section `1 = 1_D`: the global section of
`𝒪_S(D)` corresponding to the inclusion mapping `ℐ_D ⟶ 𝒪_S`.

A section of `SheafHom(ℐ_D, 𝒪_S)` over an open `U` is a morphism `ℐ_D|_U ⟶ 𝒪_S|_U` of
presheaves of modules on the slice site over `U` (Tag 03EM), so the global section in question
is the restriction of `idealInclusion` to the slice site over `⊤`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def canonicalSection : (invertibleSheaf D).val.obj (op (⊤ : Opens X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection
declarations.doc:
A global section is regular when multiplication by it gives a monomorphism
from the structure sheaf to its module sheaf.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularSection_iff_stalk
declarations.doc:
A section of the structure sheaf is regular if and only if its germ at every point is a
nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_stalk
    (X : LocallyRingedSpace.{u})
    (f : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj X.sheaf)).sections) :
    IsRegularSection X.presheaf
        ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ X.presheaf
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).mp X.IsSheaf) f ↔
      ∀ x : X, IsSMulRegular (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial (f.val (.op ⊤)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularSection_iff_affineOpen
declarations.doc:
On a scheme, a section of the structure sheaf is regular if and only if its restriction
to every affine open is a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_affineOpen
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj X.sheaf)).sections) :
    IsRegularSection X.presheaf
        ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ X.presheaf
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).mp X.IsSheaf) f ↔
      ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U →
        IsSMulRegular Γ(X, U) (show Γ(X, U) from f.val (.op U))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegularSection_iff_exists_affineOpenCover
declarations.doc:
On a scheme, a section of the structure sheaf is regular if and only if its restrictions
are nonzerodivisors on the members of some affine open covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_exists_affineOpenCover
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (f : (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj X.sheaf)).sections) :
    IsRegularSection X.presheaf
        ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ X.presheaf
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).mp X.IsSheaf) f ↔
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens), IsOpenCover U ∧
        (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i) ∧
          IsSMulRegular Γ(X, U i) (show Γ(X, U i) from f.val (.op (U i))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**The first clause of [Stacks, Tag 01X0].** For `D ⊆ X` an effective Cartier divisor on a
scheme, the canonical section `1_D` of `𝒪_X(D)` is a regular section.

Tensoring with `ℐ_D` is an autoequivalence of the category of `𝒪_X`-modules, since `ℐ_D` is
invertible, so it is faithful and therefore reflects monomorphisms; and
`Stacks.Divisors.evaluation_canonicalHom` identifies the image of `1_D` under it, up to the left
unitor and the evaluation isomorphism, with the inclusion `ℐ_D ⟶ 𝒪_X`, which is a kernel
morphism and hence a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalSection_isRegular [IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection X.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property (canonicalSection' D)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_invertibleSheafIso_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**There is a unique isomorphism from the invertible sheaf of the zero scheme of a regular
section to the original invertible sheaf that sends its canonical section to that section.**
This is [Stacks, Tag 01X0] (2): for `s` a regular section of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` the
zero scheme `D = Z(s)` is an effective Cartier divisor
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_iff_isRegularSection`) and `𝒪_X(D) ≅ L`
by a unique isomorphism matching `1_D` with `s`.

Existence is `AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleSheafIsoZeroSchemeOfIsRegularSection` and its section
identity; uniqueness is `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_id_of_sectionsMap_eq`, applied to the endomorphism
of `L` built from two such isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_invertibleSheafIso_zeroScheme (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : L.sections)
    (hs : IsRegularSection X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property s) :
    ∃! e : Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))) ≅ L,
      Scheme.Modules.Hom.app e.hom ⊤
          ((Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection'
            (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤)))).eval (op ⊤)) = s.eval (op ⊤)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveCartierDivisor_equiv_regularSectionClass
declarations.doc:
**The canonical bijection between the effective Cartier divisors on a scheme and the
isomorphism classes of invertible modules with a regular global section**
([Stacks, Tag 01X0]).

Forwards a divisor `D` goes to the class of `(𝒪_X(D), 1_D)`; backwards a pair `(L, s)` goes to
the zero scheme `Z(s)`, which is well defined on classes by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RegularSectionPair.zeroScheme_eq_of_isIsomorphic`. The two round trips are
`Z(1_D) = D` (`Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme_canonicalSection`) and
`(𝒪_X(Z(s)), 1_{Z(s)}) ≅ (L, s)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleSheafIsoZeroSchemeOfIsRegularSection`).
declarations.statement:
def effectiveCartierDivisor_equiv_regularSectionClass (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    EffectiveCartierDivisor X ≃ RegularSectionClass X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveCartierDivisor_equiv_regularSectionClass_apply
declarations.doc:
**The forward map of the bijection of [Stacks, Tag 01X0] sends an effective Cartier divisor
to the isomorphism class of its invertible sheaf with its canonical section**, which is a regular
section.
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierDivisor_equiv_regularSectionClass_apply (D : EffectiveCartierDivisor X) :
    ∃ h : IsRegularSection X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property
        (Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection' D.1),
      effectiveCartierDivisor_equiv_regularSectionClass X D =
        RegularSectionPair.classOf
          ⟨Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' D.1,
            @Stacks.Divisors.isInvertible_divisorSheaf X D.1 D.2,
            Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection' D.1, h⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveCartierDivisor_equiv_regularSectionClass_symm_apply
declarations.doc:
**The inverse map of the bijection of [Stacks, Tag 01X0] sends the class of a regular-section
pair to the effective Cartier divisor cut out by its zero scheme.** The equation holds for every
representative of the class.
declarations.statement:
theorem effectiveCartierDivisor_equiv_regularSectionClass_symm_apply (P : RegularSectionPair X) :
    ∃ h : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor P.zeroScheme,
      (effectiveCartierDivisor_equiv_regularSectionClass X).symm P.classOf = ⟨P.zeroScheme, h⟩

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.zeroScheme_canonicalSection'
declarations.doc:
**`Z(1_D) = D`.** The zero scheme of the canonical section of `𝒪_X(D)` is `D` itself: the
composite `D ↦ (𝒪_X(D), 1_D) ↦ Z(1_D)` is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem zeroScheme_canonicalSection' :
    zeroScheme X (modulesInvertibleSheaf D) (canonicalSection D) = D

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isRegularSection_canonicalSections
declarations.doc:
The canonical section `1_D` of `𝒪_X(D)` is a regular section, i.e. a nonzerodivisor
([Stacks, Tag 01WY]).
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_canonicalSections :
    IsRegularSection X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property (canonicalSections D)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MeromorphicFunction
declarations.doc:
A meromorphic function on a locally ringed space is a global section of its sheaf of

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NoChange.noChangeRing
declarations.doc: The ring `ℂ[x, {y_α}]/((x-α)y_α, y_α y_β)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NoChange.isUnit_of_isRegular_localizationAway

declarations.statement:
theorem isUnit_of_isRegular_localizationAway (f : noChangeRing)

meromorphic functions is an isomorphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.meromorphicSectionSheaf
declarations.doc:
The sheaf `K_X(F)` of meromorphic sections of `F`, obtained by extension of scalars from
`O` to its sheaf of total quotient rings.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev meromorphicSectionSheaf (O : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} X)
