declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteDirectImageCoherent.isCoherent_pushforward_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
The direct image of a coherent module along a finite morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme is
coherent.

It is quasi-coherent because a finite morphism is affine, and on every affine open of the target
its sections form a finite module, which is condition (5) of [Stacks, Tag 01XZ].
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_pushforward_of_isFinite {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsFinite f]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsCoherent

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteDirectImageCoherent.isZero_higherDirectImage_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
The higher direct images of a quasi-coherent module along a finite morphism vanish in positive
degrees, a finite morphism being affine; this is [Stacks, Tag 01XC]. No hypothesis on the target is
used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_higherDirectImage_of_isFinite {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsFinite f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (p : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerivedPlus p).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_eventually_constant_quasicoherentSubobjects
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01Y8.** An ascending chain of quasi-coherent submodules of a coherent
sheaf on a Noetherian scheme eventually stabilizes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_eventually_constant_quasicoherentSubobjects
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (G : ℕ → Subobject F) (hG : ∀ n, (G n : X.Modules).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hmono : Monotone G) :
    ∃ n, ∀ m, n ≤ m → G m = G n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_idealPowerMultiple_eq_bot_iff_supp_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01Y9.** Let `ℱ` be a coherent module on a Noetherian scheme `X` and
let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_X` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, cutting out the closed subscheme
`Z ⊆ X`. Then some power of `ℐ` annihilates `ℱ` if and only if the support of `ℱ` is contained
in `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_idealPowerMultiple_eq_bot_iff_supp_subset {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    (∃ n : ℕ, idealPowerMultiple I n F = ⊥) ↔
      SheafOfModules.supp F ⊆ (I.support : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealPowerSupport.exists_idealPowerMultiple_eq_bot_iff_supp_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01Y9.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `I` a quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals and `F` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module — here a quasi-coherent module of finite type, which on a
locally Noetherian scheme is the same thing by Tag 01XZ. Then some power of `I` annihilates `F`
if and only if the support of `F` is contained in the closed set cut out by `I`.

Both directions are affine-local, with the algebraic content supplied by Tag 00L6 over the
Noetherian ring of sections on an affine open: a power of an ideal kills a finite module exactly
when the support of the module lies in the zero locus of the ideal. For the forward direction one
affine open containing the point suffices. For the converse the exponent must be chosen uniformly,
and that is where quasi-compactness enters: finitely many affine opens cover `X`, the largest of
their exponents works on each of them, and `smul_pow_eq_bot_of_le` carries the vanishing from a
member of the cover to any affine open inside it, which is enough to conclude by sheaf
separation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_idealPowerMultiple_eq_bot_iff_supp_subset {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    (∃ n : ℕ, idealPowerMultiple I n F = ⊥) ↔
      SheafOfModules.supp F ⊆ (I.support : Set X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_ideal_pow_smul_inf_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01YA.** Artin-Rees for a coherent sheaf and a quasi-coherent subsheaf
on a Noetherian scheme: the equality holds on every affine open with a single constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_pow_smul_inf_eq {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (G : F.Submodule) [G.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent]
    (I : (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf).Submodule)
    [I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, c ≤ n → ∀ U : X.affineOpens,
      (show Ideal Γ(X, U.1) from I.toSubmodule.obj (op U.1)) ^ (n - c) •
          (((show Ideal Γ(X, U.1) from I.toSubmodule.obj (op U.1)) ^ c •
            (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1))) ⊓
            G.toSubmodule.obj (op U.1)) =
        ((show Ideal Γ(X, U.1) from I.toSubmodule.obj (op U.1)) ^ n •
          (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1))) ⊓
          G.toSubmodule.obj (op U.1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToHomRestrict_bijective
declarations.doc:
For a Noetherian scheme `X`, a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `I` with complement
`U = X \ V(I)`, a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `G` and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the canonical
map

`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ G, F) ⟶ Hom_{𝒪_U}(G|_U, F|_U)`

is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalMapToHomRestrict_bijective [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (G F : X.Modules) [G.IsCoherent] [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Function.Bijective (canonicalMapToHomRestrict I G F)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerColimit.canonicalMapToSections_bijective_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The global-sections clause of [Stacks, Tag 01YB].** For a Noetherian scheme `X`, a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `I` and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the canonical map

`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(Iⁿ, F) ⟶ Γ(X \\ V(I), F)`

is a bijection. Injectivity is `canonicalMapToSections_injective`, the first assertion of
[Stacks, Tag 01PQ]; surjectivity is
`exists_hom_idealPow_app_oneSection_eq_of_isQuasicoherent`.

**This is the second of the two displays of Tag 01YB.** The tag's *first* display,
`colim_n Hom(Iⁿ G, F) ≅ Hom(G|_U, F|_U)` for a coherent `G`, is not proved here; its `G = 𝒪_X`
case is, so the clause label records the global-sections half only. The first display is what
[Stacks, Tag 0BJZ] consumes: there `G` is the coherent module itself, never `𝒪_X`. Its arrow
is `canonicalMapToHomRestrict` and its bijectivity is
`canonicalMapToHomRestrict_bijective`, whose surjectivity half applies this clause to
`SheafHom(G, F)` and then transports the resulting morphism `Iⁿ ⟶ SheafHom(G, F)` across the
surjection `Iⁿ ⊗ G ⟶ Iⁿ G`, using the vanishing `Iⁿ ker(Iⁿ ⊗ G ⟶ Iⁿ G) = 0` and a second
Artin-Rees step.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSections_bijective_of_isQuasicoherent
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Function.Bijective (canonicalMapToSections I F)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.HigherDirectImageCoherent.exists_shortExact_coherent_of_supp_eq_union
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YD].** A coherent module whose support is a union of two closed sets is an
extension of coherent modules supported on those sets: there is a short exact sequence
`0 ⟶ G' ⟶ F ⟶ G ⟶ 0` of coherent modules with `Supp G' ⊆ Z'` and `Supp G ⊆ Z`, and `F` is
literally its middle term.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_shortExact_coherent_of_supp_eq_union
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (Z Z' : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (hZ' : IsClosed Z')
    (hF : SheafOfModules.supp F = Z ∪ Z') :
    ∃ (G' G : X.Modules) (f : G' ⟶ F) (g : F ⟶ G) (w : f ≫ g = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk f g w).ShortExact ∧
        _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G' ∧ _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G ∧
        SheafOfModules.supp G' ⊆ Z' ∧ SheafOfModules.supp G ⊆ Z

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSmul.hasSupportSplitting
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YD].** A coherent module on a Noetherian scheme whose support is the union
of two closed sets sits in a short exact sequence of coherent modules whose sub is supported in
the first and whose quotient is supported in the second.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSupportSplitting (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] :
    DevissageNoetherian.HasSupportSplitting X

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedImmersion.exists_idealCoproduct_pushforward_mono_isIso_near_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YE].** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an integral
closed subscheme with generic point `ξ`, and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose stalk at
`i ξ` is annihilated by the maximal ideal of the local ring there. Then there are an integer
`r ≥ 0`, a coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Z` and an injective map of coherent sheaves
`i_*(ℐ^{⊕ r}) ⟶ ℱ` which is an isomorphism on a neighbourhood of `i ξ`.

The subsheaf of sections of `ℱ` annihilated by the ideal sheaf of `Z` has the same stalk at
`i ξ` as `ℱ` does, because that ideal generates the maximal ideal there, so it agrees with `ℱ`
on a neighbourhood of `i ξ`; being killed by the ideal it is `i_* 𝒢` for a coherent `𝒢` on `Z`
by [Stacks, Tag 087T]; and the case `Z = X`, applied to `𝒢`, supplies the sheaf of ideals and
the monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_idealCoproduct_pushforward_mono_isIso_near_genericPoint
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X] (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion i] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral Z]
    (ξ : Z) (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ (Set.univ : Set Z))
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hF : StalkKilledByMaximalIdeal F (i ξ)) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (I : (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf).Submodule),
      I.toSheafOfModules.IsCoherent ∧
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj
        (∐ fun _ : Fin r => I.toSheafOfModules)).IsCoherent ∧
      ∃ φ : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj
          (∐ fun _ : Fin r => I.toSheafOfModules) ⟶ F,
        Mono φ ∧ ∃ U : X.Opens, i ξ ∈ U ∧
          IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).map φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentDevissage.exists_filtration_by_integral_ideal_pushforwards
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YF].** A coherent module on a Noetherian scheme has a finite filtration by
coherent submodules, starting at `⊥` and ending at `⊤`, whose successive quotients are direct
images of nonzero coherent sheaves of ideals on integral closed subschemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_filtration_by_integral_ideal_pushforwards
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : Fin (n + 1) → Subobject F) (hG : Monotone G),
      G 0 = ⊥ ∧ G (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
      (∀ j : Fin (n + 1), (G j : X.Modules).IsCoherent) ∧
      ∀ j : Fin n,
        ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i) (_ : IsIntegral Z)
          (I : (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf).Submodule),
          I.toSheafOfModules.IsCoherent ∧ ¬ IsZero I.toSheafOfModules ∧
          Nonempty (cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (G j.castSucc) (G j.succ)
            (hG j.castSucc_le_succ)) ≅
            (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj I.toSheafOfModules)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentDevissage.property_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and let `P` be a property of
coherent `𝒪_X`-modules which holds on the zero module, is stable under extensions of coherent
modules, and holds on the direct image `i_* I` of every quasi-coherent ideal `I ⊆ 𝒪_Z` along
the closed immersion of every integral closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ X`. Then `P` holds on every
coherent `𝒪_X`-module.

Every coherent module is filtered by such direct images ([Stacks, Tag 01YF]), and extension
stability propagates `P` along the filtration.
declarations.statement:
public theorem property_of_isCoherent (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (P : X.Modules → Prop) (hzero : P (⊤_ X.Modules))
    (hext : ∀ S : ShortComplex X.Modules, S.ShortExact →
      _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent S.X₁ → _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent S.X₂ →
      _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent S.X₃ → P S.X₁ → P S.X₃ → P S.X₂)
    (hideal : ∀ {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z]
      (I : (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf).Submodule),
      I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent →
      P ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj I.toSheafOfModules)) :
    ∀ F : X.Modules, _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F → P F

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IrreducibleSupportDevissage.property_of_irreducible_support
declarations.doc:
A two-out-of-three property of coherent sheaves holds for every sheaf
supported on the given irreducible closed subset if it holds on proper
integral closed subschemes and on one generically simple sheaf of full support.
declarations.statement:
public theorem property_of_irreducible_support
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (Z₀ : Set X) (hZ₀ : IsClosed Z₀) (_hZ₀irr : IsIrreducible Z₀)
    (ξ : X) (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Z₀)
    (P : X.Modules → Prop)
    (hexact : ∀ (S : ShortComplex X.Modules), S.ShortExact →
      S.X₁.IsCoherent → S.X₂.IsCoherent → S.X₃.IsCoherent →
      ((P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₂ → P S.X₃) ∧
        (P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₃ → P S.X₂) ∧
        (P S.X₂ ∧ P S.X₃ → P S.X₁)))
    (hproper : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
      [IsIntegral Z], Set.range i.base ⊂ Z₀ →
      ∀ (I : (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf).Submodule)
        [I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent],
        P ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj I.toSheafOfModules))
    (hgeneric : ∃ G : X.Modules,
      G.IsCoherent ∧ SheafOfModules.supp G = Z₀ ∧
      Stacks.ClosedImmersion.StalkKilledByMaximalIdeal G ξ ∧
      (letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (G.presheaf.stalk ξ) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) G.val ξ
       Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (G.presheaf.stalk ξ) = 1) ∧
      P G) :
    ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsCoherent → SheafOfModules.supp F ⊆ Z₀ → P F

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentDevissage.property_of_isCoherent_of_generic_stalk_of_nonempty
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YI].** Let `X` be a nonempty Noetherian scheme and let `P` be a property of
coherent `𝒪_X`-modules such that

1. for a short exact sequence of coherent modules, if two out of three have `P` then so does the
   third, and
2. every integral closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ X` with generic point `ξ` carries some coherent
   module `𝒢` with `Supp 𝒢` the range of `i`, with `𝒢_ξ` annihilated by `𝔪_ξ` and of length one
   over `𝒪_{X,ξ}`, and with `P 𝒢`.

Then `P` holds on every coherent `𝒪_X`-module.

Nonemptiness cannot be dropped: on the empty Noetherian scheme hypotheses (1) and (2) hold for
`P := fun _ => False`, while the zero module is coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem property_of_isCoherent_of_generic_stalk_of_nonempty
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hX : Nonempty X) (P : X.Modules → Prop)
    (hexact : ∀ S : ShortComplex X.Modules, S.ShortExact →
      _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent S.X₁ → _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent S.X₂ →
      _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent S.X₃ →
      ((P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₂ → P S.X₃) ∧
        (P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₃ → P S.X₂) ∧
        (P S.X₂ ∧ P S.X₃ → P S.X₁)))
    (hgeneric : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i → IsIntegral Z →
      ∀ ξ : X, IsGenericPoint ξ (Set.range i.base) →
      ∃ G : X.Modules, _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G ∧
        SheafOfModules.supp G = Set.range i.base ∧
        Stacks.ClosedImmersion.StalkKilledByMaximalIdeal G ξ ∧
        (letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (G.presheaf.stalk ξ) :=
          PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
            (R := X.presheaf) G.val ξ
         Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (G.presheaf.stalk ξ) = 1) ∧
        P G) :
    ∀ F : X.Modules, _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F → P F

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GenericRankOneDevissage.property_of_genericRankOne
declarations.doc:
**The dévissage criterion of [Stacks, Tag 01YI], with the zero module added to its
hypotheses.** On a Noetherian scheme `X`, a property `P` of coherent modules which holds for the
zero module, propagates along a short exact sequence of coherent modules from any two of its
terms to the third, and holds for one coherent module supported exactly on each integral closed
subscheme with generic stalk killed by the maximal ideal there and of length one over it, holds
for every coherent module.

The criterion of [Stacks, Tag 01YG] reduces this to the direct images of quasi-coherent ideals
on integral closed subschemes, which is
`pushforward_ideal_property_of_genericRankOne`. The hypothesis on the zero module cannot be
dropped: on the empty scheme, which is Noetherian and has no integral closed subscheme, the
identically false property satisfies the other two hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_of_genericRankOne (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (P : X.Modules → Prop) (hzero : P (⊤_ X.Modules))
    (hexact : ∀ S : ShortComplex X.Modules, S.ShortExact →
      S.X₁.IsCoherent → S.X₂.IsCoherent → S.X₃.IsCoherent →
      ((P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₂ → P S.X₃) ∧
        (P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₃ → P S.X₂) ∧
        (P S.X₂ ∧ P S.X₃ → P S.X₁)))
    (hgeneric : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z]
      (ξ : X), IsGenericPoint ξ (Set.range i.base) →
      ∃ G : X.Modules, G.IsCoherent ∧
        SheafOfModules.supp G = Set.range i.base ∧
        Stacks.ClosedImmersion.StalkKilledByMaximalIdeal G ξ ∧
        (letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (G.presheaf.stalk ξ) :=
          PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
            (R := X.presheaf) G.val ξ
         Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (G.presheaf.stalk ξ) = 1) ∧
        P G) :
    ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsCoherent → P F
declarations.comment:
corrected: the source statement is false on the empty scheme, where condition (2)
is vacuous and the identically false property satisfies both hypotheses, so `P` on the zero
module is added

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GenericRankOneDevissage.property_of_genericRankOne_of_exists_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**The dévissage criterion of [Stacks, Tag 01YI], with one integral closed subscheme added to
its hypotheses.** On a Noetherian scheme carrying at least one integral closed subscheme, a
property `P` of coherent modules satisfying conditions (1) and (2) of [Stacks, Tag 01YI] holds
for every coherent module.

Condition (2) at that one subscheme produces a coherent module for which `P` holds, and
condition (1) then carries `P` to the zero module, so the hypothesis of
`property_of_genericRankOne` is met. The added hypothesis is implied by `Nonempty X` and
implies it, and it cannot be dropped: on the empty scheme the identically false property
satisfies conditions (1) and (2) and fails for the coherent zero module.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_of_genericRankOne_of_exists_isIntegral (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (hne : ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i ∧ IsIntegral Z)
    (P : X.Modules → Prop)
    (hexact : ∀ S : ShortComplex X.Modules, S.ShortExact →
      S.X₁.IsCoherent → S.X₂.IsCoherent → S.X₃.IsCoherent →
      ((P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₂ → P S.X₃) ∧
        (P S.X₁ ∧ P S.X₃ → P S.X₂) ∧
        (P S.X₂ ∧ P S.X₃ → P S.X₁)))
    (hgeneric : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z]
      (ξ : X), IsGenericPoint ξ (Set.range i.base) →
      ∃ G : X.Modules, G.IsCoherent ∧
        SheafOfModules.supp G = Set.range i.base ∧
        Stacks.ClosedImmersion.StalkKilledByMaximalIdeal G ξ ∧
        (letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (G.presheaf.stalk ξ) :=
          PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
            (R := X.presheaf) G.val ξ
         Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk ξ) (G.presheaf.stalk ξ) = 1) ∧
        P G) :
    ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsCoherent → P F
declarations.comment:
corrected: the source statement is false on the empty scheme, where condition (2)
is vacuous and the identically false property satisfies both hypotheses, so the existence of one
integral closed subscheme is added

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.HigherRankIrreducibleDevissage.property_irreducible_higher_rank
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YL], in the corrected form.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `Z₀` an
irreducible closed subset with generic point `ξ`, and `P` a property of coherent modules which
holds for the zero module, is stable under extensions of coherent modules, descends from a
nonempty finite direct sum, holds for the direct image of every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals on
every integral closed subscheme strictly inside `Z₀`, and admits one coherent `G` of support
exactly `Z₀` whose stalk at `ξ` is annihilated by the maximal ideal there and which has, inside
every ideal multiple `J·G` with `J_ξ` the whole local ring, a quasi-coherent subsheaf agreeing
with `G` at `ξ` for which `P` holds. Then `P` holds for every coherent module whose support is
contained in `Z₀`.

The correction is the hypothesis `hzero`: the source's four conditions do not list `P` for the
zero module and do not imply it, and without it the statement is false. See this file's
implementation notes for the counterexample.
declarations.statement:
public theorem property_irreducible_higher_rank
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (Z₀ : Set X) (hZ₀ : IsClosed Z₀)
    (ξ : X) (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Z₀)
    (P : X.Modules → Prop)
    (hzero : P (⊤_ X.Modules))
    (hext : ∀ (S : ShortComplex X.Modules), S.ShortExact →
      S.X₁.IsCoherent → S.X₂.IsCoherent → S.X₃.IsCoherent →
      P S.X₁ → P S.X₃ → P S.X₂)
    (hsum : ∀ (F : X.Modules), F.IsCoherent →
      (∃ n : ℕ, P (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => F))) → P F)
    (hproper : ∀ (I : X.IdealSheafData) [IsIntegral I.subscheme],
      (I.support : Set X) ⊆ Z₀ → (I.support : Set X) ≠ Z₀ →
      ∀ (H : (SheafOfModules.unit I.subscheme.ringCatSheaf).Submodule)
        [H.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent],
        P ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward I.subschemeι).obj H.toSheafOfModules))
    (hgeneric : ∃ (G : X.Modules), G.IsCoherent ∧
      (∀ x : X, x ∈ Z₀ ↔ Nontrivial (G.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
      Tag01YEStalkBridge.IsMaximalIdealAnnihilated G ξ ∧
      (∀ (J : X.IdealSheafData), ξ ∉ J.support →
        ∃ (G' : G.Submodule),
          G'.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
          (∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (s : Γ(G'.toSheafOfModules, U.1)),
            (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app G'.ι U.1 s : Γ(G, U.1)) ∈
              J.ideal U • (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, U.1) Γ(G, U.1))) ∧
          Function.Surjective
            (((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab ξ).map
              (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf G'.ι)).hom) ∧
          P G'.toSheafOfModules)) :
    ∀ (F : X.Modules), F.IsCoherent →
      (∀ x : X, Nontrivial (F.presheaf.stalk x) → x ∈ Z₀) → P F

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NoetherianDevissage.property_higher_rank
declarations.doc:
**The dévissage of coherent sheaves on a Noetherian scheme.** A property closed under
extensions, descending from a nonempty finite direct sum, and holding for a suitable coherent
module at every integral closed subscheme, holds for every coherent module.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_higher_rank [IsNoetherian X] (P : X.Modules → Prop)
    (hzero : P (⊤_ X.Modules))
    (hext : ∀ S : ShortComplex X.Modules, S.ShortExact →
      S.X₁.IsCoherent → S.X₂.IsCoherent → S.X₃.IsCoherent → P S.X₁ → P S.X₃ → P S.X₂)
    (hsum : ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsCoherent →
      (∃ n : ℕ, P (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => F)) → P F)
    (hgeneric : ∀ (I : X.IdealSheafData) [IsIntegral I.subscheme],
      ∃ G : X.Modules, G.IsCoherent ∧
        (∀ x : X, x ∈ I.support ↔ Nontrivial (G.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
        Tag01YEStalkBridge.IsMaximalIdealAnnihilated G
          (I.subschemeι (genericPoint I.subscheme)) ∧
        (∀ J : X.IdealSheafData,
          I.subschemeι (genericPoint I.subscheme) ∉ J.support →
          ∃ G' : G.Submodule,
            G'.toSheafOfModules.IsCoherent ∧
            (∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (s : Γ(G'.toSheafOfModules, U.1)),
              (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app G'.ι U.1 s : Γ(G, U.1)) ∈
                J.ideal U • (⊤ : Submodule Γ(X, U.1) Γ(G, U.1))) ∧
            Function.Surjective
              (((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab
                (I.subschemeι (genericPoint I.subscheme))).map
                  (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf G'.ι)).hom) ∧
            P G'.toSheafOfModules)) :
    ∀ F : X.Modules, F.IsCoherent → P F
declarations.comment: plus P on the zero sheaf, which conditions (1) and (2) do not give

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteSurjectiveCoherentSupport.exists_isCoherent_supp_pushforward_eq_range
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YO].** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be finite and surjective with `X` locally Noetherian
and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an integral closed subscheme with generic point `ξ`. Then there is a
coherent module `ℱ` on `Y` whose direct image `f_* ℱ` has support exactly `Z` and whose stalk at
`ξ` is annihilated by the maximal ideal of `𝒪_{X,ξ}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCoherent_supp_pushforward_eq_range
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f] [Surjective f]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral Z] :
    ∃ F : Y.Modules, F.IsCoherent ∧
      SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) = Set.range i ∧
      (let G := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F
       let x := i (genericPoint Z)
       letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x)
           (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) G.val.presheaf x) :=
         PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
           (R := X.presheaf) G.val x
       ∀ a : X.presheaf.stalk x,
         a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x) →
         ∀ s : TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) G.val.presheaf x, a • s = 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineIdealPushforward.ideal_smul_pushforward_sections_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01YP.** If `f : Y ⟶ X` is affine, `F` is a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_Y`-module, and `I` is a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on `X`, then `I · f₊ F = f₊((f⁻¹ I) · F)`.

The equality is stated on every affine open, using the affine-open presentation of
quasi-coherent ideal sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem ideal_smul_pushforward_sections_eq (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsAffineHom f]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : X.affineOpens) :
    pushforwardIdealMultipleSections f I F U =
      pullbackIdealMultiplePushforwardSections f I F U

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag01YQClauseThree.isAffine_of_isFinite_surjective
declarations.doc: A Noetherian scheme admitting a finite surjective morphism from an affine scheme is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isFinite_surjective {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsFinite f] [Surjective f] [IsAffine Y] [IsNoetherian X] :
    IsAffine X

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveCohomology.isZero_Hgroup_of_lt
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YS], clause (2).** The cohomology of a quasi-coherent module on projective
`n`-space over a ring vanishes in every degree above `n`.

Projective space is covered by its `n + 1` standard charts, all affine, and it is separated,
hence has affine diagonal; [Stacks, Tag 01XI] then bounds the cohomological degree by `n + 1`.
As the source observes, no Noetherian hypothesis is needed, and the conclusion holds for every
quasi-coherent module, not only coherent ones. The source's remaining range `i < 0` is vacuous
in this spelling, where cohomology is indexed by `ℕ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_Hgroup_of_lt (F : (projectiveSpaceOverRing n R).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (q : ℕ) (hq : n < q) :
    IsZero (Hgroup (projectiveSpaceOverRing n R).ringCatSheaf ⊤ q F)

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.exists_epi_biproduct_tensorPowModule
declarations.doc:
**Assertion (1) of [Stacks, Tag 01YS].** A quasi-coherent module of finite type on projective
`n`-space over an affine base is a quotient of a finite direct sum of twists
`𝒪(d₁), …, 𝒪(d_r)` of the structure sheaf, and the degrees may be taken below any prescribed
integer.

The source assumes the base ring Noetherian and the module coherent; neither is needed, and
`Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.exists_epi_biproduct_of_isCoherent` is the source's reading.

The proof is the source's: `𝒪(1)` is ample on `ℙⁿ_S`
(`Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.isAmple_projectiveSpaceTwistingSheaf`), and clause (8) of
[Stacks, Tag 01Q3] (`Stacks.AmpleLocalGeneration.isQuotientOfNegativeTwists_of_isAmple`) presents
a finite-type quasi-coherent module as a quotient of a finite direct sum of negative tensor
powers of an ample invertible module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_biproduct_tensorPowModule (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] (k : ℤ)
    (F : (projectiveSpaceOver n S).Modules) (hFqc : F.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} F) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (d : Fin r → ℤ)
      (b : Bicone fun j : Fin r => tensorPowModule (projectiveSpaceOver n S)
        (projectiveSpaceTwistingSheaf n S) (d j))
      (_ : b.IsBilimit) (p : b.pt ⟶ F), Epi p ∧ ∀ j, d j ≤ k

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.SerreVanishing.moduleFinite_cohomology_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YS] clause (3).** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `n ≥ 0` and `ℱ` a coherent
sheaf on `ℙⁿ_R = Proj R[T₀, …, Tₙ]`. For every `i` the cohomology `H^i(ℙⁿ_R, ℱ)` is a finite
`R`-module.

The proof is the source's descending induction on `i`: it holds above degree `n` because the
cohomology vanishes there (clause (2)), the twists `𝒪(d)` have finite cohomology
([Stacks, Tag 01XT]), and `ℱ` is a quotient of a finite direct sum of twists (clause (1) of the
same tag), so the long exact sequence of the kernel sequence places `H^i(ℙⁿ_R, ℱ)` between two
finite modules over the Noetherian ring `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_cohomology_of_isCoherent [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (F : (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (polyGrading R n)).Modules)
    (hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F) (q : ℕ) :
    Module.Finite R
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of R)).inv ≫
          (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjPolyChart.projToSpecCoeff R n).appTop).hom).obj
        (((Stacks.Cohomology.AffineBase.moduleGlobalSections
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (polyGrading R n))).rightDerived q).obj F))

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.SerreVanishing.exists_isZero_Hgroup_twist_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YS] clause (4).** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `n ≥ 0` and `ℱ` a coherent
sheaf on `ℙⁿ_R = Proj R[T₀, …, Tₙ]`. For every `i > 0` the cohomology `H^i(ℙⁿ_R, ℱ(d))` vanishes
for all `d` large enough.

The proof is the source's: `ℱ` is a quotient of a finite direct sum of twists
(`hasTwistQuotients_polyGrading`, clause (1) of the same tag), the twists are eventually acyclic
(`hasEventuallyAcyclicTwists_polyGrading`, from the computation of `H^i(ℙⁿ_R, 𝒪(d))` of
[Stacks, Tag 01XT]), and the dévissage descends on the cohomological degree from the degree above
which everything vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isZero_Hgroup_twist_of_isCoherent [IsNoetherianRing R] (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i)
    (F : (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (polyGrading R n)).Modules)
    (hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F) :
    ∃ d₀ : ℤ, ∀ d : ℤ, d₀ ≤ d →
      IsZero (Hgroup (projRingSheaf (polyGrading R n)) ⊤ i
        (twistSheafOfModules (polyGrading R n) F d))
declarations.comment: (4) eventual vanishing of the higher cohomology of the twists

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.Cohomology.isZero_cohomology_of_lt_zero_or_dim_lt
declarations.doc:
**The cohomological dimension of projective space**: the cohomology of a quasi-coherent
module on projective `n`-space over an affine base vanishes in every degree outside `0, …, n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_cohomology_of_lt_zero_or_dim_lt (n : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S]
    (F : (projectiveSpaceOver n S).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (i : ℤ)
    (hi : i < 0 ∨ (n : ℤ) < i) :
    IsZero (((sectionsFunctor (projectiveSpaceOver n S) ⊤).rightDerivedPlus i).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveSpace.Cohomology.moduleFinite_truncation_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 01YS] clause (5).** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `n ≥ 0` and `ℱ` a coherent
sheaf on `ℙⁿ_R = Proj R[T₀, …, Tₙ]`. For every `k ∈ ℤ` the graded `R[T₀, …, Tₙ]`-module
`⨁_{d ≥ k} H⁰(ℙⁿ_R, ℱ(d))` is a finite `R[T₀, …, Tₙ]`-module.

The proof is the source's sandwich, now with both halves available: each homogeneous piece
`Γ(ℙⁿ_R, ℱ(d))` is a finite `R`-module by clause (3) at `i = 0`, and above some degree every
piece lies in the span of the piece one degree below
(`exists_forall_subset_span_twistedGlobalSectionsGrading`), so finitely many pieces generate.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_truncation_of_isCoherent [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (projRingSheaf R n))
    (hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F)
    (D : TwistedGlobalSectionsModule (polyGrading R n) F) (k : ℤ) :
    letI := D.moduleInst
    Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R)
      (TwistedGlobalSectionsModule.truncation (polyGrading R n) F D k)
declarations.comment: (5) finiteness of the graded module of twisted global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLimitPullbackCone
declarations.doc:
**Base change commutes with inverse limits of schemes.** Let `{ Dⱼ }` be an inverse system of
schemes indexed by a cofiltered category, let `c` be a limit cone over it, let `i` be an index,
and let `f : T ⟶ Dᵢ` be a scheme over the stage `Dᵢ`. Then
`(lim Dⱼ) ×_{Dᵢ} T = lim_{j ≥ i} (Dⱼ ×_{Dᵢ} T)`.

This is stated for an arbitrary limit cone `c`, so it applies in particular to the limit of a
system with affine transition morphisms, whose existence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasLimit_of_isCofiltered_of_isAffineHom`; that specialisation is recorded as
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLimitPullbackConeLimitCone`.
declarations.statement:
def isLimitPullbackCone [IsCofiltered I] (i : I) (f : T ⟶ D.obj i) :
    IsLimit (pullbackCone D c i f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStagesColimit_stagePullbackSection_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 01Z0] for a module of finite presentation on the base stage.** Let
`E` be a directed inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with affine
transition morphisms, let `c` be a limit cone on it, let `0` be a chosen index and let `ℱ₀` be a
module of **finite presentation** on `S₀ = E.obj (op 0)`.  Setting `ℱᵢ = f_{i0}⁺ℱ₀` for `i ≥ 0`
and `ℱ = f_0⁺ℱ₀`, the group `Γ(S, ℱ)` is the filtered colimit of the `Γ(Sᵢ, ℱᵢ)`, in the
elementwise form `Stacks.IsStagesColimit`: the maps to `Γ(S, ℱ)` are compatible with the
transition maps, every global section at the limit comes from a stage, and two global sections at
one stage with the same image at the limit already agree at a later stage.

The three clauses are, in order,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuleLimits.sectionsMap_canHom_modulePullbackSection_comp`,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuleLimits.exists_canonical_section_eq_of_isLimit` and
`...ModuleLimits.exists_canonical_section_eq_of_canonical_section_eq_of_isLimit`
— the cocone law for the canonical identification of an iterated pullback with the pullback along
the composite, and the surjectivity and injectivity halves, both of which read a global section
of a module as a morphism out of the structure sheaf and then apply [Stacks Project, Tag 01ZR],
(2) and (3) respectively.  That is why the coefficients are restricted to a module of finite
presentation: Tag 01ZR is a statement about finitely presented modules.

The tag is keyed because this is only part of Stacks 01Z0: the coefficient module is of finite
presentation and not merely quasi-coherent.  The whole tag is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isStagesColimit_stagePullbackSection_of_isQuasicoherent` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/ModuleLimits/SectionsColimitQuasiCoherent.lean`, which is this
statement interchanged with [Stacks Project, Tag 01PJ].  The index set lies in the universe of
the schemes, which is not a restriction that may be dropped —
`Stacks.LimitSectionsIdentification.not_card_01Z0` refutes the statement over an index set one
universe up.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStagesColimit_stagePullbackSection_of_isFinitePresentation
    [∀ {i j : αᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (E.map f)]
    [∀ i : αᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (E.obj i)] [∀ i : αᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparatedSpace (E.obj i)]
    (c : Cone E) (hc : IsLimit c) (a₀ : α) (F₀ : (E.obj (op a₀)).Modules)
    (hF₀ : F₀.IsFinitePresentation) :
    Stacks.IsStagesColimit
      (fun (a b : {a : α // a₀ ≤ a}) (h : a ≤ b) =>
        stagePullbackSectionTransition E a.2 b.2 (Subtype.coe_le_coe.mpr h) F₀)
      (fun a : {a : α // a₀ ≤ a} => stagePullbackSectionProjection E a.2 F₀ c)
declarations.comment: for a module of finite presentation on the base stage, with the index set in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStagesColimit_stagePullbackSection_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 01Z0].** Let `E` be a directed inverse system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, let `c` be a limit cone on it, let `0`
be a chosen index and let `ℱ₀` be a **quasi-coherent** module on `S₀ = E.obj (op 0)`.  Setting
`ℱᵢ = f_{i0}⁺ℱ₀` for `i ≥ 0` and `ℱ = f_0⁺ℱ₀`, the group `Γ(S, ℱ)` is the filtered colimit of the
`Γ(Sᵢ, ℱᵢ)`, in the elementwise form `Stacks.IsStagesColimit`: the maps to `Γ(S, ℱ)` are
compatible with the transition maps, every global section at the limit comes from a stage, and
two global sections at one stage with the same image at the limit already agree at a later stage.

The finite-presentation case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isStagesColimit_stagePullbackSection_of_isFinitePresentation`, and this is it
interchanged with the presentation of a quasi-coherent module as a filtered colimit of finitely
presented ones, [Stacks Project, Tag 01PJ]; see the file's implementation notes.

The index set lies in the universe of the schemes, which is not a restriction that may be
dropped — `Stacks.LimitSectionsIdentification.not_card_01Z0` refutes the statement over an index
set one universe up, so a `u`-small directed index set is exactly the source's "directed set".
declarations.statement:
theorem isStagesColimit_stagePullbackSection_of_isQuasicoherent
    [∀ {i j : αᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (E.map f)]
    [∀ i : αᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (E.obj i)] [∀ i : αᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparatedSpace (E.obj i)]
    (c : Cone E) (hc : IsLimit c) (a₀ : α) (F₀ : (E.obj (op a₀)).Modules)
    (hF₀ : F₀.IsQuasicoherent) :
    Stacks.IsStagesColimit
      (fun (a b : {a : α // a₀ ≤ a}) (h : a ≤ b) =>
        stagePullbackSectionTransition E a.2 b.2 (Subtype.coe_le_coe.mpr h) F₀)
      (fun a : {a : α // a₀ ≤ a} => stagePullbackSectionProjection E a.2 F₀ c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStagesColimit_appTop_of_isAffine_of_isLimit_of_directed
declarations.doc:
**The ring of global sections of a limit of affine schemes is the filtered colimit of the
rings of global sections of the stages**, in the elementwise form `Stacks.IsStagesColimit`: the
transition maps are the pullbacks of global sections along the morphisms of the inverse system
and the maps to the vertex are the pullbacks along the projections of the limiting cone.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStagesColimit_appTop_of_isAffine_of_isLimit_of_directed :
    Stacks.IsStagesColimit (G := fun a : α => (Γ(E.obj (op a), ⊤) : Type u))
      (T := (Γ(c.pt, ⊤) : Type u))
      (fun (a b : α) (h : a ≤ b) x => (E.map (homOfLE h).op).appTop.hom x)
      (fun (a : α) x => (c.π.app (op a)).appTop.hom x)
declarations.comment: for the structure sheaf over a directed inverse system of affine schemes, with the index set in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStagesColimit_appTop_of_isLimit_of_directed

**The ring of global sections of a limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with

declarations.statement:
theorem isStagesColimit_appTop_of_isLimit_of_directed :
    Stacks.IsStagesColimit (G := fun a : α => (Γ(E.obj (op a), ⊤) : Type u))
      (T := (Γ(c.pt, ⊤) : Type u))
      (fun (a b : α) (h : a ≤ b) x => (E.map (homOfLE h).op).appTop.hom x)
      (fun (a : α) x => (c.π.app (op a)).appTop.hom x)
declarations.comment: for the structure sheaf over a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, with the index set in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iSup_map_preimage_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01Z4, part (3).** Let `X = lim X_i` be the limit of a cofiltered inverse system
of quasi-compact schemes with affine transition morphisms. If a family of opens of a stage
`X_i` has inverse images in `X` covering `X`, then for some transition morphism
`X_j ⟶ X_i` the inverse images of the family in `X_j` cover `X_j`.

The source states this for a finite family of quasi-compact opens. Neither hypothesis is
used: a preimage of opens commutes with arbitrary suprema, so the statement for the single
open `⨆ k, V k` is the statement for the family. What the proof does use, and what
Situation 086P provides, is that every stage is quasi-compact.

The single-open case is Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_map_eq_top`, used here through
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_map_eq_top'`, its index-morphism-universe-free form, and the step
from one open to a family is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.preimage_iSup`. Mathlib records the
tag for parts (1) and (2) only, on `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_preimage_eq` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_map_preimage_eq_map_preimage`; its `exists_map_eq_top` carries no
tag, so part (3) is recorded here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iSup_map_preimage_eq_top {I : Type u} [Category.{v} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)] [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)]
    {i : I} {ι : Type*} (V : ι → (D.obj i).Opens)
    (hV : (⨆ k, c.π.app i ⁻¹ᵁ V k) = ⊤) :
    ∃ (j : I) (f : j ⟶ i), (⨆ k, D.map f ⁻¹ᵁ V k) = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01Z6.** In a directed inverse system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, if the limit is affine then every
sufficiently late stage is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isAffine
    {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (d : DescentSituation.{v, u} I)
    [IsAffine d.limitCone.pt] :
    ∃ i₀ : I, ∀ i : I, i₀ ≤ i → IsAffine (d.system.obj (op i))
declarations.comment: for an index preorder essentially small in the scheme universe

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteTypeOpenModel.exists_openModel
declarations.doc:
An open immersion of a finite-type scheme into an affine scheme
descends to a finite-type subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_openModel {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {W : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : W ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from W)]
    [QuasiCompact (terminal.from W)] [IsOpenImmersion f] :
    ∃ A : Subalgebra ℤ R, IsOpenModel f A
declarations.comment: existence of a finite-type open model

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteTypeOpenModel.openModel_directed
declarations.doc: Finite-type subalgebras admitting the open model are directed by inclusion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem openModel_directed {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {W : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : W ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from W)]
    [QuasiCompact (terminal.from W)] [IsOpenImmersion f] :
    ∀ A B : Subalgebra ℤ R, IsOpenModel f A → IsOpenModel f B →
      ∃ C : Subalgebra ℤ R, IsOpenModel f C ∧ A ≤ C ∧ B ≤ C
declarations.comment: directedness of the finite-type open models

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteTypeOpenModel.openModelCocone_isColimit
declarations.doc: The canonical cocone of finite-type open models is a colimit cocone.
declarations.statement:
public theorem openModelCocone_isColimit {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {W : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : W ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from W)]
    [QuasiCompact (terminal.from W)] [IsOpenImmersion f] :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (openModelCocone f))
declarations.comment: colimit of the finite-type open models

declarations.name: RingFibreProduct.isPullback_localization_away
declarations.doc:
Let `B' = B ×_R R'` be a fibre product of commutative rings along `s : B → R` and
`t : R' → R`, and let `h ∈ B'` map to `g ∈ B` and `f ∈ R'`, with `s g = t f`. Then the square
of localizations `B'_h → B_g`, `B'_h → R'_f`, `B_g → R_{s g}`, `R'_f → R_{s g}` is again a
pullback, that is, `B'_h ≅ B_g ×_{R_{s g}} R'_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_localization_away
    {R R' B B' : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [CommRing B] [CommRing B']
    (s : B →+* R) (t : R' →+* R)
    (πB : B' →+* B) (πR' : B' →+* R')
    (hPB : IsPullback (CommRingCat.ofHom πB) (CommRingCat.ofHom πR')
      (CommRingCat.ofHom s) (CommRingCat.ofHom t))
    (h : B') (g : B) (f : R')
    (hB : πB h = g) (hR' : πR' h = f) (hcompat : s g = t f) :
    IsPullback
      (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (Localization.awayLift ((algebraMap B (Localization.Away g)).comp πB) h (by
          rw [RingHom.comp_apply, hB]
          exact IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit g)))
      (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (Localization.awayLift ((algebraMap R' (Localization.Away f)).comp πR') h (by
          rw [RingHom.comp_apply, hR']
          exact IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit f)))
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (Localization.awayMap s g))
      (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (Localization.awayLift ((algebraMap R (Localization.Away (s g))).comp t) f (by
          rw [RingHom.comp_apply, ← hcompat]
          exact IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit (s g))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_iSup_basicOpen_comp_SpecMap_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of rings, a finite union of standard opens which descend from the
other side of the square and on which that side becomes an isomorphism maps by an open
immersion to the spectrum of the remaining corner.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOpenImmersion_iSup_basicOpen_comp_SpecMap_of_isPullback
    {B R B' R' : Type u} [CommRing B] [CommRing R] [CommRing B'] [CommRing R']
    (s : B →+* R) (p : B' →+* B) (r : B' →+* R') (t : R' →+* R)
    (hcart : IsPullback (CommRingCat.ofHom p) (CommRingCat.ofHom r)
      (CommRingCat.ofHom s) (CommRingCat.ofHom t))
    {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → R') (g : Fin n → B)
    (hfg : ∀ i, t (f i) = s (g i))
    (hloc : ∀ i, Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap s (g i))) :
    IsOpenImmersion
      ((⨆ i, PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (f i) : (Spec (.of R')).Opens).ι ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom r))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isLimit_affine_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Absolute Noetherian approximation.**  A quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme `S` is
the inverse limit of an inverse system of schemes over a directed set whose transition
morphisms are affine and whose every stage is of finite type over the integers.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_affine_locallyOfFiniteType (S : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace S]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (F : Iᵒᵈ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : (Functor.const Iᵒᵈ).obj S ⟶ F),
      (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵈ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (F.map f)) ∧
      (∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from (F.obj i))) ∧
      (∀ i, QuasiCompact (terminal.from (F.obj i))) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk S c))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isLimit_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZA.** A quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme is the inverse
limit of a directed system of schemes of finite type over the integers with affine transition
morphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isLimit_finiteType (S : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace S]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D),
      (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (v : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map v)) ∧
      (∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from (D.obj i))) ∧
      (∀ i, QuasiCompact (terminal.from (D.obj i))) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit c) ∧ c.pt = S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_isLimitPreservingOnAffineTransitions
declarations.doc:
A scheme `X` over `S` is locally of finite presentation over `S` if and only if its functor
of points `h_X = Mor_S(-, X)` turns every cofiltered inverse limit of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated `S`-schemes with affine transition morphisms into a filtered colimit.

The same characterization with the inverse systems restricted to affine schemes is
`locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_isLimitPreserving_yoneda`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_isLimitPreservingOnAffineTransitions
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ↔
      IsLimitPreservingOnAffineTransitions S (yoneda.obj (Over.mk f))
declarations.comment:
parts (1) and (3), with the inverse systems indexed by cofiltered categories
rather than by directed sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.locallyOfFinitePresentation_tfae_directed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 01ZC.** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` the following are equivalent:

1. `f` is locally of finite presentation;
2. for every directed set `Λ` and every inverse system `(T_i)` of affine `S`-schemes over `Λ`,
   the canonical map `colim_i Mor_S(T_i, X) → Mor_S(lim_i T_i, X)` is bijective;
3. for every directed set `Λ` and every inverse system `(T_i)` of `S`-schemes over `Λ` whose
   transition morphisms are affine and whose members are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the
   canonical map `colim_i Mor_S(T_i, X) → Mor_S(lim_i T_i, X)` is bijective.

A directed set is a nonempty preordered type in which any two elements have an upper bound, as in
the source, taken in the universe of the schemes; an inverse system over it is a functor out of
`Λᵒᵖ`. Bijectivity of the canonical map is `PreservesColimit` of the functor of points
`Mor_S(-, X)` for the opposite diagram.

The cofiltered readings of conditions (2) and (3) are
`locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_isLimitPreserving_yoneda` and
`locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_isLimitPreservingOnAffineTransitions`; condition (1) implies
the directed forms by specializing them along `Λᵒᵖ`, and the directed form of condition (2)
implies condition (1) by the directed criterion
`AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_directedAffineLimit_surjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_tfae_directed {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    List.TFAE
      [ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f,
        ∀ (Λ : Type u) [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirectedOrder Λ] (D : Λᵒᵖ ⥤ Over S),
          (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i).left) → PreservesColimit D.op (yoneda.obj (Over.mk f)),
        ∀ (Λ : Type u) [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirectedOrder Λ] (D : Λᵒᵖ ⥤ Over S),
          (∀ (i j : Λᵒᵖ) (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g).left) →
          (∀ i, CompactSpace (D.obj i).left) →
          (∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i).left) →
            PreservesColimit D.op (yoneda.obj (Over.mk f)) ]

registrations.name: locallyOfFinitePresentation_iff_isLimitPreserving_yoneda
registrations.comment:
parts (1) and (2), with the inverse systems indexed by cofiltered categories
rather than by directed sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finitePresentation_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZE.**  A quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme locally of finite
type over `S` immerses over `S` into a scheme of finite presentation over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_isImmersion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f' : X' ⟶ S) (i : X ⟶ X'),
      FinitePresentation f' ∧ IsImmersion i ∧ i ≫ f' = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finitePresentation_closedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZG.**  A morphism locally of finite type from a quasi-compact,
quasi-separated scheme to a quasi-separated scheme factors as a closed immersion into a scheme
of finite presentation over the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_closedImmersion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (p : X' ⟶ S) (i : X ⟶ X'),
      FinitePresentation p ∧ IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ p = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isSeparated_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZH.** Let `S` be a quasi-separated scheme and let `X = lim X_i` be a
directed inverse limit of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes over `S` with affine
transition morphisms. If `X ⟶ S` is separated, then `X_i ⟶ S` is separated for all sufficiently
large `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isSeparated_app {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    [EssentiallySmall.{u} I] (d : DescentSituation.{v, u} I) {S : Scheme.{u}}
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (t : d.system ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj S)
    (hsep : IsSeparated (d.limitCone.π.app (op d.base) ≫ t.app (op d.base))) :
    ∃ i₀ : I, ∀ i : I, i₀ ≤ i → IsSeparated (t.app (op i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isClosedImmersion_into_isSeparated_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
A separated morphism of finite type onto a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme factors as
a closed immersion followed by a separated morphism of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosedImmersion_into_isSeparated_finitePresentation
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f' : X' ⟶ S) (i : X ⟶ X'),
      IsSeparated f' ∧ FinitePresentation f' ∧ IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ f' = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_finitePresentation_closedImmersion
declarations.doc:
A finite morphism `f : X ⟶ S` of schemes whose target is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated factors as a closed immersion `X ⟶ X'` followed by a morphism
`X' ⟶ S` which is finite and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinite_finitePresentation_closedImmersion {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFinite f] [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f' : X' ⟶ S) (i : X ⟶ X'),
      IsFinite f' ∧ FinitePresentation f' ∧ IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ f' = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitDescent.exists_model_of_finitePresentation_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
Let `S = lim Sᵢ` be a cofiltered limit of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine
transition morphisms. Every scheme of finite presentation over `S` is isomorphic, over `S`, to the
base change of a scheme of finite presentation over one of the stages `Sᵢ`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.LimitDescent.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_essentiallySmall`
stated with `CategoryTheory.Over.pullback`. The index hypothesis
`CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall.{u} I` is relative to the universe of the schemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_model_of_finitePresentation_of_essentiallySmall {I : Type v}
    [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D)
    (hc : IsLimit c) [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (X : Over c.pt) (hX : FinitePresentation X.hom) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Xᵢ : Over (D.obj i)), FinitePresentation Xᵢ.hom ∧
      Nonempty (X ≅ (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj Xᵢ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_morphism_after_baseChange
declarations.doc:
A morphism between the base changes of two schemes of finite presentation
descends after passing to a later stage of a cofiltered inverse system.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_morphism_after_baseChange
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ {i j : I} (e : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map e)]
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (i : I) (X Y : Over (D.obj i))
    (hX : FinitePresentation X.hom) (hY : FinitePresentation Y.hom)
    (f : (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj X ⟶ (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj Y) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i)
      (g : (Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj X ⟶ (Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj Y)
      (α : (Over.pullback (c.π.app j)).obj ((Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj X) ≅
        (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj X)
      (β : (Over.pullback (c.π.app j)).obj ((Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj Y) ≅
        (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj Y),
      α.hom.left ≫ pullback.fst X.hom (c.π.app i) =
          pullback.fst ((Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj X).hom (c.π.app j) ≫
            pullback.fst X.hom (D.map e) ∧
        β.hom.left ≫ pullback.fst Y.hom (c.π.app i) =
          pullback.fst ((Over.pullback (D.map e)).obj Y).hom (c.π.app j) ≫
            pullback.fst Y.hom (D.map e) ∧
        α.hom ≫ f = (Over.pullback (c.π.app j)).map g ≫ β.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_eq_of_baseChange_eq
declarations.doc:
Two morphisms at one stage which become equal after base change to the
inverse limit are equal after passing to a later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_eq_of_baseChange_eq
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ {i j : I} (e : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map e)]
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (i : I) (X Y : Over (D.obj i))
    (hX : FinitePresentation X.hom) (hY : FinitePresentation Y.hom) (f g : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfg : (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).map f = (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).map g) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i),
      (Over.pullback (D.map e)).map f = (Over.pullback (D.map e)).map g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.eventually_eq_of_baseChange_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZM, part (3).** Two morphisms between schemes of finite presentation
at one stage of a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with
affine transition morphisms, which become equal after base change to the limit, are equal after
passing to a later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_eq_of_baseChange_eq
    [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ {i j : I} (e : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map e)]
    [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (i : I) (X Y : Over (D.obj i))
    (hX : FinitePresentation X.hom) (hY : FinitePresentation Y.hom) (f g : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfg : (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).map f = (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).map g) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i),
      (Over.pullback (D.map e)).map f = (Over.pullback (D.map e)).map g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitFPObjectDescent.exists_model_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZM, part (1).** A scheme of finite presentation over the limit of a
cofiltered system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms is
obtained by base change from some stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_model_of_finitePresentation {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    [EssentiallySmall.{u} I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)] [∀ i : I, CompactSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ i : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)] (X : Over c.pt) (hX : FinitePresentation X.hom) :
    ∃ (i : I) (Xᵢ : Over (D.obj i)),
      FinitePresentation Xᵢ.hom ∧ Nonempty (X ≅ (Over.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj Xᵢ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineHom_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
If a morphism over one stage of a cofiltered inverse system becomes affine
after base change to the limit, it becomes affine at some later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineHom_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [IsAffineHom ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : i ⟶ i₀),
      IsAffineHom ((Over.pullback (D.map hi)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_baseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZO.** If a morphism over a stage of a cofiltered inverse system is
locally of finite type and its base change to the limit is finite, then its base change to some
later stage is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinite_baseChange_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left]
    [IsFinite ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : i ⟶ i₀), IsFinite ((Over.pullback (D.map hi)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isClosedImmersion_baseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
If a morphism over a stage is locally of finite type and becomes a closed
immersion over the inverse limit, it becomes a closed immersion at a later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosedImmersion_baseChange_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left]
    [IsClosedImmersion ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : i ⟶ i₀),
      IsClosedImmersion ((Over.pullback (D.map hi)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSeparated_baseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZQ.** If a morphism over a stage of a cofiltered inverse system is
separated after base change to the limit, then it is separated after base change to some later
stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSeparated_baseChange_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    (hc : IsLimit c)
    [IsSeparated ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀), IsSeparated ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuleLimits.exists_pullback_map_eq_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
Let `c` be a limit cone on a cofiltered diagram `D` of
schemes with affine transition morphisms and let `ψ₁, ψ₂ : F ⟶ G` be morphisms of sheaves of
modules of finite presentation on a quasi-compact stage `D.obj i`.  If the pullbacks of `ψ₁` and
`ψ₂` to `c.pt` agree, then their pullbacks to `D.obj j` agree for some `j` over `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pullback_map_eq_of_isLimit (hc : IsLimit c) (i : I) [CompactSpace (D.obj i)]
    (F G : (D.obj i).Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] [G.IsFinitePresentation]
    (ψ₁ ψ₂ : F ⟶ G)
    (h : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (c.π.app i)).map ψ₁ =
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (c.π.app i)).map ψ₂) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i),
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (D.map e)).map ψ₁ =
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (D.map e)).map ψ₂

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuleLimits.exists_map_of_pullback_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 01ZR] (2), with the canonical identifications written out.**  This is
the statement of the clause of the tag verbatim, obtained from
`exists_map_of_pullback_canonical_of_isLimit'` by unfolding the canonical identification.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_map_of_pullback_of_isLimit (hc : IsLimit c) (i : I)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (F G : (D.obj i).Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] [G.IsFinitePresentation]
    (φ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj F ⟶
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj G) :
    ∃ (j : I) (e : j ⟶ i)
      (φj : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (D.map e)).obj F ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (D.map e)).obj G),
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (c.π.app j)).map φj ≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (c.π.app j) (D.map e)).hom.app G ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (c.w e)).hom.app G =
        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (c.π.app j) (D.map e)).hom.app F ≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (c.w e)).hom.app F ≫ φ

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuleLimits.exists_isFinitePresentation_pullback_iso_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 01ZR] (1) for a cofiltered limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated
schemes with affine transition morphisms.**  A sheaf of modules of finite presentation on the
limit is the pullback of one on a stage.  This is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuleLimits.exists_isFinitePresentation_pullback_iso_of_map` with its
hypothesis `hmap` discharged by `exists_map_of_pullback_of_isLimit`, and it is the statement
[Stacks Project, Tag 0ASY] calls.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinitePresentation_pullback_iso_of_qcqs (hc : IsLimit c)
    [∀ j : I, CompactSpace (D.obj j)] [∀ j : I, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj j)]
    (F : c.pt.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∃ (i : I) (Fᵢ : (D.obj i).Modules),
      Fᵢ.IsFinitePresentation ∧
        Nonempty (F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (c.π.app i)).obj Fᵢ)

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineFromFiniteSurjective.isAffine_of_finite_surjective
declarations.doc:
The target of a finite surjective morphism of schemes is affine when
its source is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_finite_surjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFinite f] [Surjective f] [IsAffine X] : IsAffine S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_pairwise_disjoint_affine_opens_of_generic_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZV.** A finite family of distinct irreducible components
of a quasi-separated scheme has pairwise disjoint affine open neighborhoods of its
generic points; the union of these neighborhoods is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pairwise_disjoint_affine_opens_of_generic_points
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (Z : ι → Set X)
    (hZ : ∀ i, Z i ∈ irreducibleComponents X) (hZ_injective : Injective Z)
    (η : ι → X) (hη : ∀ i, IsGenericPoint (η i) (Z i)) :
    ∃ U : ι → X.Opens,
      (∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
      (∀ i, η i ∈ U i) ∧
      Pairwise (Disjoint on U) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen (iSup U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_open_containing_generic_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZV.** The generic points of a finite family of distinct
irreducible components of a quasi-separated scheme lie in a single affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_open_containing_generic_points
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (Z : ι → Set X)
    (hZ : ∀ i, Z i ∈ irreducibleComponents X) (hZ_injective : Injective Z)
    (η : ι → X) (hη : ∀ i, IsGenericPoint (η i) (Z i)) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ i, η i ∈ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_mem_of_genericPoints_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 01ZX.** In a quasi-separated scheme, any point and
the generic points of finitely many pairwise distinct irreducible components
are contained in a common affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_mem_of_genericPoints_irreducibleComponents
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] {n : ℕ}
    (Z : Fin n → Set X) (hZ : ∀ i, Z i ∈ irreducibleComponents X)
    (hZ_injective : Function.Injective Z)
    (η : Fin n → X) (hη : ∀ i, IsGenericPoint (η i) (Z i)) (x : X) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ ∀ i, η i ∈ U

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleAffineAvoidance.exists_affineOpen_containing_finite_of_ample
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01ZY, part (3).** A finite set of points of a scheme carrying an ample invertible
`𝒪_X`-module lies in an affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_containing_finite_of_ample (hL : IsAmple X L) {E : Set X}
    (hE : E.Finite) : ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ E ⊆ (U : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCluster.exists_affineOpen_containing_finite_of_immersion_proj
declarations.doc:
A finite set of points of a scheme `X` with an immersion `X ⟶ Proj 𝒮` lies in an affine open of
`X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_containing_finite_of_immersion_proj {X : Scheme.{u}} {S : Type u}
    {σ : Type v} [CommRing S] [SetLike σ S] [AddSubgroupClass σ S] (𝒮 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒮]
    (i : X ⟶ Proj 𝒮) [IsImmersion i] {E : Set X} (hE : E.Finite) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ E ⊆ (U : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCluster.exists_affineOpen_containing_finite_of_isQuasiAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01ZY, part (1).** A finite set of points of a quasi-affine scheme lies in an
affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_containing_finite_of_isQuasiAffine {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.IsQuasiAffine]
    {E : Set X} (hE : E.Finite) : ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ E ⊆ U

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleCluster.exists_affineOpen_containing_finite_of_immersion_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 01ZY, part (2).** A finite set of points of a locally closed subscheme of an
affine scheme lies in an affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_containing_finite_of_immersion_affine {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsImmersion i] [IsAffine Y] {E : Set X} (hE : E.Finite) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ E ⊆ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_of_isImmersion_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
A scheme `X` with an immersion `i : X ⟶ Y` into an affine scheme `Y` (that is, isomorphic to
a locally closed subscheme of an affine scheme) has every finite set of its points inside a
single affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineOpen_of_isImmersion_of_isAffine {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Y]
    (i : X ⟶ Y) [IsImmersion i] {E : Set X} (hE : E.Finite) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ E ⊆ (U : Set X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_of_isQuasiAffine
declarations.doc: A quasi-affine scheme has every finite set of its points inside a single affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineOpen_of_isQuasiAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.IsQuasiAffine] {E : Set X}
    (hE : E.Finite) : ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ E ⊆ (U : Set X)
